For indeed, it is only *ṭha*, *ta*, and *śa*. 4. When followed by *śa*, there is the single substitute form (*pararūpa*). 5. By the rule "the augment *num* is added to a root that has *i* as its *it*" (*idita*), the augment *num* is applied.

*Rādhaḥ*: [The root] *as* with the suffix *niś* is udātta by position. *Advivaḥ*: [from] *advivajram*; [the sense is] "he who possesses that," hence the suffix *matup*. By the rule *chandasīraḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.15), there is the substitution of *v* for *r*. In the vocative, *num* is added by the rule *ugidacām* (Pāṇini 7.1.70). The elision of the final consonant (*halṅyādibhyaḥ*) and the elision of the final member of the conjunct (*saṃyogāntalopaḥ*) apply. By the rule *matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi* (Pāṇini 8.3.1), there is the substitution of *ru* [for the *m* of *mat*]. This becomes a *visarjanīya*. And the vocative receives the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent.
Neither of the two worlds, heaven and earth, can resist you as you exert yourself; win for us the waters of heaven and shake down the cattle for us.
Not indeed; both heaven and earth urge you on as you prosper. Conquer the sun-filled waters; shake down the cows for us. 8.
O Indra, both *rodasī*—heaven and earth—even as they make you, who are "not prospering" (*ṛdhāyamāṇa*), the source of danger for the enemy, [bear you].

In the *ukthya* chants of the third pressing during the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*, among the pairs of *stotriya* and *anurūpa* verses for the *acchāvāka*, the second pair has the triplet "āśrutkarṇa" as its *anurūpa*.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "egha pu" in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (7.8): "śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyā āśrutkarṇa śrudhī havam."
O you with ears that hear, listen to my call; now indeed take to yourself my songs.
O Indra, place this hymn of mine even closer than your own companions.
O you whose ears are ready to hear, listen! Now indeed take to heart my songs; O Indra, make this hymn of mine dearer even than a close friend. 9.
O Indra, you whose ears hear from all sides—listen quickly to our invocation!
Take to heart and hold in your mind even these songs of praise from me, the Hotṛ-priest.
Furthermore, draw near to this collection of words in the form of a hymn from me, even closer than to your own chariot-horse.
The meaning is: just as you consider his word to be pleasing, so too should you take delight in our hymns of praise.
*Āśrutkarṇa*: *āśrut* means "listen on all sides" (*ā samantāt śṛṇuta*);
it is formed with the suffix *kvip*.
By the rule *hrasvasya tuK* (Pāṇini 6.1.71), [the augment *tuK* is added]. He whose ears are of such a kind:
by the rule *āmantritasya ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.198), there is the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable.
Listen! [The root] *śru* [is used] in the sense of "hearing. The suffix *hi* is the imperative (*loṭ*) form.
This [suffix] is prescribed by Pāṇini’s rule *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* (3.1.74).

The elision (*luk*) occurs according to *bahulaṃ chandasi* (2.4.73). Because it is taught as part of that same grammatical operation (*niyogaśiṣṭatvāt*), the substitution of *śu* for *śru* is also set aside.
The substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs by the rule *śrṛṇupukṛvṛbhyaśchandasi* (Pāṇini 6.4.102).
Because it is taught later [in the sequence of rules], it takes the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

Since the preceding vocative is treated as non-existent according to *āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat* (Pāṇini 8.1.72), the word does not constitute a complete *pāda*; consequently, the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) prescribed by *tiṅaṅatiṅaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.1.28) does not apply.
In the *Saṃhitā*, there is a long vowel [in *havam*] according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.3.137: "The long vowel is also seen in other cases.
[The root] *hvṛ* [is used] in the sense of rivalry and sound.

By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.34), when the non-conditional *saṃprasāraṇa* has been applied, the suffix *ap* is added by *ṛdorap* (Pāṇini 3.2.57) because the stem ends in *u*. Since the suffix *ap* is *pit*, the accent of the root remains. [The particle] *nu*.
In the *saṃhitā*, there is a long vowel according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.3.133: "In the *ṛc*, [the final vowel] of words ending in *nudhama*, *akṣutam*, *kṛtam*, and *rūpam* [is lengthened].
*Cit*:
the particle *ca* and others are *anudātta*.
*dadhiṣva*. This is the imperative (*loṭ*) of the root *dhā*; [by Pāṇini 7.1.41] "the *thās* [ending] becomes *se*."
By the rule *savābhyāṃ vāmau* (Pāṇini 3.4.91),
there is *ślu*-elision of the suffix *śap*,
and the short vowel is substituted for the reduplicated syllable.

Because of the rule *chandasyubhayathā* (Pāṇini 3.4.117), which permits the Vedic usage of both forms, the augment *iṭ* is admitted even for the *ārṣa-dhātu* (Vedic verbal root). There is elision of the vowel *ā*.
There is *nighāta* (anudātta accentuation).
*Mama*:
By the rule *tavamamau ṅasi* (Pāṇini 7.2.96), the form *mama* is substituted for everything up to the final phoneme of *yuṣmad*.

Although the word would have been oxytone by the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*), the rule *yuṣmadasmadorṅasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.211) prescribes that it is instead acute-accented on the first syllable.
*Kṛṣva* [is the second person singular imperative]. It is derived from the root *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of "doing" (*karaṇe*), in the *loṭ* (imperative) mood.
"Thāmas te," "savābhyāṃ vāmau"; [in these cases] there is elision (luk) of the *śap* suffix because of the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi."
Because it remains [as a separate word], it bears the accent of the suffix; because it begins a quarter-verse (pāda), it does not receive the *nighāta* suppression. *Yujaḥ*.
The acute accent (*udātta*) on the case-ending is due to Pāṇini’s rule *sāvekācaḥ* (6.1.168).
The word *antaram* has the acute accent on its first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group.
For the wise know you as the showerer of blessings, the hearer of our call in battles; we invoke the aid of that showerer, which bestows a thousandfold gains.
For the wise man indeed calls upon you, the most powerful, who hears our invocation in the contests for booty; we invoke the aid of you, the most powerful, which wins a thousandfold.
1. Like that of a friend; 2. Just as one considers the word of a friend, Mṛṣaṇa, to be dear to oneself—O Indra, we, the inspired poets, call upon you.
What kind of you?
You who rain down desires most abundantly (*vṛṣantam*), and who hear our invocation (*havanaśrutam*) in battles (*vājeṣu*).
We invoke you—your protection (*ūtim*) directed toward us—who rains down desires and the like most abundantly. We call upon you.
Of what nature?
One who is most excellent at winning wealth—that is, a giver of thousands of riches.
In the word *vipra*, by the rule *vido laṭo vā* (Pāṇini 3.4.83), there is the substitution of *mā* for the suffix *mas*;
it is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In the *saṃhitā* [text], there is a long vowel according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.3.135: *avyayatiṅaḥ*. [The word is] *vṛṣantamam*.
[The root] *vṛṣu* [is used] in the sense of "to sprinkle" (*secanē*).

The suffix *kanin* is applied by the rule *kaninyutpitakṣarājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra 1.154). Because it is marked with *ṅ*, it is ādyudātta (accented on the first syllable). Since it is also marked with *p*, that same [first syllable] remains [as the udātta].

Because of the rule *ayamayaādīni chandasi* (Pāṇini 1.4.20), [the word *ayam*] is treated as a *bha*-stem; consequently, due to the absence of *pada*-status, there is no elision of the nasal (*n*) according to Pāṇini 8.2.7.
In the word *vājeṣu*, the word *vāja* belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group and is accented on its first syllable.
*havanaśrutam*:
With the word *hvah* understood from the previous rule, the suffix *syuṭ* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.34 (*bahulaṃ chandasi*), resulting in vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
The term *kri* is used in the sense of "he who hears the invocation" (*havanaṃ śṛṇoti*).
The augment *tug* is applied;
[the form] *vṛṣantamasya* has been explained.
We invoke (*hūmahe*).
The semi-vowel *samprasāraṇa* occurs by the rule "in the Veda, [the substitution is] frequent" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
Following the continued application of the term "of the suffix *śap*" (*śapaḥ*), the elision (*luk*) of *śap* occurs by the rule "in the Veda, [it is] frequent" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*, Pāṇini 2.4.73).
*Ūtim*: This is a nipātana (irregularly formed word) with an udātta accent on the final syllable, according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.3.97 (*ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca*).
*Sahasasātām*.
He who wins a thousand is "sahasasāḥ. [The root] *paṇ* is used in the sense of "giving.
[The suffix] *viṭ* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.67: "After the roots *jan*, *san*, *khan*, *kram*, and *gam*, the suffix *viṭ* is added."
The substitution of the vowel *ā* is prescribed by the rule *viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.41).
As for the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member of the compound, it remains because the suffix *tama* is marked with the *piṭ* indicator.
O Indra, son of Kuśika, come hither and, being exhilarated, drink our pressed soma! Prolong our new span of life and make the seer a master of power.
O Indra, son of Kuśika, being exhilarated, drink our pressed soma; grant us new life and extend it far; make us a seer who possesses conquering power. 11.
"O Indra, come quickly toward us"—this is the ellipsis.

O Kauśika, son of Kuśika, Indra, being *mandasānaḥ*—that is, having become joyful—drink the pressed *soma*. Although Viśvāmitra is the son of Kuśika, nevertheless, because he is addressed as Indra himself through that [son's] form, his status as the son of Kuśika is not contradictory.
This account is stated in the Anukramaṇikā: “Kuśika, desiring a son equal to Indra, practiced celibacy;
to him was born a son, Gāthin, who was indeed Indra” (Anuvāka, Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3.1).
O Indra, promote—that is, cause to increase excellently and preeminently—the new life, the span of existence devoted to the performance of sacred rites, which is worthy of praise by all the gods.
Therefore, make me an ṛṣi endowed with the attainment of thousands, a seer of that which transcends the senses.

In the *saṃhitā*, there is a long vowel according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.3.133: “*ṛci tunudhamaśrutamkutoruyāṇām*” [in a Ṛgvedic verse, the long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the particles *tu*, *nu*, *dham*, *aśrutam*, *ku*, *trotur*, and *yāt*].
*naḥ*.
In the *saṃhitā*, [the rule] "after an udātta, an anudātta becomes svarita" applies;
[here,] *indra* receives the *āmantrita-nighāta* (enclitic suppression).
Kauśika,
Nivāta,
Mandasāna.
Regarding *havyan*: [the root] *mad* is used in the senses of praising, rejoicing, intoxication, lack of sleep, beauty, and motion.
Following the recurrence of the rule *asānac* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.253), the suffix *asānac* is applied by the rule *ṛñjibhimandisahibhyaḥ kit* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.254). Thus, *havyan* is derived.
Because it has the suffix *cvi*, it is udātta on the final syllable.
*Sutam*: the accent of the suffix.
*Navyam*: from the root *ṇu* in the sense of "praise" (*stutau*), with the suffix *yat* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.97 (*aco yat*).
This is a grammatical suffix (*guṇa*).
By the rule *vānto yi pratyaye* (Pāṇini 6.1.79), there is the substitution of *av*. By the rule *yato ’nāvaḥ*, it receives the udātta accent on the first syllable.

Regarding *āyuḥ*: with the words *usi* and *nit* being supplied from the context, the suffix *usi* is applied by the rule *eterṇicca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.275). Because of the marker *ṇ*, there is the substitution of *vṛddhi* and the replacement of *i* with *ā*.
The word *nic* has an udātta accent on its first syllable.
By the rule *nipātasya ca*, there is lengthening in the *saṃhitā* [of *su*].
The substitution of *ś* for *s* occurs due to the transposition [of the rule], according to Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.100: *ṛta id dhātoḥ*.

1. [The word] *ṭha-vijñāna*. 2. Because of the *pit* designation, that very [suffix] remains; because of the *pit* designation, that very [suffix] remains. (*ka. 14; 7. 1. 100*) Thus, there is the substitution of *it*. By the rule *ato heḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.105), there is the elision (*luk*) of *hi*. [The form] *kṛdhi*. [The root] *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of "making. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the elision (*luk*) of the *śar* [consonant]. By the rule *śrugṛpṛkṛbhyaśchandasi*, there is the substitution of *dhi* for *hi*. [The word] *sahasrasām*. [This has been] explained. [The word] *ṛṣabham*. [The root] *ṛṣī* in the sense of "going. While the term *in* is being carried over, by the rule *igupadhātkit* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.559), there is the suffix *kvip*. Due to the *kit* designation, there is an absence of *guṇa*. Because of the *nit* designation, there is the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable.
In the Pravargya rite, one should recite "pari tvā" [as the concluding verse].

This is prescribed in the section on "released water" (*sṛṣṭodaka*) by the Sūtra: "O lover of songs, the songs have encompassed you; upon the two [stones] has been placed the hymnic speech" (*āśva. śrau. 4. 6*).
Likewise, this same verse serves as the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) during the moving forward of the *havirdhāna* carts.

In the section concerning "They proceed with the Havirdhāna [carts]," it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "He should conclude with the verse, 'O lover of songs, the songs [surround] thee'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.9).
Likewise, the Brāhmaṇa states: "He concludes with the final verse, 'O lover of songs, the songs [surround] thee'" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1.29).
May these songs encompass you on every side, O lover of song;
may they, increasing after your increase, be dear to you as your beloved ones.
May these songs encompass you on every side, O lover of song; may they increase your life, and as increases themselves, may they be pleasing to you. 12.

O *girvaṇas* (you who delight in songs), O Indra, may these our songs—our praises offered in all works from every side—encompass you on all sides; that is, may they reach you completely. Of what nature are these songs? They are "increasing" (*vṛddhayaḥ*), meaning they grow stronger by following after you, who are possessed of increased life (*vṛddhāyu*). Furthermore, may these songs, being "cherished" (*juṣṭāḥ*) by you—that is, served by you—become "delights" (*juṣṭayaḥ*), causes of pleasure for us. **Grammatical Notes:** * **girvaṇaḥ**: Derived from *gīrbhiḥ* (by songs) and the root *van* (to enjoy/partake) with the suffix *asun*. The lengthening of the vowel in *giraḥ* is Vedic. It takes the accent of the vocative (*āmantrita-nighāta*). * **viśvataḥ**: By the rule *liti* (Pāṇini 6.1.193), the syllable preceding the suffix is acute. * **vṛddhāyum**: From the root *vṛdh* (to increase) with the suffix *kta*. Since the root is marked with *udit*, the suffix *iṭ* is optional by *udito vā*; thus, by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*, there is no *iṭ* in the past participle (*niṣṭhā*). The accent is that of the suffix. The second member is derived from *haṇ* (to go) with the suffix *uṇ* (Vedic), resulting in *āyu*. Due to the *ṇi*, there is *vṛddhi* and the substitution of *āy*. Thus, "one whose life is increased. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first member retains its original accent. * **vṛddhayaḥ**: From the root *vṛdh* with the suffix *ktin*. There is no *iṭ* by the rule *titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca*. Due to the *ṇi*, the first syllable is acute. * **juṣṭāḥ**: There is no *iṭ* in the past participle by the rule *śrīdito niṣṭhāyām*. The acute accent on the first syllable follows the rule *nityaṃ mantre* (Pāṇini 6.1.210), which applies to words like *juṣṭa* and *āpita* in mantras. * **juṣṭayaḥ**: From the root *juṣ* (to please/serve) with the suffix *ktin*. There is no *iṭ* by the rule *titutra*. The seer (ṛṣi) of the eight-verse hymn beginning with "indra viśvā" is named Jeta, the son of Madhucchandas.
Thus it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "Indraṣṭo [is] Jeta, the son of Madhucchandas.
Regarding the meter, it was stated in the previous hymn that it is in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
Indra follows as the deity.
As for the application (*viniyoga*): the entire hymn is to be recited in the *Niṣkevalya* section of the *Mahāvrata*.

In the section titled "The Thigh" (*ūru*), Śaunaka has prescribed in his Sūtra: "Regarding the *Anuṣṭubh* hymn beginning with 'indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan,' one should recite the first half-verse of its first [verse] and then interlace it with the first half-verse of the next [verse], verse by verse, foot by foot, in the manner of an *Anuṣṭubh*, until the penultimate verse" (*Ai. Ā. 5.3.1*).
And in the Brāhmaṇa, in the first Āraṇyaka, in the section beginning with "pra vo mahe," it is stated: "The words 'indraṃ viśvā arvīvṛdhan' are [in] Anuṣṭubh meters" (Ai. Ā. 1.5.2).
Likewise, on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya sacrifice, in the Niṣkevalya Śastra, the sequence ends with the Anuṣṭubh verse "indraṃ viśvā arvīvṛdhan.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "ratome vardhamāne" in the Sūtra: "'upa no haribhiḥ sutam' and 'indraṃ viśvā arvīvṛdhan'" (Āśva. Śr. 7.12).

All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils. (1) indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhanta samudravyacasaṃ giraḥ | rathītamaṃ rathīnāṃ vājānāṃ satpatiṃ patim || 1 || All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils. (1)
All our songs—our praises—have magnified Indra.
What kind of Indra?

One who is "sea-extensive," pervading like the ocean; the best of charioteers among those yoked to chariots, the most preeminent warrior; the lord of strengths, that is, of foods; and the protector of the good, of those who abide on the path of truth.
*viśvāḥ*:
from *viś*, with the suffix *kan*; it is unaccented (*nissvara*).

*avīvṛdhan*. In the case of the root *vṛdh* with the suffix *ṇic* followed by the *caṅ* (reduplication), since the rule *urṛt* (Pāṇini 7.4.8) is still in effect, the rule *nityaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 7.4.8) prescribes the substitution of *ṛ* for the vowel *ṛ*; consequently, there is no substitution of *latva* (the change to *l*) nor the presence of *guṇa*.
The accent is the *nighāta* (unaccented).
Regarding *samudravyacasam*:
the suffix *asun* is added to the root *vyac*.

Although the status of being *ḍit* would have applied by the rule "after *gaṇ*, *kuṭ* etc., [the suffixes] *aṅ*, *ini*, and *ṅin*" (Pāṇini 1.2.1), this is prohibited for *asun* by the Vārttika "for *vyac* when *asun* follows, provided it is not *manas*" (Kāśikā on 1.2.1). Consequently, the *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) prescribed for a *ṅit* suffix by the rule "before a *ṅit* suffix beginning with a vowel" (Pāṇini 6.1.16) does not take place.
Whose expanse is like the expanse of the ocean;
in this *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member is retained.
[He is] the best of charioteers among charioteers.
The suffix *ina* follows the word *rathaśabda*;
the lengthening [of the vowel] is Vedic,
as is the acute accentuation by the accent of the suffix.
Of the strengths; [the word] *vṛṣan* has an acute accent on the first syllable due to its being a word beginning with *vṛṣan*;
[the word] *satpati*.
The original accent of the first member of the compound is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule *patyāvaiśvarye* (6.2.18).

O Indra, Lord of Might, may we, seeking strength, not fear in your friendship. We praise you aloud—victorious and unconquered. *sakhye* | *te* | *indra* | *vājinaḥ* | *mā* | *bhaima* | *śavasaḥ* | *pate* | *tvām* | *abhi* | *pra* | *nonumaḥ* | *jetāram* | *aparājitam* || 2 ||

O Indra, Lord of Might (*śavasas-pati*), protector of strength, while we abide in your friendship—that is, in your favoring companionship—may we become possessors of food (*vājinaḥ*) and not fall into fear; may we not experience dread of our enemies.
Therefore, we praise you, the cause of fearlessness, with supreme excellence from all sides. Of what kind are you?
A victor in battles, possessing the nature of victory; unconquered, meaning entirely free from defeat. *Sakhye*: friendship, the act of a friend.
*sakhyuryaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.126): the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). *vājinaḥ*.
"Vājinaḥ" means those who possess "vāja," which is food; it takes the accent of the suffix (pratyayasvara). [This is an example of] the feminine suffix *bhaim*.
‘*Jibhī bhaye*’ (the root *bhī* meaning fear). The suffix *mas* has been elided; the elision of *s* occurs by Pāṇini’s rule 3.4.99, ‘*nityaṃ ṅitaḥ*’.

By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *cli*. Since the verbal suffix (*tiṅ*) is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* by the rule *chandasyubhayathā* (Pāṇini 3.4.117), it lacks the *ṅit* designation; consequently, *guṇa* substitution occurs. Furthermore, by the rule *na māṅyoge* (Pāṇini 6.4.74), the augment *aṭ* is prohibited.
*Śavasas pate*: according to Pāṇini’s rule 8.3.53 (*śavasaḥ patyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspopeṣu*), the *visarjanīya* is replaced by *s* in *saṃhitā*.

Due to the status of being a vocative (*subāmantrita*) and its treatment as a non-initial member of a compound (*parāṅgavadbhāva*), both words undergo the *nighāta* (anudātta) accentuation according to Pāṇini’s rule 2.1.2.
*Nonumaḥ*: from the root *ṇu* in the sense of "praising" (*stutau*).
The substitution of *na* for *ṇa* occurs according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.65: *ṇo naḥ*.
There is elision (*luk*) of *yaṅ*. By the rule "in the case of a suffix characterized by [the presence of] *yaṅ*, except for *san* and *yaṅ*" (Pāṇini 6.1.9), there is reduplication.
By the rule "there is *guṇa* [substitution] in the case of *yaṅ* and *yaṅ-luk*" (Pāṇini 7.4.82), there is *guṇa* substitution for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

By the definition of a suffix (pratyaya), the designation "dhātu" [is applied], because of the prohibition of *cha*, *ṇa*, *pha*, *ya*, *ana*, *si*, and *niṣ*; and because of the prohibition of *ga* and *ca*.
2. The *ṭha*-suffixes are powerful.

3. [The words] *tha-śa-mu-bāmantritai* [are examples] by virtue of being *parāṅga*; [the words] *na-cha-ṇa-pha-su-bāmantritai* [are examples] by virtue of being *parāṅga*. [The form] *laṭo mas*: due to the presence of the *vā* in the rule *adādivad vā*, there is the elision (*luk*) of *śap*. By the rule *upasargādasamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya* (Pāṇini 8.4.14), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* in the *saṃhitā* state. *Jetāram*: from the root *ji* in the sense of "to conquer. The suffix *tṛn* is applied in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlya*) and so forth. By the rule *jinasyādiniyamaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.197), the initial syllable has the acute accent (*udātta*). *Aparājitam*: by the rule regarding the original accent of the first member of a compound where an indeclinable (*avyaya*) precedes, the negative particle *nañ* bears the acute accent.
The ancient gifts of Indra do not fail;
his aids are unfailing when he bestows wealth consisting of cattle as bounty upon his praisers.
The ancient gifts of Indra do not fail; his aids never cease, when he bestows the wealth of cattle-filled booty upon those who praise him. 3.
The gifts (*rātayaḥ*) belonging to Indra—the bestowals of wealth—are "prior," meaning established from beginningless time, or abundant.
The meaning is that the very nature of this Indra is always the giving of wealth to those who sacrifice.

This being so, even now, if the sacrificer bestows—gives as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*)—a portion of *vāja*, that is, food accompanied by cattle (*gomataḥ*), as wealth (*magham*) to the praising priests (*stotṛbhyas ṛtvigbhyaḥ*), then Indra’s protections (*ūtayaḥ*) directed toward us do not fail; they do not specifically diminish, being preceded by the granting of abundant wealth.
The word *magha* is listed among the twenty names for wealth in the passage beginning with "maghaṃ rekṇaḥ" (Nirukta 2.10.1).
Among the ten acts of giving beginning with "dāti" and "dāśati," the word "maṃhete" is recited [in Nirukta 3.20.10].
*pūrvīḥ*: The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied to the word *puru* by Pāṇini’s rule *voto guṇavacanāt* (4.1.44).
The lengthening of the initial vowel *u* is due to Vedic license (*chāndasa*).

In the case of *jasi*, the rule "vā chandasi" (Pāṇini 6.1.106), which prescribes the long vowel of the same class as the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*), overrides the prohibition stated in "dīrghāj jasi ca" (Pāṇini 6.1.105).
The vowel [of the suffix] is acute by virtue of the accent of the *ṅīp* suffix.
Thus: *rātayaḥ*.
Why is there an acute accent (*udātta*) in the word *vṛṣeṇa* [in the phrase] "those who know the *pacamana* mantra are heroes on earth" (*mantre vṛṣeṇa pacamanavido bhuvīrā udāttaḥ*)?
They destroy (*dasyanti*). [The root is] *dasu*, meaning "to perish."
‘śyan’ after roots such as *div* [is applied];
there is elision of the accent (*nighāta*);
[the form] *ūtayaḥ*.
The suffix *kin* is acute-accented by the rule beginning with *ūtiyūti* (Pāṇini 3.3.97). If [it were not so], it would be acute-accented on the first syllable due to its being a particle (*nipāta*).
In the *saṃhitā*, there is lengthening according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.3.136, *nipātasya ca*.
[The word is] *stotṛbhyaḥ*. [The root is] *ḍuñ* in the sense of praising (*stutau*).
‘The *p* at the beginning of a verbal root is changed to *s*’ (Pāṇini 6.1.64).
Furthermore, the suffix *tṛc* has its final syllable accented.
They bestow abundantly (*maṃhete*).
The root *śap* is unaccented because it is marked with the *pit* indicatory letter (*it*).

Furthermore, the elision (*nighāta*) prescribed by the rule "tiṅ before a non-tiṅ" does not apply here, because of the prohibition stated in Pāṇini Sūtra 8.1.30: "In the presence of particles such as *yat*, *yadi*, *ha*, *inta*, etc. [the elision of the accent of a finite verb does not take place].
In the *ukthas* of the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) of the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*, the *maitrāvaruṇa* triplet for the *acchāvāka* is "purā bhinduryuvā kaviḥ.
Thus it is prescribed in the Sūtra: beginning with "eha yātam," [it continues] "purā bhinduryuvā kavirvṛtrā hyasi rādhase" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.8).
The breaker of forts, the youth, the sage of immeasurable power was born;
Indra, the sustainer of every deed, the slayer of Vṛtra, is highly praised.
The breaker of forts, the youthful sage, of immeasurable vigor, was born as Indra—the sustainer of every deed, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one praised by many. 4.
This Indra was born endowed with the qualities being proclaimed; he has become perfected. What are his qualities? That is now stated:

he is the breaker, the destroyer, of the fortresses—the cities of the Asuras; he is youthful, never subject to wrinkles, grey hair, or similar signs of age; he is a seer (*kavi*), wise and possessed of immeasurable power (*amitaujas*) and abundant strength; he is the sustainer of all ritual action, such as the *Jyotiṣṭoma* sacrifice and others; he is the nourisher of wealth; and he is ever the protector of the sacrificer for the sake of warding off obstacles (*vṛtra*).
Yoked with the vajra, Indra (Puruhūta) is praised for his manifold deeds in various respective tasks.
*Bhindu*:
from the root *bhidir* in the sense of "cleaving" (*vidāraṇe*).
With the suffix *ku* understood [from the previous rule], the suffix *ku* is applied by *Uṇādi-sūtra* 1.23: "After the roots *pṛ*, *bhid*, *vyadh*, *ṛdh*, and *svid*, [the suffix *ku* is added]."
In this regard, by the rule *chandasyubhayathā* (Pāṇini 3.4.117), the designation *sārvadhātuka* applies; consequently, by *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* (Pāṇini 3.1.78), the suffix *śnam* is added.
Because it is marked with the indicator *n*, it follows after the vowel other than the final one (Pāṇini 1.1.47).
Then, by *asorallopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.111), the *a* of the root is elided.
Regarding *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa* (Pāṇini 8.3.24; 8.4.58):
the status of being a *sthānivadbhāva*, which would otherwise apply by the rule *acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau* (Pāṇini 1.1.57), is prohibited by the rule *na padānta* (Pāṇini 1.1.58) and others.
[Thus we have] *yuvā*.
The root *yu* is used in the senses of "mixing" and "not mixing.
According to the Unādi Sūtra 1.154, *kanin* is added after *yut*, *trap*, *vi*, *kṣi*, *rāji*, *vyan*, *vidyuti*, and *div*;
[the rule] ceases because of this restriction.

Even though it is a *sarvanāmasthāna* [case-ending], by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*), there is the *saṃprasāraṇa* of the vowel in *vasu*; the preceding element becomes the first member of the resulting diphthong (*parapūrvatva*);
and by the rule "śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca" (Pāṇini 8.3.60), there is the substitution of *ṣ*.

By the rule *aci anudhātu* (Pāṇini 6.4.77) and others, the substitution of *iyaṅ* would have been applicable; however, this is set aside by the substitution of *yaṇ* according to *enekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82). This is a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*).
It takes the original accent of the first member, as it begins with an indeclinable (*avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratva*).
*tujyamānāsaḥ*:
from the root *tuj* in the sense of "injuring," the suffix *śānac* is substituted for the present participle (*laṭ*) in the passive voice;
then, by the rule *sārvadhātuke yak* (Pāṇini 3.1.67), the suffix *yak* is added.
Therefore, due to the instruction regarding the vowel *a*, the subsequent *l-sārvadhātuka* suffix is unaccented;
thus, only the accent of the suffix *yak* remains.
[The form is] *āviṣuḥ*.

The root *ava* is used in the sense of protecting and so forth. From this [root], the suffix *si* is applied after the intensive (*atyartha*), and for that *si*, the suffix *jus* is substituted according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.4.109: *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca*.
Here, there is the augment *āṭ* [by Pāṇini 6.4.72:
*āḍajādīnām*]. There is the substitution of *ṣ* [by Pāṇini 8.3.59:
*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*].
O Hero, through your gifts I have come back, proclaiming the crossing of the river; O Lover of Song, the poets have stood near you, for they know that deed of yours.
O Hero, with the help of your gifts, I have come against the river while calling out to you. O lover of songs, they stood near you; the poets know this deed of yours.
O Hero, O Indra endowed with valor, through your gifts—the giving of wealth that served as the instrumental cause for your deeds—I, the Hotṛ priest, have returned to you; I have come back again.
It is said that because much wealth was obtained from you in many previous rites, one returns for this present rite.
What was I doing?
Addressing the flowing Soma as the Sindhu river from all sides,
they shall proclaim your fame for bestowing wealth in this Soma sacrifice.
O Indra, lover of songs (*girvaṇas*), the poets— the performers, the officiating priests and the sacrificers— waited upon you in former times for the sake of obtaining wealth.
And having approached him, they know—that is, they recognize—the gift of wealth bestowed by such a *saudāman*.
Regarding the word *girvaṇas*, Yāska explains it thus: “*Girvaṇas* is a god; they win him over with songs” (*Nirukta* 6.14).
In the thirteen names of the singer, beginning with “*rebha*,” the word *kāra* [is used].
It is recited [in the text] as *tava*. By the rule "yuṣmadasmador ṅasi" (Pāṇini 6.1.211), the first syllable is udātta.
By the rule "vṛṣa" etc. in the section on mantras, the suffix *kin* is applied, and [the word] is udātta.
It is *āyam*.
The suffix *laṅ* is applied to the root *iṇ*.
By the rule *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtāmaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), there is the substitution of *am* for the [first-person] endings.
By the rule *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.72), there is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*.
The augment *āṭ* is applied;
the *vṛddhi* and *ay* substitutions take place;
and by the rule "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ," the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) is applied.
*Sindhu*:
[derived from the root] *syand* in the sense of "flowing" (*prasravaṇe*).

With the word *nit* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.9) understood, [the rule] "there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of *syandi* and the substitution of *dh* for the final [letter]" (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.11) prescribes the suffix *upratyaya* and the substitution of the letter *dh* at the end.
The word *nivāda* is udātta on its first syllable. [The form] *āvadan* [is derived from] the root *vad*, meaning "to speak clearly."
The *śatṛ* [suffix] replaces the *laṭ* [present tense marker]. The *śap* [augment] follows.
Due to its being marked with *p*, it is *anudātta* (unaccented).
The *śatṛ* suffix retains its original accent—that of the verbal root—by virtue of the accentuation rule for *lasārvadhātuka* affixes.

With the prefix *āṅ*, there is a compound according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 2.2.18 (*kugatiprādayaḥ*). The accentuation is that of the original form of the final member of the compound, as it begins with a *ku*-word.
They stood [still].
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 1.3.25: *upānmantrakaraṇe* (“after the prefix *upa*, when the agent is the instrument of the mantra”).
O you who are fond of hymns (*girvaṇas*).
The root *van* (in the form *vaṇ*) means "to gather.
The suffix *asun* is applied.
There is a *nighāta* (anudātta accent) by the rule "āmantritasya ca" (Pāṇini 8.1.19).
*viduḥ* [is derived from] the root *vid* in the sense of "knowing" (*jñāne*), in the present tense (*laṭ*).
By the rule “*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*,” there is elision of the *śap* suffix;
by the rule “*vido laṭo vā*” (Pāṇini 3.4.83), the *jhi* suffix is replaced by *us*;
and because it occurs at the beginning of a *pāda*, there is no *nighāta* (anudātta accent).

In the *saṃhitā*, there is the substitution of *ṣ* according to Pāṇini’s rule 8.3.103: *yuṣmattattathuḥvantaḥpādam*. Then, by Pāṇini’s rule 8.4.41: *dhunā dhuḥ*, the following *t* undergoes the substitution of *ṣṭu*;
thus [we obtain] *tasya*.

The rule *sāvekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.168), which would have caused the udātta accent of the case-ending, is prohibited by *na gośvansāvarṇa*. 1. In the manuscript *ca*, the word "in the karmas" (*karmasu*) is absent.
2. In the manuscript *ṭha*, there is again the reading *āga*.
This is prohibited by [Pāṇini’s] rule (Pā. Sū. 6.1.182). [The word] *kāravaḥ* [is formed] with the suffix *uṇ* according to [Uṇādi-sūtra] 1.1, beginning with "kṛ-vā-pā-ji... and so forth.
The accent of the suffix.

With your wondrous powers, O Indra, you struck down the wily Śuṣṇa. The wise ones know this of yours; extend their renown. With your wondrous powers, O Indra, you struck down the wily Śuṣṇa. The wise ones know this of yours; extend their renown.

O Indra, you have indeed destroyed with your *māyās*— that is, with your strategic insights or specific forms of deception— the *asura* named Śuṣṇa, who was possessed of various kinds of guile and was the cause of the withering of living beings.
Or rather,
you have slain him by means of those very methods within the scope of your wisdom.
And this has been stated by Yāska: "Indra slew Śuṣṇa" (Nirukta 3.11).
Furthermore, this meaning is made perfectly clear in such mantras as "He drank Śuṣṇa" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.103.8).
The wise ones—the intelligent ones who grant permission—know, that is, they understand, the greatness of you who are such as that.
"O *uttira*, increase the *śravas*—the foods—of those who know and perform [the rites].
Regarding the eleven names for wisdom beginning with "ketaḥ ketuḥ," the word *māyā* is listed as *vayunaṃ* (Nirukta 3.9.1).
Yāska explains the word *śravaḥ*: "The word *śravaḥ* is a name for food; it is so called because that which exists (*sat*) is supported (*śrayate*)" (Nirukta 10.3).
By means of *māyās*. [The root] *māṅ* is used in the sense of measuring (*māne*). The suffix *ya* is applied according to the rule *mācchāsasisūbhyo yaḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.549).
The accent of the suffix:
*māyinam*. One who possesses *māyā* is a *māyī*.
The suffix *ini* is applied according to Pāṇini 5.2.116 (*brīhy-ādibhyaś ca*),
and it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

*Śuṣṇam*: from the root *śuṣ* in the sense of "drying" (*śoṣaṇe*). Following the recurrence of the suffix *nit*, the suffix *na* is applied by the rule *tṛpiśudhirasibhyaḥ kicca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.292), resulting in the form *śuṣṇa*. This [word] has the meaning of food, grass, or fuel.
The word *nivāda* has its first syllable accented (*ādyudātta*).
[The form] *ati* is derived from the root *tṛ* with the suffix *liṅ*; by transposition, the suffix *śa* is applied.

Because of the *ḍit* designation of that [suffix], there is an absence of *guṇa*, and by the rule "ṛta iddhātoḥ," there is the substitution of *it*; then follows the substitution of *ra* for the final element. Thus: *viduṣ-te tasya*.
The mantra has been explained.
Regarding *medhirāḥ*:
[the root] *miṣ* (or *meṣ*) is used in the sense of "to destroy" (*hiṃsā*) and "to lead away" (*nayana*).
The suffix *iran* is derived from the *auṇādika* [list]. By virtue of being a *nivi*-type suffix, it is udātta on its first syllable. [Thus,] *śravāṃsi*.
Because it is a *taddhita* suffix with the sense of "belonging to" (*apatya*), it is accented on the first syllable.
The hymns have sung aloud to Indra, the ruler by his might—he whose gifts are a thousand, or even more numerous than that. ||8||

The hymns (*stomāḥ*), the praisers (*stotāraḥ*), and the officiating priests (*ṛtvijaḥ*) have praised from all sides with power (*ojasā*) and strength (*balena*) Indra, the lord (*īśānam*) and controller of the world. Of that Indra, there are gifts (*rātayaḥ*), bestowals of wealth, numbering a thousand (*sahasram*), or even more (*uta vā bhūyasīḥ*) than a thousand. [The word] "him" (*tam*) connects with Indra in the preceding context. Regarding *indram*: by the rule "ṛjendra... (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.186), the suffix *ran* is applied; being a *nivāt* (a suffix causing the acute accent on the first syllable), it is udātta. Regarding *īśānam*: this is the present participle (*laṭaḥ śānac*). By the rule "adaprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," there is elision of the *śap* suffix. Since the verbal root is *anudātta-it*, the suffix *śānac* is *anudātta* by the rule "tasyanudātta... (Pāṇini 6.1.186). Regarding *ojasā*: because it ends in the suffix *asun*, it is udātta on the first syllable. Regarding *stomāḥ*: by the rule "atimmu... (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.137), the suffix *manup* is applied; being a *nivāt*, it is udātta on the first syllable. Regarding *anūpata*: from the root *ṇu* meaning "to praise. By the rule "ṇe naḥ," the *ṇ* is replaced by *n*. This is in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense.
1. With those resembling that [state].

By transposition, *jha* [is substituted]. For the three [roots], there is the substitution of *ad* (Pāṇini 7.1.5). From the root *cal*, the suffix *sic* is applied. Because this root belongs to the *kutādi* group, the *sic* suffix has the *ḍit* designation, resulting in the absence of *guṇa*. The absence of *iṭ* is Vedic (*chāndasa*), as is the lengthening [of the vowel]. The augment *aṭ* is added. [The word] *mahaḥ* [is formed]. According to “*kardamādīnāṃ ca*” (Phiṭ-sūtra 59), the second syllable is acute (*udātta*). [The word] *rātayaḥ*: by the rule “*mantre vṛṣa-*” etc., the suffix *knin* is acute. [The particle] *uta*: the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika*). [The particle] *vā*: being among the *cādi* group, it is grave (*anudātta*). [The verb] *santi*: the suffix has the initial acute. There is no elision (*nighāta*) by the rule “*tiṅatiṅaḥ*” because of the prohibition “*yadavṛttānnityam*” (Pāṇini 8.1.66). For it has been stated that this [elision] occurs even when there is an intervention. [The word] *bhūyasīḥ*: those which are more numerous than a thousand are *bhūyasyaḥ*. Here, due to the proximity of the thousand to be divided, it is treated as a subordinate term (*upapada*); thus, by the rule “*dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau*” (Pāṇini 5.3.57), the suffix *īyasun* is added to the word *bahu*. By the rule “*bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ*” (Pāṇini 6.4.158), there is the elision of the *ī* and the substitution of *bhū* for the base *bahu*. Since *īyasun* is a *nis* suffix, it has the initial acute. [The feminine suffix] *ṅīp* is added by the rule “*ugitaśca*” (Pāṇini 4.1.6). || 21 || || 3 ||
In the fourth section (anuvāka), there are six hymns (sūktas).
Among them, for the first hymn consisting of twelve verses beginning with “Agniṃ dūtam,” the seer (ṛṣi) is Medhātithi, the son of Kaṇva.
Since there is no specific exception, the metre is Gāyatrī, as established by the rule stating that for those prior to Hiraṇyastūpa, the metre is Gāyatrī (Anuvāka 12.14).
Its having Agni as its deity is perfectly clear.

For this very reason, it is enumerated [in the Anukramaṇī]: “Agni, twelve verses; Medhātithi Kāṇva [is the seer]; the hymn begins with ‘agnim īḷe’; the meter is Gāyatrī; the deity is Agni; [the fires addressed are] the Nirmathya and the Āhavanīya.
As for its application (viniyoga), the hymn beginning with ‘agnim dūtam’ is used in the Prātaranuvāka during the rite dedicated to Agni.
In the section beginning with “Now, at the time of the passing of this night,” it is prescribed in the Sūtra: “I praise Agni, Agni the messenger” (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 4.13).
Likewise, on the second day of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, this very hymn serves as the *ājya-śastra*.

In the section beginning with “The two days of the *abhiplava* [are] the *uktha* of the *pṛṣṭha*,” it is prescribed in the Sūtra: “‘Agni the messenger’ on the second day” (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 7.10).
In the *sāmidhenī* verses of the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices, there is one verse beginning with “*agnim dūtam*” (“Agni as the messenger”).

This is prescribed in the section beginning with “*namaḥ pravaktre*” in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (1.2): “*īḷenyo namasyas tito 'gnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe*. (He is to be praised and honored; we choose Agni as the messenger.)
We choose Agni as our messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing, the one of skillful wisdom for this sacrifice.
We choose Agni as the messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing one, the skillful performer of this sacrifice. 1.

Agni’s role as a messenger is recorded in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa within the commentary on this mantra: “Agni was the messenger of the gods; Uśanas Kāvya was the messenger of the Asuras” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.5.8.5).
Such a messenger of the gods, Agni, we choose and honor in this ritual act. Of what nature is he?

The Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, who possesses all wealth (*viśvavedas*), and who, by virtue of being the accomplisher of this proceeding sacrifice, is *sukratu*—one of excellent deeds or excellent wisdom.
The word *veda* is listed among the twenty-eight names for wealth in the passage beginning with *magham* (Nirukta 2.10.4).
[He is] the Hotṛ.
The root *hve* is used in the sense of "striving" (*spardhā*) and "calling" (*śabda*).
The suffix *tṛn* is applied in the sense of habitual disposition (*tācchīlya*) and so forth.

By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.34), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), followed by the substitution of the preceding vowel for the subsequent one (*parapūrvatva*), and then the *guṇa* strengthening.
The first syllable is udātta due to the rule *nisvādādyudāttaḥ*.
In *viśvavedasam*,
the final syllable of the first member is udātta by the rule *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini 6.2.106).
In the word *asya*, the acute accent (*udātta*) of the case ending is applied by the rule *ūṅidam* (Pāṇini 6.1.171).
[The word] *sukratum*.
The initial vowel is acute by virtue of the rule *kṛvādyaśca* (Pāṇini 6.2.118).
They ever invoke Agni, Agni, with oblations— the lord of all,
the bearer of offerings, the beloved of many.
With oblations they ever invoke Agni after Agni—the lord of all, the bearer of offerings, the one beloved by many. ||2||
1. Because there is no limit to the thousands [of fires].

2. Regarding the *Taittirīya Mantra-brāhmaṇa*: although fire (*agni*) is indeed one in its essential nature (*svarūpa*), it is nevertheless manifold in view of the distinctions between the *prayāja* offerings, the distinctions between locations such as the *āhavanīya* hearth, and the distinctions between qualifiers such as "the purifier" (*pāvaka*). With this in mind, there is the distributive repetition (*vīpsā*) "fire, fire" (*agnim agnim*).
They always invoke him with *havīmabhiḥ*, that is, with mantras used for invocation, because they perform [the rites] continuously.
Of what nature is he?
He is the *vispatiṃ*, the lord of the people—the protector of the subjects such as the *hotṛ* priests—and the *havyavāhaṃ*, the bearer of the oblations offered by the sacrificer toward the gods.
For this very reason, it is "dear to many," being the object of affection for a great many people.
*agni-agnim*:
the reduplication occurs due to distributive repetition (*vīpsā*) according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.1.4;
when the subsequent member is designated as *āgreḍita* by Sūtra 8.1.2, it becomes unaccented (*anudātta*) according to Sūtra 8.1.3.
[The word] *havīmabhiḥ* [is derived as follows]: The root *hveñ* means "to contend" and "to sound.

Since [the word refers to] the mantras which serve as the instruments of invocation (*āhvāna*), the suffix *manin* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*)—according to Pāṇini’s rule 3.2.75, *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*—because one intends to express the agency [of the mantras] due to their independence in their own function.
In this word, the augment *īḍ* is applied according to Vedic usage.

By the rule "in the Veda [the substitution is] manifold" (Pāṇini 6.1.34), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the root, followed by the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*), and then the application of the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutes.
Due to the *nighāta* accentuation, it bears the acute (*udātta*) accent on its first syllable.

The word *sadā* is derived from the root *sarva* by means of the suffix *dā*, according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 5.3.15 (*sarvaikānya*), and the substitution of *sa-* for *sarva-* occurs optionally before the locative case ending *-di*,
according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 5.3.6 (*sarvasya so’nyatarasyāṃ di*).
The initial udātta accent occurs by way of transposition (vyatyaya).
[The form] *havante* is the present tense (*laṭ*) of the root *hve*.
The final letter of *jha* is replaced [by *ja*]. The absence of *etva* (the substitution of *e* for *ai*) after the *ṭi* portion is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
In the case of the suffix *śap*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule "vocalization occurs abundantly in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
The *nighāta* (elision of accent) applies by the rule "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

Regarding *vispatim*: although the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*) would have applied by the rule "patyāvaiśvarye" (Pāṇini 6.2.18), the acute accent on the initial syllable of the second member (*uttarapadādyudāttatvam*) is established by the rule "parādiśchandasi bahulam."
*Havyavāham*: [derived from] the root *vah*, meaning "to carry" (*prāpaṇe*). The suffix *ṇvu* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.64: *vahaśca*.
The original accent of the final member of the compound applies; thus,
*purupriyam* means "dear to many."
The final syllable of a compound is udātta.

Now, O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass; you are our Hotṛ-priest, worthy of praise. 3. O Agni, bring the gods here; having been born for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass, you are our Hotṛ-priest, worthy of praise. 3.

O Agni, you who have been born from the two kindling woods (*araṇī*), come here to this rite to bring the gods, the consumers of the oblation (*haviḥ-bhuj*), for the sake of favoring that sacrificer who is provided with trimmed sacrificial grass (*vṛkta-barhis*) for the purpose of spreading it.
You are our Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, and you are worthy of praise (*īḍya*).

In the word *devān* here, in the *saṃhitā*, there is shortening according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.3.9, *dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*. There is the nasalization (*anunāsika*) according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.3.3, *ātāṃ ṅaṭi nityam*.
[The form is] *jajñānaḥ*.
The root *jan* is used in the sense of manifestation.
[In the formation of the word *jajñāna*,] the suffix *kānac* is applied after the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*). By the rule *gamahana-* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel.

By the rule *dvirvacane'ci* (Pāṇini 1.1.59), due to its status as a *sthānivadbhāva*, there is reduplication. Because it has the *cittva* designation, it is accented on the final syllable (*antodātta*). [Thus: *vṛktabarhiṣe*.
The root *o* [meaning] "to moisten" (*kledane*) takes the suffix *kta* by Pāṇini’s rule 3.2.102 (*niṣṭhā*). The augment *iṭ* is prohibited by Pāṇini’s rule 7.2.15 (*yasya vibhāṣā*).

In a *bahuvrīhi* compound such as *vṛktabarhiḥ*, meaning "one for whom the sacrificial grass has been trimmed" or "by which officiating priest [the grass] has been trimmed," the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*) is maintained.
It is [the word] *asi*.
The suffix *sip* follows the root *as*.
By the rule "after *ad* and the others, *śap* [is elided]," there is the elision of *śap*.
Then, by the rule "the elision of *tāsi*, *sa*, and *l*" (Pāṇini 7.4.50), there is the elision of the *s* [of *sip*].
There is no *nighāta* (anudātta accent) because it begins with a *pāda*.
*Hotā*:
from the root *hu*, the suffix *tṛn* is applied in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlya*) and so forth.
The semivowel substitution (*saṃprasāraṇa*) occurs by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.34). Due to the *nighāta* accent, it is *ādyudātta*. [Thus] *īḍyaḥ*.
The root *īḍ* is used in the sense of "praising.

By the rule *ṛhalorṇyat* (Pāṇini 3.1.124), the suffix *ṇyat* is applied. Although the *tisvarita* accent would have been expected, the rule *idvanda-vṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.214) prescribes that the initial syllable (*ādyudātta*) is acute.

Awaken them who desire [the sacrifice], O Agni, when you go on your mission as messenger; sit together with the gods upon the sacrificial grass (barhis). 4. Awaken those who desire; when, O Agni, you go on your mission as messenger, sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass. 4.
1. *ca-ta-pa-pha*—for whom there is none.
And awaken [him], saying: "In this sacrificial rite, sit down together with those gods; having come, take your seat."
In those cases, by the rule "after a long vowel, [the following vowel becomes] short when the *aṭ* follows in the same foot," there is shortening in the *saṃhitā*;
and by the rule "after an *ā*, [the *a* of] *aṭ* is always nasalized," there is the state of nasality (*anunāsika*).
*uśataḥ* [is derived from] the root *vaś* in the sense of "desire" (*kāntau*);
[it is formed by adding] the suffix *śatṛ* to the present stem (*laṭ*).
There is elision of the suffix *śap* by the rule "adi-prabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ.
There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule beginning with "grahijyā" (Pāṇini 6.1.16).
The acute accent (*udātta*) of the case-ending is applied by the rule "śataranumo nadyajādī" (Pāṇini 6.1.173).
"You go.
There is a prohibition against the *nivāta* sandhi here by the rule *yadvṛttānnityam* (Pāṇini 8.1.66).
What is seen is either the portion or the duty of the messenger.
The suffix *yat* is applied by Pāṇini’s rule *dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇi* (Pā. Sū. 4.4.120).

Since this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *tiraścaritā*, the initial acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*) that would otherwise be required by the rule *yato ’nāvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6.1.213) is restricted by the principle that "all rules are optional in the Veda" (*sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante*).
Consequently, the form becomes *tisvarita* according to Pāṇini’s rule *tisvaritam* (Pā. Sū. 6.1.185).
The remaining [roots] are unaccented.
*sasmi* means "you sit.
[The root] *pad* is used in the senses of "falling apart," "going," and "sinking down."

In the case of the *laṭ* [present tense] followed by *sip*, there is elision (*luk*) of the *śap* [present marker] "optionally in the Vedic language" (*abahulaṃ chandasi*). Because of the prohibition of *pratyayalakṣaṇa* (the application of grammatical operations based on a suffix) by the rule "na lumatāṅgasya" (Pāṇini 1.1.63), the substitution of *sīda-* [for the root *ās*] according to the rule "pāghrā... (Pāṇini 7.3.78) does not occur. [The form is] *barhiṣi*.
The root *bṛh* (in the sense of "to grow") takes the suffix *iṣ* by the rule *bṛhernalopaśca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.266). By the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), the vowel *i* is udātta.
O Agni, shining one invoked with clarified butter, burn against those who seek to harm us;
you, O Agni, [burn] the sorcerers.
O Agni, invoked with clarified butter, resplendent one, burn against those who seek to harm us; you, O Agni, consume the sorcerers. 5.

O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter (*ghṛtāhavana*) and are shining brightly (*adīdivas*), burn up—completely reduce to ashes—the malicious enemies (*ripatas*) possessed of demons (*rakṣasvinaḥ*) who are hostile toward us.
In the word *ghṛtenāhūyate'smin*, the suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*) according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.3.117, *karaṇādhikaraṇayośca*.

Here, because the root *hu* (to sacrifice) has its object not intended to be expressed (*avivakṣita-karman*), it is intransitive; consequently, *ghṛta* functions solely as the instrument (*karaṇa*) and not as the object (*karman*).
Therefore, this is not the instrumental case governed by Pāṇini’s Sūtra 2.3.3, *tṛtīyā ca houcchandasī*, which prescribes the instrumental for the object.
However, according to *Pāṇini Sūtra* 2.3.18 (*kartṛkaraṇayostṛtīyā*), [the word *kṛtvā*] denotes the instrument (*karaṇa*).
Therefore, the compound is formed by *Pāṇini Sūtra* 2.1.32 (*kartṛkaraṇe kṛtvā bahulam*).

In that case, setting aside the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*), the original accent of the *kṛdanta* second member (*kṛduttarapada-prakṛtisvara*) is applied while the word is still in its nominal stem (*prātipadika*) state. Subsequently, when the case-ending arises, the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) is applied by *Pāṇini Sūtra* 6.1.198 (*āmantritasya ca*).
*dīdivaḥ*:
[This is derived] from the root *dīc* with the suffix *kasu* in the perfect tense (*liṭ*).

Its lack of the augment *iṭ* is due to the restriction [stated in] Pāṇini’s Sūtra 7.2.67: "The augment *iṭ* is applied after roots ending in a single consonant, after *ghas*, and after those beginning with a vowel, when followed by a suffix marked with *v* or *s*."
The dual ending [is applied].
By the rule *halādiśeṣaḥ*, all but the first consonant is elided.
Then, by the rule *lopo vyor vali* (Pāṇini 6.1.66), the subsequent *v* is elided.
The suffix is *kasu*.
Due to its *kit* status, there is an absence of *guṇa*.
By the rule "In the case of *nu*, *ja*, and so forth, there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable" (Pāṇini 6.1.7), there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable.
In the vocative *saṃbuddhau*, the augment *num* is applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.1.70 (*ugidacām*).

Then, by Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.2.23 (*saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ*), the final *sakāra* is elided. For the *nakāra*, the rule *manuvasāṃ ru saṃbuddhau chandasi* (Pāṇini 8.3.1) applies, resulting in the substitution of *ru* for the short vowel.
This *ru* is then replaced by a *visarga*.
The vocative at the end of a *pāda* is subject to the *āmantrita-nighāta* (the suppression of accent on a vocative).

Now, one might object that since the preceding vocative is non-existent [due to being treated as *avidyamānavat*], the status of being at the beginning of a *pāda* does not obtain, and thus the *nighāta* is not possible.

Nor can one argue that the prohibition of the *avidyamānavat* treatment applies here by the rule "A vocative is not treated as non-existent when it is in grammatical apposition with a word of general meaning" (*Pāṇini* 8.1.73).
Because both [words] function as qualifiers of the [following] noun (*āgamaviśeṣaṇatva*), they are specific designations.

For this very reason, due to the lack of semantic connection (*asāmarthya*) through mutual coordination, and by the restrictive rule "A grammatical operation concerning words applies only when there is semantic competency" (*Pāṇini Sūtra* 2.1.1), the preceding word does not behave as if it were a subordinate member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*) of the following one; otherwise, there would be a single-word accent (*nighāta*) resulting from their forming a single compound (*aikapadya*).
It is precisely for this reason that in passages such as *iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati* (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.1.6.8), each word possesses its own initial acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*).

It is said: here, the word *dīdivaḥ* is not an adjective for the noun *nābhi*, but rather serves to illuminate the term *gṛtāhavana* itself; for *gṛtāhavana* is intended as the specific subject to be qualified.
Subsequently, however, it functions as an adjective qualifying *agni*.

In that context, because the word *dīdivaḥ* is the qualifier (*viśeṣaṇa*) with respect to the word *pratigṛtāhavana*, the rule *nāmantritaṃ samānādhikaraṇe* (Pāṇini 8.1.73)—which prohibits [the application of] the *avidyamānavat* treatment—prevents the occurrence of the *nighāta* accent.

For this very reason, due to the mutual relationship of qualifier and qualified (*viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva*), there is semantic connection (*sāmarthya*); thus, by the rule *sutrāmantritaṃ* (Pāṇini 2.1.2), the status of being like a subordinate member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*) applies, and through the subsequent *nighāta* of the remainder, the desired accentual form is achieved. However, in cases such as *ihe rante*, there is no such mutual syntactic connection; therefore, there is a distinction between the two cases.
Regarding *riphata*: [it is derived] from the root *rip* in the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*).
This is the present tense (*laṭ*) of the *auvādika* class; with the substitution of *śatṛ* for the suffix and the addition of *śap*, there is an absence of *guṇa* by Vedic license (*chāndasa*).
Alternatively, [the form *rakṣas*] is derived from the root *raś* / *riś* meaning "to injure" belonging to the *tudādi* class; the substitution of *p* for *t* is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
Due to the *ṅit*-nature of the suffix *śa*, there is an absence of *guṇa*.
From the word *rakṣas*, the possessive suffix *vini* is added according to Pāṇini 5.2.121: *asmāyāmedhāstrajo viniḥ*.
Its first syllable is udātta because it is a pratyaya.
In the fire-drilling (*agnimanthana*), this verse, "By fire is fire kindled" (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate*), is to be recited as the invitatory formula (*anuvaṣaṭkāra*).

It is stated in the section beginning with "At dawn, having been prompted for the Vaiśvadeva [offering]" (*prātarvaidhadevyāṃ preṣitaḥ*) in the Sūtra: "‘By fire is fire kindled; for you, O Agni, by fire... (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.16).
Thus, this is the invitatory formula for the one who possesses the sacred fires (*agnimant*).

In the section beginning with “Now, the [rite] for Agni,” starting from “At the leading forward of the fire into the fire,” it is sūtra-ed: “Whatever vows we have violated, may Agni be kindled by Agni” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.13).
By fire is fire kindled— the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, the one who receives the offerings.
By Agni is Agni kindled—the sage, the lord of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, the one who receives the ladle. 6.
The fire known as the Āhavanīya is kindled—that is, it blazes perfectly—along with the fire being cast into it, whether it be the churned fire (nirmathya) or the consecrated fire (praṇīta).

Of what nature is this fire? It is a seer (kavi), wise; the lord of the house (gṛhapati), the protector of the sacrificer’s home; ever-youthful (yuvan); the bearer of oblations (havyavāṭ), the carrier of the sacrificial offerings; and possessed of a mouth in the form of the sacrificial ladle (juhū).
Gṛhapati: by the rule *pathāvaiśvaryai* (Pāṇini 6.2.18), there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [of the compound]. Yuvā.
The root *yu* means "to mix.
By the rule *kaninyuvṛpitakṣarājidhanvayupratidivaḥ* (Uṇādisūtra 1.154), the suffix *kanin* is applied.
Because it is marked with *n*, the word is accented on its first syllable (*ādyudātta*).
He is called *havyavāṭ* because he carries the sacrificial offering (*havya*). The suffix *kvip* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 3.2.64, *vahaśca*.
Due to the *ṇit* designation [of the suffix], there is neither *guṇa* nor *vṛddhi* substitution.

When a word denoting a destination (*gati*), an agent (*kāraka*), or a subordinate element (*upapada*) precedes it, the initial accent of the subsequent member ending in a *kṛt* suffix is maintained. For example: *juhvāsaḥ*.
[The word] *juhūḥ* is derived from the sense "that by which one offers" (*hūyate'nayā*).
The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *dhruvaḥ ṛtvacca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.218).
Due to its specific application (*tatsaṃniyogāt*), the vowel is lengthened. Because of the treatment as if it were *ślu*, there is reduplication (*dvirbhāva*).
After *sutvajaśva*,
[the word *juhūmukha*] is oxytone by the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*).
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound "that whose mouth is the *juhū*," that same [accent] remains due to the original accent of the prior member (*pūrvapada-prakṛti-svara*).
The remainder is unaccented (*nighāta*).
In the case of the *yaṇ* substitution, by the rule "the *anudātta* vowel following a *yaṇ* derived from an *udātta* or *svarita* becomes *svarita*" (Pāṇini 8.2.4), the vowel *ā* is *svarita*.
Praise Agni, the seer, whose laws are true at the sacrifice—
the god who drives away disease.
Praise Agni, the seer, whose laws are true, the god at the sacrifice who drives away disease. //7//
At the sacrifice during the ritual season, praise Agni, who dwells with his worshippers; approach him and offer hymns of praise.
Of what nature is he? He is a seer (kavi), wise, endowed with the dharma of truthful speech, a radiant deity (deva) who destroys afflictions—meaning he is the slayer of harmful enemies or diseases.
One for whom truth is the dharma is *satyadharmā*.
According to Pāṇini’s rule 5.4.124, *dharmādanic kevalāt*, the suffix *anic* is applied as a compound-final element (*samāsānta*).

Since the word "compound" (*samāsa*) is used [in that rule], it indicates that this is a compound; thus, by the rule regarding the original accent of the first member in a *bahuvrīhi*, the final syllable becomes unaccented (*anudātta*) through the principle of "the remainder is unaccented" (*śeṣanighāta*).

The word *amīva* is derived from the root *ama* in the sense of "disease" (*roge*), and is established as such through the addition of the suffix *van* and the augment *īṭ*, according to the rule *śevayahijahvāgrīvāpavāmīvāḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.152).
Because the suffix is marked with *n*, the word is udātta-accented on its first syllable. The root *cat* is used in the senses of "moving" and "begging" (*yācane*).

Thus, from this root *hiṃs* meaning "to injure," with the causative suffix *ṇic*, the suffix *lyu* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.134 because it belongs to the *nandī* group; the substitution of *an* for *ya* occurs according to Pāṇini 7.1.1; and the elision of the *ṇic* suffix occurs according to Pāṇini 6.4.51, as it is followed by a suffix that does not take the augment *iṭ*.

By the rule *liti* (Pāṇini 6.1.193), the vowel of the root [in *cātana*] is udātta. Furthermore, when an accent is to be applied, the elision of the *ṇi*-affix does not undergo the status of being "as if present" (*sthānivadbhāva*), because of the prohibition stated in *na padāntadvirvacanavareyalopa...* (Pāṇini 1.1.58) and other rules.

In the compound *amīvānāṃ cātanaḥ*, that same [accent] remains by virtue of the rule regarding the original accent of the final member of a compound formed with a primary derivative (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*).
O Agni, be the protector of him who serves you, the god and lord of oblations.
O Agni, be the protector of that lord of oblations who serves you, O divine messenger. ||8||
O Agni, O God, for that sacrificer who is the lord of the oblation and who honors and serves you as the messenger of the gods—be his protector; indeed, be his guardian.
It is called *havis* because it is offered (*hūyate*).
The form *havis* is derived by [Uṇādi Sūtra 2.265] "aciśśuci... and so forth;
by the accent of the suffix, the vowel *i* is udātta.
*Havipah patiḥ* becomes *havippatiḥ*.
By the rule *nityaṃ samāse'nuttarapadasthasya* (Pāṇini 8.3.45), the word-final *s* is replaced by *ṣ*.
By the rule *patyāvaiśvarye* (Pāṇini 6.2.18), the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member is maintained.

From the word *sapara*, the suffix *yak* is applied by the rule *kaṇvādibhyo yak* (Pāṇini 3.1.27). Because this occurs within the context of verbal roots (*dhātu*) and serves purposes such as the prohibition of *guṇa* substitution, it is *yak*. Furthermore, since the word *sapara* functions as a verbal root due to the presence of *ki* [as a marker], the *yak* prescribed after it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix; consequently, the elision of the final vowel [of *sapara*] occurs by the rule *ato lopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.48).
By the rule *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.32), the verbal designation (*dhātusaṃjñā*) is applied, resulting in the suffix *tip*.
In the sense of the agent (*kartari*), the suffix *śap* is added.
In that context, by the rule *ato guṇe* (Pāṇini 6.1.97), the substitution of the subsequent [vowel] for the preceding [vowel] occurs.
The suffix *yaK* receives the acute accent (*udātta*) by virtue of the accent of the suffix itself.

The single substitute (*ekādeśa*) for [the vowel] together with the *ip* also receives the acute accent according to Pāṇini’s rule 8.2.5: "A single substitute for [a vowel] with an acute-accented [vowel] is acute.

The rules for elision (*nighāta*), namely *ṅiṅatiṅaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.1.28) and *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.1.28), do not apply here because of the prohibition stated in Pāṇini 8.1.66: "That which begins with *yat* [is always unaccented]."
The *yājyā* verse for the oblation prescribed when there is mutual contact between the *gārhapatya* and *āhavanīya* fires is "yo agniṃ devavītaye.
This is stated in the section titled "Now, the sacrifices to Agni" (*athāgneya iṣṭayaḥ*) in the sūtra: "yo agniṃ devavītaye... kuviṣṇo no gaviṣṭaye" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.13).
To him who, possessing oblations, seeks to win over Agni for the feast of the gods— to him, O Purifier, be gracious.
O Purifier, be gracious to him who, possessing oblations, seeks to win Agni for the feast of the gods. 9.

The sacrificer who possesses oblations (*haviṣmān*), being endowed with the sacrificial offering, seeks to win over Agni for the sake of the feast of the gods—that is, for the purpose of the sacrifice which is the cause for the gods to partake of the oblation—approaching Agni in his presence and performing service. O purifying Agni, have mercy upon him; grant happiness to that sacrificer.
Regarding *devavītaye*: from the root *vī*—meaning "to go," "to procreate," "to shine," "to eat," or "to consume"—the suffix *ktin* is applied in the sense of eating (*aśana*).
Thus, *devavītiḥ* refers to that sacrifice (*yāga*) in which there is a feast (*vīti*) for the gods (*devānām*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first member retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
In *haviṣmān*,
the word *havis* is oxytone because it is excluded by the rule "naḍvapayasyānisastasya" (Phiṭ-sūtra 26).

Because the suffix *matup* is entirely unaccented (*sarvānudātta*), it alone remains [as the final accented element]. [The form] *āvivāsāti* [is derived from] the root *vā*, meaning "to go" or "to scent."
From the root *as* (to throw), with the causative sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*) implied, the suffix *san* is added in the sense of "desiring to cause [them] to come.
Since the desire for pleasure culminates in service, the word *vivāmasi* is listed in the *Nighaṇṭu* (3.5.10) as having the meaning of "service" (*paricaryā*).
1. Ṭha: *dūtam* (messenger). 2. Śa: From the root *sapar* in the sense of worship (*pūjā*); that is, from the word *sapara*. 3. Ca-Pha: *puronuvākyā* (introductory verse).
The first *aṣṭaka* is recited as 117.
There is reduplication. The short vowel is substituted for the reduplicated syllable by the rule *sanyataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.79).
The word *jityādi* is udātta by virtue of Pāṇini’s rule 6.1.197 (*jityādinityam*).
The elision of accent (*nighāta*) prescribed by the rule *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (8.1.28) does not occur here, due to the prohibition in the rule *yadvṛttānnityam* (8.1.66).
Furthermore, the elision of accent for *āṅ* occurs by the rule *tiṅi codāttavati* (8.1.71).

In the rule *saha supā* (Pāṇini 2.1.4), because of the separation of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*) [of *saha*], when *āṅ* is compounded with a non-finite verb (*atiṅ*), the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam* (Pāṇini 6.2.199) applies, resulting in the acute accent on the initial syllable of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*). Regarding the form *tasmai*:
the dative case is used for the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) according to the Vārttika *kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam* (on Pāṇini 1.4.32).
"O Pavamāna," and "O Agni Pāvaka," are the invitatory verses (*anuvākyā*) for [the offering].
In the section titled "The Soma-offerings in the Full-Moon Sacrifices are Taught," it is stated in the *Sūtra*: "'sa naḥ pāvaka dīdivo' and 'agne pāvaka rociṣā'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.1).
O purifying, radiant one, bring the gods here to us;
come to our sacrifice and our oblation.
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us; come near to our sacrifice and our oblation. 10.
O Agni, you who are resplendent, shining, and purifying—bring the gods here to this place of sacrifice for our sake;
then, [it is implied: convey our sacrifice and the oblation belonging to it to the presence of the gods.
*dīdivaḥ* [is derived from] *divu*,
meaning "to play" and so forth.
The suffix *liṭ* is applied while the rule *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 3.4.6)— which pertains to the Vedic language— is in effect.
The suffix *kasu* follows;

there is reduplication, and by the rule of *halādiśeṣa*, all but the first consonant is elided. Then, by the rule "there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable for roots beginning with *tu*" (*Pāṇini Sūtra* 6.1.7), the reduplicated syllable is lengthened.
By the rule *avasvekājādghasām* (Pāṇini 7.2.67), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ* for the stem *vasu* when followed by a case-ending beginning with a consonant.
By the rule *lopo vyorvali* (Pāṇini 6.1.66), the letter *v* is elided. In the vocative singular, the augment *num* is applied by the rule *ugidacām* (Pāṇini 7.1.70), and so forth.
The application of *halḍyādilopa* results in the elision of the final consonant (*saṃyogāntalopa*).
By the rule *manuvasoḥ*, the vowel is shortened,
followed by the *visarga*.
In *agne*, there is no *nighāta* (anudātta accent) because it begins with a *pāda*.
In the phrase *devāṃ iha*, the vowel is shortened by Pāṇini’s rule 8.3.9: *dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*.

By the rule "āto 'ṭi nityam," the nasalization of the vowel *ā* occurs. By the rule "bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo'śi" (Pāṇini 8.3.17), the *r* is replaced by *y*. Then, by the rule "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pāṇini 8.3.19), the *y* is elided.
Because that [condition] is unestablished, the substitution of *āṅ* for *guṇa* does not occur.
Here, in the case of *iha*, the suffix *hapratyaya* is applied after the locative form according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.3.11: *idamo haḥ*.
Regarding the rule *idam iha* (Pāṇini 5.3.3):

because it ends in a secondary derivative suffix (*taddhita*), it is a nominal stem (*prātipadika*). Consequently, by the rule *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.71), there is elision (*luk*) of the seventh case ending.

Then, by the rule *taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ* (Pāṇini 1.1.38), it receives the designation of an indeclinable (*avyaya*). Finally, by the rule *avyayād āpsupaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.82), there is elision of the subsequent seventh case ending.
The vowel *a* is accented acute by virtue of its being a suffixal vowel.
Being praised by us, bring to us with your newest song nourishment accompanied by heroic sons, like a charioteer bringing a prize-winning steed.
Being praised by us, bring to us with your newest song, through your inspired hymn, nourishment accompanied by heroic sons and a chariot-borne abundance. 11.

O Agni, being praised by this most recent, newer hymn composed according to the ancient model and possessing the Gāyatrī metre, do thou, for our sake, bring—accomplish—the wealth of chariots, food accompanied by heroic sons and progeny, and strength.
*Stavānaḥ*. [The root] *stuñ* means "to praise. [In the rule] "ghāsvādaḥ paḥ saḥ," [the *pa* is replaced by *sa*].
‘svaritajitaḥ’ (Pāṇini Sūtra 1.4.25). [Note: 1. Ṭha—because it is the recipient (saṃpradāna);
2. Ca, Ta, Pha, Śa—thus;
3. Ṭha—endowed with a hero’s son and servants].

72) Thus [the suffix] *ātmanepada*. [The suffix] *śānac* takes the place of *laṭ*. [The suffix] *śap* is added for the agent (*kartari*). By the rule “*bahulaṃ chandasi*” (Pāṇini 2.4.73), there is an absence of elision (*luk*). There is the substitution of the *guṇa* vowel. The augment *muk* does not occur by the rule “*āne muk*” (Pāṇini 7.2.82), because the teaching regarding augments is non-eternal (*anitya*), according to the maxim “*anityamāgamāśāsanam*” (Paribhāṣā 96). Because *śap* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*). Because *śānac* is marked with *c*, it is *antodātta* (accented on the final syllable); however, since it follows a root taught with a short *a* (*adupadeśāt*) and the suffix *dāp*, it receives the *lasārvadhātukānudāttatva* (unaccented status of the *sārvadhātuka* affix). Thus, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) alone remains. [In the word] *bhara*: by the rule “*hyagrormbha chandasi*” (Pāṇini 8.2.32.1), there is the substitution of *bha*. [In the word] *gāyatreṇa*: that which belongs to the *gāyatrī* is *gāyatram*. The suffix *aṇ* is added by the rule “*tasyedam*” (Pāṇini 4.3.120). It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). [In the word] *navīyasā*: from the word *nava*, the comparative suffix *ḍaiyap* is added. Being a *nivāt* (beginning with *ni*), it is *ādyudātta* (accented on the first syllable). [In the word] *vīravatīm*: because the suffixes *matup* and *ṅīp* are marked with *p*, they are unaccented. The vowel *a* is accented by the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadikasvara*).

If the state of being *dātta* (acute) were to remain as it is, it would persist by virtue of the natural accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the following member ending in *-ku-*, and thus the word *su-* would be unaccented (*anudātta*). [Example:
*devāṃ agne*.
As before, [the mantras] are for one's own nose.
*Haviṣmate*:
the suffix *matup* is used because he possesses the oblation (*havis*).
Because the status of being a *pada* is sublated by the rule "tasau matvarthe" (Pāṇini 1.4.19), there is no substitution of *ru*.

Since the two vocatives *hotar* and *pāvaka* each connect independently with the verb, they lack mutual expectancy (*asāmarthya*); consequently, there is no formation of a compound (*parāṅgabhāva*), and thus no resulting monotonous accent (*aikasvarya*) based on that.

Nor does the second vocative attain a single accent (*aikasvarya*) through the suppression (*nighāta*) of the *ām* suffix, because—according to Pāṇini’s rule *āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat* (8.1.72)—the preceding word is treated as non-existent; thus, due to its being treated as non-existent, it lacks the status of following a word (*padāt*), and furthermore, it constitutes the beginning of a quarter-verse (*pādādi*).
Even if there were mutual coreferentiality (*sāmānādhikaraṇya*), the same principle of being treated as non-existent would apply to *hotar* when it functions as a qualifier.

Precisely because it is treated as non-existent, even though there is semantic capacity (*sāmarthya*), there is no status of being a subordinate member (*parāṅgabhāva*); therefore, the attainment of a single accent is not established.
Therefore, "this" (*etad*) is the substantive (*viśeṣya*).

Furthermore, by accepting the etymological derivation of the components in the term *pāvaka*—meaning "that which purifies" (*punāti*)—the suffix *u* is applied as a verbal derivative (*vikaraṇa*) according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.69 (*śy-ān-nvu-lam*), which is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *śap* suffix; by that rule, the letter *v* is replaced by *a*.
There is elision of that [suffix] by Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.4.48 (*ato lopaḥ*).

Because of its status as a *sthānivadbhāva* (as if it were the original element), the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel does not occur. Furthermore, the elision of *hi* by Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.4.106 (*utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt*) does not take place, because of the specific statement: “In the Vedic language, there is optionally no mention of the elision of *hi* after a suffix ending in *u*” (Pāṇini 6.4.106.1).
The *nighāta* (elision of accent) applies by the rule "tiṅaṅatiṅaḥ. Regarding *vītaye*: the suffix *kin* is acute-accented by the rule "mantre vṛṣeṇapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ" (Pāṇini 3.3.96).
I invoke here at this sacrifice the beloved Narāśaṃsa,
who has honeyed tongue and is prepared with oblations.
The one praised by men, the beloved here at this sacrifice—him, the honey-tongued preparer of the oblation, I summon hither. 3.
Here, at this place of sacrifice (*devayajana*), while this sacrifice is proceeding, I invoke—that is, I approach—the fire named Narāśaṃsa.

Of what kind? Dear to the gods, a cause of their delight, possessing a honeyed tongue—meaning either endowed with a tongue that speaks sweetly or endowed with a tongue that tastes the flavor of sweetness.
The *haviṣkṛt* is the one who prepares the oblation (*havis*).
The word *nara* is derived from the root *nṛ* "to lead" with the suffix *ap*;
because the suffix is marked as *pit*, the accent of the verbal root alone remains.
*Śaṃsa* means "that in which one praises."
In the rule *halaśca* (Pāṇini 3.3.121), the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of locus (*adhikaraṇa*).

When the compound *nara-śaṃsaḥ* is formed, although the rule *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva* would normally apply [giving the accent to the final syllable of the second member], the rule *ubhe vanaspatyādipu yugapat* (Pāṇini 6.2.140) applies, whereby both the preceding and following members retain their original accents (*prakṛtisvara*).
For this very reason, due to its inclusion in the list beginning with *vanaspati*, the word *nara-* takes a long vowel.
In this case, the suffix *ha* is applied by the rule *idamo haḥ* (Pāṇini 5.3.11),
and the substitution of *iś* is applied by the rule *idam iś* (Pāṇini 5.3.3).
The accent is due to the suffix (*pratyaya*).
*Priya*: it pleases, therefore it is *priya*.
The suffix *ka* is applied by the rule *igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.135). It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In this [word].
In the phrase beginning with *aḍidam*, the case ending is udātta;
in *haye*,
there is nighāta (elision of accent).
Regarding *madhujihvam*:
it has been stated that the word *madhu* is udātta on its first syllable;
in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule of the original accent of the preceding member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*), that very accent remains.
Haviṣkṛtam.
