With the Gārhapatya fire, as the leader of the seasons, bring the offerings;
worship the gods with the divine portion.
With the Gārhapatya fire, with the Sanya, for the sake of the seasons—you are the leader of the sacrifice; O god, worship the gods in this divine assembly. 12.

O Agni, being endowed with the form of the *gārhapatya*—belonging to the master of the house—and acting as the leader of the sacrifice (*yajñanīḥ*) together with *ṛtu*, the deity of the seasons, you are the one who brings the sacrifice to completion.
Therefore, for the sacrificer who possesses a desire directed toward the gods (*devayate*), do you worship the gods.
By [the rule] *gārhapatyena*—
[derived from] *gṛhapatinā saṃyukte nyaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.4.90)—
there is the elision of the suffix *ya* by [the rule] *yasya*.
From *jīva*, there is initial *vṛddhi* and the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudāttatva*).

If it were formed with the suffix *yaK* according to *apadānta-purohitādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.128) in the sense of "being the householder," it would have the acute accent on the final syllable (*antodāttatva*). [The word] *sanya* means "existing in a place for piling."
In the sense of "giving," [the root *paṇ* takes the suffix] *kvip*.
By the rule "and after *kvip*" (*kviccau ca*), the suffix *kvip* is applied.
By the rule "there is no lengthening or elision when *kvip* follows" (*na kvicci dīrghaśca*, Pāṇini 6.4.39), there is neither lengthening nor elision.
The suffix *yat* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 4.4.110 (*bhave chandasi*) or 4.4.98 (*tatra sādhuḥ*).
There is elision of the accent (*nighātaḥ*).
[The term] *yajñanīḥ* means "one who leads the sacrifice."
The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "satsṛdviṣa... etc.; the accent is that of the original form of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*). [The word is] *devayate*.

"One who desires the gods for himself is a *devayān*"; for that [word], the substitution of *ī* (as in *devīyan*) does not occur by the rule "and in some cases," because of the prohibition: "not in the Veda, except for the word *putra*."

Regarding the rule *aśvāghasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.37), it has been stated that this prohibition applies not only to the *ī*-substitution—which would otherwise be required by the application of that rule—but also to the long vowel (*dīrgha*) that might have occurred.
As for the accentuation of the case-ending, the rule *śataranumo nadyajādī* prescribes an acute accent (*udātta*) on the ending.
In this context, because the suffix *kyac* belongs to the *ciṭ* class, the final syllable bears the acute accent.

The suffix *śap* is unaccented (*anudātta*). The suffix *śatṛ* also lacks an accent due to the accentual rule governing *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes. When both [suffixes] undergo a single substitution (*ekādeśa*) with *kyac*, the resulting single substitute is accented acute (*udātta*) according to the rule "a single substitute [for an accented and an unaccented element] is acutely accented.

Consequently, because the word is oxytone (having the acute accent on its final syllable), the subsequent case-ending receives an acute accent by the rule "the case-endings following a word ending in *śatṛ*, or one having the augment *num*, or one beginning with *nadī* or a vowel, are acutely accented."
"Ā tvā vahantu" is the fifth hymn, consisting of nine verses. The seer and the meter continue as before.
Since there is no specific instruction to the contrary, Indra is the deity.
The application (viniyoga), however, is as follows: at the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), while the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa is being drawn, the hymn "ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ" [is recited].
1. Ra has the additional text "tathā ca anukrāntaṃ ā tvā naveti" after the word "devatā.
Kra. 18.
And likewise, it is stated in the section beginning with "They perform [the rites] with [offerings] for two deities" in the Sūtra: "'unnīyamānebhyo'nvāhā tvā vahantu'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.5).
Similarly, in the Goḍiśa scripture, there are three verses beginning with "ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ.
Likewise, it is stated in the section beginning with "Now the Ṣoḍaśin" in the Sūtra: "'ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ'—these three are Gāyatrīs" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.2).
May the bay steeds bring you hither, the bull, for the drinking of the Soma—
Indra, you whom those with sun-like eyes [bring].
Let the bay steeds bring you hither, O Indra, the bull, to drink the Soma; let them, whose gaze is like the sun, bring you. 1.
O Indra, let your bay horses bring you—O showerer of desires—to this soma-drinking rite; let them lead you to this sacrifice.
Likewise, let the priests, possessing the splendor of the sun’s eye, illuminate you with mantras—the sense being that they shall reveal you through their hymns.
They are called *harayaḥ* because they carry (*haranti*). The suffix *in* is applied according to the rule "after all verbal roots" (*sarvadhātubhyaḥ*, Uṇādi-sūtra 4.557).
Because it is a *niṣ* suffix, the first syllable is udātta.
*vṛṣaṇam*:
[The suffix] *kanin* is applied according to the rule "kaniny-uṣi-ta-pita-kṣa" (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.154). Because it is marked with *k*, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel.
The lengthening of the penultimate vowel is optional according to Pāṇini’s rule *vā pūrvasya nigame* (6.4.9).
[Thus we have] *somapītaye*.
This was explained in the commentary on *aibhir agne* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.14.1).
*sūracakṣasaḥ* | [The root] *cakṣiṅ* [is used] in the sense of "distinct speech. [The suffix] *asun* [is applied] after all verbal roots.

The rule *cakṣiṅaḥ syāj* (Pāṇini 2.4.54) does not apply here, because of the prohibition stated in the Vārttika: *anasoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ* (on Pāṇini 2.4.54). [The root] *pū* [is used] in the sense of "impelling."
He is called *sūra* because he impels (*su-vatīti*).

The suffix *kran* is applied according to the rule "after the roots *su*, *sudhā*, and *gṛdh*, [the suffix] *kran*" (Uṇādi-sūtra 2.182). Due to the *kit* designation of the suffix, there is an absence of *guṇa* strengthening.
The first member [of the compound] is udātta because it is not a *svādi* [term].
Those whose place (*sthāna*) is illumination (*prakāśa*), like that of the sun (*sūra*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
May these roasted grains, dripping with ghee, bring the two bay steeds here upon the most comfortable chariot to carry Indra.
These roasted grains, dripping with ghee—may the two bay steeds bring Indra here upon his most comfortable chariot. ||2||
The word *hari* denotes the two horses that carry Indra’s chariot.
Thus, another Vedic scripture states: "the rider of the two *haris*" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.4.28.1), and "may the two *haris* cause Indra to go to the gods" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.6.4.3).
Having this very point in mind, the author of the Nighaṇṭu says: "The two *haris* belong to Indra" (Nighaṇṭu 1.15.1).

Such two bay horses (harī), having stationed Indra in a most comfortable chariot for the sake of this sacrifice—referring to these parched grains (dhānāḥ), consisting of roasted barley and rice, which are present before them by virtue of being placed upon the sacrificial altar (vedi)—shall bring him hither to this ritual act. Of what sort are the grains? "Ghṛtasnuvaḥ": they are those that drip with clarified butter (ghṛta) due to the application of ornaments, the under-spreading of ghee, and the over-sprinkling thereof.

They are called *dhānāḥ* because they are "held" (*dhīyante*). The suffix *naḥ* is applied according to the rule *dhāpvasajatibhyo naḥ* (Uṇādisūtra 3.286). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
*Ghṛtasnuvaḥ*:
they drip with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) are *ghṛtasnuvaḥ*.
The absence of the augment *nuk* after the suffix *krip* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
The accent is that of the stem. In a compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the word ending in *ku* remains.
Because the suffix *snu* is preceded by a conjunct consonant, there is no application of *yaṇ*; instead, the substitution of *uvaṅ* occurs.
The root *hṛ* (in the sense of "taking away"); [the suffix] *in* is added after all verbal roots. *Harī*.
The word *nisvādādi* is accented on the first syllable. Due to its status as a *pragṛhya*, it remains in its original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) in *saṃhitā*.
[The verb] *vakṣataḥ*.
In the sense of the optative (*liṅ*) used for prayer (*prārthanā*), there is the *leṭ* suffix.
Its first person dual form is *tas*.
By the rule "leṭoḍaḍāṭau" (Pāṇini 3.4.94), the augment *aṭ* is added.
When the *śap* affix is applicable, the *sip* affix is used by the rule "sibbahulaṃ leṭi" (Pāṇini 3.1.34).
It possesses the properties of having a *ṭ* and being *kavattva*.
There is a *nighāta* (elision of accent) according to the rule "tiṅatiṅaḥ."
It has gone to the most blissful state.
We invoke Indra at dawn; we invoke Indra as the sacrifice proceeds;
we invoke Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke Indra at dawn; we invoke Indra while the sacrifice proceeds; we invoke Indra for the drinking of the Soma. ||3||
1. *ga*, *ṇa*, and *ra* [are used] after a dropped [consonant]. 2. *ca*, *cha*, and *pha* [are used] in the sense of praying for (*prārthanā*). [Mbh.
At the commencement of the rites in the morning, at the morning libation (prātaḥsavana), we invoke Indra;
likewise, when the sacrifice—the Soma-sacrifice—is proceeding, advancing, and being performed on that day, we invoke that Indra at the libation;
and similarly, at the occasion of the conclusion of the sacrifice, at the third libation (tṛtīyasavana), we invoke him for the drinking of the Soma, for the purpose of consuming the Soma.
In the morning; it is an indeclinable (nipāta) listed among the *svarādi* group, accented on the final syllable.
We invoke.

With the continuation of the rule "there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root *ah* when *laṭ*, *liṭ*, and *śap* follow," there is *saṃprasāraṇa* [of the vowel *a*] in the Vedic language by the rule "frequently in the *chandas*"; this is followed by the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*) and the *guṇa* replacement.
[Thus we have] *prayati*. The root is *iṇ* in the sense of "going."
The suffix *śatṛ* is substituted for the present indicative (*laṭ*). By the rule "the *śap* [augment] is elided after roots beginning with *ad*," there is elision of *śap*.
Because the suffix *śatṛ* is treated like *dvat*, there is an absence of the augment *guṇa*.
This is a *prādi-samāsa* (prepositional compound).

Because of the rule "when a verbal root (*kṛd*) is mentioned, that which is preceded by a *gati* or a *kāraka* is also included" (Paribhāṣā 28), and because there is no restriction regarding the mention of an affix (*pratyaya-grahaṇe*), the acute accent on the case-ending applies according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.173: "In the case of forms ending in *śatṛ*, *anum*, or those beginning with *na* or *yac*, [the case-ending is acute].
[The word is] *adhvare*.

It has been stated in the *Saṃhitā*: "In the case of a *yaṇ* substitute for an acute (*udātta*) or circumflex (*svarita*) vowel, the following grave (*anudātta*) vowel becomes circumflex" (*Pāṇini Sūtra* 8.2.4).

Here, the second case ending (*dvitīyā*) is used because this libation (*savana*) is connected with the pressed Soma; or rather, the second case is used in the sense of the object. In that case, from the word *suta*, the suffix *-a* is added according to *Pāṇini Sūtra* 5.2.127 (*arśādibhyo'c*). [The root] *tṛp* is used in the sense of thirsting (*pipāsā*). The suffix *kta* is applied by the rule "the *niṣṭhā* suffixes. It is acute (*udātta*) by the accent of the suffix. Subsequently, [the augment] *iṭ* is added; it is grave (*anudātta*) by the rule "augments are grave. ||30||
These Soma drops, the pressed juices, are upon the sacred grass;
drink them for strength, O Indra!
These Soma drops, the pressed juices, are upon the sacred grass; O Indra, drink them for the sake of strength.
The word *indu* is derived from the verbal root *undī* (to moisten).

"The *indavas* are those characterized by moisture; these *somās* are the Soma juices situated upon the sacrificial altar (*vedī*), the Somas contained within their vessels. On the *barhis*, that is, at the sacrifice, they have been *adhikasutās*, meaning they have been abundantly pressed. O *Indra*, for the sake of *sahasa*, that is, for the sake of strength, drink those Somas."
The Soma juices;
[Maṇḍala 1, Adhyāya 4, Sūkta 17] First Chapter, verse 141:
the drinker of the oblation.
The form *vṛtrahan* is derived from the root *han* with the suffix *kvip* after the words *brahman*,
*bhrūṇa*, and *vṛtra*, according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.87 (*brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip*).
The lengthening of the vowel, which was precluded by the rule *inhanpūṣāryamṇāṃ śau* (Pāṇini 6.4.12), occurs here due to the counter-exception provided by *sau ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.13).
The original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) applies because the subsequent member is a word meaning "anger" (*krud*). [In the compound] *somapītaye*,
it has been stated that this is a *vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi*.
Or, in the case of a *tatpuruṣa* compound, due to the rule *dāsībhārādi-tvāt* (Pāṇini 6.2.42), there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
O Śatakratu, fulfill this desire of ours with cattle and horses;
we, with well-disposed minds, shall praise you.
Do thou fulfill this desire of ours with cattle and horses, O Śatakratu! With well-directed thoughts, we shall praise thee. 9.
O Śatakratu, you who possess a hundred powers, fulfill—fill completely from all sides—this desired fruit of ours, this our longing, with cattle and horses;
and we too, being well-attentive and endowed with meditation on every side, shall praise you.
Semam. In the *saṃhitā*, there is elision of the suffix *su* according to the rule "so'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam. Kāmam.

Since the rule "In the case of *kamerṇi*, the final syllable of the word ending in *ghañ* is udātta" (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.159) would otherwise result in an udātta accent on the final syllable, the word is instead accented on the first syllable because it is listed among the *vṛṣādi* group.
*Pṛṇa*:
from the root *pṛṇ* meaning "to satisfy."
The *s* of the imperative (*loṭ*) is replaced by *hi*.
[In the case of] the root *tud*, the suffix *śa* is applied according to the rule "from *tud*-roots etc., *śa*.
Because that [suffix *śa*] is marked with the indicatory letter *ṭ*, there is an absence of *guṇa* [vowel strengthening].

In *gobhiḥ*, the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *he* occurs by the rule *ato heḥ*. Regarding the case-ending, although the acute accent (*udātta*) would have been required by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, it is prohibited by the rule *na gośvansāvavarṇa...*.

By [the word] *aśvaiḥ*. It has been stated that [this is] a form ending in a *kṛt* suffix marked with *n*. Because of a lack of semantic connection (*asāmarthya*), there is no application of the rule regarding "behaving like a subordinate element" (*parāṅgavadbhāva*).
We shall praise (*stavāma*).
[The root] *huñ* is used in the sense of praising (*stutau*).
[By the rule] "the *pa* at the beginning of a verbal root is replaced by *sa*" (*dhātvādeḥ paḥ saḥ*), [it becomes *stu*].

Regarding the third person plural of the imperative (*loṭ*), because it is treated like the imperfect (*laṅ*) by the rule "the imperative is like the imperfect" (*loṭo laṅvat*), there is the elision of the *s* by the rule "always [elision] of that which has the marker *ṅ*" (*nityaṃ ṅitaḥ*, Pāṇini 3.4.99).

By the rule "there is the augment *āṭ* for the third person plural, and it is also marked as *p*," (*āḍuttamasya picca*, Pāṇini 3.4.92), the augment *āṭ* is added. Because the suffix is marked with *p*, it is oxytone (accented on the final syllable).
The root is simply *dhātu* with the vowel *a*.
It is to be self-studied (*svādhyāya*).
[The root] *dhyai* is used in the sense of "thinking" (*cintā*).
The prefixes *su* and *ādi* are placed before the verbal root.
The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "it is seen after other roots as well" (Pāṇini 3.2.108).

Since the mention of the root *dṛś* in that rule is intended to include other grammatical operations, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) here, followed by the substitution of the preceding vowel with the subsequent one (*parapūrvatva*).
The long vowel [ā] is applied by Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.2 (*halaḥ*).
In the nominative plural (*jasi*), the *yaṇ* substitute is applied by Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.82 (*eranekācaḥ*).

The accent of the final member of the compound remains as its original (*prakṛtisvara*) according to the rule "a *kṛt*-derived word following a prefix, a kāraka, or an upapada retains its own accent."

The acute accent (*udātta*) for the *jas* ending does not occur by the rule *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.104), because the term *asarvanāmasthānam* is understood as a governing rule (*anuvṛtti*) there.
Consequently, by the rule *udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pāṇini 8.2.4), only the circumflex accent (*svarita*) occurs.
The hymn beginning with "indrāvaruṇayoḥ" consists of nine verses (navarcam), specifically six verses (ṣacam).
For this very reason, it is listed in the Anukramaṇī following the recurrence of the word "nava": "indrāvaruṇayoḥ, indrāvaruṇaṃ yuvāku, pādaniccatau.
Here, the deities are clearly indicated.
The seer (ṛṣi) and the meter (chandas), however, follow as before.
This, however, is the distinction:
the two verses beginning with "yuvāku hi" are composed in the *pādanicṛt* meter.
But the application (viniyoga) should be understood as either based on Smṛti or indicated by internal mark (liṅga).
I choose for myself the protection of Indra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings; may they be gracious to us in such circumstances as these.
Of Indra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign rulers, I choose their protection. May they both be gracious to us in such circumstances as these. 1.

I, the performer [of the rite], choose—that is, I pray for from all sides—the protection (*avaḥ*) belonging to the two gods Indra and Varuṇa, who possess a harmonious kingdom or who shine perfectly together.
Those two gods [are the cause] in such a manner, for the sake of this kind of protection of ours;
[this is either a *tatpuruṣa* compound with the first member in the instrumental case, or a *dvandva*].
2. When there is protection from *ca*, *ṇa*, *pha*, and *ra* belonging to us, [the two gods] "mṛḍātaḥ," meaning they gladden us.
The word *indra* ends in the suffix *ran*,
and the word *varuṇa* ends in the suffix *un*; both are *nits*, and thus have their first syllable accented (*ādyudātta*).

In the compound, by the rule "in a *devatā-dvandva* as well," there is the substitution of *ān* for the final vowel of the first member. While the phrase "both simultaneously" (*ubhe yugapat*) is understood from the previous context, the rule "in a *devatā-dvandva* as well" prescribes the original accent (*prakṛti-svara*) for both members simultaneously. Thus: *samrājoḥ*.
The root *rāj* means "to shine. By the rule *satsṛdviṣa-* (Pāṇini 3.2.61), the suffix *kvip* is applied.

When the rule *samo 'mo 'nusvāraḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.23) would have required the substitution of an anusvāra for the *m* of *sam*, the rule *mo rāji samaḥ kau* (Pāṇini 8.3.25) prescribes the substitution of *m* [for the *m* of *sama*] before the root *rāj*.
The original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member of the compound applies here.
According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 2.3.65, *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti*, the genitive case is used for the agent (*kartṛ*).
[The word is] *avaḥ*.

The root *ava* is used in the sense of protection and so forth. The suffix *asun* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*), and by virtue of being included in the *nvi*-group, it is udātta-accented on its first syllable.
*Tā*: By the rule "supāṃ suluk" and so forth, there is the substitution of *ḍā* for the dual ending;
following the elision of the *ṭi* portion, there is the accent of the cessation of the udātta of the case-ending.
*mṛḍātaḥ*. [The root] *mṛḍ* means "to gladden. This is the *leṭ* mood in the sense of the optative (*liṅ*) used for a prayerful request.
The dual ending is *tas*.
By the rule "leṭo’ḍāṭau" (Pāṇini 3.4.94), the augment *āṭ* is added. [The suffix] *śa* is applied by the rule "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ."
Due to the *ḍit*-affix, there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel.

In such cases, by the rule "In the case of *vyadādi* roots, when *dṛś* does not mean 'perception,' *kañ* is added" (Pāṇini 3.2.60), the suffix *kañ* is applied to the root *dṛś* when the word *īdṛś* is present as an upapada.
In this upapada compound, by the rule *idaṃ kimorīśkī* (Pāṇini 6.3.90), *idam* becomes *īś*. Because it is marked with the letter *ś*, it is a replacement for the whole word (*sarvādeśa*).
Due to the *kit* marker on the root *kañ*, there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution.
Because the final member [of the compound] ends in a *kit* suffix, it has the acute accent on its first syllable;
in a *upapada* compound, that same accent remains by virtue of the rule regarding the original accent of the final member ending in a *kṛt* suffix.
For you two are the ones who come to this invocation of the inspired singer from every side;
you are the sustainers of the people.
For you two are the ones who go to the invocation of the inspired singer who honors you; you are the sustainers of the people for one such as me. 2.

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two are indeed renowned as those who go to the invocation—the call—of a sage like me, a Brahmin priest, in order to protect and assist the one who performs the ritual. Of what nature are you?
You are the sustainers of the people (carṣaṇīnām), that is, the maintainers of humanity by providing for their acquisition and security (yogakṣema).

*Gantārau*: [This is formed] from the root *gam* with the suffix *tṛn* in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlya*). For the dual ending, there is the substitution of *ā* by *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39), etc.
By the rule *ṛtaścoḍi guṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.16), there is guṇa substitution;
by the rule *asni* (Pāṇini 6.4.11) and others, there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhādīrghatva*);
and because the suffix *tṛn* is marked with *ṅit*, it is udātta on its first syllable.
[The root] *sthāḥ* [is used];
[the root] *as* means "to be";
the second person dual form of the imperfect (*laṅ*) is *thas*.
By the rule "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," there is elision (luk) of the suffix *śap*. By the rule "hi ca," there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta accent). [The form is] *avase*.
The root *ava* is used in the sense of "protection" (*rakṣaṇe*).
By the rule *tumarthe seseṇa* (Pāṇini 3.4.9), the suffix *asun* is applied. Because it is marked with *ṇi*, it is udātta on the first syllable.

Regarding *havam*: by the rule *hvejo 'bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is non-conditional (*anaimittika*) *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) and subsequent substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*). Then, by the rule *ṛdorap*, the suffix *ap* is added.
Finally, the *guṇa* and *avādeśa* substitutions take place.
In *apaḥ piba*, there is the udātta accent;
it retains the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) itself.
In *viprasya*:
The root *ḍuvap* means "to sow" or "to cause the continuity of seeds.
In this case, the suffix *ran* is applied according to the rule beginning with "ṛjendra," etc., and because it belongs to the *niv* class, the accent falls on the first syllable.
*māvataḥ*:

[The suffix] *vatup* is added according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.2.39.1, which provides an addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for the sense of similarity (*sādṛśya*) after the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
By Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.98, when a suffix or a subsequent member of a compound follows, the substitute *mā* replaces the portion of *asmad* ending in *map*.
By the rule *ā sarvanāmnaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.91), the letter *d* is replaced by *ā*; this results in a long vowel by the rule of homogeneous vowels (*savarṇadīrgha*).
In the word *manuṣaḥ*, the first syllable is udātta by virtue of the suffix *piba*.
When the rule for the acute accent on the final syllable of a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) applies, that [accent] alone remains.
*Dhartārau*. [The root] *dhṛñ* means "to hold."
The suffix *tṛc* is applied by Pāṇini’s rule *ṇvultṛcau* (3.1.133). The prohibition of the *it*-augment is applied by the rule *ekāca upadeśe*.
There is *guṇa* substitution, followed by the replacement of the vowel with *ra* (*raparatva*).
In the word "asna," there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhādīrgha*). The form "asna" is derived from the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
The word ending in the suffix *tṛc* is oxytone (*antodātta*) because it belongs to the *cvi*-class.

[The word] *carṣaṇīnām*. According to the Uṇādi Sūtra 2.261, "the suffix *ani* [is added] after the root *kṛp-* with the substitution of *ca* for the initial [consonant]," the suffix *ani* is applied.
By that rule, the letter *ka* is replaced by the letter *ca*.
The final acute accent (*antodāttatva*) prescribed by Vedic usage overrides the initial acute accent (*pratyayādyudāttatva*).
For this very reason, the acute accent of the case-ending is applied according to the rule *nāmyanatarasyām*;
for there, it is explained that when there is a suffix *manu* ending in a short vowel, the following noun (*nāman*) receives the acute accent.
1. Both *ca*, *cha*, *pha*, and *śa* [occur] simultaneously in words such as *vanaspati*.
2. [Words ending in] *ca*, *cha*, *ta*, *pha*, *śa*, or a short vowel have the acute accent on the final syllable (*antodātta*). [Mbh.
1.4.17] First Aṣṭaka, Chapter 143.

Satisfy us according to our desire with wealth, O Indra and Varuṇa; we pray for that which is nearest to you both. 3. According to our desire, satisfy [us]. O Indra and Varuṇa, [with] riches. Hither. Those two, you. Most near. We implore. 3.
O Indra and Varuṇa—O Indra and Varuṇa—satisfy us completely with the granting of wealth (*rāyaḥ*) according to our desire;
that is to say, whenever we long for wealth, grant it to us at those very times.
We entreat you both, who are such, to come into our closest proximity, so that there may be an exceeding nearness.
The meaning is that wealth should be given without delay.
In the context of acts of begging, the word *īmahe* is listed [in the Nighaṇṭu] at 3.19.1.
"Anukāmam":
following after desire (kāma), thus "anukāmam"; or else, according to each respective desire, thus "anukāmam."
The prefix *anu* here has the sense of "behind" (*paścāt*), or else it signifies the sense of "distribution" (*vīpsā*) within the category of "correspondence" (*yathārtha*).
For four meanings of *yathārtha* are accepted: fitness (*yogyatā*), distribution (*vīpsā*), non-exclusion of the word-meaning (*padārthānivṛtti*), and similarity (*sādṛśya*).
By the rule beginning with "An indeclinable [in composition] with a case-ending... (*avyayaṃ vibhakti...* Pāṇini 2.1.6), this forms an *avyayībhāva* compound.

By the rule *avyayībhāvaśca* (Pāṇini 1.1.41), the designation *avyaya* (indeclinable) is applied. Consequently, the elision (*luk*) that would otherwise apply by the rule *avyayādāpsupaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.82) is set aside as an exception by the rule *nāvyayībhāvādato'm tvapañcamyāḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.83), which prescribes the substitution of *am* for the case-ending.
By the rule *samāsasya*, the word receives an udātta accent on its final syllable. [Thus:
*tarpayethām*.
After the root *nṛp* with the suffix *iyant*, the *ātmanepada* affixes *loṭ* and *liṅ* are applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 1.3.74 (*aṇiñca*).
The second person dual form is *āthām*.
When the final *ṭi* is replaced by *e*, the substitution of *ām* for *etaḥ* occurs according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.4.90 (*āmetaḥ*).

When the suffix *śap* is present, the vowel *ā* is replaced by *iy* according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.2.80 (*ato yeyaḥ*). Following this, the first *uṇ* is applied and the *y* is elided, resulting in *indrāvaruṇā*.
By the rule "supāṃ suluk," the dual ending is replaced by the vowel *ā*. It bears the udātta accent due to being in the vocative case.
In the *saṃhitā* (continuous text), the vowel *ā* is shortened.
*rāyaḥ*: by the rule beginning with *usidam*, the case ending is acute. *tā*.
The vowel *ā* [in "yuvām"] is a substitute for the case-ending according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
Because it follows a word (*padāt*), the substitute *vām* for "yuvām" is unaccented (*anudātta*).
[The word is] *nediṣṭham*.
"Exceedingly near.
[The suffix] *inan* is used in the sense of excellence (*atiśāyana*).
By the rule "antikabādhayornedasādhau" (Pāṇini Sūtra 5.3.63), the substitution of *nedas* for *antika* occurs.
In the word "yasya," there is elision [of the suffix].
Because the suffix *ichan* has the marker *n*, it is udātta on its first syllable.
[The form is] *īmahe*.
The root *īṅ* means "to go.
Because it is marked with the indicatory letter *ṭ*, the ātmanepada (middle voice) endings are used.
By the rule "in the Vedic language [there is] diversely," there is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śyan*.
The elision of the accent.

May we indeed be among those who receive your powers, may we be among those who receive your benevolent thoughts—those who bestow strength. 4. May we indeed be among those who receive your powers; may we be among those who receive your benevolent thoughts; may we be among those who bestow strength. 4.

For this reason, the oblation consisting of *soma*, which pertains to our ritual acts (*śacīnām*), is mixed with the waters known as *vasatīvarī* and *ekadhana*, as well as with other substances such as milk and curds;
likewise, the speech in the form of hymns belonging to the priests endowed with excellent intellect (*sumatīnām*) is also mixed with various qualities worthy of praise.
For that reason, O Indra and Varuṇa, may you accept such an oblation; through your grace, may we become preeminent among those men who are "vājadān," givers of food.
In the twenty-five names of ritual actions beginning with "apaḥ" and "apanah," the word "śacī" is listed as a synonym for "śamī" (Nirukta 2.1.22).
*Yuvāku*:
[The root] *yu* means "to mix.
Regarding the rule *kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.357), by virtue of the term *bāhulaka* ("by way of irregularity"), the suffix *kāku* is also applied to the root *yu*.

Because there is an absence of the *guṇa* vowel due to the suffix *kit*, the substitution *uvaṅ* applies to the vowel *u*. By the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), it has the middle-acute (*madhyodātta*) pitch.
According to the opinion of some, the word *śacī* belongs to the *śāṅgaravādi* class.

Regarding the rule *ḍīnantaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.73), the Vṛttikāra stated in the commentary on *ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat* (Kāśikā 6.2.140) that [the suffix] is ādyudātta because it is marked with the *ṅit* indicator. This is illustrated in the phrase *sumatīnām*,
as mentioned in the commentary on *vidhāma sumatīnām* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.4.3).
"May we be.
The suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of a prayer (*prārthanā*). In the first person plural, it is optionally [replaced by *ni*].
In reality, however, the substitution of *iy* occurs by the rule *āto ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.81), and the elision of the *s* occurs because [the affix] is marked with the *ṅ*-sign.
Furthermore, the augment *yāsuṭ* is introduced as acute (*udātta*) by the rule *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca* (Pāṇini 3.4.103).
The elision of the *s* is according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 7.2.79: *liṅaḥ salopo'nantyasya*.
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix.
Because it is taught later [in the sequence of rules], only the *yāsuṭ* augment, which is acute-accented (*udātta*), remains.
*vājadābhām*:
[The term] *vājadāvān* means "one who gives *vāja*. The suffix *vanip* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.74, *āto maninkvanibvanipaśca*.
Because it is a *pit* [ending], its own accent (*dhātusvara*) alone remains.
In the compound, by virtue of the rule that the original accent of the final member of a *kṛt*-derived word prevails (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva*), that same accent remains.
In the case of the *ām* ending, there is the elision of the vowel *a* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.134: *allopo 'naḥ*.

Because of the status as a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 1.1.57 (*acaḥ parasmin*), the elision of the letter *v* by Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.1.66 (*lopo vyor vali*) does not take place.

Indra is the giver of thousands; Varuṇa is the one worthy of praise among those to be praised; he becomes the will-power that is fit for hymns. 5. Indra. Of the givers of thousands. Varuṇa. Of those worthy of praise. Will-power. Becomes. Fit for hymns. 5.
This Indra is the *kratu*—the performer of the act of bestowing wealth—among those who give thousands, meaning he gives in abundance.
Likewise, Varuṇa is the most worthy of praise (*ukthya*) among those things worthy of praise (*śaṃsyānām*), meaning he is preeminently laudable.
Varuṇaḥ: the suffix *una* is udātta on the first syllable because it is *niṣ*. [The word is] *śaṃsyānām*.

Regarding the root *śaṃs* in the sense of "praising": the suffix *ṇyat* is applied by the rule *ṛhalorṇyat*. When the rule *tisṛcatasṛ* would have applied, the initial vowel becomes udātta by the rule *īḍavandvavyaṃśaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.214).

*Kratuḥ*: By the rule *kṛñaḥ katuḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.77), the suffix *katu* is applied. Because it is marked with *kit*, there is no *guṇa* substitution, and the *yaṇ* replacement (*ṛ* becomes *ar*) occurs.
It is acute-accented (udātta) by virtue of the suffix-sound.
*Ukthyaḥ*. *Uktha* means a liturgical recitation (*śastra*).

Because it is worthy of praise (*stutya*), that which exists therein is called *ukthya*. [The suffix] *yat* is applied according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 4.4.110, "In the sense of 'existing there' (*bhave*) in Vedic usage (*chandasi*).
The elision [of the *i* of *yat*] occurs by the rule "of that which [ends in *i*]" (*yasyeti ca*).

In this case, setting aside the rule *atisvacaritam*, because there is the suffix *vat* as in *tīrthāya kūpyāya* and so forth, the initial acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*) that would otherwise be required by the rule *yato 'nāvaḥ* is not applied, according to the maxim *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante* (Paribhāṣā 35).
Now, one might object: let the *tisvacarita* accent apply even before the elision (*lopa*) of the *y* by the rule *yasya*;
for at that time, the rule *yato 'nāvaḥ* does not yet exist, since the suffix *vat* has not yet appeared.

For this very reason, the svarita accent is observed in such instances as *ūrmyāya ca sūrdhyāya ca*. Nor should it be argued that, due to its subsequent position and its status as an eternal (*nitya*) rule, the elision of *y* (*yasya lopaḥ*) ought to occur first; for the elision of *y*, which depends on both the base and the suffix, is extrinsic (*bahiraṅga*), whereas the application of *tistracari-tam* is more powerful because it is intrinsic (*antaraṅga*), depending solely on the suffix.

Therefore, just as in the case of "ūrmyāya" and so forth, here too in "ukthyaḥ," the acute accent will occur by virtue of the grammatical definition itself; what need is there for a Vedic anomaly? For where there is a doubling of a consonant without the elision [of a vowel], the rule "yato ’nāvaḥ" applies, as in the examples "iyam iyam" and so on.
However, in those places where elision (*lopa*) is the basis for the accentuation, there ought to be only the *svarita* accent.
If that is so, then in examples such as *tīrthāya* and *kūpyāya*, the fact that the first syllable is acute (*ādyudātta*) must simply be considered a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).

Alternatively, in this case, by the rule "an operation pertaining to a suffix (*āṅga*) is stronger than one pertaining to a phoneme (*varṇa*)" (Paribhāṣā 55), the elision itself will occur, overriding the *svarita* accent even though it is an internal (*antaraṅga*) operation.
In that case, let [the phenomenon] in examples such as "ukthyaḥ" and "ūrmyāya sūrdhyāya" be considered Vedic;
in any event, one is not exempt from Vedic usage in a single instance.
By their very aid, may we win and lay up [wealth]; may there also be an abundance for us. (6) By their very aid, may we win and lay up [wealth]; may there also be an abundance for us. (6)
By the protection (*avas*) of those very two, Indra and Varuṇa mentioned above, may we, the performers of the rite, win (*sanema*)—the word "wealth" being understood—as our portion;
and may we store it away (*ni dhīmahi*).
Once the wealth has been obtained, having spoken [of] as much as is required, we shall set aside the remainder of that wealth.
1. ca, cha, ṇa, ra, and tatha.

"May we establish [it] in the form of a treasure. And furthermore, may there be an 'impelling'—that is, wealth exceeding even that which was spoken of after eating—may it be accomplished. *Avasā*: [The word *asu*] is udātta by virtue of being [the suffix] *tva*. *Vayam*: As stated in the verse "yūyaṃ hi chā" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.15.2), so it should be understood here. *Sanema*: The optative (*liṅ*) in the sense of a benediction; its [first-person plural] ending is *mas*. By the rule "niyam ḍitaḥ," there is the elision of the *sakāra*. By the rule "kidāśiṣi" (Pāṇini 3.4.104), there is *yāsuṭ*. Since there is also the status of being a sārvadhātuka by the rule "chandasyubhayathā," there is the elision of the *sakāra* by the rule "liṅaḥ salopo'nantyasya" (Pāṇini 7.2.79). By the rule "ato yeyaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.2.80), there is the substitution of *iy*. By the rule "lopo vyorvali" (Pāṇini 6.1.66), there is the elision of *y*. By the rule "liṅyāśiṣyaṅ" (Pāṇini 3.1.86), there is *aṅ*. [By the rule] "ādguṇaḥ," [the guṇa is formed]. Because it begins a quarter-verse (*pāda*), there is no *nighāta* (elision of accent). *Dhīmahi*: From the root *ḍudhāñ* in the sense of "holding and nourishing. The [first-person plural] ending *mahiṅ* of the optative in the sense of a benediction. Its [ending] has both the designations of *sārvadhātuka* and *ārdhadhātuka* by the rule "chandasyubhayathā. There, because it is *sārvadhātuka*, there is the elision of the *sakāra* by the rule "liṅaḥ salopo'nantyasya. By the rule "sārvadhātukamapit," there is the *ṅittva* and the *śap* [augment]. By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is the elision of *śap* even for roots of the *juhotyādi* class. Because it is *ārdhadhātuka*, there is the elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pāṇini 6.4.64). [There is] *nighāta*. With respect to *sanema*, since this is a second [verb], there is no prohibition by the rule "cavāyoge prathamā. *Syāt*: The optative (*liṅ*) of the root *as* in the sense of a request; the third-person singular ending *tip*. By the rule "itaśca" (Pāṇini 3.4.100), there is the elision of the *dakāra*. By the rule "yāsuṭ parasmaipadātto ṅicca" (Pāṇini 3.4.103), there is *yāsuṭ* with the property of *ṅittva*. By the rule "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," there is the elision of *śap*. By the rule "kṣasoralopaḥ," there is the elision of the vowel *a*. Because it begins a quarter-verse, there is no *nighāta*. *Uta*: It is antodātta by the rule "evamādīnāmantaḥ. *Prerecanam*: From the root *ricir* in the sense of "separating. The suffix *lyuṭ* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*). There is the substitution of *an* for *y*. By the rule "liti," the syllable preceding the suffix is udātta. It is a *prādi*-compound. It has the original accent of the final member (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*).
O Indra and Varuṇa, I invoke you both for wondrous bounty; may you fully protect us as victorious ones. 7.
O Indra and Varuṇa, I call upon you both for wondrous bounty; grant us complete victory in the battles.

"O Indra and Varuṇa"—I call both of you, O Indra and Varuṇa. For what purpose? For "wondrous wealth" (*rādhase*), that is, for various riches in the form of jewels, pearls, and so forth. Therefore, being thus invoked, you two "make us," the patrons, "well-victorious" (*sujigyuṣaḥ*), meaning well-endowed with victory over our enemies. *Indrāvaruṇā*: The vocative ending *-ā* is substituted according to *supāṃ suluk...* etc. In a dual deity compound (*devatādvandve*), the first member takes the substitute *ānaṅ*. It has the acute accent on the first syllable due to being a vocative. In the *saṃhitā*, the shortening is Vedic (*chāndasa*). *Huve*: This is the first person singular present indicative (*laṭ*) of the root *hū* (to call), with the augment *iṭ*. While the rule *śapaḥ* applies, the suffix is elided by *bahulaṃ chandasi*. While the rule *haḥ* applies, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and substitution of the preceding letter by the following one, also by *bahulaṃ chandasi*. By *aci śnudhātu...* etc., the substitute *uvaṅ* is applied. Nor is there the substitution of *yaṇ* by *hunuvoḥ* etc., because that rule applies specifically to the root *juhoti* (which is taught directly), whereas this [root *hū*] is derived through a secondary derivation (*lākṣaṇika*). The accent of *iṭ* is acute by the accent of the suffix. Because it occurs at the beginning of a *pāda*, there is no suppression of accent (*nighāta*). *Rādhase*: From the root *rādh* with the suffix *asun*; it has the acute accent on the first syllable because of the suffix *niṣ*. *Asmān*: In the accusative plural (*śas*), the vowel is lengthened by *dvitīyāyāṃ ca*. The *n* is substituted by *śaso na*. *Jigyuṣaḥ*: From the root *ji* (to conquer). The suffix *kasu* is added after the perfect tense (*liṭ*) by *kasuśca*. There is reduplication. By *sanalliṅojeḥ*, the second syllable becomes *ku*. In *kasu*, there is an absence of *guṇa* because it is marked with *kit*. The *iṭ* which would have been required by the rule *kādiniyamāt* is excluded by the restriction *vasvekājādghasām*. The suffix is *śas* in the accusative plural. When it is designated as *bha*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*. The preceding letter replaces the following one. There is the substitution of *yaṇ* by *ernekācaḥ*. The *ṣ* is substituted by *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*. The vowel *u* is acute by the accent of the suffix. *Kṛtam*: From the root *ḍukṛñ* (to do). The second person dual of the imperative (*loṭ*) is replaced by *tam* because it belongs to the *tan*-class. The suffix *śap* is elided by *bahulaṃ chandasi*. The suppression of accent (*nighāta*) applies by *tiṅatiṅaḥ*. [End of Kaṇḍikā 19]
O Indra and Varuṇa, now indeed, in our prayers that desire to serve you, grant us protection. O Indra and Varuṇa, now, now, in our prayers that desire to serve you, grant us protection.

"O Indra-Varuṇā," O Indra and Varuṇa, "when our intellects (*adhīṣu*) desire to win (*sipāsantīṣu*), that is, when they wish to obtain, share, and properly serve you both (*vām*), then grant (*yacchatam*) us protection (*śarma*), that is, happiness, from all sides (*ā*)—now (*nū*), meaning most exceedingly and swiftly.
Among the fifty names for "swiftly," *nu* and *makṣu* are recited in the *Nighaṇṭu* (2.15.1). Through the force of its repetition here, an intensification is obtained."
O Indra and Varuṇa! It has been said: "Now indeed..."
In the phrase "ṛci tunudhamaśvataṅkutarudhyāṇām," there is lengthening of the preceding vowel. [The form] *sipāsantīṣu* [is derived from] the roots *vana* and *paṇ*, meaning "to share" or "to enjoy."
"An *p* at the beginning of a verbal root is replaced by *s*.
[The suffix] *san* is used in the sense of desire (*icchā*). There is reduplication, followed by the replacement of the remaining initial consonant (*halādiśeṣaḥ*).
In "sanyataḥ," there is the substitution of *i* by the rule [Pāṇini 6.4.44].
There is the substitution of *ṣ* by the rule "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pāṇini 8.3.59). The absence of the augment *iṭ* is optional by the rule "sanīvanta" (Pāṇini 7.2.49), etc.
By the rule "janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.42), the letter *n* is replaced by *ā*. Following this, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied for the present tense (*laṭ*),
and the suffix *śap* is added in the sense of the agent (*kartari*).
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *ugitaśca* (Pāṇini 4.1.6). The augment *num* is inserted by the rule *śapyanoranityam* (Pāṇini 7.1.81).
Because the *ṅīp*, the *śap*, and the *śatṛ* suffix are all *lasārvadhātuka*, they are unaccented (*anudātta*).
The initial udātta accent of *san* remains;
that alone is retained.
[In the word] *dhīṣu*.
The acute accent on the case-ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. Regarding *asmabhyam*,
it has been explained in the commentary on *asmabhyam apratiṣkṛtaḥ* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.7.6).
*yacchatam* [is derived from] *dāṇ* in the sense of "giving. After the suffix *śap*, there is the substitution of *yaccha* according to the rule beginning with *pāghrā*.

May this fair praise resound forth for you both, O Indra and Varuṇa, which I invoke as a joint hymn for the sake of success. 9. May this fair praise resound forth for you both, O Indra and Varuṇa, which I invoke as a joint hymn for the sake of success. 9.

"O Indra-Varuṇa"—O Indra and Varuṇa—"I invoke you both with this beautiful hymn (su-stuti) performed by me. Furthermore, having obtained that excellent praise (su-stuti)—the act of lauding performed through the joint effort of you two—for the sake of prosperity (ṛdhāyai), may such a beautiful hymn, a collection of Ṛks serving as the cause of excellent praise, pervade (ā-śravat) you both."
May he attain. [The root] *aś* [is used] in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*).
The suffix *tip* occurs by way of transposition from the imperative (*loṭ*).
"The suffix *śnu* is applied after roots beginning with *su*. For example: *suṣṭutiḥ*.
This is stated in [the commentary on] Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.7.7: "I do not find his excellent praise (*suṣṭutim*)."
I invoke Indra and Varuṇa;
they have been addressed.
But here, because of its connection with *yat*, there is no *nighāta* (accentual suppression). Regarding *ṛdhāyai*:
[it is derived from] the root *ṛdh* in the sense of "to increase."
The suffix *laṭ* [is used];
the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition; and *śvaḥ* [is used] in the second person dual.

The elision [of the suffix] occurs by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi. By the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), the vowel *ā* is acute (*udātta*). Due to its connection with the word *yat*, there is no suppression of accent (*nighāta*).

"Sadhastutim" [means] that excellent praise (*suṣṭuti*) in which there is praise together (*saha stutiḥ*) is "sadhastuti. Here, since the word *stuti* in the compound *suṣṭuti* functions as an instrument (*karaṇasādhana*)—meaning "that by which one is praised"—it refers to a *ṛc* (verse). However, this word *stuti* [in *sadhastuti*] functions as an abstract state (*bhāvasādhana*), referring to the act of praising itself.

In that [compound], since it is directed toward the action (*kriyā*), there is the state of being a means of accomplishing a thing (*bhāvasādhanatva*); whereas this [word *ṛk*] is directed toward the instrument (*karaṇasādhanatayā*). Thus, it is something other than the meaning of the word being compounded.
Here, in the word *sahatya*, the letter *dh* occurs by the transposition of the letter *h*.
The word *saha* is oxytone because it belongs to the class beginning with *evam-ādi*.
By virtue of being a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [of the compound] applies.
In the fifth section (anuvāka), there are six hymns (sūktas).
Among them, the first hymn, beginning with "Somānam," consists of nine verses (ṛcas). The seer (ṛṣi) and the meter (chandas) are as previously stated.
The emergence of specific deities is desired [in the following]: "With the five [verses] beginning with *somānam*, for the Brāhmaṇa; Indra and Soma are [the deities] in the fifth [verse].
It is joined with the act of praising being performed;
and there is another [verse] for the *dakṣiṇā* (sacrificial fee), another for the *sadasaspati*, and another for the *nārāśaṃsī*.
The first five verses of this hymn have Brahmaṇaspati as their deity.
Among them, in the fourth verse, "asa gha vīraḥ," there are three deities: Brahmaṇaspati, Indra, and Soma.
In the fifth verse, "tvaṃ tam," the aforementioned three deities are joined with Dakṣiṇā.
Starting from the sixth [verse], Sadasaspati is the deity for three [verses].
For this ninth verse, "anārāśaṃsam," Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa are optionally prescribed as the deities.
The application (viniyoga), however, is as before.
O Brahmaṇaspati, make Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij, the one who causes our hymns to resound.
Make him famous, O Brahmaṇaspati, as one who brings forth praise—the Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij. 1.
O Brahmanaspati, make this one named Soma—the performer of the pressing—resonant among the gods, making him manifest;
here is the illustration:
[make him like] the seer named Kakṣīvat.
The word *iva* (like) should be supplied here;
the meaning is "just as Kakṣīvat is well-known among the gods, so too [is he].
Kakṣīvat is the Ṛṣi who is Auśija, the son of Uśij.
The phrase "tam ibeti" is to be connected with the preceding context.

Kakṣīvān is well known among the sages who were performers of rites; he is recorded by the Taittirīyas as follows: "Para Ānara, Kakṣīvān Auśija, Vītahavya Śrāyasa, and Sadasyu Paurukutsya, desiring offspring, built this [fire-altar]" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5.6.5.2). Furthermore, his renown as a performer is indicated by the mention of him as a seer (*ṛṣi*) in another *ṛc*: "I am Kakṣīvān, a seer, a sage" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4.26.1).

Therefore, it is appropriate that he serves as an illustration for one who performs this [rite]. This mantra has been explained by Yāska as follows: "O Brahmaṇaspati, make the presser of Soma illustrious, just as Kakṣīvat was, the son of Uśij. Kakṣīvat is 'possessing a girth'; Kakṣīvat is the son of Uśij; Uśij is the son of Uśiga, from the root *uś*, meaning 'to desire' or 'to shine. Alternatively, this may simply refer to a human named Kakṣa; O Brahmaṇaspati, make him, the presser of Soma, illustrious. (Nirukta 6.10).

Regarding this mantra, the Taittirīyas record the intended meaning indicated by the line *somānam* and the line *kṛṇuhi brahmaṇas pate*: "He says, 'The Soma-drinker, the one who makes [the voice] resound'; verily he secures the drinking of Soma.
He says, 'Make [him], O Lord of Prayer'; verily he secures spiritual luster" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.5.8.4).
*Somānam*.
"He hears" (*sunoti*). The root *puñ* means "to press.
The suffix *manin* is applied according to the rule "it is seen [that this suffix is used] after other roots as well."

Because the inclusion of the term *dṛśi* would entail the application of other rules, even though it is a *nipāta*, it does not have the udātta accent on its first syllable; rather, it retains the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
Alternatively, the word *soma* should be regarded as belonging to the *uṇhādi* group (Pāṇini 6.1.160).
Or, due to the mention of the term *bahula*, the *uṇādi* suffix *man* should be understood [as applied here].
"Svaraṇam" is well-known.
The root *sṛ* means "to sound" and "to heat.
According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.3.113 (*kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*), the suffix *lyuṭ* is applied here in the sense of the object (*karman*).
In *liti*, the vowel *a* is udātta. [The root] *kṛṇuhi* [is derived from] *kṛvi*, which means "to injure" and "to do."
The augment *num* is applied by the rule *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.58).
The *sip* of the *loṭ* [imperative] is replaced by *hi*.
Although the *śap* suffix would normally apply, the *upratyaya* is used by the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyora ca*; along with that, the *v* is replaced by *a*.
By the rule *tasya ato lopaḥ*, there is elision of that [final *a*].

Because of its status as a *sthānivat* (as if it were still present), there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*). Furthermore, because of the doubling of *hi*, there is no *guṇa* for the vowel *u*.
Furthermore, by the rule *utaśca pratyayācchhandovāvacanam* (Pāṇini 6.4.106), the *luk*-elision of the suffix *he* does not apply;
because of the statement that "the accent taught later is stronger, except in the case of *vikaraṇa*s," the word is accented acute (*udātta*) by the accent of the suffix *he* itself.
Due to its position at the beginning of a *pāda*, it does not undergo elision of accent (*nighāta*).
In *brahmaṇaḥ*,
the visarga is replaced by *s* in the *saṃhitā* according to Pāṇini’s rule 8.3.53, *pati-putra-...*.
Because the two words follow a vocative (*subāmantrita-parāṅgavat*), they take the *āmantrita-nighāta* accent.
*Kakṣīvantam*:
*kakṣa* itself [means] a girth-rope connected to the belly of a horse.
The suffix *ya* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 4.4.110: *bhave chandasi*.

In the sense of "she possesses that," the word *kakṣīvān*—which is the name of a specific seer (*ṛṣi*)—is established as an irregular formation (*nipātita*) by Pāṇini’s rule 8.2.12: *āsandivadavīvakṣvīvatkakṣīvat*.

According to the rule *chandasyubhayathā*, it may be treated as a nominal stem; thus, the *ī* in its place, substituted for the suffix *ya*, is established as accented (*udātta*) by the accent of the suffix *ya*.
The suffixes *matup* and *sup* are unaccented (*anudātta*) when they follow a word ending in a *pi*-class vowel. [Example:
*auśijaḥ*. [Root:
*vaś* in the sense of "desire."
With the word *iji* continuing from Uṇādi-sūtra 2.228, the suffix *ij* is applied by Uṇādi-sūtra 2.229 (*vaśeḥ kicca*).
Because that suffix is marked with *k*, there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) according to Pāṇini-sūtra 6.1.16 (*prahijyā*),
and when the preceding vowel is substituted for both, there is an absence of *guṇa*.
By the rule *tasyāpatyam* (Pāṇini 4.1.92), [the suffix] *aṇ* is applied by the rule *prāgdīvyato ’ṇ* (Pāṇini 4.1.83).
There is vṛddhi of the first vowel. By the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*), it has an udātta on the final syllable.

He who is wealthy, the dispeller of disease, the finder of riches, the increaser of prosperity—may he, the swift one, be gracious unto us. 2. He who... wealthy... the dispeller of disease... the finder of riches... the increaser of prosperity... may he... be gracious unto us... the swift one. 2.

May that Brahmaṇaspati—who is wealthy and possessed of riches; who is the remover of disease, the slayer of ailments; who is the finder of wealth and the increaser of prosperity, the one who causes growth; and who is swift, endowed with speed, and the bestower of quick results—may he attend to us, may he favor us. The meaning is: "having taken us under his protection, may he grace us. Regarding the word *siṣaktu* having the sense of "attending" or "serving," Yāska says: "He says *siṣaktu* and *sacate* are [used] for one who serves" (Nirukta 3.21).
The words "two words of reproach" (*pratyayako śabdau*) are to be supplied as the remainder [of the sentence].
*Arupaḥ* refers to a mortal; *dhūtiḥ* means a destroyer, [referring to] a man in the form of an enemy who has approached our vicinity to cause harm;
*śaṃsaḥ* means praising, that is to say, reviling.

May such a specific speech not reach us, nor may it reach us completely; that is to say, let not an insult instigated by an enemy ever come upon us. For that purpose, O Brahmaṇaspati, protect and preserve us.
*mā* is a particle.
*Śaṃsa* means praising.
The suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*). Because the root contains a *ji*-class vowel, it is udātta on its first syllable. Thus, it is *arūpaḥ*.
From the root *ṛ* meaning "to go" (*ṛ gatau*), with the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) implied by the rule *atereraḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.519), the form *arus* is derived.

There is *guṇa* substitution, followed by the replacement of the vowel with *ra* (*raparatva*). Although the accent of the suffix would normally apply, it is instead *ādyudātta* (accented on the first syllable) because it belongs to the *vṛṣan*-class.
*Dhūrti*: *dhurvī* has the sense of injury (*hisārtha*). The suffix *kic* is applied by the rule "The suffix *kic* is used after roots ending in *u* when a name (*saṃjñā*) is to be formed."
By the rule *titutratatha-sisusarakaseṣu ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.9), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*.
By the rule *upadhāyāśca* (Pāṇini 7.1.101), there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*).

When the elision of *ūṭh* would have applied by overriding the elision of the semivowel (*vali lopaṃ bādhitvā*) according to *ūṭhi prāpte* (Pāṇini 6.4.19), the elision of the letter *v* occurs by the rule *rālopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.21).
*praṇak*. [The root] *pṛcī* [is used] in the sense of contact (*saṃparka*). [This is] the third person singular present indicative (*laṭ*) form.
Furthermore, there is the elision of the vowel *i*;
the elision according to the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt* [Pāṇini 6.1.68]; and the substitution of *ku* [for *k*].
From the roots beginning with *rudh*, the suffix *śnam* is applied;
for that [suffix], the augment *aṭ* is added by the rule "There is frequent deviation [from the regular rules]" (Pāṇini 3.1.85),
and there is the substitution of *ya*.
The udātta accent of the vowel *a* in *akāra* occurs by way of exception (*vyatyaya*), overriding its status as unaccented due to being an augment (*āgama*).
There is no absence of the *nivāta* (non-sandhi) rule here, because of the provision in Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.1.63: *cādilope vibhāṣā*.
[This applies to] *martyasya*.

The root *mṛḍ* means "to abandon life. By the rule *asihasimṛ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.366), the suffix *tan* is applied according to the Uṇādi class. In the sense of "existing among mortals," the suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *bhave chandasi* (Pāṇini Sūtra 4.4.110).
The word *anātraḥ* has an udātta accent on its first syllable. The root *rakṣ* means "to protect."

The suffix *śara* is unaccented (*anudātta*). Only the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains. Because it occurs at the beginning of a *pāda*, it does not undergo the *nighāta* (elision of accent).
"May there be protection for us.

The substitution of *ṇ* for *n* in *naḥ* occurs even when it is not preceded by a prefix (*anupasargāt*), because of the inclusion of the term "optionally" (*bahulagrahaṇāt*) in Pāṇini Sūtra 8.4.28, *upasargād ahulam*.
In *brahmaṇaspate*,

because it is a vocative (*sudāmantritam*) that has become part of a larger syntactic unit (*parāṅgabhāvāt*), both words undergo the low-pitched accent (*āmantritanighāta*).
That hero indeed does not come to harm, whom Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, and Soma impel—that mortal man. ||4||

Indra, the god, impels—that is, reaches or causes to prosper—the mortal who is about to sacrifice; likewise, the god Brahmaṇaspati impels him; likewise, Soma impels him. He, that very sacrificer, being a hero (vīra) endowed with virility, does not perish, he does not come to ruin. [The particle] *gha* belongs to the class beginning with *ca* and is unaccented (*anudātta*). Because the *tip* ending is marked as *pit*, the accent of the *śnu* suffix alone remains.
O Brahmaṇaspati, may you, Soma, and Indra, along with Dakṣiṇā, protect that mortal from distress. ||5||

"O Brahmaṇaspati, protect that mortal man who performs [the rite] from *aṃhas*—that is, from sin; this is the ellipsis. Likewise, may Soma protect him, and may Indra protect him, and the deity called Dakṣiṇā also protect him. Regarding *dakṣiṇā*: from the root *dakṣ* meaning "to increase," with the suffix *inn* according to Uṇādisūtra 2.208 (*dudakṣabhyāminn*). By virtue of being a *niv* suffix, it is udātta on the first syllable. Regarding *aṃhas*: by the rule beginning with *naḍvapayasya*, it is udātta on the first syllable. || 34 ||
1. Regarding the sacrificer:
this verse, "sadasaspatim," is prescribed for the oblation of the *anupravacanīya* rice-porridge.

Accordingly, it is recited in the *Gṛhyasūtra*, in the section beginning with "having tied the girdle" (*mekhalāmābadhya*), as follows: "The teacher, while [the student] maintains contact, should offer the oblation with the verse: 'sadasaspatimadbhutam'" (Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra 1.22.11).

I have approached—that is, I have attained—the god named Sadasaspati in order to obtain intelligence (*medhā*). Of what nature is he? He is wonderful (*adbhuta*), marvelous; beloved of Indra because of his companionship in drinking Soma; desirable (*kāmya*), lovely; and a *sani*, a giver of wealth. Regarding the words: *Sadah*: from the root *sad* in the sense of "sitting" or "dwelling. By the rule *sarvadhātubhyo'sun*, the suffix *asun* is added. It is accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) according to the *nipāta* rules. *Patim*: from the root *pā* (to protect). The suffix *dati* is applied (Uṇādi-sūtra 4.497), with the elision of the *ṭi* portion. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). *Priyam*: by the rule *igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*, the suffix *ka* is added. The substitution of *iyaṅ* occurs. The accent is that of the suffix. *Kāmyam*: from the root *kāmayati*. By the rule *aco yat*, the suffix *yat* is added. By the rule *ṇeraniṭī*, there is the elision of the causative marker *ṇi*. By the rule *yato'nāvaḥ*, it is accented on the first syllable. *Sanim*: from the root *paṇ* in the sense of "giving. By the rule *dhātvādeḥ paḥ saḥ*, the *pa* becomes *sa*. With the word *aca iḥ* (Uṇādi-sūtra 4.578) still in force, the suffix *i* is added by the rule *khani-kaṇyayasivasivasinidhavanigranthivaribhyaśca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 4.579). The accent is that of the suffix. *Ayāsiṣam*: from the root *yā* (to go/attain). The suffix *luṅ* is used. *M* replaces the initial *a*. By the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), the augment *iṭ* is added to *sic*, and the augment *sak* is added to the root. There is the *nighāta* (elision of accent) for the verb.

Without whom even the sacrifice of the wise man does not succeed—he it is who promotes the application of our prayers. (7) Without whom, even the sacrifice of the one possessed of inspired wisdom (*vipaścit*) does not succeed—he is the one who impels the union of our thoughts. (7)

This sacrifice must be performed; for even a wise sacrificer does not succeed without the deity Sadasaspati. This very deity Sadasaspati promotes—that is, pervades—the connection (*yoga*) with our thoughts (*dhīnām*), meaning either our mental intentions regarding performance or the ritual acts to be accomplished.
The sense is that, by favoring the sacrificer, he brings his sacrifice to completion.
For this reason...
By the rule "anyārāt... (Pāṇini 2.3.29), the fifth case ending (*pañcamī*) is applied due to its connection with *ṛte*.
Although the rule "sāvekācaḥ" would have required the acute accent (*udātta*) on the case-ending, the prohibition "na godhnasāvavargaḥ" prevents this. Thus, [the desired form] is established.

‘*pidhu saṃrāddhau*’ [DhP 1.102]. Here, *iy* has the udātta accent on the first syllable due to its being *nisvādi*. Alternatively, there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision) by the rule ‘*na cchavyapraśān*’.
[The word] *dhīnām* [receives its accent] because the case-ending is acute by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. [The word] *yogam*.
The root *yuj* means "to join. Due to the suffix *ghañ*, which has the phoneme *j* as its marker, the word is udātta-accented on the first syllable. [He] impels (*invati*).
The root *vi* has the meaning "pervasion.
The suffix *śap* is added.
By the rule *idito num dhātoḥ*, the augment *num* is applied.
The elision of the accent.

He indeed perfects the preparation of the oblation; he makes the sacrifice proceed forward; the invocation goes to the gods. (8) Then he pierces [the darkness]; he perfects the preparation of the oblation; he makes the sacrifice proceed forward; the invocation goes to the gods. (8)
Immediately thereafter, he pierces the *haviskṛt*—the sacrificer engaged in the preparation of the oblation—the god who dwells in the assembly (*sadasaspatir devaḥ*) causes him to prosper;
that is to say, he bestows the fruit immediately after the offering of the oblation. For the attainment of such a fruit, the *adhvara* (sacrifice) is performed by the sacrificer.

1. Because of its cooperation with the *ṭha* [suffix]. That which is being sacrificed (*yajam*)—that is, that which is going forth pre-eminently and is endowed with completion through what is desired—the *kṛt* suffix effects this.
The deity, being invoked by the *hotṛ*, becomes satisfied and goes among the gods in order to cause the sacrificer (*yajamāna*) to attain [his goal].

Alternatively, *hotrā*—our speech in the form of praise—goes among the gods to satisfy them. Among the fifty-seven names of speech beginning with *śloka* and *dhārā*, it is recited in the *Nighaṇṭu* (1.11.35): "Hotrā is speech (*gīḥ*)."
*Haviṣkṛti*:
he for whom there is the making (*kṛti*)—that is, the preparation (*saṃpādana*)—of the oblation (*havis*) is *haviṣkṛt*.
In this *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent of the first member remains as its original form (*prakṛtisvaratva*), according to the rule "in a *bahuvrīhi*, [the first member retains] its original form."
*prājam*:
By the rule *aniganto'nataḥ* (Pāṇini 6.2.52), which applies when there is no elision of *va*, the *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratvam*).
Subsequently, the accent of the single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*) applies.
*Adhvara*:
that in which *dhvara*, meaning violence (*hiṃsā*), does not exist.
By the rule *mantra-subhyām*, the final syllable of the compound is udātta.

*Hotrā* refers to the deity, because [the deity] is invoked (*hūyate*) in this [sacrifice]. The suffix *tran* is applied according to *uṇādi-sūtra* 4.607: "After the roots *hu*, *yā*, *mā*, *āśu*, and *bhasi*, [the suffix *tran* is added]. It is acutely accented on the first syllable by virtue of the *nistva* rule.
I have beheld Narāśaṃsa, the most courageous and most widely renowned,
like the entire sacrificial wealth of heaven.
I have beheld Narāśaṃsa, the most courageous, the most widely renowned, like the entirety of heaven, possessing all sacrificial wealth. 9.
Narāśaṃsa is a specific deity bearing that name;
alternatively,
through the etymological analysis of its constituent parts, this word refers to the deity Sadasaspati.
And Yāska demonstrates the etymological derivation: "Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice, so says Kāthakya; 'Men praise him here,' so says Śākapūṇi; he is praised by men" (Nirukta 8.6).
In this context, like Agni, Sadasaspati is also called Narāśaṃsa because he is praised by men.
Keeping this very intention in mind, the Brāhmaṇa text is handed down thus: "Men are indeed offspring, and speech is the praise" (Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 6.27).
Therefore, being praised by men, I beheld—meaning I saw through the vision of the scriptures—that Lord who is the Master of the Assembly (*sadasaspati*) or the deity named Narāśaṃsa.
Of what nature was he?
He was exceedingly bold, possessed of great audacity; most renowned, being pre-eminently famous; and possessing the splendor attained from all sacrifices.

"like the heavens," that is, like the specific regions of the celestial world presided over by the sun, the moon, and so forth; just as those are radiant, so too is this Narāśaṃsa radiant—this is the meaning.
