The form is an irregularly derived (nipātita) infinitive used in the sense of the suffix -tum, according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.4.11: "For the purpose of seeing and for the purpose of looking about."
In the animal sacrifice, during the cleansing, this verse, "O waters, carry away this [impurity]" (*idam āpaḥ pra vahata*), is prescribed for use;
it is stated in the section beginning with "When the omentum has been offered" (*hutāyāṃ vapāyām*) in the Sūtra: "O waters, carry away this" (*idam āpaḥ pra vahata*, Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.5).
This same verse is also prescribed for use during the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*) at the end of the sacrifice.

In the section beginning with "Having performed the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings," it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "O Waters, carry this away; may the waters and plants be auspicious for us" (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 6.13).
May these waters carry away whatever evil is in me—
whatever wrong I have committed by malice or whatever falsehood I have uttered.
O Waters, carry away this—whatever evil has been committed by me, whatever transgression I have perpetrated, or whatever curse or falsehood I have uttered. 22.

Whatever evil has been committed by me while acting as a sacrificer, whether it arose from ignorance or because I, as a sacrificer, have practiced malice—that is, intentionally wronged others on all sides—or whatever I have reviled the virtuous, or even whatever untruth I have spoken: carry away all this collection of offenses; having removed them from me, lead them elsewhere by means of your flow.

In the case of *mayi*: when the substitute *mā* is applied to *mad* ending in the singular by the rule "tvamāvekavacane," and the substitution of the single form (*pararūpa*) is made by the rule "ato guṇe," the substitution of *y* for the *d* occurs by the rule "yo'ci.
By the accent of the single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*), the vowel *a* following the *m* becomes udātta.

*dudroha* [is derived from] the root *duh* in the sense of "desire to harm" (*jighāṃsā*). After the suffix *liṭ*, there is *guṇa*; then follow reduplication, shortening, and the substitution of the remaining initial consonant (*halādi-śeṣa*). By the rule "*liti*" (Pāṇini 6.1.193), the syllable preceding the suffix is acute (*udātta*).
Just as there is an absence of elision (*nighāta*) due to its connection with that, [so it is here]. *Śeṣa*.
[The root] *śap* [is used] in the sense of "reviling."

In the case of the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, the *taṅ* [middle voice] endings are used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). This is the first person singular ending. The substitution of *e* for the final vowel (*ṭi*) applies.

By the rule *ata ekahalmadhye* (Pāṇini 6.4.120), there is the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsalopa*). The word is oxytone due to the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). As before, there is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*).
Regarding the worship of the Āhavanīya fire in the animal sacrifice, the verse is "āpo adyānvacāriṣam.
This is stated in the section beginning with "manotāyai saṃpreṣita" in the Sūtra: "They worship here with [the verse] 'āpo adyānvacāriṣam'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.6).
I have followed after the waters today; we have united with their essence.
Come to us full of milk; endow me with splendor.
O Waters! Today I have moved along you; we have united with your essence. Come hither, full of milk; endow me with splendor. 23.
Then, on this day, for the sake of the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), I followed the waters;
I entered the waters.
And having entered, we have come together with the essence of the water, its vital flavor.
O Agni, you who are rich in milk (*payasvān*) by virtue of abiding in the waters, come hither. [1. ḍha:
"all my collection of offenses"; śa: "O Waters, all my collection of offenses"; ṣa: "for indeed, O Waters, all my collection of offenses"] Come!
"Come to this rite;
unite me, who am thus bathed, with *varcas*—that is, with splendor."
The word *āpaḥ*: when the suffix *śas* was expected in the sense of the object (*karman*), *jas* is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). [The form] *acāripam*.
The root *car* has the meaning "to go.
In the *luṅ* tense, *cli* is replaced by *sic*.
By the rule *ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.35), the augment *iṭ* is added.

When the prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4) would otherwise apply, the *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) occurs by way of its exception, according to the rule *ato lāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.2).
Thus: *agasmahi*. The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by the rule *samo gamyucchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29).
The suffix *cli* is replaced by *sic*.
The absence of *luk* elision for *cli* in the rule "ghas etc. in mantras" (*mantre ghasa*) is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
There is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ* by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.2.10: "after a root that is monosyllabic and has an anudātta vowel in its original form (*upadeśa*)."
Because the suffix *sic* is marked with *kittva* by the rule *vā gamaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.13), there is the elision of the nasal [of the root] according to the rule *anudāttopadeśa...* and so forth.
*Gahi*: in the imperative (*loṭ*), *hi* replaces the *sip* suffix of the root *gam*.
Because [the suffix] has the marker *ṅ*, the nasal is elided by the rule "anudāttopadeśa... and so forth.
The elision of *hi* by the rule "ato heḥ" does not occur, because the elision of *m* is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) in this context by the rule "asiddhavadatrā bhāt."
Unite me, O Agni, with splendor, unite me with progeny, and unite me with long life.
May the gods and Indra, together with the seers, take note of this for me.
O Agni, unite me with splendor, unite me with progeny, and unite me with long life!
May the gods take note of this of mine; may Indra, together with the seers, take note. 24.

O Agni, unite me with splendor and with offspring. O gods who drink Soma, may you know—may you recognize—the performance of this sacrificer. Furthermore, may Indra, together with the hosts of seers, know my performance. [The verb] *vidyuḥ* [is derived from the root] *vid* "to know. In the potential mood (*liṅ*), by Pāṇini 3.4.108, *jher jus* [is substituted for the suffix *jhi*]. There is the augment *yāsuṭ*. By the rule "the *sa* of the *liṅ* is elided," there is the elision of the letter *sa*. By Pāṇini 6.1.96, there is the substitution of the single substitute form (*pararūpa*). Because *yāsuṭ* is acute, the single substitute vowel *u* is also acute. In the word *asya*, by the rule "for *idam* in subsequent reference" (*anvādeśe*), *aś* is substituted and is grave (*anudātta*). The case-ending is also grave because it is a *sup* suffix. In the phrase *saha ṛṣibhiḥ*, there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) by Pāṇini 6.1.128. 12 || 5 ||

In the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala, there are seven sūktas. Among them, the first sūkta, consisting of fifteen verses beginning with "kasya nūnam," is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Śunaḥśepa, the son of Ajīgarta, and is in the triṣṭubh meter.
The triplet beginning with "abhi tvā deva" is in the Gāyatrī meter. Because the first verse is undefined (anirukta), its deity is Prajāpati; for the verse "agnervayam," the deity is Agni.
Savitṛ is the deity of this triplet beginning with "abhi tvā deva";
the verse "bhagabhaktasya" has Bhaga as its deity; the remaining verses are addressed to Varuṇa.

And thus it is enumerated: "Kasya pañcona... the *jagatī* [hymn] belongs to Śunaḥśepa; he is the adopted son of Viśvāmitra, also called Devarāta; the first [verse] is addressed to Varuṇa and is in the *triṣṭubh* meter; the two following [verses] are addressed to Agni and Kavi; the triplet is addressed to Savitṛ and is in the *gāyatrī* meter; its last [verse] is addressed to Bhaga.

On the day of the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) during the Rājasūya sacrifice, when the *marutvatīya* litany has been completed, this group of seven hymns beginning with this one is to be recited by the Hotṛ priest before the king who is surrounded by his sons and others for the sake of the consecration.

And so it is stated in the Sūtra: "When the Marutvatīya offering has been completed, seated upon a golden cushion to the south of the Āhavanīya fire, one should recite the Śaunaḥśepa narrative for the consecrated king who is surrounded by his sons and ministers" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 9.3).

There is also a Brāhmaṇa passage: "This very narrative of Śunaḥśepa, consisting of a hundred verses and stanzas, the Adhvaryu relates to the consecrated king; seated upon a golden cushion he relates it, and seated upon a golden cushion he responds" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 7.18).
1. *Ḍha-varcasā mām amṛja*: "Cleanse me with splendor; unite me with progeny and long life. In place of "saṃyojaya" (unite), read "saṃsṛja saṃyojaya" (unite and join).
In the first *Chandoma*, regarding the word *vaiśvadeva*, the triplet beginning with "abhi tvā deva savitaḥ" serves as the hymn (*sūkta*).
This is prescribed in the section titled "Now the *Chandomas*" in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (8.9): "abhi tvā deva savitaḥ... pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuvā."
The verse beginning with "abhi tvā" is also employed in the churning of fire;
this is prescribed in the section on the morning Vaiśvadeva sacrifice by the sūtra: "abhi tvā deva savitarmahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.16).
And it is heard in scripture: "He recites the Sāvitrī verse beginning with 'abhi tvā deva savitar'" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1.16).
Likewise, in the Pravargya rite as well, this very [verse] is employed;
it is prescribed in the section beginning with "Now the northern" (*athottaram*) as: "O divine Savitṛ, [I have approached] thee... like a calf with its mothers" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.7).
Similarly, it is also [employed] for the Grāvastut priest.

In the section beginning with "At this time the Grāvastut [priest]," it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "With a medium tone, [he recites] this *savana*: 'Towards you, O God Savitṛ... (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.12).

Toward you, O God Savitṛ, the lord of all desirable things, we ever seek our portion, O protector. 3. Toward you, O God Savitṛ, the lord of all desirable things, we ever seek our portion, O protector. 3.
Then, impelled by Agni, he prays to Savitṛ with the triplet beginning "Abhi tvā.
Thus it is heard in scripture: "Agni said to him, 'Savitṛ indeed is the lord of instigations; you should approach him. He approached Savitṛ with this triplet, 'Abhi tvā deva savitar... (AiB 7.16).
O ever-present protector, O Savitṛ, we solicit from you—who are the lord and master of desirable riches—everywhere a share, that is, wealth worthy of being enjoyed.
Īśānam:
from the root *īś* in the sense of "lordship" (*aiśvarya*),
with the suffix *śānac* substituted for the present tense marker *laṭ*.

By the rule "tāsyanudāttet," the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, so the accent of the verbal root remains. [The word] *vāryāṇām* [is derived from] the root *vṛñ* in the sense of "to choose" (*saṃbhakti*).
By the rule *ṛhalorṇyat*, [the suffix] *ṇyat* is applied.
By the rule *īḍavanda-* etc., the initial syllable receives the udātta accent. Thus: *avan*.
The vocative has the *nighāta* (elision of accent). In the word *bhāgam*, the final syllable of the suffix *ghañ* is acute according to the rule "karṣātvataḥ."

For indeed, that very Bhaga, striving thus before reproach, free from hatred, has placed [the prize] within your hands. 4. For indeed, that very Bhaga, striving thus before reproach, free from hatred, has placed [the prize] within your hands. 4.
O Savitṛ, that specific wealth which is *bhaga*—meaning worthy of being enjoyed—which has been placed in your two hands, that specific wealth we seek; this is the connection with what precedes.
The word *cit* is used for the sake of honor, and the word *hi* indicates well-known fact.
That wealth is worthy of honor is well known everywhere.
He clarifies that very renown for being worthy of worship: *itthā śaśamānaḥ*—in this manner, being praised; being extolled.
They know every manner of praise for wealth;
however, fearing that they might not be constant, he says:
"Nidaḥ" means "free from hatred"—that is, when [wealth] was previously established as one's own, at that time one is devoid of aversion toward it.
Therefore, the meaning is that being praised was stated with the intention of [the object] being one's own.
*Itthā*:
by the rule *idamsthamuḥ* (Pāṇini 5.3.24), which expresses manner (*prakāra*).
The substitution of the suffix *ḍā* for the case-ending occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*) according to the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
Due to the elision of the *ṭi* suffix, the vowel *ā* becomes acute by virtue of the *udāttanivṛtti-svara*. [The word] *śaśamānaḥ*:
[the root] *śaś* [is used in the sense of] "leaping" (*plutagati*).
But here, it is for the purpose of praise. The suffix *śānac* is used in the sense of habitual action according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.129 (*tācchīlyavayovacana*).
The suffix *śap* is added in the sense of the agent.
The word *citaḥ* has its final syllable accented (antodātta). Regarding *nidaḥ*: [it is derived from] the root *ṇidi* in the sense of "censure" (*kutsā*).
The suffix *kip* has the sense of "abundance" and so forth.
By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the fifth case (*pañcamī*) receives the acute accent (*udātta*). Thus: *adveṣaḥ*.
In the bahuvrīhi compound *na vidyate dveṣo 'sya* ("in whom there is no hatred"), the final syllable of the last member is udātta according to the rule *nañ-subhyām*.
[The form] *dadhe* is the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) in the passive voice (*karmaṇi*).

Because it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the rule "the first syllable of reduplicated (*abhyasta*) stems is acute" does not apply; rather, the accent of the suffix itself remains. Due to its connection with *yad-vṛtta*, there is an absence of the *nighāta* (elision of accent).
1. Herein, *ḍha* signifies hatred.

"O thou devoted to Bharga, may we rise up through thy protection; may we grasp the summit of wealth. (5) "O thou devoted to Bharga, may we rise up through thy protection; may we grasp the summit of wealth. (5)

O Savitṛ, may we, being yours, through your protection (*avasā*), which is joined with the wealth of Bhaga—that is, of you who possess [that] fortune (*bhaga*)—attain eminence (*udaśema*). To do what? To undertake (*ārabhe*) the head, that is, the excellence, of wealth (*rāyaḥ*). The meaning is: "May we become pervaded by the renown of possessing wealth. The word *bhaga* is acute-accented on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group. In the compound, the original accent of the first member is retained according to the rule *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*. Regarding *aśema*: the root is *aś* in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāptau*). By metrical transposition (*vyatyayena*), the Parasmaipada ending is used; the suffix is *śap*. Regarding *rāyaḥ*: the sixth case is acute-accented according to the rule *uḍidam*. Regarding *ārabhe*: the suffix *ken* is used in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) by the rule *kṛtyārthe tavaiken*. It is acute-accented on the first syllable by the rule *nisvareṇa*. 13.
For neither the warrior power, nor might, nor wrath have these sons attained, nor even their vital strength;
nor do these waters that move without blinking reach it, nor those who pierce the belly of the wind.

No, indeed; neither their dominion, nor their force, nor their wrath, nor even those birds, though crying out, have attained it. Nor these waters flowing without blinking, nor those who overcome the might of the wind.
Then, impelled by Savitṛ, Śunaḥśepa praised Varuṇa with the remainder of this hymn and with the following hymn.

Thus it is heard in the scripture: "Savitṛ said to him, 'You have been appointed for King Varuṇa; go to him. He approached King Varuṇa with thirty-one [verses] of the subsequent [hymn]" (AiB 7.16). O Varuṇa, even those birds—such as hawks and others—that are seen flying, soaring through the vast sky, have not attained your *kṣatra*, your bodily power; they have truly not reached it.
The meaning is that even among birds, there is no bodily strength equal to yours;
likewise, they did not attain your endurance (*sahas*), nor your prowess (*parākrama*), nor even your capacity (*sāmarthya*); and similarly, they did not attain your wrath (*manyu*).
The meaning is that when you are enraged, [your power] is impossible to withstand.
The waters, which flow perpetually in the form of a current, have not attained your strength;
and the specific movements of the wind (vāta) do not shatter—that is, they do not harm—your formidable speed (abhva).
The meaning is that they were not able to cross over;
"they too did not reach" connects with what precedes.
*Patayantaḥ*. [The root] *pat*,
meaning "to go," belongs to the *curādi* class and ends in *n*.
The suffix *śatṛ* replaces *laṭ*; [the addition of] *śap*;
[and the application of] *guṇa* and *ayādeśa*.
Because it is taught as having an initial vowel (adupadeśa), when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the accent falls on the *ṇic* affix. [Thus we have] *āpuḥ*.
[The root is] *āplu* in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*).
In the case of the *liṭ* [perfect] suffix *usi*, there is reduplication and the application of the *halādi-śeṣa* rule.
Then, by the rule *ata ādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.70), the substitution of *ā* for the initial vowel occurs.

Here, because the word *āpuḥ* is connected with "not with *saha*" (*na sahaḥ*) and "not with anger" (*na manyum*), and because it stands first in relation to those, the first *tiṅ* inflection is not elided according to the rule *cādilope vibhāṣā*.
Moving along;
[the form] *vā chandasi* [applies], resulting in the long vowel of the same quality as the preceding (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*). They split open.
The root *mī* is used in the sense of "injury.
By the rule *śryādibhyaḥ kṣāḥ*, the suffix *kṣa* is applied.
Then, by the rule *bhābhyastyorātaḥ*, there is the elision of the vowel *ā*.
The shortening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule *mīnāter nigame* (Pāṇini 7.3.81). The accent belongs to the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
By the rule *tiṅi codāttavati* (Pāṇini 8.1.71), the prefix (*gati*) is unaccented (*anudātta*).
The absence of elision occurs due to its connection with the preceding metrical foot.
1. "May we become [like] ḍha. 2. "They are unable to fight with ḍha.
Varuṇa, the king of the forest, whose will is pure, bestows a lofty pillar upon the waters;
their bases lie below, while their banners are fixed within us.

The King Varuṇa, of purified skill, bestows upon the forest its lofty summit. Their branches stand directed downwards, while their base is above. May their radiant rays be deposited within us—so may it be! 7.

Varuṇa, whose will is pure and whose strength is cleansed, standing in the unfathomable and rootless mid-air, holds aloft—in the upper region—the *stūpa*, that is, the assembly (*saṃgha*) of the desirable splendor of the forest. "They stand directed downwards":
here, it should be supplied that these are the rays of Varuṇa who abides in the upper region.
For they stand with their faces turned downwards.
The "bottom" (budhna) or root of these rays stands above—this is the remainder [of the sense].
That being so, the "comets" (ketavaḥ)—that is, the indicators or vital breaths (prāṇāḥ)—are within us (asme).
The word *udāttaḥ* is accented. By the rule "hi ca," there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of accent). The word *panthām*.
In the word *pathimadhyukṣamāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.85), the substitution of *ā* occurs even for the second case ending by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).

Although the word *pathin-* would normally be oxytone because it ends in the suffix prescribed by *patestha ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 4.452), it instead becomes ādyudātta (accented on the first syllable) by the rule *pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne* (Pāṇini 6.1.199).
[The form] *anvetavai*.
From the root *eti* preceded by *anu-pūrva*, the suffix *tavai* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule *tum-arthe seseṇ*.
By the rule *tavai cāntaś ca yugapat* (Pāṇini 6.2.51), both the initial and the final syllables are acute (*udātta*).
[The word is] *pādā*.
The substitution of the vowel *ā* is according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
[The form] *pratighātave* is derived from the root *dhā* with the suffix *taven*, by means of the very sūtra *tum-arthe*.

By the rule *tādau ca niti* (Pāṇini 6.2.50), the root-vowel accent (*prakṛtisvara*) applies to the prefix *ati*. [The form] *akaḥ* is derived from the root *kṛ*; by the rule *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*, the aorist (*luṅ*) is used in the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*).
The suffix *tip* is applied to that [root].
By the rule *mantre ghasa* (Pāṇini 2.4.80), there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *cli*; there is *guṇa* substitution, and the replacement of *r* as the subsequent element (*raparatva*).
By the rule *halḍyābbhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), there is the elision of the suffix *tip*;
the augment *aṭ* is added;
[the result is] *hṛdayāvidhaḥ*.
The root *han* means "to strike.
By the rule *vṛhoḥ pugduko ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.540), the suffix *kya* is applied. The root *vyadh* means "to strike."
In *kip*,
the lengthening of the first member of the compound is according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.3.116 (*nahitṛpti* etc.),
and the accentuation follows the rule for the original accent of the final member when it ends in a *kṛt* suffix.
A hundred physicians are yours, O King, a thousand; let your benevolence be vast and deep.
Drive Nirṛti far away into the distance; release us from whatever sin we have committed.
A hundred are your physicians, O King, a thousand; may your benevolence be wide and deep. Drive far away misfortune to a distance, and release us from even the sin we have committed. 9.
O King Varuṇa, you have a hundred physicians—either a hundred medicines that ward off bondage or a hundred learned healers.

May your benevolent mind, which is inclined toward favoring us, be vast, profound, endowed with depth, and steadfast. Having turned Nirṛti—the goddess of evil who brings us misfortune—away from us, having placed her far away in a distant region, do you drive her away.
Whatever sin (*enaḥ*) has been committed by us, even though it was performed, release us from it—completely release it, that is, cause it to be destroyed.

In *sumatiḥ*, although the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member would have applied by the rule *tādau ca*, the final syllable of the second member is acute by the rule *man-uk-kinaḥ* and so forth.
In the *saṃhitā*, the *s* replaces the *visarjanīya* of *su-* by the rule *yuṣmattattathuḥdhvantaḥpādam* (Pāṇini 8.3.103).
*bādhasva* [is used]; [the root] *bādh* means "to agitate. Due to the *pit* designation of the suffix *śap*, there is an udātta accent on the final syllable.
And here, by the accent of the suffix *t* (which is part of the *avadhātuka*), the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) alone remains.
In *nirṛtim*,
because of the rule “*tādau ca*,” the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) of the prefix *niḥ* is preserved.
*Mumugdhi*. [The root] *muc* [is used] in the sense of "releasing.
The *ślu* [substitution] occurs by the rule "In the Vedic language, [the suffixes are applied] diversely."
By the rule *huśśalyo hedhiḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.101), the substitute *hedhi* takes the place of *hi*.
Because this [substitute] is treated as having an indicatory letter *ṅ*, there is an absence of *guṇa* [vowel strengthening].
Furthermore, by the rule *coḥ kuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.30), the change to a guttural (*kutva*) occurs.
These stars that were placed on high are seen at night; where indeed has their brilliance departed?
Unfailing are the ordinances of Varuṇa; the moon moves through the night, shining brightly.
These stars, set on high, are seen by night; where have they gone by day? The laws of Varuṇa are inviolable; the moon moves through the night, looking out upon all. 10.
1. A hundred physicians, a thousand warders of disease, numbering in the hundreds of thousands; a hundred physicians, a thousand warders of bondage, numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
2. The ḍha-maker (the female demon).
These *rakṣas* who were seen by us last night, together with the seers (*ṛṣis*).
And thus the Vājasaneyins record: "In ancient times, they used to call the constellations by the name 'Rakṣas'. Or alternatively, *rakṣas* refers to all the specific types of stars.
As Yāska has stated [in Nirukta 3.20], "‘rakṣaḥ stubhiḥ’ refers to the stars. Those who are "high," that is, placed aloft in the bright region, are seen by all at night;
but during the day, they go somewhere—where indeed they may go.
The meaning is that they are not seen.
The *vrata*—the ritual acts such as the observation of the stars and so forth—of King Varuṇa are *adṛbdha*, unimpeded by anyone.
Furthermore, by the very command of Varuṇa, the moon (*candramas*) goes at night (*naktam*), shining intensely (*vicākaśat*).

Regarding *nihitāsaḥ*: by [the rule] *ājjaserasuk*, the suffix *asun* is added. Thus, although the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) would normally be udātta by the rule *ādyaudāttam* (Pāṇini 6.2.144), the preceding prefix (*gati*) retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) by the rule *gatiranantaraḥ* (Pāṇini 6.2.49).
It was seen (*dadṛśe*). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*) of the root *dṛś*, there is the substitution of *re* [for the suffix] according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.76 (*iryo re*).
By means of transposition (*vyatyaya*), there is the acute accent on the first syllable.
Because of its metrical position, there is no *nighāta* (absence of accentuation).
In the word *kuha*, the substitution of *ha* for the suffix *tral* following the word *kim* occurs by the rule *vā ha ca chandasi* (Pāṇini 5.3.13).
By the rule *ku tihoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.104), the word *kim* undergoes the substitution *ku*.
Due to the status of the original element (*sthānivadbhāva*), it is acute-accented on the first syllable by the accent of the *liṭ* suffix.
[The form is] *vicākaśata*.
From the root *kas*, meaning "to shine," in its *yaṅ*-lopped (*yaṅ-luk*) form, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied.
By the rule “*abhyastānām ādiḥ*,” the first syllable is udātta.
In the compound, the accent is determined by the rule for kṛt-derivatives (*kṛtsvara*).
Alternatively, [the word] *candramas* is derived from the root *kāś*, with the vowel in the penultimate syllable shortened by way of metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*). *Candramāḥ*.
The suffix *asi* is applied by the rule *‘candre māḍo ḍit’* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.667).

Although the original accentuation of the final member (*uttarapada*) would have been expected according to the rule for *kṛt*-formed compounds, the accent of the first member (*pūrvapada*) prevails because the word belongs to the *dāsībhāra* group.
For the omentum and the cake of the animal sacrifice dedicated to Varuṇa belonging to the Ekādaśinī, there are two verses beginning with “taccā yāmi” as the invitatory and offering verses (*yājyā*).

This is stated in the Sūtra: “‘taccā yāmi’ and ‘brahmaṇā vandamānaḥ’—these two [are used] for the [sacrifice] not performed on the full moon day” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7). Among the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, this verse “taccā yāmi” is the offering verse for the oblation to Varuṇa; it is prescribed in the Sūtra for the fifth full-moon day: “‘imaṃ me varuṇa śrudhi’ and ‘taccā yāmi brahmaṇā vandamānaḥ’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.17).
I approach that [divinity] with prayer, offering homage; then the sacrificer prays for blessings with oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not cut short our life-span.
That I implore of you, worshipping with a sacred prayer; that the sacrificer seeks from you with oblations. O Varuṇa, be gracious here; O thou of wide renown, do not cut short our span of life. 11.
O Varuṇa, I, desiring to die well, entreat that life-span from you. Of what sort am I?
Praising—that is, extolling—you with a mature hymn of praise (*brahman*).
In every case, the sacrificer also prays for that life with oblations.

And you, being "aheḷamānaḥ" (not showing disregard) toward this ritual act, "bodhi"—be aware of what we require. O "uruśaṃsa" (one praised by many), do not "pra mauṣīḥ" our "āyuḥ" (life); do not cause it to be stolen away.
In the ritual acts of begging that occur in equal numbers, the phrase "īmahe yāmi" (Nirukta 3.19.1) is recited;
the elision of the letter 'ca' is a Vedic archaism.

*aheḷamānaḥ*. [The root *hī*] is used in the sense of "disregard. Since it is taught with a short *a* as its upadeśa (original form), the *lasārvadhātuka* suffix is unaccented; furthermore, because the suffix *śa* is *pit*, it is also unaccented, and thus the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
Therefore, in this negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member, which is an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
*Bodhi*:
from the root *budh* in the sense of "understanding" (*avagamana*).
By the rule *loṭaḥ ser hiḥ*, the suffix *si* of the imperative is replaced by *hi*.
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is elision (*luk*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*).

Because of the rule *vā chandasi* (Pāṇini 3.4.88), since it is not marked with *p* (apit), it lacks the status of being marked with *ṭ* (ḍittva); consequently, the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) takes place.
By the rule "huśśalabhyo hadhiḥ," the substitute *dhi* is applied for *hi*;
the elision of the final letter of the root is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
[Thus,] *mauṣīḥ*.

In the root *muṣ* meaning "to steal," the *luṅ* suffix is used in the sense of the *lāṭ* (past tense). Although the rule *vadavraja* (Pāṇini 7.2.3) would have required *vṛddhi*, this is prohibited by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), and thus the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) applies.
The absence of the augment *aṭ* is due to the rule: "In the Vedic language, *aṭ* is generally absent even when used in conjunction with *mā*."

They say that he is like one who has been divided, and they say he is like one who is near to me; he whom the heart perceives through its sign—that King Varuṇa, seized by whom Śunaḥśepa cried out, may he release us.
That indeed they say to me by night, that indeed by day; that this thought from my heart proclaims: "May King Varuṇa release us—[us] whom Śunaḥśepa, while seized, has praised. 12.
That very hymn pertaining to Varuṇa, they—the experts—declare to me, Śunaḥśepa, as that which is to be performed at night;
likewise, they declare that same one by day as well.
This specific insight (*keta*), produced from my heart—that is, from my mind—also proclaims that very same thing as the duty to be performed, illuminating it clearly and in every respect.
Seized, captured, and bound to the sacrificial post—Śunaḥśepa, a person by that name, who has invoked Varuṇa; may that King Varuṇa release us Śunaḥśepas from our bonds; may he set us free.
For me;
by the rule "ḍayi ca," there is the acute accent (udātta) on the first syllable. They say.
By the rule *‘bhuvaḥ pañcānām’* (Pāṇini 3.4.84), when the suffix *laṭ* follows the root *brū*, there is the substitution of *us* for *jhi* and the substitution of *āha* for the root.
[The form is] *hṛdaḥ*. By the rule beginning with *‘paddan’* (Pāṇini 6.1.63), there is the substitution of *hṛd* for the word *hṛdaya*.
In the word *aḍitpadādi*, the fifth case ending (*pañcamī*) is acute-accented. Regarding *śunaḥśepaḥ*:

in the compound meaning "one whose tail (*śepa*) is like that of a dog (*śunaḥ*)," the elision of the genitive case ending (*aluk*) is applied by the rule *śunaḥ śepa-chalāṅguleṣu saṃjñāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyā aluk vaktavyaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.21.4).

When the rule for the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member would have applied, the rule *ubhe vanaspatyādipu* (Pāṇini 6.2.140) prescribes that both the first and the second members simultaneously retain their original accents.
[The form] *ahat*: in the *luṅ* tense, by the rule *lipisicihvaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.53), there is the substitution of *ah* for the *cli* affix.
The elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by Pāṇini’s rule 6.4.64, *āto lopa iṭi ca*. The augment *aṭ* is acute (*udātta*).
Due to its connection with the particle *yad*, it does not undergo elision of accent (*anighāta*).
Seized.
By the rule "hṛ-maho-bhaiḥ," there is the substitution of *bha*.
He [protects] us.
The absence of sandhi (prakṛtibhāva) is due to the rule "prakṛtyantaḥpādam.
[In the form] mumoktu,
the substitution of *bh* for the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*) occurs by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi."
Śunaḥśepa, seized by Yama and bound to three wooden posts for the Āditya, may King Varuṇa release him from his enmity; may the wise, undeceived one loosen his bonds.
Śunaḥśepa has indeed been struck down; seized and bound upon three wooden posts, may King Varuṇa release him. May he, the wise and undeceived one, loosen his bonds. 13.

Seized—that is, captured for the sake of binding—and bound upon the three-fold *drupada* (wooden posts), specifically at the particular places of the *drupada*, which is a wooden sacrificial post (*yūpa*), Śunaḥśepa called upon Aditi’s son, Varuṇa. Because he did so, may King Varuṇa release him—Śunaḥśepa—from his bonds; that is, let him set him free and release him from captivity. The manner of this release is made explicit: [Varuṇa] is "the wise one," meaning he is one who knows the means and methods of liberation.
Unharmed by anyone, unassailed, may Varuṇa loosen his snares—those specific binding cords—and having severed them, set him free.
In the word *triṣu*, the acute accent on the case-ending is according to Pāṇini’s rule 6.1.179: *paṭtritricaturbhyo halādiḥ*.
In the *Saṃhitā*, according to the rule “*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*,” the following vowel *ā* is marked with the *svarita* accent.
[The form] would be *sasṛjyāt*. [The root] *sṛj* means "to emit."
The suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of a prayer (*prārthanā*). By the rule "in the Veda [it is] manifoldly," there is the elision (*luk*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*). [The form is] *vidvān*.

1. From the absence of the letter *ḍha*. 2. In the three [consonants], namely *ta*, *śa*, and *ṣa-ha*, which are numbered as three. 3. There is no *śa*, *ha*, or *yam*. 4. Free from the hypocrisy (*dambha*) of *ḍha*.
[Regarding the root] *vid* in the sense of "knowing": by the rule *videḥ śatur vasuḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.36).

The suffix *tum* is applied by the rule *ugidacām*. There is the elision of the final consonant of the *hal*-beginning [suffix] and the elision of the final member of the conjunction (*saṃyogāntalopa*).
In the *saṃhitā*, the *n* is shortened by the rule *dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*.
By the rule "āto 'ṭi nityam," the vowel *ā* is nasalized; thus, *adagdhaḥ*. [The root] *dambh* is used in the sense of "injuring."
In the case of the gerundive suffix (*niṣṭhā*), after the elision of *n* by the rule "aniditām" (Pāṇini 6.4.24), the substitution of *dh* occurs by the rule "jhapastathordhodhaḥ" (Pāṇini 8.2.40).
The accentuation follows that of the original form of the first member, as it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
For the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath), the two verses beginning with "ava te heḷaḥ" are the invitatory and offering verses (*yājyānuvākye*) for the oblation to Varuṇa.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "Having performed the *patnīsaṃyājas*" in the Sūtra: "'ava te heḷo varuṇa namobhiḥ'—these two" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 6.13).
We seek your favor, O Varuṇa, with prostrations; we seek it with sacrifices and oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you dwell among us, loosen the bonds of the sins we have committed.

Release us from thy wrath, O Varuṇa, through our prostrations; we entreat thee with sacrifices and oblations. O wise Asura, O King, as thou dwellest among us, loosen for us the bonds of the sins we have committed. 14.

O Varuṇa, we appease your wrath with salutations—that is, with prostrations. Likewise, we appease it with sacrifices, through the performance of all constituent parts, and with worshipful oblations; O Varuṇa, having satisfied you, we remove your anger. O Asura—one whose nature is to cast away what is undesirable—O Pracetāḥ, endowed with supreme wisdom, O shining King Varuṇa, dwelling (*kṣayan*) within this ritual for our sake, loosen (*śiśrathaḥ*) the sins (*enāṃsi*) committed by us; make them slackened and weakened. Regarding the words: *heḷaḥ*: the initial vowel is acute due to the rule *asuno niśvādādyudāttatvam*. *Yajñaiḥ*: the substitution of *ais* occurs according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. *Īmahe*: from the root *īṅ gatau*; there is elision of the *vikaraṇa*. *Kṣayan*: from the root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*; the suffix *śatṛ* is used for the present tense (*laṭ*), and *śap* is applied by irregular extension (*vyatyaya*). It has the acute accent on the first syllable because it is a vocative (*āmantrita*). *Asura*: derived from *as* with the suffix *an* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.42). It is subject to the suppression of the vocative accent (*āmantritanighāta*). *Śiśrathaḥ*: from the root *śratha daurbalye*, belonging to the *curādi* class and ending in *ad*. In the Vedic *luṅ* (aorist), *caṅ* is substituted for *cli* by the rule *ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ*. There is reduplication and the elision of the remaining consonant (*halādi-śeṣaḥ*). Because the root is *aglopi* (having an elided penultimate vowel), the rule for *sanvadbhāva* does not apply; however, by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the vowel of the reduplicated syllable is shortened. As before, there is no *aṭ* augment.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, being sinless under your law, may we belong to Aditi.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, loosen the lowest, and release the middle one. Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless in your service and before Aditi. 15.
O Varuṇa, loosen—that is, draw off and slacken—the highest, most excellent noose bound upon our head;
loosen—that is, draw down and slacken—the lowest, meanest noose situated at our foot;
and loosen—that is, unfasten and slacken—the middle noose located in the region of our navel.
Then immediately after, O Āditya, for Aditi—[1.
endowed with knowledge (ḍha); 2. loosen (ḍha); 3. having disregarded (ca-cha-pha-śa-ṣa-śa); 4.
loosen (ḍha)]—O son Varuṇa, may we, the Śunaḥśepas, in your service (*vrate*), that is, in your ritual act, be free from injury (*aditaye*) and sinless (*anāgasaḥ*), being devoid of transgression.
*Uttama* [is derived from *ut* + *tama*].

Then, since it would otherwise be *ādyudātta* due to the *anudātta* status of the prefix *anu*, the rule "and *uttama* [is *antodātta*] when followed by *uttama*" (Pāṇini 6.1.160, Gaṇapāṭha) provides for its final syllable to be *udātta* because it is listed among the *uñchādi* group. *Adhama*.
According to the Uṇādi Sūtra 5.732, *avacāvamādhamāvarephāḥ kutsite*, the suffix *amac* is added to the root *ava*; the *v* of this [suffix] becomes *dh*.
Thus, *śrathāya*. The root *śrath* means "weakness."
In the *saṃhitā*, there is a Vedic lengthening. [The form] *tava* has its acute accent on the first syllable by the rule: “*yuṣmadasmador ṅasi*” [Pāṇini 6.1.211].
[The word] *anāgasaḥ* [is derived as follows]:

in a bahuvrīhi compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*) applies; however, the rule “*nañ-subhyām*” [which would normally require udātta on the second member] is set aside by this exception.
Alternatively,
from the word *āgas*, the suffix *vini* is added in the sense of possession according to Pāṇini 5.2.121 (*asmāyāmedhās*).
Its elision occurs by Pāṇini 5.3.65 (*vinmatorluk*).
In a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member, which is an indeclinable (*avyaya*), is retained.
The second hymn consists of twenty-one verses beginning with “yaccit.
Thus it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: “yaccitta saikā.
According to the technical rule “ṛṣiḥ śrāmyasmāt,” Śunaḥśepa himself is the seer (ṛṣi).
The meter is *gāyatrī*, because it has been defined [in the Paribhāṣā] as "the first is *gāyatra*.
The deity is Varuṇa, because it was previously stated as "but that which belongs to Varuṇa" (*vāruṇaṃ tu*), according to the definition beginning with *tuha* (Anuvāka 12.3).
The application (*viniyoga*) has been stated in the narrative of Śunaḥśepa.
As for its specific application: in the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*, this hymn is to be inserted (*āvāpa*) as the motive for the *stoma* in the *hotraka-śastra*.

This is precisely how it is prescribed in the section titled "The Days of the *Abhiplava* and *Pṛṣṭhya*": "The Maitrāvaruṇa should insert the triplet beginning with 'yacciddhi te viśa' as the verse dedicated to Varuṇa" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.5).
For whatever transgression of yours we may commit day by day, O God Varuṇa, like subjects [against their lord], according to your law.
For whatever transgression we may commit against your law day after day, O divine Varuṇa, as subjects do—whatever it may be.

O Varuṇa, just as in this world the subjects (viśaḥ), that is, the people, sometimes commit negligence, so too have we—whatever vow or ritual act (vrata) belonging to you we may have daily violated through negligence—that very vow, [please] make complete with all its parts by avoiding such negligence; this is the implied sense.
For example: when the initial udātta accent would otherwise apply by virtue of being a *lisatva* [word], there is instead total anudātta according to the rule *ayatheti pādānte* (Phiṭ Sūtra 85),
as in *minīmasi*.
The root *mīñ* is used in the sense of "injury. [The suffix] *masi* ends in *i*.
[The suffix] *śra* is applied after words such as *ṛc*.
The shortening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule *mīnāternigame* (Pāṇini 7.3.81).
The substitution of the vowel *ī* occurs by the rule *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.113).

According to the maxim *satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvamanyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ* ("the accent of that which remains after all other operations has greater force, except in the case of verbal suffixes"), the accent of the personal ending (*tiṅ*) alone is retained.
Because of its connection with the word *yad*, there is an absence of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent.
Do not deliver us to the blow of the one who is angry,
nor to the wrath of the one who is enraged.
Do not deliver us to slaughter, to be slain; do not yield us to the wrath of one who is provoked, nor to the fury of one who is enraged. 2.

O Varuṇa, do not deliver us over to the slaughter—that is, to the death caused by you—of one who has shown contempt and is thus worthy of being slain; do not make us objects for his destruction. Do not deliver us over to your wrath, that is, to the anger of you who are being provoked and are filled with rage.
[This is for the sake of] slaughter.

By the rule *hanaśca vadhaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.3.76), the word *vadha* is formed with the suffix *ac*. Because it is listed among the *uñchādi* group, it is accented on the final syllable (*antodātta*). [The form is] *hantave*.
The root *han* means "to injure" and "to go.
By the rule *grahajṛbhyāṃ knuḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.310), the suffix *knu* is applied; the *n* of the verbal root is changed to *t*. [This refers to the form] *jihīḷānasya*.

*Heṭ*: [This is] from the root *hiḍ*, meaning "to destroy evil" (*pāpahananaśīla*) or "in disregard. From this, the suffix *kānac* is applied after the perfect tense (*liṭ*). There is reduplication, the retention of the initial consonant (*halādiśeṣa*), and the substitution of *vatv* and *vajv*. The change of the vowel *e* to *ī* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). By the rule "the final of *cit*" (*citaḥ*), there is the substitution of *t* for the final letter. Thus: *rirathaḥ*. *Rādha*: [From the root] *rādha* or *sādha*, meaning "to accomplish" (*saṃsiddhi*). With the causative suffix *caṅ*, there is the elision of *ṇi*, the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhāsvatva*), reduplication, the retention of the initial consonant (*halādiśeṣa*), the treatment as *sanvadbhāva*, and the lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsadīrgha*). By the rule "not before *mā*, *ru*, *ge*", there is the absence of the augment *aṭ*. Thus: *raṇānasya*. *Haṇānasya*: [From the root] *haṇīṅ*, meaning "shame" (*lajjā*). From this, with the suffix *śānac*, the desired form is established by virtue of belonging to the *pṛṣodarādi* class.
O Varuṇa, we entreat your mind with our hymns for the sake of your favor, as one might loosen a tethered horse.
O Varuṇa, for the sake of your favor, we grasp your mind with our songs, as a charioteer holds a harnessed horse. 3.

O Varuṇa, with our songs—our hymns of praise—we fasten, that is to say, we especially bind and propitiate *your mind* for the sake of mercy and for our own happiness. Therein lies an illustration: like a charioteer (*rathīḥ*), the master of a chariot, [propitiates] a horse that is *sanditam*, meaning thoroughly broken down and exhausted by traveling a long distance; just as a master propitiates an exhausted horse by providing fodder and the like, so do we. Regarding *rathīḥ*: the suffix *ī* has the sense of possession (*mattvarthīya*). Regarding *sanditam*: from the root *do* in the sense of "cutting" (*avakhaṇḍane*), the suffix *kta* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.2.102 (*niṣṭhā*). By Pāṇini 7.4.40 (*yatisyatimāsthām*), there is the substitution of the vowel *i*. By Pāṇini 6.2.49 (*gatiranantaraḥ*), the preceding prefix retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). Regarding *gīrbhiḥ*: the acute accent on the *bh* of *bhis* is due to Pāṇini 6.1.168 (*sāvekācaḥ*). Regarding *sīmaha*: from the root *ṣivu* in the sense of "weaving" (*tantusantāne*), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by irregularity (*vyatyaya*). The suffix *vikaraṇa* is elided by Pāṇini 2.4.73 (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). The *v* is elided by Pāṇini 6.1.66 (*vali lopaḥ*). Alternatively, it is derived from the root *piṣ* in the sense of "binding," with the suffix elided and the lengthening of the vowel being Vedic.
For my arrows, free from anger, fly forth to seek what is better,
like birds returning to their nests.
For my [sacrificial offerings], free from anger, fly forth toward greater wealth, like birds returning to their nests. ||4||

O Varuṇa, may my thoughts—those of Śunaḥśepa—be free from anger; for the sake of attaining a more excellent life, one that is exceedingly wealthy (*vasīyasaḥ*), they fly away, turning their backs and proceeding without returning.
The word *hi* expresses the universal renown of this fact.
There is an illustration regarding this flight away.
It is not so; just as birds reach their *avasatīs*, that is, their dwelling places, by approaching them closely, so it is in this case.
They fall;
there is no *nighāta* (elision of the accent) because it begins with a foot (*pāda*).
For the sake of his desire (*vasyaiṣṭaye*).

From the word *vasumat*, following the rule *vinmator luk* (Pāṇini 5.3.65), there is elision of the suffix *matup*; then, after the elision of the *ṭi* portion (*u*), the elision of the letter *y* of the suffix *īyasun* occurs by Vedic license. Thus we have *vasatīḥ*.
[In this formation], the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied according to the rule *śataranumaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.7), and it bears the udātta accent.
When, O Varuṇa, will you bestow upon us the glory of sovereignty, for the sake of mercy, that which is radiant to behold?
When shall I bring the manly Varuṇa, whose wide gaze beholds all, hither for the sake of his grace, so that he may bestow the glory of sovereignty?

"O Varuṇa, for our mercy—that is, for our happiness—at what time (*kadā*), at which moment (*kasmin kāle*) in this rite, shall we cause you to come? Of what sort [are you]? A leader (*naraṃ*) who possesses the glory of sovereignty (*kṣatraśriyaṃ*), who is devoted to strength, and who is far-sighted (*urucakṣasaṃ*), a beholder of many. Regarding *kṣatraśriyam*: he who rests upon (*śrayati*) sovereignties (*kṣatrāṇi*) is *kṣatraśrīḥ*. By the rule *kvibvacipracchi...* (Pāṇini 3.2.178), the suffix *kvip* is applied and the vowel is lengthened; the accentuation follows the rule for the original form of the second member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). Regarding *naram*: by the rule *ṛdorap*, it ends in *ap* and is accented on the first syllable. Regarding *karāhe*: from the root *kṛ*, the suffix *śap* is applied by irregular transposition (*vyatyaya*). Regarding *urucakṣasam*: by the rule *cakṣerbahulaṃ śinac* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.672), the suffix *asun* is applied; because of the presence of the *śit*-marker, there is no substitution of *sy* for *s*. ||5||"
1. That which is approved by Ḍha; 2. that which is served by Bala.

These two, longing for it, have attained it together; they do not neglect the donor who maintains his vows. 6. Only those two have attained the same [state]; longing, they do not neglect the donor who maintains his vows. 6.

To the one who maintains his vows, who has performed the ritual acts, and who is a donor having offered the oblation— the sacrificer— Mitra and Varuṇa, who are longing for him (the word *venantau* being understood),
both of them partake of that very same common oblation given by us;
they never neglect it, nor do they ever show negligence.
They two reached [it]. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) of the root *aś*, there is reduplication and the application of the *halādi-śeṣa* rule;
then, by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.70, *ata ādeḥ*, the initial vowel is lengthened to *ā*.
Because of the statement, "the final [form] is *āgamanaśāsana*," there is the insertion of the augment *nuṭ* by the rule *aśnoteśca* (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.4.72).
*Venantā*:
the root *venati* signifies the act of desiring.
The vowel *ā* [in *prayucchataḥ*] is substituted according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*. [The root] *yuccha* means "to neglect" (*pramāda*).

Regarding *dāśuṣe*: from the root *dāś* in the sense of "giving," by the rule *dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini 7.1.67), the suffix *nu* is added; then, by the rule *acaḥ kartṛyaki* (Pāṇini 6.1.195), the first syllable is udātta.
By the rule *tiṅi codāttavati* (Pāṇini 8.1.71), there is the elision of accent (*nighāta*) for the prefix;
nor does the elision apply by the rule *tiṅatiṅaḥ*, because of the prohibition in the rule *yadvṛttānnityam*.
He knows the path of the wind that moves with wide-sounding breath;
he knows those who dwell upon it.
I know the path of the wind; I know those who sit upon the wide, lofty, and great [vault of heaven]. 9.
Varuṇa knows the path, the course of the wind—vast, expansive, lofty, beautiful to behold, great, and preeminent in its qualities;
he also knows those gods who dwell above, who stand over it.
Regarding *vātasya*: by the rule beginning with *asihasi*, the word *vāta* ending in the suffix *tan* is acute-accented on the first syllable because it is *nita*.
[The word is] *vartinam*.
"By means of this it proceeds," thus [it is called] *vartinī*, meaning "in the hymn" (*stotre*).

(Pāṇini 6.1.160) May that Āditya, the one of excellent wisdom, make for us all days a good path; may he prolong our lifespans. || 12 || He; for us; all days; of excellent wisdom; Āditya; by a good path; may he make; may he; for us; lifespans; prolong. || 12 ||
May that Varuṇa, the Āditya of excellent wisdom and beautiful insight, who brings all things at all times, lead us along the auspicious path;
and furthermore, may he cause our lifespans to increase. [Along] the auspicious path.

Regarding the rule *svatī pūjāyām* (Pāṇini Mañjarī 2.2.18.4), in the compound [svatī-pūjita], there is a prohibition of the compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*) by the rule *na pūjanāt* (Pāṇini Sūtra 5.4.69).

When the original accent of the first member (*prakṛtisvara*) of the indeclinable (*avyaya*) would otherwise apply, the initial vowel of the second member becomes udātta according to the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*.
The rule *ṛvādayaśca* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.2.118) does not apply here because it is not a *bahuvrīhi* compound.
For that [accent] is prescribed for a *bahuvrīhi* compound.

Furthermore, the rule “in the Veda, a word with two syllables has its first syllable acute” (*ādyudāttaṃ dvya-cchandasī*, Pāṇini 6.2.119) does not apply here either, because the word *pathin* has its final syllable acute.
[Thus, the form is] *karat*.
From the root *kṛ*, in the *leṭ* mood, the suffix *śap* is applied by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
When *śap* is elided, the augment *aṭ* is added according to the rule "in *leṭ*, there are *aṭ* and *āṭ*. Then, the vowel *i* is elided according to the rule "there is also the elision of *ha*."
Alternatively, in the Vedic *luṅ* tense, by the rule *kamudruhisabhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.59), there is the substitution of *aṅ* for *cli*; then,
by the rule *ṛtaśchoṅi guṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.16), the *guṇa* substitution [of *o* for *ṛ*] occurs.
In the phrase *pra naḥ*, there is an absence of the augment *aṭ* because of the rule *bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge ’pi*. Furthermore,
the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* in *naḥ* occurs according to the rule *upasargād dhasvam* (Pāṇini 8.4.28).
*tāriṣat*. [This is derived] from the root *tṛ* (to cross) in the *leṭ* mood; there is the augment *aṭ*, and the suffix *sip* is applied according to the rule:
*siv bahulaṃ leṭi*.
The substitution of *p* occurs by the rule "ādeśapratyayayoḥ."

Wearing a golden mantle, Varuṇa has clothed himself in a radiant garment; his spies have settled all around him. 13. Wearing, a mantle, golden, Varuṇa, has clothed, a radiant garment; around, the spies, have settled. 13.
Bearing a golden, gold-made breastplate (*vdrāpi*), Varuṇa puts on a bright garment (*nirṇija*) to clothe his well-nourished body.
His spies—the rays that touch gold—have settled all around, pervading everywhere.
In *bibhrat* and *bibharthaḥ*, there is an absence of the *num* augment due to Pāṇini 7.1.78, *nābhyastācchatuḥ*.
Furthermore, the first syllable is acute-accented (*ādyudātta*) according to Pāṇini 6.1.189, *abhyastānām ādiḥ*.
*Drāpi*: from the root *drā*, meaning "to go in a contemptible manner. That which causes enemies to attain a contemptible state is *drāpi*; thus, it refers to armor (*kavaca*).
The augment *pu* is added by the rule *arti-hrī-* (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.3.36) and others;
with the *i*-affix of the *uṇādi* class, there is the elision of the *ṇi*. [Thus: *hiraṇyayam*.

In the rule *ṛtyavāstavyavāstavādhvīhiraṇyayāni chandasi* (Pāṇini 6.4.175), the elision of the letter *m* from the suffix *mayaṭ*—which is prescribed after the word *hiraṇya* in the sense of a derivative—is specifically enjoined. [The word] *vasta*: [from the root] *vasa* in the sense of “covering.”
In the *laṅ* [tense], there is elision of *śap* due to its belonging to the *adādi* class;
as before, there is the absence of *aṭ*. [The form is] *nirṇijam*.
The root *gij* is used in the sense of purification (*śauca*) and nourishment (*poṣaṇa*).
*Sparśaḥ*. The root *spṛś* is used in the sense of harming (*bādhanā*) and touching (*sparśana*).
The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "kvip ca.
They split apart (*ni bhedire*).
[The root] *paṭh* is used in the senses of "falling apart," "going," and "fading away."
From this root meaning "to go," in the periphrastic perfect (liṭ) used in the passive sense, there is the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplication;
by the rule "sadiprateḥ," there is the substitution of *p* for *s*.

Neither those who wish to harm, nor the injurious among men, nor those with hostile intentions can deceive that god. 14. Neither those who wish to harm, nor the injurious among men, nor those with hostile intentions can deceive that god. 14.
1. In the manuscripts ca, pha, and sa, there is an addition after the rule *uttarapadādyudāttatvam*: “Alternatively, there is the substitution of *āl* for the third case ending;

however, this is overridden by the accent of the original form (*prakṛtisvara*) when the preceding member is an indeclinable. In manuscript sa, there is further added: “Alternatively, the state of having the original form’s accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) is prohibited. 2. In the manuscripts ca, cha, jha, ta, na, pha, ṣa, ha, and śa, there is the reading: *śapo vā*.
3. Regarding the root *ḍha*, signifying contempt:

those enemies who desire to harm (*dipsavaḥ*), being afraid, do not wish to harm Varuṇa; they abandon their intent to injure him. Even those among living beings who harbor malice toward people do not bear malice against Varuṇa.
"Abhimāti" means "evil. For another Vedic text states: "Evil, indeed, is abhimāti" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.1.3.5). They do not touch that divine Varuṇa.
They desire to deceive.
The root *dambh* means "to deceive.
From this root, with the suffix *san*, the absence of the augment *iṭ* occurs by the rule *sanīvantardha-* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), etc.

In the rule *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), because the mention of *hal* refers to the class (*jāti*), and because the suffix *san* is *kit*, the vowel *a* following the letter *d* in the root *dambh* is changed to *i* by the rule *dambha icca* (Pāṇini 7.4.56).
There is elision of the nasal (*n*) by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24).
The absence of the substitution of *bha* for *bh* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
Here, by the rule *lopo 'bhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.58), there is elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*).

Due to the *pit*-nature of the suffix *śap*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*). And because the suffix *san* has the marker *ni*, it is acutely accented on its first syllable (*ādyudātta*) by the accent rule for *ni*-marked elements, which overrides the general accent of the *lasārvadhātuka* *tiṅ* suffixes.
For by virtue of which [quality] they are free from injury (*anighāta*).
[The word] *dipsavaḥ* [is derived as follows]: from the root *dambh* with the suffix *san*, the suffix *u* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.168, *sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ*.
The accent of the suffix:
*duhvānaḥ*.
[The root] *duh* is used in the sense of desiring to injure.

The suffix *kan* is applied [after roots] other than those [already mentioned], according to the rule "it is seen after others as well. Since the suffix is marked with *p*, it is anudātta; consequently, by the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*), the word is udātta on its first syllable.
And he who among men has established incomparable glory,
[placing] the sun within his belly.
And he who has established complete glory among men, let him establish it within our bellies. 15.
Moreover, that Varuṇa who has brought glory and food among men from all sides—that Varuṇa, while acting, has made it complete from all sides; he has not made it deficient.
Specifically, he has made it full within our bellies from every side.
Regarding the word *mānuṣa*: the suffix *añ* is applied according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 4.1.161, *manorjātāv añ yañ ca*,
and by the rule *ntyādinirnityam*, it bears the udātta accent on its first syllable.
He made [it].
The accent is that of the suffix.
It is not incomplete.
The original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member, being an indeclinable (*avyaya*), applies according to the rule *avyaye nakunipātānām* (Pāṇini 6.2.2–3).
[The word] *yaśas* [is derived] by the suffix *asun* according to the rule *aśoryud ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.630).
In the word *udareṣu*:
[the suffix] *al* is applied by the rule *udi hāterajalau pūrvapadāntyalopaśca* (Uṇādisūtra 5.697), and it bears the accent of the *liṭ* suffix.
By the rule *gatikārakopapadāt*, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member [of the compound] is maintained.
My thoughts go forth like cows to their pastures, seeking the one of far-reaching vision.
My thoughts go forth to him, like cows seeking pastures, yearning for the one who beholds from afar. 16.

My prayers—the thoughts of Śunaḥśepa—seeking Varuṇa, who is far-seeing and worthy to be beheld by many, go forth; they proceed away, turning their backs and lacking any return. In this regard, there is a simile: like cows.
Just as cows go toward pastures and cow-pens, so it is in that manner.

*gavyūtī*: [The word *gavyūtī* is derived as follows: because cows (*gāvaḥ*) are measured (*mīyante*) therein, the suffix *ktin* is applied in the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇe*). By the rule *goḥ pādānte chandasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.79.2), the substitution of *av* for *au* occurs.
The original accent of the first member [of the compound] applies because it belongs to the class beginning with *dāsībhāra*.
Alternatively,
*yūti* means "joining" (*yavana*).
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound *gavāṃ yavanam eti*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
[The form] *icchantīḥ* [is derived from] the root *iṣ* in the sense of "desiring."
The suffix *laṭ* [is replaced by] *śatṛ*.
From roots such as *tud*, the suffix *śa* [is applied].
By the rule *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.77), there is the substitution of *cha* for [the *ś* of *śa*].
Because it is taught as having an initial accent (adupadeśāt), when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes become unaccented, the accent of the *vikaraṇa* remains.
Let us two speak together again, since honey has been brought for me;
like a *hotṛ* priest, you shall consume what is dear.
Let us two speak again together, since the honey has been brought to me, like a Hotṛ-priest to consume the beloved [oblation]. 17.

Since, for the sake of my life, you have consumed the sweet oblation (havis) prepared for my ritual act, therefore, like a Hotṛ priest—the performer of the sacrifice—you yourself consume your own dear oblation.
Furthermore, after the acceptance of the oblation, being satisfied and alive, let us surely speak together; let us both join in pleasant conversation.
*vocāvahai*: In the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*), there is the *luṅ* (aorist) suffix due to Vedic usage; for the root *bhū*, there is the substitution of *vac*.
By the rule "asyativakti... etc., the *cli* suffix is replaced by *aṭ*.
In "vaca um," there is a *guṇa* [substitution] due to the augment *um*;
by transposition, the *ṭi* [portion] becomes *ai*.
Alternatively:
The region of Lūṭa itself is the country of Lūjā.
Because of the status of being a substitute (sthānivadbhāva), [the forms] *devam* and *ābhutam* [are derived].
'Haprahormeḥ. By the rule "gatiranantare," the preceding member (gati) retains its original accent (prakṛtisvara).
Behold him who is visible to all; behold his chariot upon the earth.
May he take pleasure in these my songs.
Behold now him who is worthy of being seen by all; behold his chariot upon the earth; may he take pleasure in these my songs. 18.

O Varuṇa, wise and intelligent one, visible to all and worthy of being beheld by everyone, you shine forth—you reign—within the midst of the entire universe, consisting of both heaven (the celestial world) and earth (the terrestrial world). As such, listen attentively to our prayer; grant us your assent to our command.
The meaning is: "Give me the reply, 'I shall protect [you].'"
*divaḥ*: the acute accent on the penultimate syllable is according to the rule beginning with *uḍidam*. *gamaḥ*.
The word *'gmā'* (Nirukta 1.1.2) is listed among the names for the earth (*bhūnāman*).

In the rule *'āto dhātoḥ'*, because of the division of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*) as *'ātaḥ'*, even though there would otherwise be a prohibition by the rule *'āto lopaḥ'*, the elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). The acute accent (*udāttatva*) of the case-ending is due to the accent of the disappearance of the acute [of the stem] (*udāttanivṛttisvara*).
*Yāvani*:
[derived from] the root *yā* in the sense of "to reach" (*prāpaṇe*),
with the suffix *manin* according to the rule *āto maninkvanipvanipaśca*.
The first syllable of *niḥ* is udātta.
*Śrudhi* has been explained.
Release us from the highest bond; loosen the middle one;
untie the lower ones so that we may live.
Loosen us from above; loosen the highest bond. Untie the middle bond and release the lowest so that we may live. 21.

"Unloose (*un mumugdhi*)—that is, having drawn out, release—the *uppermost* (*uttamam*) bond that has gone to our heads; *untie* (*vi cṛta*)—that is, having separated, destroy—the *middle* (*madhyamam*) bond that has gone to our bellies; and for the sake of living (*jīvase*), *untie* (*ava cṛta*)—having drawn down and destroyed—the *lower* (*adhamāni*) bonds that have gone to my feet. Regarding the word *uttamam*: it has an udātta accent on the final syllable because it is listed among the words beginning with *ucchādi*. *mumugdhi*: from the root *muc* in the sense of "releasing. By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," the suffix *śnu* is applied [instead of *śap*]; there is reduplication; the *halādiśeṣa* rule applies; and by "hujhalbhyo herdhiḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.101), the substitute *dhi* is applied for *hi*; the *nighāta* accent is applied by "tiṅatiṅaḥ. *cṛta*: from the root *cṛt* in the senses of "injury" and "tying. This is the imperative (*loṭ*) ending *hi*; the suffix *śa* is added by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ"; and the elision of *hi* occurs by "ato heḥ. *jīvase*: from the root *jīv* in the sense of "maintaining life. The suffix *ase* is applied by "tumarthe sesen," and it bears the accent of the suffix. || 19 ||
"Vasiṣva"—this is the third hymn, consisting of ten verses. Regarding this, it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "Vasiṣva; ten [verses]; Śreyaṃtu.
The seer (ṛṣi) is Śunaḥśepa.
The metre is Gāyatrī. This subsequent hymn and the following one are dedicated to Agni.
In the Prātaranuvāka, during the rite dedicated to Agni, these two initial hymns are to be recited when the metre is Gāyatrī.
And thus it is stated in the Sūtra: "With the hymn beginning 'Vasiṣva,' one should extract the last [verse]" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).
Clothe yourself indeed in garments, O worthy of sacrifice, Lord of Strength; perform this sacrifice of ours.
Clothe yourself in garments, O worthy of sacrifice, O Lord of nourishments; do thou [accept] this our rite and sacrifice.

Impelled by Varuṇa, Śunaḥśepa praised Agni with this pair of hymns beginning here. And it is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: "Varuṇa said to him, 'Agni is the mouth of the gods and their heart; praise him now, and then you shall have well-being. He praised Agni with the following twenty verses" (Ai. Br. 7.16).

O *miyedhya*, worthy of the sacrifice (*medha*), O Lord of nourishments (*ūrjām pate*), O Agni, protector of foods, "clothe yourself" (*vasiṣva*)—that is, cover yourself with "garments," meaning radiant splendors.
The meaning is: "Become one whose splendor blazes.
For since you are blazing, therefore, as such, "sacrifice"—that is, bring to completion—"this" "adhvara," our sacrifice.
"Vasiṣva" [is derived from] the root "vasa" in the sense of "covering. In the imperative (loṭ), "thās" is replaced by "se."
Regarding "savābhyāṃ vāmau":
because it is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix by the rule "chandasyubhayathā" (Pāṇini 3.4.117), the augment *iṭ* is applied according to "ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ" (Pāṇini 7.2.35).
Since the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
In the word *miyedhya*, the vowel lengthening occurs according to the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* in the *saṃhitā*; furthermore,
the insertion of *iy* between the letter *m* and the vowel *i* is a Vedic (*chāndasa*) anomaly.
"O Lord of Strength! (*ūrjāṃ pate*).

Because of the rule "the vocative is treated as a secondary member of the preceding word" (*subāmantrite*), the entire compound consisting of the genitive and the vocative receives the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent as a vocative.
[The phrase is] "him" (*semam*).
In this case, there is the elision of the suffix *su* according to the rule: "When *su* is elided, [the particle] *ca* is used to complete the meter. Thus, *su* is elided.
O Agni, most youthful one, you are the desirable Hotṛ-priest evermore through our prayers; with your celestial splendor, grant us luster.
O Agni, most youthful one, you are our desirable Hotṛ-priest; ever through our prayers, grant us celestial splendor. 2.

O Agni, "most youthful" (ayaviṣṭha)—meaning always the youngest—you who are "excellent" (avareṇya), that is, worthy of being chosen; having become our "Hotṛ," the performer of the oblation, being praised with "speech" (vacaḥ) endowed with "splendor" (divitmatā); [the word] "sit down" (nipīda) is to be supplied as the remainder of the sentence.
Of what nature are you?
You are "endowed with mental perceptions" (manmabhiḥ), meaning possessed of the splendors that make things known; this is to be supplied as the remainder.
*Yaviṣṭha*:

From the word *yuva*, by adding the suffix *iṣṭhan*, the letters beginning with *ya* are elided according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.156 (*sthūladūra* etc.), and the preceding vowel *u* undergoes *guṇa*. Then the substitution of *ava* occurs.
The vocative is unaccented.
[The word] *manmabhiḥ* [is derived from] the root *man*,
meaning "to know."
The suffix *man* [is applied] according to the rule "it is seen after other [roots] as well";
because it has the marker *n*, it is accented on the first syllable.
[Thus we have] *divitmatā*.
The root *div* means "to play" and so forth.
By the rule *ikṣitapau dhātunirdeśe* (Pāṇini 3.3.108), the suffix *ip* is applied;
thus, by the word *div*, which denotes the verbal root, the meaning of the root—namely, "shining"—is indicated through metonymy (*lakṣaṇā*).
Alternatively, the suffix *ki* is added in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) according to the *uṇādi* rules;
and in the word *divi*, the addition of the letter *t* before the possessive suffix *matup* is a Vedic archaism (*chāndasa*).
Alternatively, by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the suffix *itac* is applied to the root *div* in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).

In the case of the possessive suffix *matup*, the absence of the substitution of *jaś* occurs because of its status as a *bha*-stem, according to the rule "in the sense of the possessive suffix, [the word ending in] *at* or *as* is a *bha*."
Regarding the word *vacaḥ*: by the rule *supāṃ suluk*, there is elision (*luk*) of the third-case singular ending.
For indeed, the father bestows his love upon the son; the friend, most excellent, bestows it upon the friend for his protection.
For indeed, the father offers [oblations] to his son; the excellent friend offers to his friend for protection. 3.

"O Agni, you who are most excellent (*avareṇya*), worthy of being chosen (*varaṇīya*), and our father (*pitā*)—that is, occupying the position of a father—grant what is desired to me, who am like a son (*sūnu*); this is the ellipsis.
The two particles *hi* and *ṣma* express the sense of 'in every way' (*sarvathā*).
Two examples regarding the granting of what is desired are now stated."

Just as a kinsman (*āpiḥ*) gives in every way to a kinsman (*āpaye*), and a dear friend (*sakhā priyaḥ*) gives whatever is desired in every way to a dear friend (*sakhye priyāya*), so too do you give. (The word *yajati* implies "he gives" in all respects. Thus, you also must give.
In "smā sūnave," the vowel lengthening occurs by the rule "nipātasya ca.

Since the word *sakhā* (friend) is included in the list [of words] following "yajati" in the rule "sakhye," this nominative case ending is not subject to the optional elision (*nihata*) prescribed by the rule "cādilope vibhāṣā."
Or rather, there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* accent by the rule "hi ca.
[The word is] *sakhye*.
According to the rule "In the case of *samāna*, [the suffix] *iṇ* is udātta," the word *sakhi* ends in the suffix *iṇ* and is udātta on its first syllable;
since the case endings (*sup*) are anudātta because they possess the *pit* designation, that [original udātta] alone remains.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the destroyers of enemies, sit upon our sacred grass, just as they did for Manu.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the destroyers of enemies, sit upon our sacred grass, as they did for Manu. 4.
O Agni, may these gods, who are your kinsmen, impelled by you, and who are destroyers of enemies—meaning they do not cause harm—sit upon our *barhis*, that is, upon our sacrifice.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
just as [the gods] sit upon the sacrifice of Manu Prajāpati, so [should they sit here].

*barhiḥ riśādasaḥ*. When the *visarjanīya* is changed to *r*, there is the elision of the *repha* by Pāṇini 8.3.14 (*aro ri*). Then, by Pāṇini 6.3.111 (*ḍhalope pūrvasya dīrgho’ṇaḥ*), the vowel *i* is lengthened.
*riśādasaḥ*: [The root] *riś* is used in the sense of "to injure. Those who injure—that is, those who cause harm—are *riśāḥ*, meaning enemies.
[The suffix] *ka* [is applied] after roots ending in *i*, *u*, or a semivowel (*upadha*), as well as after *jñā*, *prī*, and *kṛ*. Those who devour them are *riśādasas*.
[The suffix] *asun* is applied after all verbal roots; the accent of the final member remains its original form (*prakṛtisvara*) because it is a *kṛt* derivative with a subsequent member.
Let them sink.
[The root] *pad* is used in the senses of "falling," "going," and "sinking. By the rule beginning with *pāghrā*, there is the substitution of *sīda*.

The suffix *śap* is unaccented because it is marked with *pittva*. Since the suffix *śatṛ* is also unaccented by the rule regarding the accent of verbal roots (*dhātusvara*), the accent of the root remains. [Thus we have] *manuṣaḥ*.
Regarding "mana jñāne":

he who thinks and knows is *manu*, [namely] Prajāpati. This is because, while the rule "the suffix *hasi* is applied after the root *jan*, and it is *nit*" is in force, [the suffix is applied] diversely (*bahulam*).

In other instances as well, the suffix *usi* is applied according to the *uṇādi* rules (*u. sū.* 2.278). By virtue of being *nivat*, it bears the udātta accent on its first syllable. For example: [as in the following].
The entire [word] is unaccented because of the rule: "The word *yathā* at the end of a pāda" (Phiṭ-sūtra 85).
O ancient invoker, rejoice in this our friendship; indeed, hear these songs well. (5) O ancient invoker, rejoice in this our friendship; indeed, hear these songs well. (5)

O ancient Hotṛ, Agni, who arose before us and others, you who accomplish the oblation—rejoice for the sake of the success of this sacrifice now proceeding, of our friendship, and of your favor toward us; be glad.
O ancient one, listen also to these songs, these words of praise being offered by us. O ancient one!

The word *hotar* has its initial syllable accented because of the rule "an *āmantrita* [vocative] is not [accented] when followed by a word in grammatical apposition. Thus, the eighth-case form *viśvapatiḥ*—the protector of the *viśas*, that is, of all creatures; the *hotṛ*, the performer of the oblation; the *mandra*, the joyful; the *vareṇya*, the one to be chosen—may this Agni be dear (*priya*) to us (*naḥ*).
The ellipsis is: "May we also, being devoted to you and engaged in what is auspicious, become dear to you."
*Viśvapatiḥ*:

Since the rule “*paśyāvaiśvaryam*” would have required the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member, the rule “*parādiś chandasi bahulam*” applies to provide the acute accent (*udātta*) on the initial syllable of the second member. *Vareṇyaḥ*.
By the rule *vṛña eṇyaḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.308), the suffix *eṇya* is applied; because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group, it bears the udātta accent on the first syllable. Thus: *svamayaḥ*.
In a bahuvrīhi compound, by the rule "nam-subhyām," there is acute accent on the final syllable of the last member.

For the gods have bestowed upon us what is desirable and full of noble men; we too meditate upon that which is full of noble men. 8. For the gods have bestowed upon us what is desirable and full of noble men; we too meditate upon that which is full of noble men. 8.

Since the *devāsas*—the shining officiating priests (*ṛtvijas*) who are *svamayas*, endowed with splendor—have indeed *dadhire*, held fast for us our *vārya*, the desirable oblation; therefore, being ourselves *svamayas*, endowed with splendor, we *manāmahe*, we entreat you. *vāryam*: from the root *vṛñ* in the sense of "choosing" or *vṛñ* in the sense of "partaking. By the rule *ṛhalorṇyat*, the suffix *ṇyat* is applied. By the rule *īdvaṃśca*, etc., the first syllable is udātta. *dadhire*: because the root *hṛ* has the *cit* designation, the final syllable is udātta. By the rule *hi ca*, there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. *manāmahe*: from the root *man* in the sense of "knowing. The suffix *śap* is applied by way of irregularity (*vyatyayena*).
May there be wealth for both of us, O Immortal One, for mortals; may there be mutual praises between us. 9. Wealth. For us. Of both. O Immortal One. Of mortals. Mutually. May there be. Praises. 9.
O immortal Agni, free from death, after the performance of this rite, may there be mutual praises between us mortals and you, our lord—praises consisting of words that are mutually commendatory:
the praise concerning the sacrificer that "the sacrifice has been well performed," and the praise concerning yourself that "you have been well favored."
Now, by the rule "nipātasya ca," there is a long vowel in the *saṃhitā* [text] for the particle *amṛte*.

Because of the exclusion [contained in the rule] *apādādau*, the first syllable is udātta according to the sixth [chapter of Pāṇini’s grammar]. [The word] *martyānām* [is derived from the root] *mṛṅ* [meaning] "to abandon life."
The word *marta* ends in the suffix *tan* according to the rule *‘asihasi...’* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.366).
From that [root], the suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *‘tasmād bhave chandasi’* (Pāṇini 4.4.110).
Its acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudāttatva*) is established by the rule *‘yato ’nāvaḥ’*.
May they be praiseworthy; [here] there is elision of the *bh* and *s* sounds (*bhsoralopaḥ*). Praiseworthy ones.
By the rule "tādau ca," the verbal root retains its original accent (prakṛtisvaratvam).

O Agni, with all your fires, bestow this sacrifice and this splendor as food upon us, O son of strength! 10. With all [fires], O Agni, with fires, this sacrifice, this splendor, food, bestow, O son of strength. 10.

O Agni, son of strength, O you who possess a divine form, accompanied by all the fires—the Āhavanīya and others—favouring this our sacrifice and this our speech, our hymn of praise, bestow upon us food and grant it to us.
With all [the gods].
The absence of the substitution of *ais* for the instrumental ending *bhis* is due to the rule "it occurs abundantly in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
*Canas*.

From the roots *cāy* in the sense of "to worship" or "to observe," the suffix *asun* is applied according to the rule *cāyareje hrasvaśca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.639); by virtue of that [suffix], the augment *juṭ* is added. Due to its being marked with *n*, it is udātta-accented on the first syllable.
The suffix *dhāḥ* [is used].
In the *luṅ* tense, by the rule "gātisthā0," there is elision (*luk*) of *sic*.
By the rule "bahuḷaṃ chandasyamādyoge 'pi," there is the absence of the augment *aṭ*.

In the phrase *sahaso yaho*, because of the status of being like a subsequent member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*) according to the rule *subāmantrite parāṅgavat*, the entire collection consisting of the vocative and the following word is pronounced with a low pitch (*nighāta*) by the rule *āmantritasya ca*.
Ṛgveda 26: The fourth hymn, consisting of thirteen verses beginning with "aśvaṃ na tvā," has the same seer and other details as the preceding one.
