Regarding the thirteenth [verse], "namo mahadbhyaḥ": its meter is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is the Viśvedevas. Thus it has been enumerated: "Aśvaṃ sasohnā is in Gāyatrī; the other is a divine Triṣṭubh."
The application of the hymn excluding the final verse for both the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra has been stated:
"I shall praise with reverences Agni, who is like a horse possessing a tail, the sovereign lord of sacrifices. (1)
Not even to praise you, Agni, who possess the choicest gifts and reign supreme over the sacrifices, do we fail with our prostrations. ||1||
We have set out to praise—with salutations, that is, with hymns—*you*, Agni, the sovereign lord who rules over *adhvarāṇām*, the sacrifices.
Herein lies a simile:
like a horse (*aśvam na*) that possesses a tail (*vāravantam*), one endowed with a tail.
Just as a cloud avoids harmful mosquitoes, gnats, and the like with its hairs, so too do you avoid those who oppose us with your flames—this is the meaning.
Regarding the word *vāravantam*: due to the *pit* status of the suffix *matup*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*).
Because the suffix *ghañ* is marked with *ṅit*, the word *vāra-* is udātta on its first syllable;
the rule “*karṣātvataḥ*” (Pāṇini 6.1.159), which would otherwise cause the udātta accent on the final syllable, does not apply here due to metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*).
[The form] is *vandadhyai*.
The root *vad* is used in the senses of salutation and praise.
By the rule “*idito num dhātoḥ*,” the augment *num* is added. By the rule “*tum-arthe seseṇa*,” the suffix *aip* is applied here.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In *samrājantam*,
the suffix is unaccented because it is marked with the indicatory letter *p* (*pittva*).
The suffix *śatṛ* retains the accent of the verbal root by virtue of the accentuation rule for *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes;
likewise, in a compound, that same accent remains by virtue of the rule for the original accent of the final member of a *kṛt*-derived word.
[Thus,] *adhvarāṇām*.
By the rule "nansubhyām," the final syllable of the compound is udātta.
May he, our son, by his might, widely striding and most gracious, be a bountiful giver for us. 2.
May he, our son, by his might, wide-striding, most gracious, and bounteous, become ours. 2.
He, that very Agni, is indeed our *suśevaḥ*—the remainder of the sentence being "he becomes most gracious or most pleasant.
Of what nature is he? He is the *sūnuḥ*, the son, of *śavas*, strength; he is *pṛthupragāmā*, one whose movement is wide-reaching.
Furthermore, may he who is *mīḍhvān*, the showerer of desires, be for us (*asmakam*).

[The form] *ghā naḥ* [is used]; the lengthening [of the vowel] occurs according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.133: "In the Ṛgveda, [the final vowel of] *tu*, *nu*, *dham*, *akṣu*, *dru*, *kru*, *uru*, and *vyacaḥ* [is lengthened before *na*]."
*Śavasā*: according to the rule *supāṃ supo bhavanti*, the genitive suffix *ṅas* is replaced by *tā*. *Pṛthupragāmā*.

*Pragāma* means going forth with excellence (*prakarṣeṇa gamanam*). The suffix *ghañ* is applied here according to the rule *halaśca*. He whose stride (*pragāma*) is broad (*pṛthu*) is called *pṛthupragāma*.
The vowel *ā* is substituted by the rule *supāṃ suluk* [Pāṇini 7.1.39], resulting in a homogeneous vowel with the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇa*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratva*) applies; thus, *suśevaḥ*.
By the rule *iṇśībhyāṃ van* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.150), the word *śeṣa* ends in the suffix *van* and is ādyudātta (accented on the first syllable).

Consequently, in a bahuvrīhi compound, although the rule *nañsubhyām* would normally require the final syllable of the second member to be udātta, the rule *ādyudāttaṃ chandasi* applies, resulting in the initial syllable of the second member being udātta. Thus: *mīḍhvān*.
The word *mīḍhvān* is derived from the root *miha* (to sprinkle) with the suffix *kasu*, and is thus included among the irregularly formed words (*nipātita*) such as *dāśvān*, *sādvān*,

and *mīḍhvān*. [The form] *babhūyāt* is a substitute for the optative (*liṅ*) of the root *bhū* in its Vedic (*chāndasa*) perfect (*liṭ*) tense, according to the rule *tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti* (Prātiśākhya 7.1.39).
Due to the status of *yāsuṭ* as being like its substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*), it possesses the nature of an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix; consequently, there is the substitution of *ś* for *s*.
In the case of the dual, there is the substitution of *a* by Pāṇini’s rule 7.4.73, *abhavateḥ*. There is also the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) by the rule *tiṅatiṅaḥ*.
Protect us from the mortal who seeks to harm us, both from afar and from near; guard us so that we may possess full life. 3.
Do thou, O possessor of all life, protect us forever from the malicious mortal, both from afar and from nearby.

1. *ca-pha-sa-vāravantam*. It is called *vāra* because it wards off (*vārayati*) gadflies; [the suffix] *ac* is added according to the rule beginning with *pacādyac*. There is an optional form due to its inclusion in the *kapilakādi* group (or the *sakapilakādi* group).

O Agni, you who are all-encompassing and whose movement is far-reaching—do you, as such, protect us always and at all times from the mortal enemy who desires to inflict evil, sin, or misfortune upon us, whether he be far away or even close at hand. Guard us evermore with complete protection.
Regarding *aghāyoḥ*: by the rule *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* [Pāṇini 3.1.8], the suffix *kyac* is applied; then, by the rule *aśvāghasyāt* [Pāṇini 7.4.37], the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel occurs.
Protect! [The word] *pāhi* is unaccented because it begins with *pāda*. [The word] *viśvāyuḥ*.
From the verbal root *iṇ* in the sense of "going" (*gatau*), the suffix *usi* is applied by the rule *etenicca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 2.275).
The term is a *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "one whose movement or course (*mayana*) is universal (*viśva*).
According to the rule *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*, the final syllable of the first member (*pūrvapada*) is acute-accented (*udātta*).
O Agni, do you proclaim this our newest hymn of praise among the gods. This—Oṃ—well, you, for us, this hymn of praise, most recent, O Agni, do you proclaim among the gods. 4.

O Agni, you must proclaim before the gods—on behalf of us and for our sake—this newest *sani*, the gift of oblation being performed here in front of the altar, as well as this newest *gāyatra* speech in the form of praise.
*ū pu*: In the *saṃhitā*, there is lengthening according to the rule *nipātasya ca*;
there is the substitution of *ṣ* according to the rule *sujaḥ*.
*navyāṃsam*:
from the word *nava*, when the suffix *īyasun* is added, there is a Vedic elision (*chāndasa*) of the vowel *ī*;
because the suffix *īyasun* has the marker *n*, it is accented on its first syllable.
He says:

"In the Vedic language, the *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* [are used] for the sense of the *loṭ*. Thus, in the sense of a request (*prārthanā*), the *luṅ* is employed; by the rule *asyativakti* (Pāṇini 3.1.52), the *cli* is replaced by *aṭ*; and by *vaca um* (Pāṇini 7.4.20), the vowel *u* is substituted [for the final *c*].

Grant us a share in the highest spoils, and in those that are middling; bestow upon us wealth from the nearest source. 5. Grant us a share in the highest spoils, and in those that are middling; bestow upon us wealth from the nearest source. 5.
O Agni, bestow upon us our share in the highest, most excellent foods (vāja) residing in the heavenly world; bestow it upon us in the middle foods residing in the intermediate space;
and grant us wealth (vasu) belonging to the nearest, lowest world, the earth.
‘Śikṣa’ [is derived from] the root √vic with the prefix upa. Because the root is marked with *p*, it retains its original accent (dhātusvara).
By the rule “aco ’taḥ tiṅaḥ,” there is lengthening in the *saṃhitā* [text].
The word *anta* here means "the nearest" (*antikātama*). According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.4.149, *tame tādeśa*, there is the elision of the suffix *tika*.

You are the distributor, O you of wondrous luster; from the wave of the Sindhu, you flow hither immediately for the sake of the donor. 6. You are the distributor. O you of wondrous luster. From the Sindhu. Upon the wave. Hither. Immediately. For the donor. You flow. 6.
O Citrabhānu, O Agni endowed with variegated rays, you are the distributor and the bringer of distinguished wealth.
Regarding this, an illustration is stated:
the word *okaḥ* has the sense of comparison.

Just as near the vicinity of a river, they divide wave after wave—the stream characterized by waves such as canals and the like—in the same way, for the donor, the sacrificer who has offered the oblation, you flow forth at that very moment (*sadyas*) the stream consisting of the fruits of action in the form of canals and so forth. (Note: *kulyādirūpa-pravāham* occurs in versions *ca-cha-pha-śa*; *kulyādirūpaṃ pravāham* occurs in version *jha-ṣa*.)

"You cause rain to fall. Regarding *sindhoḥ*: from the root *syandū*, meaning "to flow," the suffix *u* is applied according to *Uṇādi Sūtra* 1.11, "In *syandi*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and *dha* [is substituted]. Because the term *nit* is understood as a governing rule (*anuvṛtti*), the word is accented on the first syllable. Regarding *ūrmiḥ*: the suffix *mi* is applied according to *Uṇādi Sūtra* 4.484, "After the root *ṛ*, [the suffix] *ūrc". The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). Regarding *dāśuṣe*: this has been explained in the commentary on *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.25.6, "To the donor who maintains the vow of clarified butter (*ghṛtavratāya dāśuṣe*)."
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—
he shall be the master of eternal refreshments.
O Agni, the mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—he shall be the master of eternal nourishments.

O Agni, that mortal sacrificer whom you have protected (*avāḥ*)—that is, whom you have guarded and preserved—in battles (*pṛtsu*), and whom you impel (*junāḥ*) toward spoils (*vājeṣu*) in the contests, that man, the sacrificer, becomes capable of controlling (*yantā*) eternal refreshments (*śaśvatīriṣaḥ*), that is, constant food-supplies. Regarding *pṛtsu*: by the rule "The addition of *pṛt* to *māṃstṛstṛn* is prescribed" (Pāṇini 6.1.63.1), the word *pṛtanā* undergoes the substitution of *pṛt*. The acute accent on the case-ending is due to the rule "sāvekācaḥ. Regarding *avāḥ*: this is from the root *ava*; there is a transposition of the vowels *a* and *ā*. Alternatively, in the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, there is the augment *āṭ*, and by the rule "itaśca," the *i* of the suffix *sip* is elided. Regarding *junāḥ*: the root *jū* meaning "to go" is a Vedic (Sautra) root. It takes the suffix *sip* of the *laṭ* (present indicative). By the rule "ṛyādibhyaḥ bhā," the augment *aṭ* is absent according to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge'pi" (even in the absence of the prohibitive particle *mā*). Due to its connection with *yat*, it does not lose its accent (it is *anighāta*). Regarding *yantā*: the initial vowel is acute because the suffix *tṛn* has the marker *ni*. Regarding *śaśvatīḥ*: the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "ugitaśca."
O most powerful one,
no one at all can encompass the glorious strength of this active hero.
None, O Conqueror, can encompass him; even for one who acts, there is no strength worthy of renown. ||8||
O you two who are ever-conquering, habitually overcoming enemies—no one at all exists who can overcome this sacrificer, whoever he may be, this one who sees clearly.
Furthermore, for this sacrificer there is *vāja*—that is, a specific strength worthy of being heard about. Whose [strength]? [Whosoever it may be.]
The insertion of the letter *ya* is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
[The word] *śravāvyaḥ* is formed with the suffix *āyya*, according to the rule: “After the roots *śru*, *dakṣi*, *sṛhi*, and *gṛhi*, the suffix *āyya* is added” (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.376).
May he, who is observed by all people, be the conqueror of enemies for the sake of booty;
may he, through the inspired poets, be the winner of wealth.
May he, who belongs to all people, be a conqueror of booty with his steeds; may he be a winner of wealth with his inspired singers. 9.
May that Agni, who is attended by all people (viśvacarṣaṇiḥ), be the one who carries us across the battle for booty (vāja) with his swift horses;
and may Agni, accompanied by wise and intelligent officiating priests (vipra), being well-pleased, be the bestower of the fruit of our actions.
*Viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*:
one whose subjects (*carṣaṇīyaḥ*) are all (*viśve*).
The acute accent on the final syllable of the first member of the compound is due to the rule *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*.
*Arvadbhiḥ*:
from the root *ṛ*, meaning "to go";
the suffix *vanip* is applied according to the rule "it is seen after other roots as well."
In the word *bhisi*, by the rule *arvaṇastṛ-asāv anañaḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.127), the *na* is replaced by the substitute *tṛ*. [Thus we have] *tarutā*.
[The root] *tṛ* [is used] in the sense of "floating" and "crossing."

From this [root], the form *grasitṛ* is derived as a nipātana (irregular formation) ending in *tṛn* in rules such as Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.34 (*grasitaskabhitastṛbhiḥ*); the substitution of *u* for the vowel *i* occurs precisely because it is a nipātana.
In this third watch, when the *kathā* has been exceeded, the three-verse hymn (*stotriya*) beginning with "O Jarābodha, know that" is used.

This is prescribed in the section [of the *Śrautasūtra*] beginning with "For whom the cattle are not present," in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 9.11: "The *atirikta-kathās*: 'O Jarābodha, know that'."
O Jārabodha, know this for him who is worthy of sacrifice among all people:
offer a visible hymn of praise to Rudra.
O unawakened one, understand that! O you who pervade the universe, offer a visible hymn of praise to the worshipful Rudra. 10.

O Agni, who are awakened by praise (*jarabodha*), for the sake of bestowing grace upon each of these subjects in the form of the sacrificers, and for the sake of accomplishing the performance related to the sacrifice for the one worthy of sacrifice (*yajñiya*), enter—that is, penetrate—this place of divine worship (*devayajana*).
It remains implied that the sacrificer also offers a beautiful, well-composed hymn of praise (*stoma*) to you, O Rudra, the fierce Agni.

Regarding this, Yāska has explained as follows: "Jarā is praise; it comes from the root *jṛ*, meaning 'to praise. Understand that [praise], or [understand him] as one who causes it to be understood by means of that [praise]. Know that, perform that—for the sacrifice of every man, a beautiful hymn for Rudra" (Nirukta 10.8).
*Jarabodha*:
[The root] *jṛp* [is used] in the sense of "wasting away of age";
however, in this context, it is for the purpose of praise.
The suffix *aṅ* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 3.3.104, *piñjidādibhyo’ṅ*;
from that, the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is added.
Thus, *jarabodhaḥ* refers to one whose awakening (*bodha*) occurs through praise (*jarā*).
Alternatively,
*jarabodha* means "awakened by old age"; the suffix *ghañ* is used here in the sense of the object (*karman*).
The initial syllable of the vocative is acute;
[thus] *vividdhi*. [The root] *viś* is used in the sense of "entering."
For in the imperative (*loṭ*),
by the rule "in the Veda [it is] diversely," there is *ślu* (elision) of the *śap* suffix;
then follow the substitution of the reduplication and the retention of the initial consonant of the root.
In the case of *‘huślyo herdhiḥ’*, there is the substitution of *herdhi*. [This applies] when *pluta* and *ṣṭutva* [are involved].
Or else:
From the root *vi-pū* in the sense of "pervasion," in the second person singular middle voice (*loṭ*), there is an absence of *guṇa* in the reduplicated syllable:
*viśviśe*. By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the fourth case ending receives the acute accent (*udātta*).
By the rule *anudāttaṃ ca*, the first vowel of the *iṭ* augment becomes unaccented (*anudātta*).
[The form] *yajñiyāya*:
by the rule *yajñavigbhyāṃ ghakhañau* (Pāṇini 5.1.71), the suffix *gha* is applied.
*dṛśīkam*: the suffix *kīkan* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.139 (*anidaśibhyāṃ ca*). Due to the *nit*-designation, it is accented on the first syllable.
May he, the great one, free from pride, whose banner is smoke, and who is many-shining,
impel us toward wisdom and toward booty.
He is the great one; he is without measure; he is the smoke-bannered; he is the many-mooned; may he impel us toward wisdom and toward strength. 11.
May that Agni impel us toward wisdom, action, strength, and food; may he gladden us.
Of what sort?
Great, possessing superior qualities, immeasurable—meaning devoid of measurement and thus uninterrupted.
Dhūmaketu is known by its smoke; it is a man-moon with manifold radiance.
In the *saṃhitā* [text] for the word *mahāṃ anī*, it is stated that the *nakāra* becomes either *ru* or *anunāsika*. [The example is] *animānaḥ*.
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "one for whom there is no measure" (*na vidyate nimāno'sya*), the final syllable of the second member is accented acute by the rule *nansubhyām*.
Dhūmaketu: In a bahuvrīhi compound, the first member retains its original accent. Puruścandra.
The root *cad* is used in the senses of "delighting" and "shining.
From this root, the suffix *rak* is applied according to the rule *sphāyitañci-* etc., in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*).
In the compound *puruścāsau candraśca*, the final member is accented acute (*samāsāntodāttatva*).
The augment *suṭ* is applied by the rule *‘hasvāccandrottarapade mantre’* (Pāṇini 6.1.151).
Its *ś* sound arises from the substitution of *śru* for *su*. [Thus:
*dhiye*.
The word *hinvatu* has an acute accent (*udātta*) on the fourth syllable by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. The root *hivi* means "to please" or "to gladden."
The augment *num* is applied after a verbal root ending in *i*.
May he, the lord of the people, the divine banner, hear us like the Revā river—
being exalted by these hymns of praise.
May he, like Revat, the lord of the people, the divine banner—Agni of great radiance—hear us with our hymns. 12.
May that Agni hear us, who are joined with hymns and praises;
there is an illustration for this:
like one who is wealthy.

Just as in the world a wealthy king listens to the praise of bards, so it is here. Of what nature [is he]? He is the lord of the people (*viśapati*), the protector of subjects, and divine (*daivya*), belonging to the gods.
"Fire is indeed the Hotṛ of the gods," according to another scriptural passage (Ai. Brā. 3.14).
*Ketu* means a knower or indicator, like a messenger.
1. [This is] to be understood from the variants *jha*, *ḍha*, *dha*, and *ha*.
2. Understand the state of *ca-pha-tvam*.
For it is stated in the Śruti: “Agni was indeed the messenger of the gods” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.5.8.5).
[He is] the Brahman, the Supreme, the Most Exalted.
He is *revān*.
There is elision of the *m* by the rule "etattadoḥ" (Pāṇini 6.1.132). There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "reyematau bahulam."
The state of having another [vowel] preceding it; "ā" is substituted for "ar" by the rule *ād guṇaḥ*; and the substitution of *vat* for the suffix *matup* occurs by the rule *chandasy iraḥ*.

The suffix *matup* is accented according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.176.1, which states: "The accentuation of the suffix *matup* following the word *āre* must be stated. Thus, there is the acute accent on *matup*.

In the word *vispatiḥ*, the initial vowel of the second member (*uttarapada*) is accented by the rule: "In the Vedic language, the initial of the second member is frequently [accented]. Thus, there is the acute accent on the beginning of the second member.
Brahmānu: In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [is maintained].
In the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, this mantra, "Homage to the great ones," occurs in the *japa* that precedes the *śugādāpana*.
It is prescribed in the section concerning the *brahmaudana* being consumed: "May Sūrya protect us from heaven; homage to the great ones, homage to the young ones" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 1.4).

Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones, homage to the young, homage to those who have attained old age! Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; O gods, may I not cut off the praise of one more venerable than myself. 13. Homage to the great ones. Homage to the small ones. Homage to the young. Homage to those who have attained old age. Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able. May I not, O gods, cut off the praise of one more venerable [than myself]. 13.
Impelled by Agni, Śunaḥśepa praised the Viśvedevas with this [hymn].

Thus it is recorded in the scripture: "Agni said to him, 'Praise the Viśvedevas with the verse beginning, "O you who are worthy of praise. He then praised the Viśvedevas with the verse, 'Homage to the great ones, homage to the young ones' (AiB 7.16). Those who are superior in qualities are called "great" (mahāntaḥ).
The children are deficient in qualities;
the youths are young;
the elders are advanced in age and aged.
Salutations be to the gods who possess the fourfold bodies as previously described.
"If" we are somehow able—meaning, if we are capable through the accumulation of wealth and so forth—"then" we shall "sacrifice to the gods.
O "gods," may I "not cut off"—that is, may I not cause the interruption of—the "praise," the hymn of praise, "extended on all sides" toward the "elder," the most eminent specific deity.
Regarding *āśina*:
[it is derived from] the root *aśū* in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāptau*).
The suffix *inac* is applied according to the Uṇādi Sūtra 2.207: "It is used extensively elsewhere as well. This is an *auṇādika* (derivative) suffix.
The word *citaḥ* has its final syllable accented (*antodātta*). In *yajāma*,
the suffix *śap* is unaccented because it is marked with the *pit* designation.
And by the accent of the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes, the root-accent [prevails] in *tiṅ* forms; as in *śakvāma*, from the root *śaklṛ* meaning "to be able."

In the word *jyāyasaḥ*, because the suffix *tiṅ* is marked with *piṭ* by the rule *āṅuttamasya picca*, it becomes unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇasvara*) remains. Furthermore, the prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of the accent) applies here by the rule *nipātairyadyadihanta*.
*Jyāyasaḥ*.

From the word *praśasya*, when the suffix *īyasun* is added, there is the substitution of *jya* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.3.61 (*jya ca*). Then, by Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.160 (*jyādīdīyasaḥ*), the vowel *ī* of the suffix *īyasun* is replaced by *ā*.
Due to its being marked with the *n*-augment (*nit*), it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.
Praise. [The suffix] *ghañ* is applied by the rule "halaśca" (Pāṇini 3.3.121).
I grow.
The root *ovaśc* means "to cut.
By way of grammatical anomaly (*vyatyaya*), there is the first person singular of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) with the augment *iṭ*.
There is also the suffix *sic* for the conditional (*caleḥ*).
The absence of the augment *iṭ* is due to the rule beginning with *svaratisūtī*.
The elision of the penultimate *s* is by the rule *skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ*.
The substitution of *p* is by the rule beginning with *vraśca*.

In *paṭhoḥ kaḥ si*, the substitution of *k* occurs by the rule *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*; the substitution of *p* occurs by the rule *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*; and the absence of the augment *aṭ* occurs by the rule *na māṅyoge*.
The fifth hymn, “yatra grāvā,” consists of nine verses.
The first six are *anuṣṭubh*s;
the three beginning with “āyajī” are *gāyatrī*s.
At the beginning, Indra is the deity for four [verses].
After that, two have the mortar as their deity. Following those, there are two belonging to both the mortar and the pestle as deities.
Regarding the last [verse], "ucchiṣṭam": its deity is any one of the following—Hariścandra, the pressing-skin (adhipavana-carma), or Soma.
Thus it is stated in the *Bṛhaddevatā*: "It praises either the skin, the pressing-stone, or Soma" (*Bṛhaddevatā* 3.101).

This has been stated in the *Anukramaṇī*: "Where there is 'grāvā', 'nava', 'palu', the *anuṣṭubh*-beginning [verses], 'yaccit', the two 'ulūkhalyau', and the two 'mausalyau' [verses], these belong to Prajāpati; the last [verse] belongs to Hariścandra."
1. Regarding "ḍha-revān," [the commentary states]:
"In the opinion of Reyima, it is either a praise of leather."
The first four cups are employed at the *ajña* sacrifice and the *homa*;
the next four cups at the pressing (*abhiṣava*);
and the others at the pouring of the Soma into the *droṇakalaśa*.

And so says the Brāhmaṇa: "Now Śunaḥśepa saw this *asaṃva* vessel; he pressed [the Soma] with these hundred verses beginning with 'Whatever you have in every house. Then he poured it into the *droṇakalaśa* with the verse, 'Carry away the remnant from the cups. Then, at this very undertaking, he offered oblations with the previous hundred verses together with the *svāhā*-utterances" (AiB 7.17).
Where the broad-based pressing-stone stands upright for the sake of pouring out the soma,
O Indra, drink greedily of the juices pressed by the mortar.
Where the broad-based pressing-stone stands upright for the sake of pouring out the juices pressed by the mortar—there, O Indra, drink deeply with a roar! 1.
O Indra, at that sacrifice, in that ritual for the sake of pressing— wherein the broad-based, thick-rooted stone for the purpose of extraction is raised,
and where the woman teaches the downward and upward movement—
the presser gulps down the juices extracted from the *ulūkhala* mortar and *khalu* pestle. O Indra, you have swallowed them all.
Where the woman learns the downward and upward movement of the grains ground by the mortar and pestle—hither, O Indra, let the courser swallow them down repeatedly! 3.

"In which [rite], in which action, the woman—the wife—'practices,' that is, performs the exercise of 'apacyavam,' the departure from the hall, and 'upacyavam,' the arrival at the hall. The rest is as before. Regarding *apacyavam*: from the root *cyuṅ* meaning "to move," the suffix *ap* is applied by the rule *ṛdorap*. There is the substitution of *guṇa* and *avādeśa*. By the rule *thāthādinā* (Pāṇini 6.2.144), the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. Similarly for *upacyavam*. Regarding *śikṣate*: from the root *śikṣa* meaning "to learn" or "to take up. Since it is taught with a short vowel (*adupadeśāt*), the *lasārvadhātuka* suffix is anudātta, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains. By the rule *nipātairyadyadihanta*, there is a prohibition against the *nighāta* (elision) of the accent."
Wherein Indra, as if with reins, bound the churning-stick,
he drank repeatedly the soma-juice of the sons of Ulūka and Khalu.
Where they bind the churning-stick as if to restrain the reins, let the courser, having drunk of the grains ground in the mortar and pestle, come hither and roar loudly for you, O Indra! 4.
"In which [rite], that is, in whatever ritual action they fasten the *manthā*— the churning-stick, the cause for churning the *āśira* (milk-mixture)—
therein is the illustration: "as if having restrained (*yamitavāiva*), that is, as if to control the reins (*raśmīn*), the traces for binding the horses."
The rest is as before. Regarding *manthām*:
by the rule *pathimadhyumukṣāmāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.85), the substitution of *au* occurs even in the accusative case by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*).

When the final udātta accent would have been obtained by the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*), the initial udātta is applied by the rule *pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne* (Pāṇini 6.1.199).
Alternatively,
*manthā* is so called because it is churned (*madhyate*) by means of it.
From the root *miś* in the sense of "churning" (*viloḍane*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*) by the rule *halaśca*;
thereafter, the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is added.
By the rule *miśvādyudāttatvam*, the word is udātta-accented on its first syllable.
*vibadhnatai* [is derived from] the root *bandh*, meaning "to bind," with the suffix *bhā* applied according to the rule *kryādibhyaḥ bhā*.

By the rule "aniditām," there is the elision (lopa) of the *n* [of the suffix], and by the rule "bhābhyastayorātaḥ," there is the elision of the long *ā*. This is the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
By the rule "titi codāttavati," there is the suppression of the accent (*nighāta*) of the motion (*gati*).
*yamitavai*:
[derived from] the root *yama* in the sense of "to cease" (*uparame*).
The suffix *taven* is applied according to the rule *tum-arthe seseṇ*.
The augment *iṭ* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
Alternatively,
when the augment *iṭ* is applied to the suffix *tavi*, the elision of the *ṇi*-affix is a Vedic anomaly.
By the rule *antaśca tavai yugapat* (Pāṇini 6.1.200), there is acute accent on both the beginning and the end [of the word].
"Even though you are joined in every house, O *ulūlakhalaka*,
here speak most loudly, like a drum being sounded for the aged."
For wherever you are joined, O *ulūlakhalaka*, in every single house, here speak most brilliantly, like a drum being sounded for those who must listen.
1. In the *ḍha*-manuscript, "the rest is as before" (*anyat pūrvavat*) does not appear.
2. In the *ca*, *pha*, and *ha* manuscripts, it reads *vibadhnate* and *vibadhnanti*.

O mortar (*vulūkhalaka*), speak clearly (*vyacciddhi*). Even though you are employed in every house for the purpose of threshing, nevertheless here in this Vedic ritual, speak with a very loud sound—most intensely resonant and exceedingly brilliant—by means of a forceful blow from the pestle.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like the drum of those who are victorious.
Just as the drum of kings who have achieved victory in battle produces a great sound, so too [is it here].

Yāska has explained the word *ulūkhala* as follows: “*Ulūkhalam* means either *utkaram* (that which is thrown out), or *ūrdhvam* (upward), or *uru me kuru* (make room for me); it was called *ulūkhalam* because it provided (*avīt*) [space]. Or rather, it is called *ulūkhalam* because it is *urukaram* (wide-making); this is the Brāhmaṇa’s explanation in an indirect manner” (Nirukta 9.20).

In the form *ulūkhalaka*, because of the exclusion rule “not at the beginning of a word” (*apādādau*), there is an absence of the initial acute accent (*ādyudātta*) resulting from the *ātmika* (inherent) rule; instead, there is the acute accent on the first syllable according to the sixth [rule] (*ṣāṣṭhika*).

It is appropriate [to say that] because it is taught with an *ad*-suffix, when the *lasārvadhātuka* accent is rendered *anudātta*, the accent of the *yak* suffix remains; and there is no elision (*nighāta*) by the rule "a *tiṅ* [is unaccented] after a *tiṅ*."
This is because of the prohibition [stated in Pāṇini 8.1.30]: “When particles such as *yad*, *yadi*, *hi*, and *hanta* [precede], [the augment *naT* is not applied]. [The word] *ghumattamam*:
from the root *div* (in the sense of playing), the suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule for *saṃpad* and so forth.
The substitution of *u* [for *v*] occurs by Pāṇini’s rule 6.1.131, *diva ut*.
The substitution of *yaṇ* [for *u*] follows, and the acute accent (*udātta*) on the suffix *matup* is applied by the rule *hasvanṅyāṃ matup*.

Now, an objection may be raised: since it is stated that in the rule *diva ut* the nominal stem (*prātipadika*) is intended and not the verbal root (*dhātu*), the substitution of *uṭh* [for *v*] must occur here as well, just as in examples such as *akṣadhūḥ* (by Pāṇini’s rule 6.4.19).

In that case, since the nominal stem *div* denotes a luminous heaven, "luminosity" (*dīpti*) is indicated by means of secondary signification (*lakṣaṇā*), and thus the substitution of *ut* will occur.

[Ṛgveda 10.94.6] uta sma te vanaspate vāto vi vātyagramit | atho indrāya pātave sunu somamulūkhala || 6 || And indeed, O Lord of the Forest, the wind blows through the very tip of you; therefore, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink. || 6 ||

Furthermore: O *vanaspate*, O tree in the form of a mortar (*ulūkhala*), even before you the wind blows; indeed, it spreads forth by means of the specific wind produced by the blows of the pestle placed upon you. Immediately thereafter, O mortar, for the sake of Indra—that is, for the benefit of Indra—perform the pressing of Soma (*sunu*) so that he may drink (*pātave*) it. Regarding the word *vanaspate*: the suffix *suṭ* is applied because it belongs to the *pāraskarādi* group. The word for the effect (the tree) is used here for the cause (the wood). Regarding *pātave*: from the root *pā* "to drink," the suffix *taven* is added according to the rule *tum-arthe sesen*. By the rule *jity-ādiniyam*, it has the acute accent on the first syllable. Regarding *sunu*: the *hi* is elided according to the rule *utaśca pratyayād asaṃyoga-pūrvāt*. It has the acute accent on the final syllable due to the accent of the *vikaraṇa*. It is not subject to *nighāta* (suppression of accent) because it stands at the beginning of a *pāda*. Regarding *ulūkhala*: it is called *ulūkhala* because its cavity (*kha*) is directed upwards (*ūrdhvam*). It belongs to the *pṛṣodarādi* class.

The two who sacrifice, most excellent in strength—verily they, with their mouths wide open, devour the food like two bay horses; thus they are celebrated in song. (7) *Āyajī* means "the two who sacrifice. *Vāñjasātamā* means "most excellent in strength. *Tā* means "those two. *Hi* means "verily. *Uccā* means "with their mouths wide open. *Harī-iva* means "like two bay horses. *Andhāṃsi* means "the food. *Bapsatā* means "devouring. (7)

Those two, the mortar and pestle, which are the winners of the prize (*vāja*) and the supreme achievers of the sacrifice from every side—being the bestowers of food beyond measure—they indeed produce a loud sound for that purpose; likewise, they gape wide and repeatedly perform their movement.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
like two steeds, the horses of Indra, devouring the *bandhū*—that is, grains such as barley and other edible foods.

Regarding this, Yāska explains as follows: "The two *āyajī* are for the purpose of sacrifice; they are the sharers of foods, and they are called 'high' (*uccaiḥ*) because they consume the foods like two bay horses (*harī*). (Nirukta 9.36).
*Āyajī*: the suffix *ip* is added in the sense of an instrument according to the Uṇādi rules.
The word retains the original accent of the final member of the compound (kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam).
*Vājasātamā*: [one who] best wins the prize (*vāja*). [He is called] *vājasāḥ* because he wins (*sanoti*) the prize (*vāja*).
In the word *paṇadāna*,
the suffix *viṭ* is applied by [Pāṇini 3.2.64] *janasanakhanakramagamaviśibhyaḥ kviṅ*;
[and according to Pāṇini 6.4.41] *viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt*.
1. Because it is preceded by *ga*, *ca*, *cha*, *kṣa*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *dha*, *pha*, *ra*, *śa*, *ṣa*, or *ha*, [the vowel] becomes long;
thus, by rule 27, there is the substitution of *ā*.
The compound has the accent of the original form of the final member due to the rule *kruduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*.
The suffix *tamap* is an *ātiśāyanika* (superlative) suffix.
By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, there is a long vowel of the same class (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*) [replacing the case-ending].
*vijarbhṛtaḥ*:

from the root *hṛ* in the sense of "taking away" (*harane*), when the *yaṅ* suffix is elided (*yaṅluk*), and after the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) has undergone the substitutions of *diś*, *īrt*, *ja*, and *bha*, the augment *rum* is added by Pāṇini’s rule 7.4.91: *rumikau ca luki*.
Then, by the definition of a suffix (*pratyaya*), the designation "verbal root" (*dhātu*) is applied; consequently, there is reduplication in the *liṭ* [perfect] tense.
By the rule "and like the roots beginning with *ad*" (*adādivat ca*), there is elision of the *śap* suffix.
When *guṇa* substitution would otherwise apply, it is prohibited by the rule "also before *jh* and *it*" (*jhjhiti ca*).

The status of *hi* as a *bha*-stem is established by the rule *hy-apra-horm-aś chandasi*; it bears the accent of a suffix (*pratyayasvara*); and the prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent applies by the rule *hi ca*.
*bapsatā* | [The root] *bhas* [is used in the senses of] eating and shining;
[the form is derived from] the present participle (*laṭ*) of the suffix *śatṛ*.
The suffix *śnu* is applied after roots such as *hu* (to sacrifice) by the rule *juhotyādibhyaḥ śnuḥ*.
By the rule *ghasimasor hali ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.100), there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*).
By the rule *nābhyastāc chatuḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.78), there is a prohibition of the augment *num*.
The word *abhyastānām* has the acute accent on the first syllable according to the rule *abhyastānām ādiḥ*. "O two lofty lords of the forest, today with the lofty pressers,
press for Indra the honeyed [juice]."
O lofty Vanaspatis, with the lofty pressers, press today the honeyed juice for Indra. 8.

"O two lords of the forest, you who take the form of the mortar and pestle, today in this rite, together with the lofty, beautiful pressers—the agents of extraction—becoming yourselves lofty and beautiful, press out for Indra, for the sake of Indra, our own pressed Soma substance endowed with sweetness."
*Tā* [is derived] from the case-ending *tām*, with the substitution of *ā* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
*No adya*.
The *prakṛtibhāva* (non-application of sandhi) occurs by the rule "prakṛtyāntaḥpādam.
[Thus we have] *vanaspatī*.
Although the accentuation of both members (*ubhayapadaprakṛtisvara*) would otherwise apply, the entire word becomes unaccented (*sarvānudātta*) by the rule "āmantritasya" (Pāṇini 8.1.19).
The original form is preserved by the rule *plutapragṛhyā aci* (Pāṇini 6.1.125). [The word is] *sutam*.
[It is derived from] the root *ṣuñ* in the sense of "pressing."
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is elision (luk) of the verbal suffix (vikaraṇa); [the first word] is unaccented (nighāta).
Kissing the remnant, O Soma, flow through the filter;
place yourself upon the cow's hide.
Pour it out! The remnant of the kinsman; bring the Soma for the lips. Let it flow through the filters; deposit it upon the ox-hide. 9.

O specific officiating priest (*ṛtvij*), in the context where Hariścandra is the deity: "O Hariścandra! Bring forth (*ud bhara*)—that is, carry up onto the cart—the *śiṣṭa* (remaining) Soma, which remains after the two pressing-boards (*adhipavaṇaphalaka*) that effect the consumption of the Soma from the cups (*camu*).
Pour the pressed Soma into the *pavitra*, the fringed filter (*daśāpavitra*).
Once it has been poured in, place the remaining Soma upon the skin of a cow—that is, upon the hide of a bull (*ānaḍuha*)—having set it down there."
In the word *camvoḥ*:
[the root] *cam* means "to eat. That in which one eats—that is, is consumed—is called *camūḥ*.
The suffix *u* is added by the rule *kṛpicaṃci* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.81), etc., which belongs to the Uṇādi class;
it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
Regarding the dual form in the locative case, it receives the circumflex accent (*svarita*) according to the rule *udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svaritaḥ*.
The rule "udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt" does not apply here due to a grammatical anomaly (vyatyaya). [In the word] bhara,
[the substitution of] m [occurs] by the rule "hyagrahormaḥ."
"Give! [The form *dhehi* is derived from *dhā* with the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication, according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.119:
*ghasor edāv abhyāsalopaś ca*. There is also the *nighāta* accent.]
In the word *tvaci*, the acute accent (*udātta*) of the case-ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*.
The sixth hymn, consisting of seven verses beginning with "yacciddhi satya somapāḥ," is the seerly composition of Śunaḥśepa; it is in the Pāṅkta meter and is addressed to Indra.
The Anukramaṇikā states: "yacciddhi [is] seven [verses], Pāṅkta."

On the fifth day of the *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, at the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*), regarding the recitations of the Hotṛ priests (*hotrāḥ*), they should cause [the priests] to recite one *ṛc* from each of their respective *śākhās* out of the seven-verse hymn beginning with "yacciddhi," after having performed three [repetitions].
This is prescribed in the section titled "On the fourth day" (*caturthe'hani*) in the *Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* (7.11): "'yacciddhi satya somapā'—one [ṛc] for each, in this very manner."
For even though we are, O truthful Soma-drinkers,
as if unprotected, do thou, O Indra, grant us hope for beautiful cattle and horses, in thousands, O thou of great wealth!
For whatever reason, O truthful Soma-drinker, we are as if unpraised; therefore, O Indra, grant us a share in cattle, in horses, and in beautiful thousands, O bounteous one! 1.
Urged by the Viśvedevas, Śunaḥśepa praised Indra with twenty-two verses beginning with these.

Thus says the Brāhmaṇa: "The Viśvedevas said to him, 'Indra indeed is the most powerful, the strongest, the most enduring, the best, and the one who will carry us across among the gods; praise him now, and we shall reach safety. He then praised Indra with the hymn beginning 'For you, O true drinker of Soma,' and with fifteen verses of the following [hymn]" (AiB 7.16).

O Indra, drinker of Soma, protector of Soma, you who speak the truth—though we may be as if unpraised, as if we are without praise, nevertheless, O Indra of abundant wealth (*tuvīmagha*), on account of our cattle, our riches, our beautiful things, and our thousands in number, do you cause us to be praised from all sides. The meaning is: regardless of our faults, grant us cattle and other gifts.
*somapāḥ* [is a vocative];
*vijantaḥ* [is a vocative];
[both] have the accent of the vocative (*āmantritanighātaḥ*).
*Anāśastā* means "not praised. The root *śaṃs* means "to praise. The suffix *kta* is used here in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*) according to the rule for *niṣṭhā*.
By the rule "yasya vibhāṣā," there is a prohibition of the *iṭ* augment.
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound with the negative particle *nañ*, by the rule "nañsubhyām," the final syllable of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) is udātta-accented.
[The form is] *smasi*.
"Idanto masi. "Tū naḥ. By the rule beginning with "ṛci tunugha," there is a long vowel.

In the case of *goṣu*, there is a prohibition— by the rule *na gobhantsāvavarṇa*— of the acute accent on the case-ending (*vibhaktyudāttatva*) that would otherwise have been prescribed by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*.
In the case of *aśveṣu*, [the same applies].
It is called *aśva* because it traverses the path (*adhvan*).
The suffix *kan* is applied according to the rule "after the root *aś*, etc.
Due to the presence of the *nit* augment, it has the udātta accent on its initial syllable.
In the word *śubhrīṣu*:
from the root *śubh* in the sense of "to shine," the suffix *krin* is applied according to the rule *adi-śadibhū-śubhibhyaḥ krin* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.505).
The final udātta accent occurs by way of transposition.
O Lord of the *vāja*s, you who wear the *śiprā* helmet, O powerful one, through your wondrous deeds,
do you, O Indra, grant us a share of thousands of beautiful cattle and horses, O most wealthy one!

O you with the beautiful nose-ring, Lord of spoils, possessor of power, through your wondrous deeds, do you, O Indra, most bountiful one, truly grant us a share of cattle, of horses, and of splendid thousands.

O you who possess power, O possessor of strength, O fair-cheeked one endowed with beautiful jaws, O Lord of Vājas, protector of foods—your wondrous deed (*daṃsanā*), which conforms to the truth, exists eternally.
The rest is as before.
Śiprin: Yāska [states] that "śipre" means either the jaws or the nostrils (Nirukta 6.17).
The suffix *ini* is added in the sense of possession according to the rule "ata iniṭhanau."
The first syllable of the vocative is udātta.
In "vājānāṃ pate," because it is a vocative (sub-āmantrita), the entire compound of five vocatives is unaccented (nighāta) due to being a subsequent member (parāṅgātva).

Furthermore, because of the rule "an address (āmantrita) is treated as non-existent when preceding [another address]," the word *śiprin* is treated as non-existent; consequently, since it does not follow a word (*padāt*) and begins the quarter-verse (*pādādi*), it does not receive the *nighāta* accent. This is because the rule "an address is not treated as non-existent when it is in grammatical apposition with a general term" prohibits its being treated as non-existent.
[The form] *śacīvas*: the substitution of *vat* for *matup* occurs by the rule "in the Veda (*chandasi*), after *ira*, [the suffix *matup* becomes *vat*]."

By the rule "matuvaso ruḥ," the substitution of *ru* occurs; then, by the rule "kharavasānayorvisarjanīyaḥ" (Pāṇini 8.3.15), the *visarjanīya* is substituted [for *r*]. Because it stands at the beginning of a *pāda*, there is no suppression (*nighāta*) of the vocative accent.

Lull to sleep those two who look at each other alternately, those who do not wake up easily. O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, grant us a share now in thousands of cattle and horses! 3. ni | svāpaya | mithudṛśā | sustām | abudhyamāne iti | ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi'magha || 3 ||

"O two messengers of Yama, who are seen together as a pair (*mithudṛśā*), cause them to sleep deeply (*niṣvāpaya*); and while they remain unaware of our being killed, let them fall into sleep (*sas-tām*). The rest is as before. *niṣvāpaya*: [The form is derived from] *svap*, due to the rule *supāmādi-vāt caram* (Pāṇini 8.3.98). The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*. [The compound *mithudṛśā* means] those who see in the state of a pair, in the form of a couple. Thus, *mithudṛśā*. By the rule *kvip ca*, the suffix *kvip* is applied to the root *dṛś* in the sense of the agent. It takes the original accent of the final member of the compound (*kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam*). As before, there is lengthening of the first member. The case-ending becomes *-ā* by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. *sas-tām*: [From the root] *sas* "to sleep. In the imperative (*loṭ*), the ending *tas* becomes *tām*. By the rule *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*. It bears the accent of the suffix. Because it begins the quarter-verse (*pāda*), there is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*). *abudhyamāne*: In this negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), the original accent of the first member, which is an indeclinable, prevails.

Let those enemies sleep; O Hero, let the givers awaken! O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, do thou indeed grant us a share of thousands of cattle and horses. 4. Let those enemies sleep; O Hero, let the givers awaken! O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, do thou indeed grant us a share of thousands of cattle and horses. 4.
"May those 'arātayaḥ'—those who are invisible to us, beyond our perception, and who are by nature non-givers, that is, enemies—'sasantu', sleep;
O 'śūra', O Indra endowed with heroism, may the 'rātayaḥ'—those who are by nature givers, that is, kinsmen—'bodhantu', wake up, perceive us.
The rest is as before."
May they be pacified; this is a svarita accent on the suffix;
[the word] *arātayaḥ*.
In the sense of "giving" (*dāna*),
the suffix *ktin* is applied by the rule "after the root *vṛṣ*, etc., [the suffix *ktin* is used] in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound "that in which there is no giving" (*na vidyate rātiryasya*), the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*) is maintained.
However, the rule "namsubhyām" does not apply because of the principle that "all grammatical rules are optional in the Vedic language.
Alternatively,
the suffix *ktic* is used in the sense of the agent according to the rule "kticktau ca saṃjñāyām."
In a *namsamāsa* compound, the initial member retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
[The word] "bodhantu" [is used];
because it begins with a *pāda*, there is no suppression of accent (*nighāta*) by the rule "tiṅ-anta-tiṅah."

O Indra, crush the braying donkey with that evil fate! O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, grant us a share of thousands of cattle and horses. sam indra gardabhaṃ mṛṇa nuvantam pāpayā amuyā | ā tu na indra śaṃsaya goṣvaśveṣu sahasreṣu tuvimagha || 5 ||

O Indra, with this [verse] being recited by us— this evil speech in the form of censure— completely destroy (saṃ mṛṇa) that one who praises (anuvantam), meaning one who manifests infamy; destroy such a person, who is like a donkey (gardabham),
just as a donkey [is destroyed].

The enemy likewise utters harsh words that cannot be heard; the rest is as before. *Gardabham*: [Derived from] *nada* and *garda* with the meaning "to sound. By the rule *kṛgṛ-śaśalliādibhyo'bhac* (Uṇādi-sūtra 3.402), the suffix *abhac* is added. By the rule *citaḥ*, it has an udātta accent on the final syllable. *Mṛṇa*: [From] *mṛṇa* in the sense of "injury. It belongs to the Tudādi class. Because the suffix *śa* is marked with *ṅ*, there is an absence of *guṇa*. *Nuvantam*: [From] *ṇu* in the sense of "praising. In the present participle (*śatṛ*), there is elision of *śap* because it belongs to the *adiprabhṛti* group. Due to the *ṅit* nature of the suffix *śatṛ*, there is an absence of *guṇa*, and the substitution *uvaṅ* occurs. The suffix has an udātta accent on its first syllable.
Let the wind blow far away from the forest of Kuṇḍunācya;
O Indra, most wealthy one, bestow upon us that [booty] in cattle, in beautiful horses, by the thousands!
Let it fall! From Kuṇḍunācya, from afar, let the wind blow from the forest. O Indra, most bounteous one, grant us a share of cattle, of horses, and of beautiful things by the thousands. 6.
May the wind that is adverse to us, moving with a crooked course like that of the *kuṇḍuṇācī* bird, fly away—may it fly from the forest, to a place even further than the wilderness.
The rest is as before.
"Patāta" [is used]; here the augment "āṭ" is applied. [The form] is "kuṇḍuṇācyā."

In the word *kuṇḍana*, derived from the root *kuḍi* with the suffix *lyuṭ*, the vowel *ṛ* replaces the vowel *a* following the letter *ḍ*; this is a Vedic usage. The substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs according to the rule: "It should be stated that [the substitution applies] after a vowel of the *ṛ*-class."

She is called Kuṇḍunācī because she anoints (*añjati*). The suffix *kin* is applied by the rule beginning with “*ṛtvig*” etc. (*Pāṇini 3.2.59*). Following the elision of the nasal *n* by the rule “*aniditām*” (*Pāṇini 6.4.24*), the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added by the statement “*añjateśca vaktavyam*” (*Vārttika on Pāṇini 4.1.6*).
The elision of the vowel *a* is by Pāṇini 6.4.138 (*acaḥ*).
The lengthening of the preceding member is by Pāṇini 6.3.138 (*cau*).
The acute accent (*udātta*) on the vowel *ā* is by Pāṇini 6.1.222 (*cau*).
Destroy all reproach; crush the Kṛkadāśva.
O Indra, most wealthy one, cause us to share in thousands of beautiful cattle and horses.
Destroy all clamor! Crush Kṛkadāśva! O Indra, most bounteous one, grant us a share of beautiful cattle and horses by the thousands! 7.
Slay and kill every man who utters cries of lamentation and reproach throughout our territory.
Crush and slay the enemy Kṛkadāśva, who inflicts violence upon our territory.
The rest is as before.
*Parikrośam*: [The root] *kruś* means "to call out. One who calls out on all sides (*paritaḥ*) is a *parikrośa*.
The suffix *ac* is applied according to the rule *pacādyac*.
There is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member of the compound due to the rule *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*.
[The form is] *jahi*.
The root *han* is used in the senses of "killing" and "going.
By the rule *hanter jaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.36), the substitution of *ja* for *han* occurs.
Because this substitution is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) by the rule *asiddhavad atrā bhāt*, the elision of the particle *hi* by the rule *ato heḥ* does not take place.
*jambhaya* [is derived from] *√jabh* in the sense of "destroying. Because it belongs to the *tudadi* class, there is the augment *gic* (i.e., *ya*) added after the root vowel.
Since the root *śap* is marked with the *pittva* indicatory letter, it is *anudātta*; therefore, the accent of the *gic* suffix alone remains.
*Kṛkadāśvam*. [The root] *kṛñ* is used in the sense of "injury."
The suffix *kan* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) according to the rule *kṛdādhārādhikalibhyaḥ kan* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.120).
Because the term *kit* is understood to carry over [from the previous rule], there is no *guṇa* strengthening.
Thus, *kṛka* means injury; one who gives (*dāśati*) or bestows that injury is a *kṛkadāśuḥ*.

Because of the inclusion of the term *bahula* [in the rule], the suffix *uṇ* is applied to the root *dāś* as well when *kṛka* is the upapada, according to the *Uṇādi-sūtra* 1.6: *akṛke vacaḥ kaśca*. It is udātta by virtue of the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
When the second case ending *am* follows, although *amipūrvatva* would have been expected, it is set aside by the rule *vā chandasi*, and thus the *yaṇ* substitution takes place.
The circumflex (svarita) accent of the case-ending is due to the rule: "Of a semivowel [substituted] for an acute (udātta) or circumflex (svarita)."
The seventh hymn, consisting of twenty-two verses beginning with “ā va indram,” is the seer Śunaḥśepa’s composition; it is in the Gāyatrī meter.
The verse beginning with “asmākam” is a Pādanicṛt Gāyatrī, because it has been stated: “A Pādanicṛt consists of three groups of seven [syllables]. (Anuvāka 4.4).
‘śaśvad indraḥ’—this is a Triṣṭubh verse.
The first sixteen verses are dedicated to Indra.
‘ābhināvādhāvati’ and the two following are three verses dedicated to the Aśvins.
The three verses beginning with ‘kasta uṣaḥ’ have Uṣas as their deity.
Thus says the Anukramaṇikā: “‘ā vo bādhikā’ and ‘asmākam’ are Pādanichṛt and Dhatu Triṣṭubh respectively; the two subsequent triplets (tṛcau) are addressed to the Aśvins and Uṣas.”
Like those seeking booty, we call Indra hither with drops— the Lord of a hundred powers, the most bountiful and most gracious.
As those seeking booty [pour] for you, I pour out Indra—the one of a hundred powers, the most bountiful—with drops of soma, like Krivi.
Seeking strength and desiring food, we, the Śunaḥśepas—the priests and the sacrificers—sprinkle this Indra of yours with drops of Soma from all sides; that is, we satiate him. Of what sort is he?
To him of a hundredfold power, impelled by a hundred [means], most bountiful, and exceedingly increased—
there is an illustration regarding the pouring:
just as they fill a hollow pit with water in such a manner, so too [is he].
The word *krivi* is listed among the fourteen names for a well in [the section beginning] "vatriḥ kāduḥ" etc., as in: "kriviḥ, kūpaḥ, sūdaḥ" (Nirukta 3.23.8).
*Krivi*:
from the root *kṛtī* in the sense of "cutting"; that which is cut is *krivi*.
In [the rule] *krivi-pvicchavi-sthavi-* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.496), etc., the word is derived as a nipātana ending in the suffix *kip*. For this very reason, there is the elision of the syllable *ta*.
Due to its being marked with the *nit* designation, it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.
For example:
"yathā" [is used] at the end of a quarter-verse (pāda), and thus it is entirely unaccented;
[as in the word] "vājayantaḥ."
“Desiring strength for themselves. [The suffix] *kyac* is applied according to the rule *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*.

The prohibition of the substitution of *ī* and lengthening—by the rule *na chandasyaputrasya*—is established by the indicative force (*jñāpaka*) of the subsequent prescription of lengthening in the rule *aśvāghasyāt*.
*Maṃhiṣṭham*: from the root *mahi*, meaning "to grow" (*vṛddhau*). *Maṃhiṣṭhaḥ* means "most greatly increased" (*atiśayena mahitā*).
By the rule *tubh chandasi* (Pāṇini 5.3.59), the suffix *iṣṭha* is added to a stem ending in *ṛ*.
By the rule *turiṣṭhemayaḥsu* (Pāṇini 6.4.154), there is elision of the suffix *tr*.
Due to the *nit*-characteristic of the suffix *iṣṭhan*, the word is accented on its first syllable.
He sprinkles (*siñce*).
[The root] *bici* means "to flow.
The singular number is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
The augment *num* is applied according to the rule "śe sucādīnām."
Whether it be a hundred of the pure or a thousand of those mixed with milk,
it flows down like water to the low ground.
Whether it be a hundred of the pure ones, or a thousand of those who have gathered together, they flow toward him like water to the low ground. 2.

May Indra come to know—indeed, he surely comes to—the hundredfold collection of pure, purified *soma* juices, or the thousandfold collection of *soma* juices accompanied by the proper curdling agent (*samāśira*) as the cooking ingredient;
may he favor us—this is the sense remaining [in the verse].
This is the illustration for the attainment of *soma*.
It is not low; just as water flows toward a low-lying place, so it is in this case.
Regarding *samāśīrām*: from the root *śrī* (meaning "to cook") with the prefix *sam-ā*, the form *āśīḥ* is prescribed as a substitute for the suffix *kvip* in examples such as *apaspṛdhethām*.
In this *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accentuation follows the natural accent of the preceding member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*).
It flows. [The root] *rīṅ* means "to hear.
[The suffix] *śyan* is applied after roots beginning with *div*.
1. Regarding the substitution of *ḍha*: in examples such as *vatriḥ*, *khātaḥ*, *kādaḥ*, and so forth.

2. Regarding the substitution of *jha* for *āśira* and *ḍha* for *śiras*: *saṃ yanmadāya śuṣmiṇaṃ enā hasyodaraṃ | samudro na vyaco dadhe || 3 ||* *saṃ | yat | madāya | śuṣmiṇe | enā | hi | asya | udaraṃ | samudraḥ | na | vyacaḥ | dadhe || 3 ||* When [the Soma] has entered together for the sake of exhilaration, for the impetuous one—then indeed his belly, like the ocean, has assumed a vast expanse. || 3 ||
The hundred or the thousand previously mentioned come together for the exhilaration—that is, for the sake of intoxication—of the powerful Indra.
Indeed, by this very hundred and by this thousand, the vast capacity within the belly of this Indra is maintained.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
Just as water pervades the ocean in the midst of the ocean, so it is [with this].
*enā*: by the rule *supāṃ suluk0*, the third case ending (*tṛtīyā*) is replaced by *ā*.
*vyacaḥ*.

Because the status of being treated like a *ḍit* suffix is prohibited by the rule *‘vyaceḥ kuṭādiṣu manasi’* (Kāśikā 1.2.1.1), there is no vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *‘prahijyā-’* etc. [Pāṇini 6.1.16].
Due to the *niṅ* augment of the suffix *asun*, the word is udātta on its first syllable.
[Thus we have] *dadhe*.

In the case of the root *dadhāti* used in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*), once the reduplication (*abhyāsa*), the substitution of *ha* for *dh*, and the substitution of *jaś* (the voiced unaspirated stop) have been applied, the elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca" [Pāṇini 6.4.64]. It is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
There is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*) because of the prohibition [by Pāṇini 8.1.34] "hi ca."

This one of yours you swallow up completely, as a pigeon swallows its young; yet even that splendor of yours you do not abandon us. 4. This one of yours you swallow up completely, like a pigeon [swallowing] its brood; even that splendor of yours you do not abandon us. 4.

O Indra, this very Soma which is being seen here has been prepared for you—this Soma which you shall obtain (*sam-a-tāsi*) perfectly and continuously. Therein lies the illustration: "like a pigeon" (*kapota-iva*). Just as the bird called a pigeon obtains its mate, the female pigeon who bears the young (*garbha-dhim*), so it is with you. For that very reason, you accept (*ohase*) our speech. Regarding *atasi*: from the root *at*, meaning "to go continuously. Regarding *kapota-iva*: by the rule "from the root *kabṛ*, the suffix *otac* [is added] in the sense of 'beast' or 'bird'" (Uṇādi-sūtra 1.62), the suffix *otac* is applied. The middle udātta accent occurs by transposition (*vyatyaya*). Regarding *garbha-dhim*: it is called *garbha-dhi* because the embryo (*garbha*) is placed (*dhīyate*) within it; the suffix *kip* is applied by the rule "after a verbal root, when the object or the location is expressed" (Pāṇini 3.3.39). The original accent of the final member of the compound remains due to the rule concerning the accent of the final member of a *kṛt*-derived word. Regarding *ohase*: from the roots *tuhi*, *duhi*, and *uhi*, meaning "to injure"; the Ātmanepada ending occurs by transposition (*vyatyaya*).

O Lord of the Rādhas, you who are borne by hymns, O Hero! May there be for you abundant and truthful prosperity. 5. Hymn. O Lord of the Rādhas, you who are borne by hymns, O Hero! May there be for you abundant and truthful prosperity. 5.

O Indra, Lord of bounties, protector of riches, you who are borne by songs, invoked with hymns, O hero endowed with valor—may that prosperity and fortune of yours, whose praise is such as this, be *sūnṛtā*, consisting of what is dear and true.
The word *stotra* [is derived as follows]:
by the rule *dāmnī-śasa-* (Pāṇini 3.2.182), the suffix *ch* (i.e., *ya*) is applied;
subsequently, the suffix *ac* is added according to the rule for words beginning with *arśas*.
Alternatively, the suffix *aṇ* is applied in the sense of "one who praises" (stotṛ);
there is no *vṛddhi* strengthening because of the rule "a grammatical operation conditioned by a technical designation (*saṃjñā*) is not mandatory.
[Thus, it means] "O Lord of the Rādhas."
*Radhāni* means riches (*dhanāni*), derived from the sense that "they are acquired by these.

According to the rule *subāmantrita*, because the status of being like a subsequent member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*) applies, there is the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) for the entire group consisting of the genitive and the vocative.
*Girvāhaḥ*.
The root *vah* means "to carry.
By the rule *vahādhābhyaśchandasi*, the suffix *asun* is applied to the root *vah*, even when it is preceded by a kāraka (object).
This is because it has been stated that "even in the case of a gati or a kāraka, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the preceding word is maintained."
Because the term *ṇit* is understood [from the previous rule], there is vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*).

Regarding the first member of the compound, [the rule] *vorupadhāyāḥ...* (Pāṇini 8.2.76) applies. [In the second member,] following the root *satatya-gamane* (Dhātupāṭha 1.459), there is the suffix *laṭ*, then *sip*, then *śap*; thus, by the rule *tiṣṭhater iti nighātaḥ*, there is the *nighāta* accent. (Note: The additional text provided in the manuscript variants 2, śa, ṣa is: "after the root 'sātatyagamane', there is *laṭ* in the *sip* form; *śap*; by the rule 'tiṣṭhateḥ', there is *nighāta*").
2.76) Thus, the absence of the long vowel is a Vedic (chāndasa) feature;
there is the acute accent on the first syllable of the vocative due to the rule for the sixth case-ending (pāṣṭhika).
[The word is] *vibhūtiḥ*.
By the rule "tādau ca niti," the verbal root retains its original accent (prakṛtisvara).
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Śatakratu;
let us two converse together in other matters as well.
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Śatakratu; let us two deliberate together on other matters.
O Śatakratu, you who are endowed with a hundredfold deeds, stand up—lofty and eager—for our protection in this engaged battle;
and you and I, having come together, shall deliberate thoroughly upon other matters at hand.
"Stay!"—
the long vowel [ā] occurs in the *saṃhitā* according to the rule "aco 'ntyam tiṅaḥ. For the sake of protection (*ūtaye*).
In the word *utiyūti* and so forth, the acute accent (*udāttatva*) is due to [the rule] beginning with *kin*. In this [word],
the acute accent of the locative case ending is due to [the rule] beginning with *aḍidam*.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we, as friends, invoke Indra, the most powerful one, for our protection.
In every conflict and in every fray, we, as friends, invoke Indra for our protection. 7.

In every yoga, at every entry, or at the commencement of each respective rite; in every battle that obstructs the performance of action—in each such conflict, we, your friends who are dear like brothers, invoke Indra, the most powerful of all, for our protection.
In the phrase *yoge-yoge*: the root *yuj* means "to join" (*yoge*). The suffix *ghañ* is applied according to the rule *halaśca*.

The substitution of *k* for *c* and *j* occurs by the rule *cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.52). Because the suffix *ghañ* belongs to the *bhi* group, it is accented on the first syllable. When reduplication occurs due to the distributive sense (*vīpsā*) according to the rule *nityavīpsayoḥ*, the first member is unaccented as it is followed by an *anudātta* vowel.
*Tavastaram*:
from the word *tavasa*, the suffix *vini* is added in the sense of possession according to Pāṇini’s rule 5.2.121 (*asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ*).
Its elision is Vedic.
May he indeed come hither if he hears us, with his thrice-sevenfold aids and with strengths,
to our invocation.
May he surely come if he hears us; may he approach our invocation with thousandfold aids and with strengths. ||8||
If Indra should hear this our invocation, then he himself would surely come near with thousands of protections, many aids, and with strengths—that is, with foods.
Ghā: by the rule "ṛci tunugha," etc., there is a long vowel in the *saṃhitā*.
Gamat.

"In the sense of the optative (liṅ), [the suffix] leṭ [is used]. By the rule "In leṭ, there is the augment aṭ," the augment aṭ is added. By the rule "And there is elision of the 'i'," the letter *i* is elided.

Alternatively, in the Vedic *luṅ* tense, there is the substitution of *aṭ* for *cli* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.55, "After roots beginning with *puṣ* and *dyut*, when followed by an *udit* [augment], in the *parasmaipada*. However, due to the rule "In the Veda, *aṭ* is frequently absent even when not joined with *māṅ*," the *aṭ* augment is omitted.
*śravat*.
[The root] *śru* is used in the sense of "hearing.
As before, the augment *aṭ* is applied in the *leṭ* mood.
With *vājebhiḥ*: the absence of *ais* for the beginning of the case-ending *bhis* occurs because of the rule "in the Veda (*chandasi*) it is frequent" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). [The word] *havam*.

By the rule *‘bhāve'nupasargasya’*, the suffix *ap* is added to the root *hā* with vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Since the suffix *ap* is marked with *p*, it is *anudātta*; consequently, by the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*), the word is *ādyudātta*.
1. *Jha-sa-ghā*:

Following the ancient dwelling, I invoke the hero of many manifestations, whom your father invoked of old. 9. Following the ancient dwelling, I invoke the hero of many manifestations, whom your father invoked of old. 9.
From the presence of the ancient, primordial abode—that is, the heaven-like place—I invoke in succession for my ritual acts Indra, the hero, the person who goes toward many sacrificers.
Him, that very Indra, whom our father, our progenitor, invoked in the past at the time of his own performance;
him I invoke—this is the connection with the preceding.
O friends!
[The word *naḍivapasya*] has its initial syllable accented according to the rule "naḍivapasya... etc. I invoke.
The root *heñ* is used in the sense of "striving" (*spardhā*) and "sound" (*śabda*).

According to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*). Although the *guṇa* substitution would normally apply, it is prohibited by the rule *kṅiti ca*.
There is the substitution of *ubaḍ*. It is oxytone by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). There is no suppression of tone (*anighāta*) because it occurs at the beginning of a *pāda*.
*Tuvipratim*:
one who goes toward (*pratigantāraṃ*) many (*tuvīnām*, i.e., *bahūnām*).
Here, the word *prati* indicates the word *pratigantṛ* (goer-toward), and by means of that [word], it indicates its meaning, just as in the case of "Bhīmasena" [indicating] "Bhīma."

Therefore, because *prati* denotes a substantive—as in Pāṇini’s sūtra 1.4.92, *pratiḥ pratinidhipratidānayoḥ*—it is not an indeclinable (*anipāta*). Consequently, since it is not an indeclinable (*anavyaya*), the prohibition of the genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*) by the rule *pūraṇaguṇa* (Pāṇini 2.2.11) and others does not apply.
[The form] *huve*:

from the root *hve*, in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), the semivowel is replaced by its corresponding vowel (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the preceding vowel is lengthened, according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*.
In the section concerning reduplication (*dvirvacana*), it should be stated that "in the Vedic language (*chandas*) there is an option" (*vā*); thus, there is an absence of reduplication.
Furthermore, because of its connection with *yadvat*, there is no lack of accentuation (*anighāta*).
We entreat you for that, O possessor of all boons, O much-invoked one—for friendship with you, O Vasu, for the sake of those who sing your praises. || 10 ||

O Viśvavāra, one who possesses all desirable things; O Puruhūta, invoked by many through their respective deeds; O Sakhe, friend-like beloved; O Vaso, Indra, the cause of our dwelling—[we] entreat you, who are endowed with the previously mentioned qualities, for the sake of favoring the jaritṛs, the singers of praise. We pray for you.
We pray (*ā śāsmahe*). [This is derived from] *āṅaḥ śāsu icchāyām* ("the root *śās* with the prefix *āṅ* in the sense of desiring").
By the rule *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*.
O Vasu!

Because of the rule "not [subject to accentual suppression] when followed by a word in apposition," the preceding word is not treated as non-existent; thus, since the status of being a subsequent member (parāṅtva) arises, there is either a total lack of acute accent (*sarvānudāttatva*) due to the *śeṣanighāta* rule or due to the rule "and [the vocative] of an *āmantrita*.
[The form] *jaritṛbhyaḥ*.
The root *jarati* has the meaning of "praising.
Because it belongs to the *tṛca* class, it has an udātta accent on the final syllable.

In the friendship of us who have broad foreheads, who drink Soma, O wielder of the thunderbolt, we are your friends. 11. Of us; of those with broad foreheads; of the Soma-drinkers; in the friendship; O wielder of the thunderbolt; of the friends. 11.

"O *somapāḥ*, drinker of Soma; O *sakhe*, friend-like beloved; O *vajrin*, wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra; [this] herd of cows belonging to us—our *sakhīnām*, friend-like beloveds; our *somapānām*, drinkers of Soma; our *śipriṇīnām*, possessed of long jaws or nostrils—is present through your grace," is the ellipsis.

In *śipriṇīnām*, the suffix *ḍīp* is applied by the rule "ṛṣebhyaḥ ḍīp. Since this suffix is marked with *p* (indicating it is *pit*), it receives an acute accent (*udātta*); consequently, the accent of the suffix remains as the final surviving accent.
*somapāḥ*: because it is a vocative (*āmantrita*), it receives the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) as it is prescribed by the rule for vocatives. *somapānām*.
The suffix *vanip* is applied by the rule *āto manin-kvanib-vanipaś-ca*.
By the rule *alloponaḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.134), there is the elision of the vowel *a* of the suffix *ana*.

1. *ga-ca-cha-jha-pha-ra-pratigacchantam*. 28. "So be it, O Soma-drinker; O friend, O wielder of the thunderbolt, act in such a way that we may desire your sacrifice. 12. So be it; O Soma-drinker, O friend, O wielder of the thunderbolt, act accordingly, so that we may desire your sacrifice. 12.

O Soma-drinker, O friend, O wielder of the thunderbolt, act in such a way that we may desire your favor for the attainment of our desired object; by your grace, let that which is wished for be so. [Grammatical derivation: Regarding *kṛṇu*: from the roots *kṛc* (injury) and *kṛ* (making), because it is marked with *it*, there is the augment *num*. By the rule "after *dhav* and *krumbh*, there is *u*" (*dhanvikrumbhyora ca*), there is the suffix *up*; simultaneously with that, the letter *v* becomes *a*. By the rule "elision of *a*" (*ato lopaḥ*), that [augment] is elided. Because of its status as a *sthānivat*, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel. By the rule "and after *ut* when the suffix does not have a conjunct consonant preceding it" (*utaśca pratyayādasayogapūrvāt*), there is the elision of *hi*. Regarding *uśmasi*: from the root *vaś* (to desire). By the rule "masi has *i* at the end," there is the suffix *masi*. Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision of *śap*. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule beginning with "pra-hi-jyā. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). As for *yadvattayo*... [text ends].

O Indra, a destroyer endowed with boldness, a divine being equal to yourself, being *dhamanāsaḥ*—that is, possessing the power of your favor—and being *iyānaḥ*, that is, entreated by us, for the sake of favoring our hymns (*stotrebhyaḥ*), may you surely (*gha*) bring and bestow (*ā ṛṇoḥ*) the desired object upon those who praise you.
Therein lies an illustration:
like the axle (*akṣam*) in the two wheels (*cakrayoḥ*) of a chariot.
Just as they cast the dice, so it is.

*tvāvān*: The suffix *vatup* is applied by the rule *‘vatupkaraṇe yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam’* (Pāṇini 5.2.39.1). By the rule *‘pratyayottarapadayośca’*, the form *tvā* replaces the portion of *yuṣmad* ending in *m*.

By the rule *ā sarvanāmnaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.91), the *d* of [the suffix] is replaced by *ā*. Since the suffix *vatup* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika-svara*) remains. This [accent] is what is left.
*manā*: there is elision of the vowel *ā* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.141, which states "in mantras, there is elision of the *ā* of *ātman* when preceded by a prefix. *ghno*.
The root *jighṛṣ* is used in the sense of audacity (*prāgalbhya*). According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.140, “*grasigṛdhripakṣipeḥ knuḥ*,” the suffix *knu* is applied [to these roots].
There is the unaccented (*anudātta*) quality of the vocative (*āmantrita*).
The word *iyānaḥ* [is derived from] the root *īṅ* in the sense of "going. [The suffix -śānac is applied] by Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.105: "In the Vedic language, the Liṭ [is used]."
For that [root], the substitute *kānac* is applied by the rule *liṭaḥ kānaj vā* (Pāṇini 3.2.106).
The substitution of *iyaṅ* is applied by the rule *aci śnudhātu* (Pāṇini 6.4.77) and so forth.
Because of the statement, "In the section on reduplication, it should be stated that in the Veda it is optional," the reduplication is not performed.
The word *citaḥ* has its final syllable udātta (accented).
[He] causes to move; [the root] *ṛṇ* means "to go."
In the *laṅ* [tense], by the transposition (*vyatyaya*) of *tip* for *sip*, there is the elision of the vowel *i* according to Pāṇini 3.4.100 (*itaśca*).
By Pāṇini 3.1.79 (*tanādikṛbhya uḥ*), the suffix *u* is applied;
this is followed by the *guṇa* substitution of the *sārvadhātuka* [affix].
The absence of the augment *aṭ* is due to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pi" (Pāṇini 6.4.75).
The word is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇasvara*). *Akṣam*.
The initial acute accent [of *akṣasya*] is due to the rule *akṣasyādevanasya* (Phiṭ-sūtra 35).
Regarding *cakrayoḥ*:
the substitution of *i* for the vowel *a* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).

O Śatakratu, when you, with your powers, have fulfilled the desire of the singers like a difficult path, as one opens a gate. 15. When, O Śatakratu, you fulfill the desire of the singers with your powers, as one [unlocks] a gate. 15.

O Indra, O Śatakratu, you bring that wealth which is desired by those who long for it and is to be obtained through the praises of the singers; you bestow that very desire upon the chanters as a favor.
You bring it and cast it [into their hands], just as one casts the axle into place with skillful actions—that is, with the specific operations appropriate for a cart. This is the illustration.
By means of the *śacīs*.
The word *śacī*, ending in the feminine suffix *ṅīn* according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 4.1.73, is udātta on its first syllable.

Evermore Indra has won riches with his snorting, roaring, and panting [steeds]. May he, the possessor of wondrous deeds, grant us a golden chariot; may he, our winner, give it to us for our gain. 16. Evermore. Indra. With snorting. He conquered. With roaring. With panting. Riches. He. For us. A golden-charioted. Possessor of wondrous deeds. He. For us. Our winner. For gain. He. To us. Has given. 16. Śaśvad indraḥ popruthadbhir jigāya nānadadbhiḥ śārśvasadbhir vardhanāni | sa no hiraṇyarathaṃ daṃsanāvān taṃ naḥ sanitā sanaye sa no 'dāt || 16 || Śaśvat | indraḥ | popruthadbhiḥ | jigāya | nānadadbhiḥ | śārśvasadbhiḥ | dhanāni | saḥ | naḥ | hiraṇyaratham | daṃsanāvān | saḥ | naḥ | sanitā | sanaye | saḥ | naḥ | adāt || 16 ||

Indra, being pleased, gave a golden chariot, which she accepted. And thus says the Brāhmaṇa: “To him Indra, being praised, joyfully gave a golden chariot; he went toward it with this [verse], ‘Ever indeed is Indra’” (AiB 7.16). Indra, *śaśvat*—that is, always—*jigāya*, i.e., conquered, the *dhanāni*, the riches belonging to his enemies; *aiḥ* is the ellipsis.
By what kind [of horses]?
By those "neighing loudly" (popruthadbhiḥ).
[Variant reading ḍha: Because they are [the means] for our favor.

With those "roaring" (nānadadbhiḥ), making the sound of their lips immediately after eating grass; with those "neighing" (nānadadbhiḥ), making the sound of neighing (heṣāśabda) from within their mouths; and with those "panting repeatedly" (śāśvasadbhiḥ);

[Indra], who is "possessed of deeds" (daṃsanāvān), being "the winner" (sanitā) or giver—*that Indra*, for our "acquisition" (sanaye), that is, for our enjoyment, "gave" (adāt) a "golden chariot" (hiraṇyaratha), a chariot fashioned out of gold. The repetition of "sa naḥ sa naḥ" is for the sake of emphasis.
By those nourishing [us].

Regarding *pothayadbhiḥ*: in the form *protha* with the suffix *paryāsau*, when the suffix *yaṅ* is elided (*yaṅluk*), there is the substitution of the remaining initial consonant for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa-halādiśeṣaḥ*).
When the shortening (*hrasva*) is applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.59 (*hasvaḥ*), the *guṇa* substitution is applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.82 (*aguṇo yaṅlukoh*).
The change of the penultimate vowel of the root to *u* is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
From this *yaṅ*-lopped form, when the suffix *śatṛ* is added, the first syllable receives the acute accent (*udātta*) by the rule "the beginning of reduplicated forms" (*abhyastānām ādiḥ*).
He conquered (*jigāya*).
[The root] *ji* means "to conquer.
In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), with the suffix *ṇal*, there is *vṛddhi*.
Due to the status as a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) by the rule *dvirvacane 'ci*, there is reduplication of the element *ji*.
