*Medhyātithiḥ*: In the *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "one whose guests (*atithayaḥ*) are pure (*medhyāḥ*)," there is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
*Dhanaspṛtam*.
He is called *dhanaspṛt* because he "satisfies" (*spṛṇoti*) or "pleases" (*prīṇayati*) us with riches;
[the root] *spṛ* is used in the sense of "pleasure" and "strength. The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule *kvip ca*.
Then [the suffix] *tuk* [is added];
it has the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member of the compound;
thus, *upastutaḥ*.

In the word *kaṭaka*, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the agent according to the rule *‘kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam’*; the acute accent on the final syllable of the compound is due to the rule *‘thāthādisvareṇa’*.

That Agni whom Medhyātithi Kaṇva kindled from the Truth—his offerings have shone forth; him these verses [gladden]; that Agni we magnify. 11. That Agni whom Medhyātithi Kaṇva kindled from the Truth—his offerings have shone forth; him these verses [gladden]; that Agni we magnify. 11.

Kaṇva, the seer whose guests worthy of sacrifice are the officiating priests (medhyātithi), having drawn [the fire] from Ṛta—that is, from Āditya—kindled that Agni. The *iṣas*—the rays of that Agni, whose nature is to move forward—shone forth; they blaze intensely.
Likewise, these *ṛcas* being employed by us augment that Agni; this is the ellipsis.
We too augment that Agni with our hymns of praise.
He kindled (*īdhe*).
[The root] *indh* means "to shine.
The perfect tense (*liṭ*) is applied by the rule *indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca* (Pāṇini 1.2.6).
Due to the presence of the *kittva* marker, there is the elision of the nasal *n* according to the rule *aniditām*.
Once the rules for the reduction of two vowels (*dvyac*) and the retention of the initial consonant (*ahalādiśeṣa*) have been applied, the *savarṇadīrgha* (long vowel of homogeneous quality) occurs.
This bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
Because of its connection with the *vṛtta* (meter), there is no loss of accent.
*Iṣaḥ*. [The root] *iṣ* means "to go."
They are called *iṣaḥ* (rays) because they go forth (*iṣyanti gacchanti*). They have shone; *dīdipuḥ* is a Vedic verbal root (*dhātu*) meaning "to shine" (*dīpti-karman*).
In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], there is the substitution of *iyaṅ*. The absence of the *yaṇ* substitution, as prescribed by the rule *eranekācaḥ*, is due to Vedic usage (*chāndasa*). [Thus:
*vardhayāmāsa*.
‘This is I’: thus we have declared our own month.
1. He who possesses such exceedingly pure sacrificial offerings as are fit for the sacrifice—O self-sustaining Agni, you indeed possess among the gods a share of wealth;
you are the king of glorious booty; as such, be gracious to us, for you are great.
Bestow wealth, O self-dependent one! For you, O Agni, possess kinship among the gods. You rule over renowned booty; as such, be gracious to us, for you are great. 12.

O Agni, you who possess *svadhā* and food—since the word *svadhā* is listed among your names in the Nirukta (2.7.17)—fill (*pūrdhi*) our riches (*rāyaḥ*), that is, bestow wealth upon us; for Yāska says: "Fill means 'fulfill' or 'bestow'" (Nirukta 4.3). O Agni, you indeed possess a friendship (*sakhya*) with the gods that is to be attained (*āpya*). You rule (*rājasi*) over the glorious (*śrutyasya*) or famous (*śravaṇīyasya*) prize (*vājasya*), which is to say, food. As such, do you favor (*mṛḷa*) us and grant us happiness; you are great, preeminent in virtues. Regarding the words: *Rāyaḥ*: The acute accent on the case-ending is by the rule *uḍidam*. *Pūrdhi*: From the root *pṛ* meaning 'to protect' or 'to fill'. The substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs by the rule *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaśchandasī*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the elision of the suffix *śap*. Since *hi* is not a *pit* affix, it is treated as *ṅit*, resulting in the absence of *guṇa*; then the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* occurs by *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*, and the lengthening by *hali ca*. *Svadhāvaḥ*: The *r* sound is substituted by the rule *saṃbuddhau matuvasoḥ*. *Āpyam*: Although it does not end in the suffix *an*, by transposition (*vyatyaya*), the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of the object by *poradupadhāt*. The initial acute accent is by *yato'nāvaḥ*. Alternatively, the initial acute accent is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*). *Śrutyasya*: From the root *śru* meaning 'to hear'. The suffix *kyap* is added by the *uṇādi* rules, followed by the augment *tug*. Alternatively, from the word *śruti*, the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of 'occurring therein' by *bhave chandasi*. *Mṛḷa*: From the root *mṛḍ* meaning 'to gladden'. Because the suffix *śa* is *ṅit*, there is no *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel.
For the raising of the sacrificial post (*yūpocchrayaṇa*), there are two verses beginning with "ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa utaye.
This is prescribed in the section titled "The Animal Sacrifice" (*paśāviṣṭi*) in the Sūtra: "ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa utaye iti dve" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.1).
These same two verses are also employed in the *abhiṣṭava* (the recitation of praise).

In the section titled "Now, the subsequent [portion]," it is stated in the Sūtra: "'O friend, come toward your friend; draw us upward; our aids are truly high'—these two [verses]" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.7).
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ;
standing erect as the winner of booty, when we call upon you with the fires and the priests.
Upright! "Ūm!"—stand up for our protection like the god Savitṛ, upright as the winner of booty, when we call upon you with the fires and the officiating priests. 13.
O sacrificial post (*yūpa*), or rather, O fire residing in the wood that constitutes the sacrificial post, stand upright for our protection— that is, for our preservation—
just as the god Savitṛ does.

Just as the divine Sun stands elevated, so too, being upright and exalted, you shall be the winner— the giver— of *vāja*, that is, of food. For this reason, with fires, with clarified butter, with the sacrificial post, and with the three priests (*vāghat*) who carry the sacrifice, we invoke you specifically for the sake of bestowing food.
Therefore, the connection with the preceding [verse] is: "Be a giver of sacrifice."
In *ū ṣu naḥ*,
there is a long vowel in the *saṃhitā* stage according to Pāṇini 6.3.134 (*ikaḥ suji*),
and the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* according to Pāṇini 8.3.107 (*sujaḥ*).
"naśca dhātusthoruṣubhyaḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.4.27).
1. Ḍha—for the preparation of the oblation.
Thus, there is the substitution of *ṇ*.
In the word *ūtaye*, from the root *av* (to protect), the suffix *ktin* is applied; by the rule "jvaratvara... and so forth, the vowel is changed to *ū*.
In the word *utiyūti* and so forth, the suffix *ktin* is acute by virtue of the rule beginning with *utiyūti*.
In the case of *tiṣṭha*, the substitution of *tiṣṭha* occurs by the rule beginning with *pāghrā* when the suffix *śap* follows.
The long vowel [in *vājasya*] is due to the rule *aco 'tiṅaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.130) regarding *saṃhitā*.

As for *vājasya*, because the word *vāja* is the object of the action, the sixth case is used in the sense of the fourth case (*saṃpradāna*) according to the rule *kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam* (Pāṇini 1.4.32).
The root *paṇ* means "to give.
In the *luṭ* [future] tense, the suffix *tāsi* is applied.
The augment *iṭ* is applied according to the rule for *valādi* (Pāṇini 7.2.35).
The substitution of *ḍā* for *tip* occurs according to Pāṇini 2.4.85.
There is the elision (*lopa*) of the *ṭi* portion.

By the rule for the accent of the cessation of the acute (*udāttanivṛttisvara*), the substitute *tiP* becomes acute; however, by the rule "the [affix] after *aT* is unaccented" (*atāsy-anudāttet*), that [substitute] becomes unaccented.
The accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
By the rule "not in the case of *luṭ*" (*na luṭ*, Pāṇini 8.1.29), the prohibition of the elision of the accent (*nighāta*) applies.

Regarding *akṣibhiḥ*: [the root] *akṣū* is used in the senses of manifestation (*vyakti*), opening (*akṣaṇa*), and movement (*gati*). The suffix *i* is applied according to the rule beginning with *khanikapyakṣi* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.579).

We invoke [him]. By the rule *ni-sam-upa-vi-bhyaḥ hreḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.30), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is employed even when the action does not benefit the agent. Since the root is taught with an initial *a*, the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, and thus the accent falls on the verbal root.
By the rule "tiṅi codāttavati," the verb [gacchati] would be unaccented; however, because it is connected with *yad-vṛtta*, it does not undergo suppression (anighāta).
Standing upright, protect us with your banner; burn up every devouring demon.
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us favor among the gods.
Stand upright; protect us from distress. With your banner, burn down every devouring demon. Raise us up so that we may move about and live. Find for us wealth among the gods. 14.
O sacrificial post (yūpa), whether it be that one or another, being most excellent and standing upright, protect us thoroughly from distress through your light—that is, through knowledge.
Completely consume every devourer, every consumer, the Rākṣasa; reduce him entirely to ashes.
Make us stand upright and exalted.
For what purpose?
For movement in the world, for wandering, and for our very life—to grant us wealth, that is, the oblation in the form of *havis*, among the gods; O finder, bestow it upon us!
*Atriṇam*:
[derived from] the root *ad* in the sense of "eating. The suffix *trin* is applied according to the Uṇādi Sūtra 4.508: *ade-ktini ca*. This is an Uṇādi formation.
Alternatively,
they are called *annāḥ* because they are eaten (*adyante*) by those who have not [yet] eaten;
the suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule *āto 'nupasarge kaḥ*.
Therefore, the suffix *ini* is used in the sense of possession (*matvarthīya*).

[The form] *kudhī* [is derived from *kudhi*, where] the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs according to the rule: "In the Veda, [the imperative endings] *hi* and *dhi* are substituted [for the imperative suffixes] after roots ending in *śru*, *śru*, *pu*, and *kṛ*."
The elision of the suffix occurs by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*;
the lengthening in the *saṃhitā* occurs by the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*. [Thus:
*ūrdhvān*.
Because of the optional rule *ubhayatharju* (Pāṇini 8.3.8), there is an absence of the substitution of *ru* for the *na* by the rule *naścavyapraśān* (Pāṇini 8.3.7).
[The form is] *carathāya*.
The suffix *atha*, which is *auṇādika*, is applied to the root *car* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*).
"Jīvase" [is used] in the sense of "to live. [The root] "jīva" means "to sustain life.
The suffix *ase* is applied according to the rule "tumarthe sesenū."

*Vidā*: from the root *vid* in the sense of "obtaining" (*lābhe*), with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it, in the *leṭ* mood with the suffix *sip*, there is the augment *āṭ* according to the rule *leṭo'ḍāṭau*.
The suffix *śa* is applied because [the root] belongs to the *tudādi* class.
The augment *num* does not occur by the rule “*śe sucādīnām*” because that rule is non-permanent (*anitya*), according to the statement “the teaching regarding augments is not permanent.
By the rule “*itaśca lopaḥ*,” there is the elision of the vowel *i*; and since the augment is unaccented, the accent of the verbal derivative (*vikaraṇasvara*) prevails.
1. And the letters *ca*, *cha*, *ṇa*, *ta*, *tha*, *pha*, *la*, *śa*, and *dhana*.

Protect us, O Agni, from the demon; protect us from the malicious enemy. Protect us from the one who pours forth [hostility] or from the one who seeks to kill us, O Bṛhaddāna (O you of great luster), O Most Youthful One! 15. Protect us, O Agni, from the demon; protect us from the malicious enemy. Protect us from the one who pours forth [hostility], or indeed from the one who seeks to kill us, O Bṛhaddāna, O Most Youthful One! 15.
O Agni, O you of great bounty, whose splendors are vast—O most youthful Agni, protect us from the *rakṣas*, from the obstructing demons and the like;
likewise, protect us from the malevolent thief who withholds wealth and other goods;
and likewise, protect us from the harmful one who seeks to injure us through travel and such.
Or rather, protect [us] from the enemy who desires to strike— that is, who wishes to kill—
from the deceitful ones;
for the root *dhūrv* has the meaning of "to injure."

In the case of the [root] *kṛc*, the suffix *ki* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartari*) by the rule "and when there is a technical name (*saṃjñāyaṃ*)"; the prohibition of *it* is by the rule beginning with "titutra" (Pāṇini 7.2.9);
and the elision of the letter *v* is by the rule "rālopaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.21).
The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule "hali ca.
[Thus we have] *arāṇṇaḥ*.
[The root] *rā* means "to give."
The suffix *vanip* is applied by the rule "āto manin... and so forth.
In the negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the initial member, which is an indeclinable (*avyaya*).
In the singular ablative case, the vowel *a* of the suffix *an* is elided according to the rule "alopo'naḥ."
From the root *rip*, meaning "to injure. [The suffix] *śatṛ* is applied to the present tense (*laṭ*).

By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is elision of the *śap* suffix. When the accent of the affix (*pratyayasvara*) would otherwise apply, the initial vowel is acute by way of metrical displacement (*vyatyaya*). [This applies to the form] *jighāṃsataḥ*.

In the case of the desiderative suffix *san* after the root *han*, there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.16 (*ajjhanagamāṃ sani*). By Pāṇini Sūtra 7.3.55 (*abhyāsācca*), the *ha* following the reduplication is changed to *gh*.
Then, by the rule *sannataḥ*, the short *i* is substituted [for the radical vowel].

Because it is taught as having an *ad*-affix (*adupadeśāt*), when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the *san* suffix— being marked with *n* (*nittvāt*)— causes the word to be accented on its first syllable by the rule for *nis-svara*. In *bṛhaddāno*,
the initial acute accent is optional according to the rule "and [the first syllable] of a vocative" (*āmantritasya ca*).
Because it begins with a *pādādi* (the first word of a quarter-verse), there is no elision (*nighāta*) of the *ādhamika* accent.
In *yaviṣṭhya*,
by the rule "sthūladūra" etc., there is the elision of the *yaṇ* and following sounds, and the substitution of *guṇa* for the preceding vowel.
The insertion of the letter *ya* is a Vedic archaism.

Like clouds, O all-pervading one, strike down the one who is alien, O you with the burning jaws! Let not that mortal enemy—who, like a mortal, whets his weapons excessively against us—have power over us. 16. Like clouds, O all-pervading one, strike down the one who is alien, O you with the burning jaws! Let not that mortal enemy—who, like a mortal, whets his weapons excessively against us—have power over us. 16.
O Agni, whose jaws are glowing and who possesses heating rays, O you who do not stay still, utterly strike down and especially slay those enemies who do not give us the wealth that is to be given.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like a woodcutter."
Just as one breaks vessels and the like with a hard object such as a staff or a stone, so it is here:
whatever other enemy (*ripu*) who is hostile to us (*asmad-druk*), that is, who commits acts of treachery against our domain, afflicts us with threats and the like;
and whatever other mortal (*martya*), a human enemy, sharpens his weapons (*akkubhiḥ*) excessively—that is, whets them to a fine edge and strikes at us.
May that enemy who inflicts insults and blows—both kinds of foe—not prevail over us; may he not be a master, nor have power over us.
"Like a cloud" (ghanāiva): the third case ending is replaced by the suffix -ḍā according to the rule "supāṃ suluk". [The command] "slay" (jahi).
In *hantarloṭi*, the substitution of *j* by the rule *hantejaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.36) occurs; because that [substitution] is treated as *asiddha*, there is no elision of *hi*. Thus: *tapurjambha*.
The root *tap* means "to heat.
It is derived from the *uṇādi* suffixes.

O Bṛhaddāna—one whose rays (*bhānavaḥ*) are great—O Yaviṣṭhya, most youthful one, [protect] us (*naḥ*); O Bṛhaddāna... such [one], O Yaviṣṭhya, most youthful one, [protect] us (*naḥ*); [save] us (*sa naḥ*).
2. Ḍha means "to injure."

The word *tapasu* ends in the suffix *usiṇ*; because it has the marker *ṇ*, it is *ādyudātta* (accented on the first syllable). The root *jabh* means "to destroy. Weapons are called *jambhāni* because enemies are destroyed (*jabhyante*) by them; this is formed with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). He whose weapons (*jambhāni*) are like fires (*tapūṃṣi*) is *taparjambhaḥ*. It takes the accent of the vocative (*āmantrita-ādyudāttatvam*). Regarding *asmadruk*: the root *druh* means "desire to harm" (*jighāṃsāyām*). By the rule *satsṛdvipa-* etc., the suffix *kip* is applied. By the rule *vā druhmuhasnuhasnihām* (Pāṇini 8.2.33), the letter *h* becomes *gh*. Then there is the substitution of *b* for *gh*. Regarding *śiśīte*: the root *śo* means "to sharpen" (*tanūkaraṇe*). The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by irregularity (*vyatyayena*). The elision (*ślau*) of the suffix occurs by the rule *bahulam chandasi*. There is the substitution of *ā* for *e* by the rule *ādeca upadeśe'śiti*. Then, in the reduplication (*dvirvacana*), the vowel *i* is substituted for the reduplicative syllable by the rule *bahulam chandasi* (Pāṇini 7.4.78). The substitution of *ī* occurs by the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*. By irregularity, it is *ādyudātta*. Because it is connected to *yad* (in *yad vṛtraṃ*), it does not receive the *anudātta* accent. Regarding *īśate*: in the *laṅ* tense, by the rule *bahulam chandasi*, there is no elision of the suffix *śap*. By the rule *na māṅyoge*, there is no addition of the augment *aṭ*.
Agni [granted] great heroism to Vana; Agni [granted] prosperity to Kaṇva;
Agni protected Mitra and Medhyātithi; Agni [protected] Upastuta at the winning of booty.
Agni [bestowed] great heroism in the forest; Agni [bestowed] prosperity upon Kaṇva. Agni protected both Mitra and Medhyātithi; Agni [protected] Upastuta in the winning of booty. 17.
The divine Agni was entreated in the forest for the sake of wealth endowed with excellent heroic power (*suvīrya*).
That Agni bestowed auspicious fortune (*saubhaga*)—consisting of excellent wealth and the like—upon the great seer Kaṇva; this is the sense to be supplied.
Likewise, Agni has eminently protected our friends (*mitrāḥ*).
Moreover, he protected the sage who had approached as a guest worthy of the sacrifice (*vamedhya*), accompanied by guests fit for the sacrifice;
likewise, he protected another who was praised—the singer or sacrificer—for the sake of winning wealth and other gifts—this is the implied sense.
In the root *van*,
meaning "to request" (*yācana*),
the perfect tense (*liṭ*) is used in the passive voice (*karmaṇi*).

By the rule *na śasadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126), there is a prohibition against the substitution of *e* for *ai* and the elision of the reduplicated syllable. The elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*) is Vedic. Thus, *saubhagam*.

Because of its inclusion in the list beginning with *udātta* in the rule *subhagān mantre* (Pāṇini 4.1.74), the suffix *añ* (Pāṇini 5.1.129) is applied in the sense of "the state of being that"; due to the marker *j*, the word is accented on the first syllable. Thus: *mitrā*.
The elision of the suffix *śe* occurs by the rule "śecchandasi bahulam.
[The form] *upastutam* [is derived as follows]: the suffix *ka* is applied to the root *stu* in the sense of the agent by the rule "kiccā ca saṃjñāyām."
By the rule *thāthādinā*, the final syllable of the compound receives the udātta accent.
By means of Agni, we call Turvaśa and Yadu from afar, as well as Ugrādeva;
may Agni lead Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turvīti as a force of power against the Dasyu.
With Agni we call Turvaśa, Yadu, and Ugradeva from afar. May Agni lead Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turviti against the Dasyu with conquering might. 18.
By means of Agni, we invoke from afar—from a distant land—the royal seers named Turvaśa, Yadu, and Ugradeva.
And that Agni brought here the royal seers named Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turviti.
Of what nature is Agni? He is the subduer of the Dasyu, the overcomer of him who is the cause of our affliction.
He led. [The root] *ṇīñ* is used in the sense of "leading. In the *leṭ* mood, the augment *aṭ* is applied.
By the rule "itaśca lopaḥ," there is the elision of the vowel *i*.
[The term] *navavāstvam* means that which has nine sites (*vāstu*). Thus, he is one who possesses nine sites.
[Ma. 1. a. 8. sū. 36] First Chapter, 277: *navavāstuḥ*.

Because of the continued application of the rule "vā chandasi" (Pāṇini 6.1.106), there is the substitution of *y* for the vowel in the absence of the *pūrvarūpa* (single-substitute) operation before the accusative singular ending *am*.
*bṛhadratha*. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratva*) applies.
Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for all people forever;
you shone forth, O Kaṇva, born of Truth, strengthened by the people who pay homage to you.
O Agni, Manu established you as a light for all people forever; you shone forth among the Kaṇvas, born of Truth and grown strong, you whom the peoples revere. 19.

O Agni, Manu, the Lord of Progeny, established you—whose form is light and radiance—for the sake of the eternal, manifold people, within the place for the sacrifice to the gods. O Agni, born of *ṛta* (the cosmic order) through the sacrifice as its instrumental cause, nourished and gratified by oblations, you shone forth among the sage Kaṇva, who bears that name. That very Agni whom the *kṛṣṭayaḥ*, the human beings...
Because "kṛṣṭayaḥ" and "carṣaṇayaḥ" are listed among the names for humans in Nirukta 2.3.7,
they "namasyanti," meaning they pay homage or offer salutations.
The word "sa" (he) connects with the preceding part of the sentence.
*dīdetha*. The root *dīdeti* is used in the Veda (*chāndasa*) in the sense of shining.

Regarding the suffix *thali*, there is the doubling [of the root] according to the rule: "In the section on reduplication, it should be stated that in the Veda it is optional" (Kātyāyana-vārttika 6.1.8.1). Thus, the state of reduplication occurs.
The absence of the *iṭ* augment follows from the statement, "The teaching of the Āgamas is impermanent.
By the accent rule for the *liṅ* suffix, the syllable preceding the suffix is udātta.
[The word is] *ṛtajātaḥ*.
He is born from the *ṛta* (cosmic order), thus he is "born of the *ṛta*" (*ṛtajāta*).
The prohibition of the *it*-augment applies here according to the rule "śrīditaḥ niṣṭhāyām. The substitution of *ā* for the vowel occurs by the rule beginning with "janasana."
The third [rule] concerns the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the preceding member.
[In the word *namasyanti*: "They pay homage. [This is derived] by adding the suffix *kyac* in the sense of worship, according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.19: *namo-varivasas-karoti-jīvātubhyaḥ kyac*.
Because it is taught as having an *ad*-suffix, when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the accent falls on the root-final vowel of the verbal root ending in *vy*.
Thus: *kṛṣṭayaḥ*.
[The root is] *kṛp* in the sense of "plowing" (*vilekhane*).
The suffix *kic* is applied by the rule "kiccaktau ca saṃjñāyām" (Pāṇini 3.3.174).
Flashing forth are these impetuous flames of Agni, terrible and not to be withstood;
burn up every devouring demon, the sorcerer who seeks to strike us down.
The flickering, powerful flames of Agni are like terrors; they are not to be withstood by the Rakṣasas. Always burn every sorcerer and every devouring fiend.

The flames (*arcayaḥ*) of Agni are flickering (*tvepāsaḥ*), blazing, impetuous (*amavantaḥ*), powerful, and formidable (*bhīmāsaḥ*). Therefore, they are "not to be approached" (*na... pratītaye*); the ellipsis implies that they cannot be encountered by us. O Agni, always (*sadamit*) burn up and reduce to ashes the powerful *rakṣasvinḥ*, the sorcerers (*yātumāvataḥ*) who are demons; likewise, burn up every (*viśvam*) devouring (*atriṇam*) enemy who oppresses us. Regarding the words: * *Tvepāsaḥ*: From the root *tviṣ* (to shine). The suffix *ac* is added according to Pāṇini 3.1.134 (*pacādyac*). By the rule *citaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.163), the word is oxytone. * *Amavantaḥ*: From the root *am* (to afflict). *Amaḥ* is strength, because it overcomes or strikes down enemies. The suffix *ac* is added (*pacādyac*). It is ādyudātta (accented on the first syllable) because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* class. Those who possess this are *amavantaḥ*. * *Pratītaye*: In the compound *prati-itaye*, the prefix *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratvam*) according to Pāṇini 6.2.49 (*tādau ca niti*). * *Rakṣasvinḥ*: That by which one protects is *rakṣaḥ* (strength). The suffix *sun* is used in the sense of an instrument. The possessive suffix *viniḥ* is added according to Pāṇini 5.2.121 (*asamāyāmedhā*). * *Yātumāvataḥ*: *Yātavaḥ* means movements or wanderings. Those who perform these are the activities of Rākṣasas, called *yātumāḥ*. The suffix *ā* is added according to Pāṇini 3.2.3 (*āto'nupasarge*). [Note: The final portion of the provided Sanskrit commentary appears to be an incomplete grammatical derivation for *yātumāḥ*.]

1. *śa-ṛtena*. What is "ka"? It is "ka". The suffix *matup* is added because it is thought that this [quality] exists in him (*tad eṣām asti*). There is lengthening by Pāṇini 6.3.119: *matau bahv-añ-jirādīnām*. There is the substitution of *va* by Pāṇini 8.2.11: *saṃjñāyām*. Since the suffix *matup* is unaccented due to being included in the *pit* class, the original accent of the final member of the compound is maintained (*kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svara*). [The word is] *atraṇam*. The suffix *trin* is added in the sense of the agent according to the rule *adestrini ca*. || 11 ||
The second hymn, "krīḷaṃ vaḥ," consists of fifteen verses.
Regarding this, the index (anukramaṇikā) states: "krīḷaṃ [is] five less; it belongs to the Maruts and is in the Gāyatrī meter.
According to the technical rule (paribhāṣā), "the seer is distinguished by being other than [the subject of] the preceding [hymn]," the seer is Kaṇva, the son of Ghora.
This and the following [verse] are in the *gāyatrī* meter.
These first three hymns have the Maruts as their deity, because it is defined by the rule "tuhi-havā" [etc.].
In the expanded (*vyūḍha*) second *chandoma*, this hymn is to be inserted with the *nivid* in the *ābhimāruta-śastra*.
In the section beginning with "dvitīyasyāmi vo devam," it is sūtra-ed: "krīḷaṃ vaḥ śardho agne mūle—this is for the Ābhimāruta [offering]" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.10).
And the Brāhmaṇa states: "krīḷaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutam" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 5.19).
In this iṣṭi, regarding the offering "to the playful Maruts, a cake on six potsherds," the verse "krīḷaṃ vaḥ" serves as the invitatory prayer (anuvākyā) for the principal oblation.
In the section beginning with "tathā tataḥ," it is aphoristically stated: "krīḷaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutam ayāso na ye marutaḥ svañcaḥ" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.18).
Sing forth, O Kaṇva, to your sporting host of Maruts, the unassailable, who shine upon their chariots!
Sing forth, O Kaṇvas, to the sportive host of Maruts, the unassailable, adorned with chariots! 1.

*He kaṇvaḥ*: the great seers born of the Kaṇva lineage; or alternatively, the wise officiating priests (*ṛtvij*). *Vaḥ*: for your sake, *mārutam śardhaḥ*—the host or force consisting of the Maruts—*abhipragāyata*: sing forth [songs] toward them in praise. What kind of host? *krīḷam*: playful by nature; *anarvāṇam*: free from heat or distress. For this very reason, another mantra in a different Brāhmaṇa is explained thus: "He says, 'Go, O unassailable one' (*anarvā prehi*), for the ass is indeed afflicted by heat; [this is said] to remove that distress" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6.3.8.4). *ratheśubham*: shining while stationed upon their own chariot. *krīḷam*: from the root *krīḍ* (to sport); with the suffix *ac* (Pāṇini 3.1.134). *śardhaḥ*: from the root *śṛdh* (to overpower); that by which one overpowers enemies is *śardhaḥ*, meaning strength. With the suffix *asun*, there is acute accent on the first syllable due to the *niṅ* designation. *Mārutam*: belonging to the Maruts; the suffix *aṇ* is applied according to Pāṇini 4.3.120 (*tasyedam*), and there is a shift in accent to the first syllable. Alternatively, in the sense of a collection, the suffix *añ* is applied according to Pāṇini 4.2.44 (*anudāttāder añ*) because it begins with an unaccented vowel. *Anarvāṇam*: a shift to the masculine gender; the final syllable of the compound is accented according to Pāṇini 6.2.172 (*nañsubhyām*). *Ratheśubham*: from the root *śubh* (to shine); that which shines on the chariot is *ratheśubh*. With the suffix *kip* (Pāṇini 3.2.76), and the non-elision of the *a* vowel according to Pāṇini 6.3.14 (*tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam*). The accent is that of the original form of the second member of the compound. *Gāyata*: from the roots *kai*, *gai*, or *rai* (to sound); the verb is unaccented according to Pāṇini 8.1.28 (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*).
Those who were born with self-effulgence, together with spotted deer, spears, axes, and glittering ornaments.
Those who were born together with spotted deer, spears, axes, ointments, and self-luminous splendor. ||2||

The connection is that those Maruts, together with the spotted deer and the others, were born "svabhānavaḥ," meaning endowed with their own splendors. The *pṛṣatyaḥ* are spotted female deer who serve as the vehicles of the Maruts, as stated in the *Nighaṇṭu*: "The spotted deer belong to the Maruts" (1.15.6). The *ṛṣṭayaḥ* are weapons. The *vāśyaḥ* are specific sounds that cause terror in the enemy armies; for it is listed among the names for speech in the *Nighaṇṭu*: "The axe (*vāśī*) is speech" (1.11.11). The *añjyaḥ* are ornaments. The ellipsis is "we praise them. Regarding the form *ajāyanta*: from the root *jan* in the sense of "manifestation," the suffix *iyac* is applied. By Pāṇini’s rule 7.3.79, *jñānajorj*, there is the substitution of *ja* for the root vowel. The augment *ad* is acute-accented. Regarding *svabhānavaḥ*: this means "those whose splendors (*bhānavaḥ*) are their own (*svakīyāḥ*). In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent remains on the original accent of the first member.
1. The word "iti" does not exist [in the manuscript marked] ḍha.

2. Ḍha: The causes of confusion regarding another's army: "Just as one hears here, so too their whips are in their hands; when they speak, they direct their brilliant [chariot] toward the goal. (3) iha'iva | śruṇe | eṣām | kaśāḥ | hastaiṣu | yat | vadān | ni | yārman | citram | ṛñjate ||3||

I hear right here, standing in this very place, the sound—which they utter and which they produce—of those great ones whose whips rest in their hands for the purpose of striking their respective mounts.

That particular sound, in battle, exceedingly adorns (*ni-vṛñjate*) their various (*citram*) and manifold heroism (*śauryam*). Yāska [states]: “The root *ṛñj* has the sense of adorning (*prasādhanakarmā*). (Nirukta 6.21).
Śruṇe; from the root *śru* in the sense of "hearing," the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by way of transposition.
By the rule *śruvaḥ śra ca*, *śru* is substituted;
by the rule *huśruvoḥ sārvadhātuke*, the *yaṇ* substitution occurs, resulting in *vadān*.
The root *vad* means "in distinct speech.

In the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, there is the augment *āṭ*. Following the rule "there is elision of the *i* [of *it*] after this," the *i* is elided, and then the final consonant of the conjunct (*saṃyogānta*) is elided.

They have gone. Regarding *jambhe*: from the root *jabhi* meaning "to destroy. That by which something is destroyed or consumed is called *jamman*, namely the mouth; the suffix *ghañ* is used here in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*). Regarding *vavṛdhe*: from the root *vṛdh* meaning "to grow"; this is the perfect tense (*liṭ*). The lengthening of the vowel in the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is a Vedic (*chāndasa*) feature in the *saṃhitā*. || 13 ||

Who among you, O heroes, shakers of heaven and earth, is the most exalted, when you shake them as if shaking the hem of a garment? 6. Who? Of you? Most exalted? Hither? O heroes? Of heaven? And of earth? O shakers? When? That very hem? As it were? You shake? 6.

O Maruts, leaders and shakers, among you—who is the most exalted (*varṣiṣṭhaḥ*), the greatest, [ruling] over both heaven (*divaḥ*) and earth (*gmaḥ*)? For *gauḥ* and *gmā* are listed among the names for the earth in the Nighaṇṭu (1.1.2). O leaders (*naraḥ*), who is the most ancient among you?
Since you shake [her] from all sides, like the tip of a tree, for that reason, the question is:
who among you shakers is the most powerful?

*Varṣiṣṭhaḥ*: From the word *vṛddha*, when the suffix *iṣṭhan* is added, the substitution *varṣa-* occurs according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.157 (*priyasthirasphirorubahulaguruvṛddhatṛpradīrghavṛndārakāṇāṃ prasthasphavarbahigarvarṣitrabdrādhivṛndāḥ*). It is udātta on the first syllable because it begins with a *niṅ*.

*gmaḥ*: From the word *gmā*, in the sixth case singular, there is elision of the vowel *ā* because it has been stated that "in the rule *āto dhātoḥ*, a separation of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*) must be made for the term *āt*" (Kāśikā 6.4.140). The accentuation of the case ending is due to the *udāttanivṛttisvara*. *dhūtayaḥ*.
The root *dhūñ* means "to shake.
The suffix *kvin* is applied by the rule *kvinkau ca saṃjñāyām*. By the rule *titutra* etc., there is a prohibition of the *it*-augment.
By the rule "āmantritasya ca," there is the state of being entirely unaccented (sarvānudātta).
[The form] is *dhūnutha*.
[The suffix] *kṣu* is applied after roots beginning with *su*.

According to the rule "The accent of that which is subsequently prescribed is stronger, except in the case of suffixes," even an accent subsequently prescribed for a suffix (*vikaraṇa*) does not override the accent of the *l*-affix *sārvadhātuka*.
Therefore, the accent belongs to *atam* alone.
Its lack of *nighāta* (absence of suppression) is due to its connection with the word *yat*.

A mortal has submitted himself to your march, to your fierce wrath; the mountain, the rocky peak, has yielded. 7. A mortal has submitted himself to your march, to your fierce wrath; the mountain, the rocky peak, has yielded. 7.

O Maruts, for your journey—meaning for the sake of your coming—a certain human householder has firmly set up a pillar to support his home, fearing that the house would collapse due to the shaking caused by your passage; thus, he has cast down this firm pillar as a means of prevention. Of what sort of journey?
To the fierce and intense wrath, which considers itself capable of shaking [the world];
for fear indeed arises from your coming.
For by your movement, the mountain—endowed with many kinds of peaks, a peaked hill—would tremble and depart.
*Mānuṣaḥ*: [This is derived] from the word *manu* by adding the suffix *añ* in the sense of offspring and the augment *puK*, according to Pāṇini Sūtra 4.1.161 (*manorjātāvanyatau puk ca*).
By the rule "the first syllable is always udātta" (*ntyādirnityam*), it has an udātta accent on its initial syllable.

*dadhre*. This is from the root *dhṛñ* in the sense of "remaining steady" (*avasthāne*), in the *liṭ* (perfect) tense; because the suffix is marked with *k*, there is an absence of *guṇa*, and the substitution of *yaṇ* occurs. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
There is no *nighāta* because it begins with a word-initial (*pādādi*). [The form] *jihītaḥ* [is derived from] the root *ohāṅ* in the sense of "going."
In the optative (*liṅ*), due to its inclusion in the *juhoty-ādi* class, there is the substitution of *ślu* for *śap*.
By the rule "bhrāmit" (Pāṇini 7.4.76), the penultimate vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes short *i*. Then, by the rule "bhābhyastayorātaḥ," there is the elision of the long *ā*.
*Parvavān* means "mountain" (*parvata*);
it is formed by adding the possessive suffix *tap* in the sense of possession.

On whose goats the earth trembles in fear during their journeys, like a ruler of the people who has fled. 8. On whose goats; on the goats; the earth; like one who has fled; the lord of the people; through fear; on the journeys; trembles. 8.
O Maruts, at whose journeys—those movements consisting of unyoked projectiles—the earth trembles and shakes;
therein the simile is:
like a ruler of the people who has fled in haste.
Just as an aged king who protects his subjects trembles out of fear of enemies due to the decline of his youth and the onset of disease, so it is in this case.
In the word *ajeṣu*:
[the root] *aja* is used in the senses of "going" and "throwing.
Due to the inclusion of the term *bahulam* (in various ways), the suffix *man* is applied according to the *Uṇādi* rules.

The substitution of *vī* does not occur [for the root *ji*] by the rule "ajevyaṅjapoḥ" (Pāṇini 2.4.56), because of the statement: "In the case of affixes beginning with *va*l, the option is desired for the *ardhadhātuka* suffixes" (Kāśikā on 2.4.56).
Due to the *niṭ* augment, the word is udātta-accented on the first syllable.
*jujurvān*:
from the root *jṛṣ* in the sense of "loss of vitality," with the suffix *kasu* applied after the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*).

The substitution of *u* for *i* occurs by Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.103, "bahulam chandasi. The *halādiśeṣa* (retention of the first consonant) applies to the reduplicated syllable. There is no addition of the augment *iṭ* due to the restriction "vastrekājād dhātoḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.67).

The *guṇa* substitution [of *ṛ* for *ṝ*] occurs by the rule *ṛcchayṛtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), and the lengthening [of the vowel] by *hali ca* (Pāṇini 6.3.111) does not take place because of the maxim *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*. Thus we have *viśāṃ patiḥ* as *viṣpatiḥ*.

Although the original accent of the first member (*prakṛtisvara*) would apply by the rule *patyāvaiśvarye*, the acute accent on the initial syllable of the second member (*uttarapadādyudāttatvam*) is applied by the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*.
*bhiyā* (out of fear):
according to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the case-ending (*vibhakteḥ*) is udātta. *yāmeṣu*.
The root *yam* is used in the sense of "restraint.
The suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
Although the rule "karṣātvato ghañaḥ" would have required the final syllable to be udātta, its initial syllable is udātta because the word is listed among the *vṛṣādi* group.
*rejata*. [The root] *rej* means "to tremble.
Because it is taught with an initial vowel (*adupadeśa*), the *lasārvadhātuka* suffix is unaccented, and thus the accent falls on the verbal root (*dhātusvara*).
Non-stress occurs due to its connection with the following syllable.
For their birth from the mother is indeed firm, so that they may reach their full span of life;
for Śarva has twice followed after them.
For firm indeed is their vigor to emerge from the mother; for a second time, they have followed her power.

The birthplace (*jana*)—the place of origin—of these Maruts is the sky (*ākāśa*), for it is indeed *sthiram*, motionless. From that mother—the sky, which stands in the place of the progenitor of the Maruts—the *vayaḥ*, the birds, are able to *niretave*, to fly forth; this is the ellipsis.
Thus, "their birth is from such a sky" is the praise of the Maruts.

Because (*yat*) for that reason your force (*śavaḥ*), in due order (*anukrameṇa*), exists (*sī*) on both sides (*dvitā*) everywhere (*sarvataḥ*), having divided itself between heaven and earth; therefore, "your power (*jāna*) is indeed firm (*sthiram hi*)"—this is the connection with what precedes.
*Jāna*: that in which something is born (*janyate 'smin*) is *jāna*, namely the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). The suffix *ghañ* is used here in the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇe*).
In the case of these [pronouns],

the substitute *aś* for *idam*— by the rule "in a subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), [the substitute] for *idam*"— is unaccented (*anudātta*). Furthermore, the case-ending (*vibhakti*) is also unaccented because it belongs to the category of *sup* (nominal suffixes).
Nor is there an acute accent on the case-ending by the rule "aḍidam 0" and so forth, because that [rule] is prescribed for the word *idam* when it is oxytone (*antodātta*). [The form] *niretave*:
[the root] *iṇ* means "to go."
The suffix *taven* is applied by the rule "tumarthe śeṣeṇa";
and by the rule "tādau ca," the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the root *gam* (in the form *gati*) is preserved.
These sons have extended their songs like racing steeds toward the goal, lowing as they go on bended knees.
The stars—Om!—these sons have extended their songs like goal-posts in their courses, lowing as they go on bended knees. 10.
These aforementioned "songs" (*giraḥ*) are the "sons," that is, the Maruts who produce speech;
for it is the winds (*vāyavaḥ*), moving within the palate, lips, and other vocal organs, that generate speech.
While their own "courses" (*ajmeṣu*), meaning movements, are occurring, they [reach] the "limits," that is, the waters.
"Water is also called *kāṣṭhā*, for it stands firm," says Yāska (Nirukta 2.15). "They have stretched it out (*atata*)—that is, they have extended it upward with excellence.

Having spread out the water, they impelled the lowing cows (*vāśrāḥ*)—cows possessing the sound of lowing—to go toward the knees (*abhijñu*), that is, so as to be directed toward their knees, in order to cross over; this is the sense to be supplied.
*Sūnavaḥ*: [derived from] the root *pū* in the sense of "impelling. The suffix *sup* is applied according to the rule *sūvaḥ kit* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.315).
Due to the presence of the *kittva* designation, there is an absence of *guṇa*. [The form] is *atata*;
[the root] is *tanu* in the sense of "expansion."
In the *laṅ* [tense], *jha* is replaced by *ad*; the *vikaraṇa* suffix is elided by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 2.4.73).
The penultimate vowel is elided by the rule "tanipatyośchandasi" (Pāṇini 6.4.99). The augment *aṭ* is added.
*Abhijñu*:
one whose knees (*jānunī*) have gone together (*abhigata*) is *abhijñu*.

According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 5.4.129, *prasaṃbhyāṃ jānuno'rjuḥ*, the word *jānu* following the prefix *abhi* undergoes the substitution of *jñu* as a compound-ending suffix (*samāsānta*), even though the rule specifically mentions the prefixes *pra* and *sam*. Thus, by way of transference (*vyatyayena*), the word *jānu* after *abhi* is replaced by *jñu*.
For the word *yātave*: the suffix *taven* is applied in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) by the rule "sesen...
etc.; it is acute-accented on the first syllable because it is *nic*.

Come forth with your swift horses; there are dwellings for you among the Kaṇvas. Rejoice there indeed!
Come hither with your swift steeds to the one with the beautiful head; for you have dwellings among the Kaṇvas. There, indeed, may you rejoice well.

O Maruts, come quickly with your swift and impetuous steeds—“*śībham*” being listed among the names for “quickly” in *Nirukta* 2.15.9—proceed to the sacrificial ground, the field of action. Among the Kaṇvas, the wise performers of the rites, there are your services (*durvaḥ*), that is, your acts of attendance. Rejoice (*mādayādhvai*) and be satisfied right there among those serving attendants, the Kaṇvas. Regarding the words: *Āśubhiḥ*: from the root *aś* (to pervade); the suffix *uṇ* is applied by the rule *kṛvāpājī* etc.; the accent is that of the suffix. *Santi*: the elision of the vowel *a* occurs by the rule *bhasoralopaḥ*. *Mādayādhvai*: from the root *mad* (in the sense of satisfaction); it belongs to the *cur*-class, is *ākusmīya*, and is *ātmanepada*. In the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, the augment *āṭ* is added; the final *ṭi* becomes *e*; and by the rule *vaitonyatra*, the single *e* is replaced by the diphthong *ai*.
For indeed there is [a draught] for your exhilaration; may we truly partake of these [Somas], so that we may live out the full span of life.
Truly, there was [joy] for your exhilaration; we have indeed attained all of these.
Long life!
May you live!
O Maruts, this oblation (dhma) being offered by us exists indeed for your exhilaration and satisfaction;
we are truly your servants, as we know well.
Grant us all life, even the full span of existence, so that we may live—this is the sense of the remainder.
In the *saṃhitā*, there is a long vowel by the rule "and [the substitution of a long vowel occurs] for a particle" (*sma*).
[The form] is *smasi*; [here] the suffix *mas* ends in *i*.
For the purpose of living; the suffix *ase* is applied according to the rule "tumarthe śeṣena."

The third hymn, consisting of fifteen verses beginning with “*kadrū nūnam*,” has Kaṇva, the son of Ghora, as its seer (*ṛṣi*), because of the technical rule stating, “and the seer [is named] from another [source]. Furthermore,
since the previous hymn mentions the Maruts with the words “*marutaṃ hi*,” this hymn also has the Maruts as its deity.
Because it is stated that "it is indeed Gāyatra," it possesses the Gāyatrī metre; "Kadrū" is the entry in the Anukramaṇikā;
the application [of the mantra] is indicated by its internal characteristics (liṅga).
O you who love the sacred grass, surely your father Kadrū shall now hold you in his hands, as one holds a son, O you for whom the sacrificial grass is trimmed.
When indeed will you take us by the hands, as a father takes his dear son, O you for whom the sacrificial grass is trimmed? 1.

O Maruts, when indeed will you surely hold us in your hands? You hold us in your hands. Therein is an illustration: "as a father his son in his hands," just as in the world a father holds his own son in his hands, so [do you]. Of what nature are the Maruts? *kadhapriyaḥ*: pleased by praise; *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*: those for whom the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) has been cut (*vṛkta*) for the sake of the sacrificer—such are the Maruts. *kat*: "When? (*kadā*). Because it is stated, "And there are two others: modification and elision of letters" (*kā. 6. 3. 109*), there is the elision of the vowel *ā*. Thus, *kadhapriyaḥ*. *Kathā* means praise. They please by that, hence *kadhapriyaḥ*. From the root *prīñ* (to please), with the suffix *kip*. The shortening of the first member is according to Pāṇini 6.3.63: "In names and in the Veda, the long vowels *ī* and *ā* are frequently shortened. The letter *dh* is a Vedic archaism. The *āmantrita-nighāta* (the accentual suppression of the vocative) applies. *dadhidhve*: from the root *dhā*, in the sense of the present tense, the suffix *liṭ* is used according to the rule "In the Veda, the *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* suffixes may be used for the present. By the rule governing roots beginning with *krī*, the augment *iṭ* is added. The accent is that of the suffix. *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*: the *āmantrita-nighāta* applies.
1. Ḍha—in those very places;
2. Ḍha—in one's own hands;
3. Ḍha—for the sacrifice of those Maruts.

4. To whom indeed, to what purpose do you go from heaven as if to earth? Whom do you delight, like cows? || 2 || To whom? Indeed. What? From there. For what purpose? Go. From heaven. As if to earth. Whom? You. Like cows. Delight. || 2 ||

O Maruts, "now indeed" (*anūnam idānīm*), "where are you?"—that is, where are you situated? "When"—that is, at what time—"is your *araṇam*," your journey to the region of the gods? The meaning is: do not delay! "From heaven" (*divaḥ*), go from the world of light; "from earth" (*pṛthivyāḥ*), do not go from the world of mortals. "Who" (*ka*) "calls you" (*raṇyanti*)? Where else but on earth, which consists of the divine folk, do they call you? The sacrificers praise you. Therein is an illustration: "like cows" (*gāvo na*). Just as cows low (*raṇanti*), so [do they call]. From the interrogative pronoun *kim*, in the locative case (*saptamyantāt*), the suffix *apratyaya* is added by Pāṇini 5.3.12 (*kimot*). By Pāṇini 7.2.105 (*kāti*), there is the substitution of *kā* for *kim*. It is svarita according to the rule "tisvaritaḥ. Regarding *artham*: the root *ṛ* means "to go. The suffix *than* is added in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*) by Uṇādi-sūtra 2.161 (*upikuṇigātibhyaścan*). Because of the *ni*-augment, it is udātta on the first syllable. Regarding *ganta*: from the root *gam* in the imperative (*loṭ*), the *śap* suffix is elided by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi. For the replacement *thā*, there is the substitution of *ta* by the rule "tasanasanathanāśca. Precisely because of this absence of reduplication (*dvitvābhāvāt*), there is no loss of the nasal by the rule "anudāttaupadeśa... etc. Since the suffix is *pit*, it is anudātta, and thus the accent of the root remains. By the rule "vyo'talmiṅaḥ," there is lengthening in the *saṃhitā* form. Regarding *divaḥ*: the case ending is udātta by the rule "uḍiḍam. Regarding *pṛthivyāḥ*: the case ending is udātta by the rule "udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt. Regarding *raṇyanti*: the root *raṇati* means "to sound. The *śyan* suffix is used by way of transposition (*vyatyayena*).

Whose are your human-like favors, O Maruts? Whose are your blessings? And whose are all your auspicious fortunes? 3. Whose? Of you? The favors? Human-like? O Maruts? Whose? The blessings? And whose? All? The auspicious fortunes? 3. Whose are your human-like favors, O Maruts? Whose are your blessings? And whose are all your auspicious fortunes? 3. Whose? Of you? The favors? Human-like? O Maruts? Whose? The blessings? And whose? All? The auspicious fortunes? 3.

O Maruts, where are your ever-new, human-like favors (*sumnā*)—wealth consisting of progeny and cattle; for another Śruti states, "Progeny indeed, and cattle, are *sumna*" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5.4.6.6)?
And where are your beautiful, attainable riches (*suvitā*), such as jewels, pearls, and the like? Where do they abide?

"Where indeed do all [viśvāni]—that is, all (sarvāṇi) forms of prosperity (saubhagā), such as elephants, horses, and so forth—exist? The meaning is that one should go together with all your auspicious blessings (sumna) and the like."
*sumnā*: the elision of the *śe*-case ending occurs by the rule "in the Veda, [the case endings] are frequently [elided]. *narvyāṃsi*.
From the word *nava*, when the suffix *īyasun* is added, the vowel *ī* is elided by Vedic license. *Suvitā*: well-traversed; those things well traversed are *suvitāni*.
The substitution *uvaṅ* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.77.1: "In the Vedic language, the substitution [of *uvaṅ*] for *tanu* and so forth is frequent. Thus, we have *saubhagā*.
According to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.1.129 (Gaṇapāṭha), the suffix *añ* is added in the sense of "the state of being" to *subhaga* when used in a mantra. Thus, *saubhagya* becomes *saubhagā*.
As before, there is the elision of the suffix *śas*.
If you, O sons of Pṛśni, were mortals, your worshipper would be immortal. 4. If—ye—O sons of Pṛśni—were mortals, your worshipper would be immortal. 4.
O Maruts, sons of Pṛśni and Dhenus, even if you were mortals—human beings—nevertheless, may the singer of your praise, the sacrificer, become immortal; may he become a god.

"Pṛśnimātaraḥ" means those whose mother is Pṛśni. Due to the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the rule governing the formation of compound endings (*samāsānta*), there is an absence of the suffix *kap* [which would otherwise be required] by Pāṇini’s sūtra 5.4.153: *nadyṛtaśca*.
Mortals.
[The purpose of the suffix] -ḍa is as follows: 1. [To denote] the object.
2. A delay in the journey. 3. *Ḍha-pṛśnimātaraḥ*: sons of the cow named Pṛśni.
[Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 8, Sūkta 38] First Chapter, Verse 285.

By the rule *hasi* etc., there is the substitution of *tan* for the root *trai*. [In the form] *syātana*, [the suffix] *liṅ* occurs; for that, by the rule *tasanasanathanāśca*, the substitute *tan* is applied. There is the acute accent (*udāttatva*) of the *yāsuṭ* augment. In the word *amṛtaḥ*, by the rule *najo jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*, the initial syllable of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) is acute.
Let not your singer be like a wild beast that finds no pasture; let him not go upon the path of Yama.
Let not your singer be like a deer that seeks pasture; let him not go upon the path of Yama, being one who is not pleasing to you. 5.
O Maruts, let your singer—your praiser—not be one who is unloved or unworthy of service.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
like a wild beast in the pasture.
Just as a deer, when grass is to be eaten, is never to be shunned but always eats the grass, so too [is this].
Furthermore, let this praiser not approach, that is, not go, by his path—the way connected with the world of Yama;
the meaning is: "May there be no death for him."
Jaritā: from the root *jṛṣ* "to grow old" (Nirukta 10.17);
it is a word for the act of praising.

"In the desert land, even in the Marut region, the *rudriyās*—the Maruts protected by Rudra—bring forth from all sides rain (*miham*) devoid of wind; this is true. Of what nature are these *rudriyās*? They are "shining" (*vepāḥ*), meaning radiant, and "mighty" (*amavantaḥ*), meaning powerful. The protection of the Maruts by Rudra is well-known in the narrative accounts (*ākhyāneṣu*). Regarding the word *dhanvan*: the roots *riv*, *rav*, and *dhav* have the sense of "motion. Because it is marked with the *it*-suffix, the augment *num* is applied. By the rule *kaninyuvṛṣitakṣi* etc., the suffix *kanin* is added. Due to its being [a root] ending in *n*, it is accented on the first syllable. By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, there is elision (*luk*) of the locative case-ending. Regarding *rudriyāsaḥ*: these belong to Rudra, thus they are *rudriyāḥ*. The suffix *gha* is used in the sense of "belonging to him" (*tasyedam*). By the rule *ājaserasuk*, the suffix *asuk* is applied. Regarding *miham*: the root *miha* means "to sprinkle. By the rule *kvip ca*, the suffix *kvip* is applied. Regarding *kṛṇvanti*: the root *kṛvi* has the senses of "injuring" and "making. By the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyośca*, the suffix *up* is applied; due to its connection, the letter *v* is replaced by *a*. Because of the elision of the *a* (by *ato lopaḥ*), the position of the elided element is treated as if it were still present (*sthānivadbhāva*), and thus there is an absence of the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel.

For the oblation "mārutaṃ sasakapālam" in the Kārīrī sacrifice, the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) is "vāśveva vidyut. This is prescribed in the section titled "Varṣakāmeṣṭi" in the Sūtra: "vāśveva vidyunnimāti parvataścinmahivṛddho bibhāya" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 2.13). When their rain has been released—
like a lowing cow, endowed with sound and possessing full udders, appearing within the clouds, the lightning "mimāti," that is, it makes a sound;
for it is well known that thunder accompanies a streak of lightning.
"The mother-cow 'sipakti' [suckles] her calf; this lightning, O Maruts, 'siṣakti' [attends to] you.
The root *siṣakti* has the sense of attending (*sevana*). For Yāska has stated: 'The roots *sipaktu* and *sacata* belong to one who is attending' (Nirukta 3.21)."

Because "this rain belonging to these Maruts was released"— that is, it rained during a time of thundering lightning— "therefore the service of the Maruts by the lightning is appropriate. [The root] *vāś* means "to sound."
The suffix *rak* is applied by the rule "sphāyitañci," etc. He measures (*mimāti*). [The root] *māṅ* is used in the senses of measuring and sounding.
The *parasmaipada* ending is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
Due to its inclusion in the *juhotyādi* class, there is *ślu*-elision.
By the rule *bhṛjāmit* (Pāṇini 7.4.76), the short vowel is substituted for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).
He follows (*siṣakti*).
[The root] *pac* means "to join together.
In the present tense (*laṭ*), the *śap* suffix is replaced by *ślu* according to the rule "frequently in the Vedic language" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," the reduplication is shortened:
*asarji*.
[The root] *sṛj* means "to emit" (*visarga*).
The suffix *luṅ* is used for the object (*karman*).
By the rule "ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ" (Pāṇini 3.1.66), the suffix *ciṇ* is applied.
By the rule "ciṇo luk" (Pāṇini 6.4.104), there is elision (*luk*) of the *ta*-suffix.
The augment *aṭ* is acute;
because it is joined with a word that begins a new clause (*yadvṛtta*), it does not lose its accent (*anighāta*).
By day they make the mind dark with the rain-bearing cloud when they drench the earth. 9. By day. Mind. Darkness. They make. With the rain-cloud. Water-bearing. When. The earth. They drench. 9.

Those Maruts, having covered the sun with the rain-cloud (*parjanya*) which carries water, create darkness—even during the day—making it gloom. When they thoroughly moisten the earth, that is, when they cause it to overflow with water at the time of excessive rain, then they create darkness; this is the connection with the preceding clause.
[The word *udavāhena* means] by that which carries water.
It carries water, thus it is *udavāhaḥ*. [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied according to the rule *karmaṇyaṇ*. This is a technical name (*saṃjñā*) for a particular kind of cloud.
In the word *udaka*, the substitution of *uda* occurs by the rule *udakasyodaḥ saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.57). [Reference:
Ya-dṛṣṭā; Ma. 1. Bha. 8. Sū. 38]
By such [rules] as these, through the transposition of phonemes (*varṇavyatyaya*), the letter *ā* becomes *i*.
And it has been said: "The addition of a phoneme and the transposition of a phoneme" (Pāṇini 6.3.109).
"The reins impel the actions," so says the Nirukta (3.9).
Speak clearly with this continuous song; praise Brahmaṇaspati, who is visible like Agni or Mitra.
Speak clearly with your voice; praise the Lord of Prayer, Agni, who is visible like Mitra. 13.

O assembly of officiating priests, with this "speech"—that is, with the voice which reveals the nature of the deities—speak toward, that is, address directly, "Brahmaṇaspati," the protector of the mantra or of the sacrificial food characterized by oblation; [speak toward] "Agni," who has been manifested as worthy of being seen; and [speak toward] "Mitra" as well, for the sake of praise, so that they may grow old together.
"Acchā.
The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs in *saṃhitā* by the rule "nipātasya ca. Say it!
In the *saṃhitā*, there is a long vowel according to the rule "a-baco-'matiṅaḥ. [The root is] *tan*:
"the root *tan* means 'to expand' (*vistāre*)."
*Tanā* means that which extends or expands the greatness of the deity; it is derived from the root *tan* with the suffix *ac* according to the rule for roots beginning with *pac*.
It has an acute accent on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group.
In the third case, there is the substitution of *ḍā*:
*girā*.
By the rule "sāvekācaḥ," the case ending receives the udātta accent.
Brahmā says: "In the *saṃhitā*, there is the substitution of *s* [for *ṣ*] in the form *paṣṭyāḥ patiputraḥ*."
Measure out the hymn within your mouth; like Parjanya, extend it—sing the Gāyatra, the song of praise.
Measure out a verse in your mouth; like Parjanya, you have stretched it out. Sing the Gāyatra, worthy of praise! 14.

O assembly of priests (*ṛtvij-samūha*), "measure out" (*mimīhi*)—that is, compose—the hymn (*śloka*) in your own mouth (*āsye*). And "extend" (*tatanaḥ*) that hymn. Therein is an illustration: "like Parjanya. Just as a cloud extends rain, so too [should you]. Sing—that is, recite—the *ukthya*, which is worthy of praise, the *gāyatra*, a hymn (*sūkta*) composed in the *gāyatrī* meter. Regarding *mimīhi*: from the root *māṅ* "to measure," belonging to the *juhotyādi* class. The *parasmaipada* ending is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). By the rule "for *bhṛ*, *ñi*, and *ām*" (*bhṛñjāmit*), there is shortening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Regarding *āsye*: from the root *asu* "to cast"; that in which something is cast (*asyate*) is *āsya*. The suffix *ṇyat* is used in the sense of location (*adhikaraṇe*) according to Pāṇini 3.3.113 (*kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*). It has the *svarita* accent according to the rule "the *tisvarita*. Regarding *tatanaḥ*: from the root *tanu* "to extend. In the *leṭ* mood with the ending *sip*, the *vikaraṇa* suffix is elided by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). The augment *aṭ* is added by the rule "the augments *aṭ* and *āṭ* for the *leṭ*" (*leṭo'ḍāṭau*). The vowel *i* is elided by the rule "elision of *i* after *it*" (*itaśca lopaḥ*). Regarding *gāyatram*: it belongs to the *gāyatrī*; thus, the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule "this belongs to that" (*tasyedam*). Alternatively, it is *gāyatram* because it protects (*trāyate*) the *gāyatra*; the suffix *ka* is applied by the rule "after a word ending in *ā*, the suffix *ka* occurs when no upasarga precedes" (*āto'nupasarge kaḥ*).
Worship the host of Maruts, the brilliant, the praiseworthy, the singers of hymns;
may they, grown strong, be present here with us.
Worship the host of Maruts—the brilliant, praiseworthy, and hymn-singing one—so that they may be increased for us here. 15.
O assembly of officiating priests, pay homage to, bow before, or praise the host—the collective group—belonging to the Maruts.
Of what nature? Resplendent, worthy of praise, and accompanied by hymns of worship.
May the Maruts be exalted for us here in this rite; may they be greatly increased.
Vandasva. [The root] *vad* means "to salute" and "to praise.
Because it is taught with a short vowel (*adupadeśa*), the suffix *ū* (the *śnu* vikaraṇa) is unaccented by virtue of being a sārvadhātuka suffix, and thus the accent falls on the verbal root itself.
*panasyum*: the verbal root *pan*,
meaning "to praise," with the suffix *asun*.
Furthermore: "He desires praise for himself" is *panasyu*. [The derivation is as follows: by the rule *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*, the suffix *kyac* is applied;
then, by the rule *kyāc chandasi*, the suffix *up* is added.
*Arkiṇam*. [The root] *ṛc* is used in the sense of "praising. 1.
The long vowel [is applied].

2. Ḍhaparṇā: | The suffix *gha* is applied [to the root *as*] by the rule "puṃsi saṃjñāyām" (Pāṇini 3.3.118). [The word *akī* is derived from *asan*: that which has a vowel (*ak*) is *akī*. [The form *asan* is derived from the root *as*] by the rule "ata iniṭanau" (Pāṇini 5.2.115). The absence of the elision of the *śap* augment occurs by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 2.4.73). The elision of the vowel *i* occurs by the rule "dvataśca lopaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.1.67). The *nighāta* (anudātta accent) is applied by the rule "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pāṇini 8.1.28). || 17 ||

The fourth hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with “pra yaditthā,” is the seerage of Kaṇva, the son of Ghora; its deity is the Maruts. The even-numbered verses are Sato-bṛhatīs, and the odd-numbered verses are Bṛhatīs. The Anukramaṇī states: “pra yad vā prāgārthaṃ tu. The application (viniyoga) has been explained.
When you thus send forth your flame from afar like a banner, by whose wisdom, O Maruts, and by whose form do you come? To whom do you go, O shakers?
When you thus cast forth your measure from afar like a flame, by whose wisdom, O Maruts, and by whose form do you go? To whom, O shakers, do you go? To whom indeed? 1.
Those winds, the shakers of mountains and other things, when they cast down from afar— that which is worthy of thought, your own power—
from the distance (for "āre parāvataḥ" is listed among the names for "far"),
or when they thus hurl it from this intermediate space onto the earth.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
like heat or radiance.
Just as the heat of the sun is cast from the atmosphere onto the earth, so it is here.
At that time, with whose sacrifice (*kratu*) do you join?—this is the ellipsis.

Likewise, with whose form (*varpas*), that is, with whose hymn of praise (*stotra*), do you join? With reference to which sacrificer (*yajamāna*) do you go—that is, do you proceed to the place of sacrifice (*devayajanadeśa*)?
"Whom indeed, which patron-sacrificer, do you favor?"—this is the remainder of the sentence.
*Itthā*: By the rule *thā hetau ca chandasi* (Pāṇini 5.3.26), the suffix *thā* is applied to the word *idam* to express manner (*prakāra*).

If there is no recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of the word *idam* in that context, then, by the analysis of the case-ending following the word *idam* ending in the suffix *thamu*, the substitution of *ḍā* occurs according to *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
In the first case, it is the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*);
in the second case, however, it is the accent of the disappearance of the acute (*udāttanivṛttisvara*).
Thus: *asyatha*.

The root *as* is used in the sense of "throwing. Because it is taught with a short *a* vowel (*adupadeśāt*), the *lasārvadhātuka* affixes are unaccented; however, due to the *śyan* suffix being marked with *n*, the word is accented on its first syllable.
The lack of the *nighāta* (elision of accent) occurs because of its connection with *yad-vṛtta*.

By *kratvā*. Because the substitution of *nā* [for *na*] is optional in the Vedic language according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 7.3.109.1 (*jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam*), the form *bhāvaḥ* [is used]. By *varpasā*.
Regarding the root *vṛdh* in the sense of "to nourish" (*saṃbhaktau*):

by the rule *vṛḍ-śīḍbhyāṃ rūpasvādyoḥ puk ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.640), the suffix *asun* is applied, and by its concomitance (*tatsaṃniyogena*), the augment *puk* is added. Due to the prefix *nis*, it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.
In this context, by the word *varṣa*, which denotes form (*rūpa*), the hymn that reveals the essential nature of the deity is indicated, due to its association with the ritual act (*kratu*).
May your weapons be firm for driving away the foe, and solid for resisting the attack;
may your power be most glorious, not that of the deceitful mortal.
May your weapons be firm for the striking down of enemies, strong for the firm resistance; may your power be most praiseworthy, not that of the deceitful mortal. 2.
O Maruts, may your weapons—your arms—be firm for the repelling of enemies, for their driving away; let them be steadfast, let them be solid.
And furthermore, for the obstruction of enemies, let them be strong, let them be firm. May your power, your strength, be most praiseworthy, exceeding all others in its excellence.
Of the deceitful one among us, the one who moves in disguise, the mortal enemy of man.
(Ṛgveda 37)

"Let there be no force, let there be no power. The word *sthirā* ("firm") has its case-ending elided in both instances by the rule *śeṣchandasi bahulam*. *Parāṇude*: from the root *ṇud* meaning "to impel," with the suffix *kvip* according to the *saṃpadādi* group. The substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs by the rule *upasargādasamāne'pi* (Pāṇini 8.4.14). The accentuation follows the rule *kuduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*. *Vīḷu*: here the case-ending is elided by the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39). The original form is retained because it belongs to the *īṣākṣatvādi* group (Pāṇini 6.1.127.2). *Pratikambhe*: *skambhu* is a Vedic (sautra) root. The suffix *kvip* is added in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) according to the *saṃpadādi* group. The nasal *n* is dropped by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24). *Panīyasī*: the root *pan* means "to praise. From this, the suffix *asun* is added in the sense of the object (*karman*) according to the Uṇādi rules. Then, when the comparative suffix *īyasun* is added, the final vowel is elided by the rule *ṭeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.155). The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added by the rule *ugitaśca* (Pāṇini 4.1.6). The initial vowel is acute because of the *nistva* (the presence of *ni*) in *īyasun*. *Māyinaḥ*: since the word *māyā* is listed in the *vrīhyādi* group, the possessive suffix *ini* is added by the rule *vrīhādibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 5.2.116).
When you strike down what is firm, O heroes, and whirl about that which is heavy;
you traverse the hollows of the earth, and the spaces between the mountains.
O heroes, when you strike down what is firm, you turn back the heavy [burden]; you pass through the hollows of the earth and through the clefts of the mountains.
O Maruts, leaders of men, when you strike down— that is, shatter and break— unstable objects such as trees and the like;
when you hurl— that is, propel— the hidden— that is, that which is concealed within rocks and the like—
at that time, you go apart through— that is, you pass through the midst of— the forest-dwellers, the trees belonging to the earth.
In the midst of dense trees growing in the forest, when any one tree breaks, a wide path is formed by the mutual separation of the other trees;
in that same manner, "O mountains," you "go apart"—that is, you depart, separating yourselves from the directions along the flanks of the mountains.
The root *hana* means "to injure" and "to go.
By the rule beginning with "anudāttettvopadeśa," there is the elision of the nasal. Due to its connection with *yad-vṛtta*, there is no *nighāta* (suppression of accent).
The word *naraḥ* [is used]; because it begins with a consonant (*pādādi*), there is no elision of accent (*āmantritanighātābhāva*).
[The verb is] *vartayatha*.

Because it is taught as having an *at* (short *a*) as its penultimate vowel, when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the accent of the *ṇic* itself remains. Due to the *anubandha* *y*, there is no elision of the accent (*nighāta*). [Thus:
*yāthana*.
In the phrase "tasanaśanathām ca," there is the substitution of "tha" for "na."
No enemy of yours has been found in heaven nor upon the earth, O destroyers of foes; may your power remain with your progeny, for you, O Rudras, are not to be assailed even now.
No enemy of yours has been found in heaven, nor upon the earth, O destroyers of foes; may your power remain with your progeny, O Rudras, so that it may never be assailed by an ally. 4.
O Maruts, destroyers of enemies, no foe has been found above you in the heavenly world (*divi*),

nor has any foe existed upon the earth. O Rudras, sons of Rudra, may your strength (*tarviṣī*)— the power of you forty-nine who are joined together in mutual accord— be truly extensive and swiftly spread abroad for the total subduing of your adversaries.
*vivide*: from the root *vid* in the sense of "existence" (*sattāyām*); the accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*) in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*).

Because the meaning of the word "ca" (and) is understood from the phrase "not in heaven, nor in the three worlds, nor on earth," the first case ending is applied according to the rule "ādi-lope vibhāṣā.
There is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) for the verbal inflection (*tiṅ-vibhakti*).
And the primacy [of the root] is with respect to the action that is closely connected;
[the term is] *riśādasaḥ*.
[The root] *riś* is used in the sense of "injuring."
They are called *riśāḥ* because they injure (*riśanti*) or harm; the suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule for roots ending in *i* or *u*. Those who devour them are *riśādasaḥ*.

*asun*: [the suffix] *asun*. *āmantrita-nighātaḥ*: [the first word receives] the suppression of accent (nighāta) because it is a vocative. *yujā*: from the root *yujir* in the sense of "joining" (*yoge*). By the rule *ṛtvig-ādi*, the suffix *kin* is applied. The acute accent (*udāttatva*) of the case-ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. *hlāsaḥ*: by the word *rudra*, his related Maruts are indicated. [The form *rudrebhyaḥ* is derived thus: *ājaserasuk* [is applied]. *nū cit*: the lengthening [of the vowel] is according to the rule *ṛci tunugha-* etc. *ādyeṣe*: from the root *bhṛṣvā* in the sense of "boldness" (*prāgalbhye*). The suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*) according to the *saṃpad-ādi* group. It has the original accent of the final member of the compound (*kṛd-uttara-pada-prakṛti-svara*).
They cause the mountains to tremble; they pass through the lords of the forest.
The Maruts have come forth like the wildly intoxicated, O gods, with their entire host.
They make the mountains tremble; they shatter the lords of the forest. O Maruts, you have come forth like those intoxicated with pride—O gods, with your entire host. 5.

The Maruts cause the mountains, such as Meru and Himavat, to tremble; they violently shake them. They scatter the lords of the forest, such as the banyan and the holy fig tree, separating them from one another. O Maruts, O gods, together with your entire host—that is, with all your progeny—you advance forth, moving everywhere. Therein lies the illustration: like those intoxicated by pride (*durmadāḥ*). Just as those maddened by intoxication sport everywhere according to their own will, so do you. *Vepayanti*: from the root *ṭuvep*, meaning "to shake. They cause those who are already shaking to move; this is formed with the causal suffix *ṇic*. *Viśvanti*: from the root *vicir*, meaning "to separate. Because it belongs to the *rudhādi* class, there is the insertion of *śnam*. By the rule "the elision of *at*," the vowel *a* is dropped. *Vanaspataun*: "lords of the forests" (*vanānāṃ patayaḥ*); the form *vanaspati* is derived with the augment *suṭ* because it belongs to the *pāraskarādi* group. The words *vana* and *pati* have the acute accent on the first syllable. By the rule "in the case of *vanaspati* and similar compounds, both members take their original accent simultaneously," both the preceding and following members retain their respective original accents. *Ārata*: from the root *ṛ*, meaning "to go. In the imperfect (*laṅ*) middle voice, plural number, the suffix *śap* is optionally elided by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). Alternatively, there is elision (*luk*). By the rule "after *as*, *śās*, *ṛ*, and *ti*," the suffix *aṅ* is applied. The augment *āṭ* is added by the rule "for *āṅ* and others. Then, by the rule "and after *āṭ*," there is *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening). *Devāsaḥ*: the initial syllable has the acute accent because it is a vocative (*āmantrita*). *Sarvayā*: the initial syllable has the acute accent by the rule "of *sarva* before a case-ending" (*sup*). *Viśā*: the case-ending has the acute accent by the rule "for a monosyllabic word ending in *sā-*" (*sāvekācaḥ*). You have yoked the spotted mares to your chariots; the ruddy horse carries you on its back. Even the earth trembled at your approach, and mortal men were struck with fear.
O you who are near! For the sake of wealth, you have yoked the spotted mares. The back bears the red horse. At your approach, even the earth has trembled; mortal men were struck with fear.

O Maruts, you harnessed the spotted deer (*pṛṣatīḥ*)—dappled with drops—to your chariots for the sake of speed; the *pṛṣṭi*, a specific type of yoke situated between the three poles of the vehicle, draws it, and the *rohita*—a species of deer of red color—carries the chariot. Even the earth and the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) listened toward you for your journey; that is to say, they gave their assent.
"Pṛthivī" is a name for the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*), because it is listed among its names in [the Nirukta] as "pṛthivī bhūḥ svayaṃbhu" (Nirukta 1.3.9).
The humans—meaning the persons residing in the world of earth—were terrified; being themselves afraid, they caused fear to arise in others as well. 1. [They cut down] the trees.
2. Ḍha is a particular kind of deer.

They spoke thus. The word *upo* is another indeclinable (*nipāta*) consisting of a combination of two proclitics (*nighāta*). Its status as a *pragṛhya* is established by Pāṇini 1.1.15 (*ot*). [The form] *ayuṣdhvam* is derived from the root *yu* in the *luṅ* tense; the *s* is elided by Pāṇini 8.2.26 (*jhalo jhali*), and the change to *k* occurs by Pāṇini 8.2.30 (*coḥ kuḥ*). [The word] *rohitaḥ* ends in the suffix *itac* according to Uṇādisūtra 2.374 (*rahe raśca lo vā*). Because the suffix is marked with *ṇ*, the word is *ādyudātta*. [The word] *yāmāya*: the suffix *ghañ* is added to the root *yam* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*). Although the rule "the final syllable of words ending in *karṣa* or having *ā* as an *it*" would have required the *antodātta* accent, its *ādyudātta* status is established by its inclusion in the *vṛṣādi* group. [The form] *aśrot*: from the root *śru* ("to hear"). The suffix (*vikaraṇa*) is elided by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). [The form] *abībhayanta*: from the root *bhi* ("to fear") with the causative suffix (*ṇic*). In the *luṅ* tense, the *ātmanepada* is used by Pāṇini 1.3.68 (*bhīsmyorhetubhaye*). The augment *puK* would apply by Pāṇini 7.3.40 (*bibheterhetubhaye*), but it is not applied here because the rules regarding augments are not always mandatory (*anitya*). The shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) and other operations occur by Pāṇini 7.4.1 (*ṇau caṅyupadhāsvat*).
O Rudras, we quickly choose your protection for the sake of our offspring; come now to us with your aid, just as you did formerly for the terrified Kaṇva. 7.
O Rudras, we quickly choose your aid for our progeny; come now to us with your protection as in former times, even as you did for the trembling Kaṇva.
O Rudras, O Maruts, sons of Rudra, for the sake of our offspring (*tanaya*), we choose—indeed, we pray for from all sides—your protection (*avaḥ*) quickly (*makṣu*).
*Makṣu* is a word for "swiftly," as it is listed among the synonyms for speed in the Nirukta (2.15.2): "Now, *makṣu*."

Just as in former times, on other occasions, you came for our protection—that is, for the sake of guarding us—so now, in this manner, come quickly (*nūnam*) to the terrified Kaṇva, the wise sacrificer, for the sake of bestowing favor upon him.
[The lengthening of the vowel in *makṣu* is according to the rule:
*ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruvyāṇām*.]
*Tanaya*: that which extends (*tanoti*) is *tana*; [the suffix] *ac* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.134 (*pacādyac*).
The word is acutely accented on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group;
or alternatively,
there is a Vedic elision (*lopa*) of the syllable *ay* within the word *tana*.
The particle *kam*, when employed at the end of a verse-quarter (*pādānta*), serves to fill out the meter, as in the example: *śiśiraṃ jīvanaya kam*.
And it has been said: "Furthermore, *kam*, *īm*, and *it* are used for the purpose of filling out the verse-quarters" (*Nirukta* 1.9). [Thus ends the section on] the Rudras.
They are called *rudrāḥ* because they cause weeping (*rodayanti*).
The suffix *ra* is applied according to the rule "after the root *rud*, there is *ṇi*-elision" (Uṇādi-sūtra 2.179). The first member of the vocative case is accented on its initial syllable.
There is no *nighāta* (elision of the accent) because it begins with a *pāda*.
[The form] *ganta*: in the *loṭ* [mood], there is elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
By the rule beginning with "tasanap," the substitution of *ta* occurs;
because this [suffix] is marked with *p*, there is no elision of the nasal.
[The form is] *vibhyuṣe*.
