The suffix *kasu* is substituted for the *liṭ* [perfect] of the root *bhī*. Due to the restriction "after a monosyllabic root ending in a single consonant, or after *vas*, there is no *iṭ*," there is an absence of the augment *iṭ*. In the dative singular, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "there is vocalization of *vas*."
The state of having another [vowel] preceding [the sibilant].
The substitution of *ṣ* occurs by the rule "śās-vasi-ghasīnāṃ ca.

O Maruts, that which is sent against us by you, sent by mortals—that monstrous thing which assails us—drive it away with your power, drive it away with your might, drive it away with your protections! 8.
O Maruts, you who are impelled by us, impelled by mortals—whatever monstrous thing assails us, drive it away with your might, drive it away with your strength, drive it away with your various aids.
1. The *ta* [consonant] is followed by *phala*, *upa*, *upa*, and *u*.
2. The sequence *ca-cha-ha-ta-dha-na-pha-śa-sa* does not exist as "yathā.
3. Or, it belongs to the sacrificer (*yajamāna*).

O Maruts, whatever enemy— whether sent by you, dispatched by you, or sent by mortals or by others— comes against us, approaching us face-to-face, separate that enemy from us with your might (*śavas*),
separate him with your power (*ojas*),
and separate him with your protections belonging to you.
In *yuṣmeṣitaḥ* and *yuṣmābhirīpataḥ*,

although there is elision (*sul-uk*), the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* occurs by virtue of the rule "the [final vowel] of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* [is replaced by *ā*] when no substitute [for the case-ending] follows," because the characteristic of the suffix still applies.

Nor does the prohibition "na lumatāṅgasya" apply, because its optionality has been stated by the inclusion of the term *aj* in the rule "iko 'ci vibhaktau" (Pāṇini 7.1.73). By the rule "tṛtīyā karmaṇi," the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvara*) is applied.
[Thus we have] *maryaiṣitaḥ*.
As before:
*avaḥ*.
This enemy of yours has become [subdued].
The desired form and accent are established by virtue of its belonging to the *pṛṣodarādi* group. It is derived from the root *īṣ*, meaning "to go," "to injure," or "to see."
Because it is taught as having an initial vowel (adupadeśāt), when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented (*anudātta*), the accent falls on the root (*dhātusvara*).
[The form is] *yuyota*. [The root is] *yu*, meaning "to mix" and "not to mix."

In the middle *loṭ* plural, there is the *ślu* replacement of *śap* by the rule "optionally in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). There is the substitution of *tab* by the rule "the suffixes *tasan*, *san*, and *than*.
Due to its being marked with the *pi*t indicator, it is *udātta*.

"By yours" means by those related to you. The substitution of *yuṣmākā* for the word *yuṣmad* is according to Pāṇini’s rule 4.3.2: "In that [context], and in the case of the suffix *aṇ*, there is the substitute *yuṣmākā* and *asmākā*.
The feminine suffix *ṅīp* and the vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) are applied because this is Vedic usage.
In the word *ūtibhiḥ*, the suffix *ktin* is applied to the root *avati*; by the rule beginning with "jvaratvara," the vowel *u* is substituted for *ava*.
By the rule beginning with "ūtiyuti," the suffix *ktin* receives the udātta accent.
For the wise Maruts, you who are not masters over others, have bestowed wealth upon the sacrificing Kaṇva;
come to us with your aids, O Maruts, like lightning bringing rain.
For you, O wise Maruts, have given to Kaṇva who was not a sacrificer; come to us with your perfect aids, as lightning brings rain. 9.

O Maruts, possessed of supreme wisdom, you who are worthy of sacrifice must perform the sacrifices most excellently so that they are indeed complete and not deficient. O wise ones, uphold Kaṇva— the intelligent sacrificer, or one named after this [sacrifice].
Indeed, because you have supported the sage named Kaṇva, for that reason, come toward us with full protections—complete aids.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
like lightning bringing rain.
Just as lightning goes toward the rain, so it is.
*asāmi*.
*sāmi* means "half"; that which is not half is *asāmi*.
[In this compound] there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*) of the indeclinable (*avyaya*) which constitutes the prior member (*pūrvapada*).
*Prayajvaḥ*:

those who are to be sacrificed to preeminently (*prakarṣeṇa yaṣṭavyāḥ*). The suffix *yu* is applied in the sense of the object (*karmaṇi*) according to the rule: "The suffix *yu* [is added] after the roots *yaj*, *mani*, *dhundi*, *das*, and *jan*" (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.300).
The vocative is unaccented.
*Dada*:
from the root *ḍudāñ* (to give).

In the case of the third-person plural ending *loṇmadhyama*, there is the substitution of the third-person plural *laṭ* middle-voice (*ātmanepada*) by the rule "for *tiṅ*s, [substitutes] of *tiṅ*s" (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
When reduplication occurs due to the *ślu* suffix, the long *ā* is elided by the rule "the *ā* of the root and the reduplicated stem" (Pāṇini 6.4.112).
Then, the *t* is elided by the rule "there is elision of the *t* in *ātmanepada* endings" (Pāṇini 7.1.41).

The substitution of *guṇa* results in the form *parapūrva*. Because [the suffix] is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* by the rule "in the Veda, both ways," the initial acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*) prescribed by "the first syllable of reduplicated stems" does not apply; rather, only the accent of the suffix remains. Furthermore, by the rule "and after *hi*," there is a prohibition against the *nighāta* (elision) accent.
*Pracetasaḥ*: those whose minds (*cetas*) are excellent (*prakṛṣṭa*). [The first word] takes the low-pitched accent (*nighāta*) because it is a vocative (*āmantrita*).

*ganta*: This is the substitute *ta* for the middle voice third person plural ending of the root *gam*. By the rule "optionally in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*), there is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*.
Because the suffix *pratyaya* is marked with the *pittva* indicatory letter, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains.
Due to its position at the beginning of a *pāda*, there is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*).
In the *saṃhitā* reading, the vowel lengthening occurs according to the rule *aco 'ntyādi ṭiṅaḥ*.
Regarding *vidyut*:
it is called *vidyut* because it flashes (*viyotate*). The suffix *kvip* is applied according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.2.177, *ājabhāsa-*, etc.
O bounteous givers, you sustain a power that is never deficient; O shakers, your strength is never exhausted.
O Maruts, wrathful against the hater of the seer, do not release your hostility like an arrow.

O bounteous givers, you possess complete vigor; O shakers, you possess complete power. O Maruts, against the one who hates the seer and against the one who is full of wrath, do not discharge hostility like an arrow. 10.
O Maruts, you who are most bountiful (*sudānavaḥ*), endowed with excellent giving, you possess and maintain (*bibhṛtha*) complete (*asāmi*) vigor (*ojaḥ*) and strength (*bala*).

O shakers (*dhūtayaḥ*), O Maruts, for the sake of destroying the enemy—the one filled with wrath (*parimanyave*), the hater of the seers (*ṛṣidviṣe*) who bears malice toward the seers—send forth (*sṛjata*) a slayer (*hantāram*) of that hater (*dviṣam*) so as to destroy him with complete (*asāmi*) power (*śavaḥ*).
Therein lies the illustration.
"Like an arrow"—just as they release an arrow upon an enemy, so it is here.
Regarding this, the *Nirukta* states: "Asāmi; *sāmi* is negated; *sāmi* is that which is exhausted."
"O you of liberal gifts, you sustain immortality;
O you who bestow auspicious gifts, you sustain strength that is never exhausted" (Nirukta 6.23).
*bibhṛtha*. [The root] *ḍubhṛñ* [is used] in the senses of "supporting" and "nourishing.
Because it belongs to the *juhotyādi* class, there is *ślu*-elision.
By the rule "bhṛñām it," the short *i* is substituted for the reduplicated syllable. [The term] *ṛṣidviṣe*:
one who hates sages (*ṛṣīn*) is a *ṛṣidviṭ*.
The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "sasṛdviṣaḥ" and so forth. Regarding *parimanyave*: one who is surrounded by anger (*manyu*) is *parimanyu*.
In the *prādi* compound, by Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.2.182, "apareḥ abhitobhāvi maṇḍalam," there is udātta accent on the final syllable of the second member. Regarding *iṣum*:
[it is derived from] the root *iṣu* in the sense of "motion."
It is called *iṣu* because it goes (*eti*) excessively (*ati*).
The suffix *up* is applied by the rule *iṣeḥ kicca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.13).
Since the term *nit* from the rule *dhānye nit* continues to apply, the word is acutely accented on its first syllable due to the presence of the *nit* suffix.
*sṛjata*.
[The root] *sṛj* [is used] in the sense of emission (*visarga*).
Due to the *ṅit*-nature of the suffix, there is an absence of *guṇa*.
*dviṣam* [is formed] by the *kvip* suffix according to the rule "kvip ca."
"Uttiṣṭha" is the fifth hymn, consisting of eight verses; its seer is Kaṇva, its meter is Bṛhatī.
The even-numbered verses are Satobṛhatīs, and the odd-numbered verses are Bṛhatīs.
It has Brahmanaspati as its deity. And it is listed [in the Anukramaṇī]: "The hymn beginning with 'uttiṣṭha' is dedicated to Brāhmaṇaspati.
The application of this hymn is based on its indicative marks (liṅga).

On the twenty-fourth day, before the *brāhmaṇaspatya* *pragātha* of the archetypal *marutvatīya* [śastra], there is this *pragātha*: "Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati. This is prescribed in the section on the *marutvatīya* in the Sūtra: "The two *brāhmaṇaspatya* verses, 'May Brahmaṇaspati go forward' and 'Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati,' are inserted; the former [is used] in the archetype" (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 7.3). However, the first [verse] is also employed in the *pravargya* rite during the *abhiṣṭava*.
For it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "Having recited this verse, 'uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate,' he stands [there]. (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.7)
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! Seeking the gods, we entreat you.
May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift with us.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! Seeking the gods, we pray to you. May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward. O Indra, be swift in our company. 1.
O Brahmaṇaspati, O deity of that name, arise; for the sake of bestowing grace, rise up from your dwelling.
Desiring the gods, we entreat you.
May the Maruts, endowed with noble generosity, come forward and approach us.
O Indra, together with Brahmaṇaspati, you, being swift, become a consumer of the Soma;
or rather, become a slayer of Vṛtra.
Arise!
Because the action is directed upward (*ūrdhvakarma*), there is an absence of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) [according to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.24].
O Lord of Prayer (*brahmaṇaspati*).

Regarding the term *sumāmantrita*: because it functions as a subordinate member of a compound (*parāṅgavadbhāva*), the entire vocative aggregate ending in the genitive case is initially acute-accented (*ādyudātta*) and the remainder is unaccented (*sarvānudātta*).
*Devayantaḥ* means "desiring to take hold of the gods."
Regarding *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*:

by the rule *na chandasyaputrasya*, there is a prohibition of the long vowel *ī*—even though [the rule] *ītva* [would otherwise apply]—due to the force of the subsequent prescription of *atva* in *adhāghasyāt*. Forms such as *īmahe* have already been explained. *Prāśvaḥ*: from the root *śru* in the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*). One who thoroughly (*pra*) and completely (*ā*) injures (*śruṇāti*) is *prāśvaḥ*. The substitution of *u* is according to *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 7.1.103). There is lengthening of the penultimate vowel by *vorupadhāyā dīrghaḥ*. It takes the accent of the original form of the second member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). *Bhava*: in the *saṃhitā* text, there is lengthening according to *aco 'ntyādi ṭi kaḥ*.
For indeed, O son of strength, a mortal calls upon you alone when the prize is set;
O Maruts, may he who has honored you possess great heroic power and noble wealth.
For indeed, O Son of Strength, the mortal man invokes you when the prize is set; may he who has won your favor, O Maruts, obtain great heroic power and excellent horses.

O Sahasraputra, O Balasya, O Bahupālaka, O Brahmaṇaspati! According to the Nirukta (2.11), "A son protects in many ways from destruction. When wealth has been placed among enemies—that is, when it is at stake—a mortal, a human being, indeed approaches you alone; having come into your presence, he praises you.
The meaning is that [the sacrificer] entreats them for the sake of accomplishing that [desire].

O Maruts, whatever mortal seeking wealth praises you—accompanied by Brahmaṇaspati—that mortal shall possess (dadhīta), that is, hold fast to, wealth endowed with *svabhvyam* (a beautiful abode) and *suvīryam* (excellent heroic power).

In *sahasasputra* and *brahmaṇaspate*, the *visarjanīya* becomes *s* according to the rule "the [substitution of *s* occurs] for the *visarjanīya* of the word *ṣaṣṭhī* when followed by *pati* or *putra*" (*ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrau*).
Thus: *upabrūte*.
In "hi ca," there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of the accent). In "tiṅi codāttavati," there is the lack of accent (*anudātta*) for the verbal prefix (*gati*). [The word is] *hite*.
In the formation of the absolutive (*niṣṭhā*), there is the substitution of *hi* for *dvit* according to the rule "dvit-ater-hiḥ.
Regarding *suvīryam*: in the *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "one whose valor (*vīrya*) is excellent (*śobhana*)," the initial vowel of the final member is acute by the rule "vīra-vīryau ca."

The word *svabhvyam* means a collection of horses (*aśvānāṃ samūhaḥ*). The suffix *cha* is applied in the sense of a collection according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 4.2.47: *keśāśvābhyāṃ yacchāv anyatarasyām*. Thus, [the form] *aśvīyam* is derived.
The substitution of *ai* for *cha* occurs;
that which has beautiful horses (*aśva*) is "possessing good horses" (*svabhvyam*).
The elision of the vowel *ī* is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
In the phrase *dadhīta*, the acute accent (*udātta*) falls on the first syllable of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) according to the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*.
When the *s* of the *sīyuṭ* suffix is elided, the acute accent falls on the first syllable according to the rule *abhyastānām ādiḥ*.
There is no *nighāta* (elision of the accent) because it begins with a *pāda*. [The form] *ācuke* [is derived from the root] *kai*, *gai*, or *rai* in the sense of "sound."
By the rule *ādecaḥ*, there is the substitution of *ā* [for *ai*].
In the reduplicated form (*liṭ*) with dual number, after the shortening of the reduplication,
there is the elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca*.
The accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*):
that which, due to its connection with a particular metrical foot (*vṛtta*), does not receive the low tone (*anighāta*).
On the twenty-fourth day, at the Marutvatīya [offering], this *pragātha*—"May Brahmaṇaspati go forth"—is prescribed as being placed before the *pragātha* "Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati.
However, the Sūtra cites it specifically in connection with "Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati.
While they are returning toward the hall after taking up the Mahāvīra vessel, the Hotṛ should follow them while reciting this verse: "May Brahmaṇaspati go forth."
And the Sūtra states: "One should recite the verse, 'Let Brahmanaspati go forth' (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.7).
This very same [verse] is also employed for the carrying forward of the fire and Soma (agniṣomīya-praṇayana).
And it is Sūtrated: "'Let Brahmanaspati go forth—the immortal divine Hotṛ' (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.10)."
May Brahmanaspati go forward; may the goddess Sūnṛtā go forward;
may the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the friend of men, who bestows fivefold wealth.
May Brahmanaspati come forward; may Sūnṛtā, the goddess, come forward. May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the manly one who bestows wealth in fivefold portions. 3.
May Brahmaṇaspati, the god, come toward us;
may Sūnṛtā, the goddess—the deity of speech whose form is pleasantness—come toward us.
May the gods, Brahmaṇaspati and the others, drive the enemy hero away entirely to a distance.
May they lead us toward that noble sacrifice, beneficial for men, which provides fivefold offerings and is proclaimed by the Brāhmaṇas through the *vipaṅkti* and other meters;
may it proceed! [In the formation of *pretu*:
although the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) would apply according to Pāṇini 6.1.94, the vṛddhi substitution occurs according to Pāṇini 6.1.89.]
In the word *devyetu*, there is the circumflex (*svarita*) accent according to the rule “*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito'nudāttasya*” [Pāṇini 8.2.4]. *Naryam*:
beneficial for men (*narebhyaḥ hitam*).
The suffix *yat* should be understood here according to Pāṇini’s rule 5.1.2, which prescribes it after words such as *paṅkti* and *ṛc*.
Thus, *paṅktirādhāḥ*:
one who accomplishes (*rādhnoti*) by means of the *paṅkti* [verse] is called *paṅktirādhāḥ*.
By the rule "‘gatikārakayor api pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ca’," there is also the preservation of the original accent (prakṛtisvara) of the preceding member.
[Thus we have] *yajñam*.
By the rule "‘yajayāca-’" etc., the suffix *ha* is applied to the root *yaj*.
He who gives excellent wealth to the singer gains imperishable fame.
For him we offer this nourishing oblation, rich in heroes, victorious, and free from blemish.
He who bestows excellent wealth upon the singer wins imperishable fame; for him we offer the oblation that brings heroic sons, which is victorious, peerless, and free from blemish.

That sacrificer who bestows excellent wealth (*sūnaraṃ vasu*) upon the officiating priest (*vāghat*), the ritual minister, that sacrificer—by the grace of Brahmaṇaspati—attains and maintains imperishable (*akṣiti*) renown (*śravaḥ*), which here signifies food.

For such a sacrificer, we, the officiating priests, offer this *iḷā* from all sides; she is the daughter of Manu, as another Vedic text states: "Iḷā, the daughter of Manu, was the mistress of the sacrifice" (*Tai. Brā. 1.1.4.4*). We go toward her completely.
What kind of blessing?

One that possesses excellent heroes, joined with noble husbands; one that is "well-advancing," meaning it effectively inflicts injury upon enemies; and one that is "unassailable," meaning it cannot be harmed by anyone.
It bestows this.
By the rule *anudātte ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.190), the first syllable of the reduplicated form (*abhyasta*) is udātta; its non-udātta status is overridden by its connection with *yadvṛtta*. *Sūnaram*.

It is called *sūnara* because it is led (*nīyate*) with ease (*sukhena*). This is indeed due to the rule *īṣadduḥsuṣu*. Furthermore, the lengthening of the vowel in the prefix is according to the rule *jigāttasya ca*.
*Akṣiti*:
"That which has no destruction" (*kṣaya*) is *akṣiti*.
In this *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent remains on the original form of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratva*).
However, because of the statement, "In the Veda, all [grammatical rules] are optional," the rule *nansubhyām* does not apply. *Śravaḥ*:
it is heard, thus *śravaḥ*.
The root *śru* means "to hear. By virtue of the suffix *asun* being marked with the *ṇi*-sign (*ṇit*), the word is accented on its first syllable.
[The term is] *suvīrām*.
She who possesses beautiful heroes is *suvīrā*; [the word] refers to her.
According to the rule “*vīra-vīryau ca*,” there is acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable of the final member of the compound. [He approaches] *supratūrtim*.
The root *tur* has the meaning "to injure.
From this root, preceded by the prefix *pra*, the noun *pratūrti* is formed in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*).
Thus, *supratūrtim* refers to her whose beautiful *pratūrti*—that is, the injuring of enemies—is present.
The acute accent on the first syllable of the second member of the compound is due to the rule "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pāṇini 6.2.199),
or it should be understood as belonging to the "ṛtvādi" group. [The word is] anehasam.

"He is not slain" means "Anehaḥ. [This is derived] by adding the suffix *us* and replacing the root with *eha*, according to the rule *naji hana eha ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.663). Furthermore, the letter *na* is elided according to the rule *nalopo najaḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.73).
Therefore, by the rule *tasmānnaḍaci* (Pāṇini 6.3.74), the augment *nuṭ* is applied.
In the *marutvatīya* śastra of the *agniṣṭoma*, following the *indranivaha-pragātha*, there is the *pragātha* beginning with *pra nūnam*.
This is prescribed in the section on the *marutvatīya* in the Sūtra: *pra nūnaṃ brahmaṇaspata iti brāhmaṇaspatyaḥ* (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.14).
1. [The syllable] *dhana-pha* signifies "he obtains.
2. After the *indrapragātha* and *indranihavapragātha*, [the verse begins]: "Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati utters the hymn worthy of praise."
In whom Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—the gods—have made their dwellings.
Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks the hymn worthy of praise, in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the gods have made their dwellings. 5.
Brahmaṇaspati, the god worthy of praise, standing at the mouth of the Hotṛ priest, certainly proclaims and utters a new mantra fit for recitation.
In that mantra, all the gods, including Indra and others, have made their abodes;
such is the mantra that represents all the gods—this is the connection with what precedes.
The word *mantra* [is derived from] the root *matri*, meaning "to speak secretly";
[the suffix] *ac* is added according to the rule for *pacādyac*.
Because it is listed among the *vṛṣan*-class words, it has the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*).
The word *ukthyam* means "worthy of hymns" (*uktha-arha*); the suffix *ya* is applied in the sense of "fit for" (*arha*) according to the rule *chandasi ca*.
Alternatively,
the suffix *yat* is applied by the rule "in the Veda (*chandas*) after [the root] *bhū*" (*bhave chandasi*).

According to the statement "all rules are optional in the Veda" (*sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante*), since the acute accent on the first syllable— prescribed by the rule "after *yataḥ*, except for *nau*" (*yato ’nāvaḥ*)— is absent, the circumflex accent (*svarita*) applies by the principle of "transposition" (*vyatyayena tisvaritam*).
*Okāṃsi*. [The root] *uc* means "to assemble. In the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇa*)—meaning "they assemble here"—the suffix *asun* is applied according to the *uṇādi* rules.

Regarding the form *cakrire*, it is stated in the commentary (*vṛtti*) on Pāṇini 7.3.64 (*oka ucaḥ ke*) that the substitution of *ku* should be understood due to the inclusion of the word "frequently" (*bahula*). Furthermore,
because the suffix *irec* has the marker *c*, it is *antodātta* (accented on the final syllable).
Non-stress occurs due to its connection with the following syllable.
At our assemblies, O Gods, we utter this hymn that brings well-being and is free from blemish;
and may you, O Heroes, graciously accept these words, so that all our riches may be accompanied by horses.
Let us address him at the assemblies—the auspicious, peerless mantra—O Gods. And if you, O Heroes, take pleasure in this speech, then may all your boons be accompanied by horses.

O gods, beginning with Brahmaṇaspati, may we—the officiating priests—proclaim that very mantra which sets forth all the deities, such as Indra and others, during the *vidathas*, that is, the sacrifices. Of what nature is it? It is *śambhuvam*, the bringer of happiness; *anehasam*, the non-injurious, meaning free from defect.
O leaders, O gods, you take pleasure in this speech consisting of mantras which is being uttered by us;
if you so desire it, then may all desirable and praiseworthy speech pervade you like horses.
We shall say: from the root *vac* in the sense of "speaking," in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*) mood,
the suffix *aṅ* is applied by the rule "in the benedictive, *aṅ* is substituted for *liṅ*."

In the word *vaca um*, there is the augment *um*. Because [the suffix] is treated as *sārvadhātuka* by the rule "in the Veda, both ways" (*chandasyubhayathā*), there is the elision of the *sakāra* of *yāsuṭ* by the rule "the elision of the non-final *sakāra* of the *liṅ*" (*liṅaḥ salopo'nantyasya*).
Then, the substitution of *iy* occurs by the rule "for *ataḥ*, *iy*" (*ato yeyaḥ*).
The suffix is *ādyuṇ*.
There is the *nighāta* (elision of accent) by the rule "tiṅaṅatiṅaḥ.
[The word is] *vidatheṣu*.
In the sense of "knowing" (*vida jñāne*):
that which is known as a means to attain a fruit is *vidatha*, meaning a sacrifice (*yajña*).
The suffix *-atha* is applied according to the rule *ruvidvibhyāṃ kit* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.395).

*Śambhavam*. From the root *bhū*, with the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) implied, the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *kvip ca*. The substitution of *yaṇ* [for the vowel *u*] by the rule *oḥ supi* (Pāṇini 6.4.83) is prohibited by the rule *na bhūsudhiyoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.85).
The [section on] mantras and so forth has concluded.
Now, [the root] *pratiharya* [is considered]; [it is derived from] *harya*, meaning "to go" and "to desire."
Because the root *śap* is classified as *pittva*, it has an udātta accent on the final syllable.
Furthermore, by the rule regarding the accent of *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes, the verbal suffixes have an udātta accent on the first syllable according to the accent of the root.
In the phrase *imāṃ ca*, the word *ca* has the sense of "and."
*caṇ* is another particle (*nipātāntara*) and does not have the sense of conjunction (*samuccaya*).
Therefore, by the rule *nipātairyadyadihantakuvinecceccaṇ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.1.30), there is a prohibition of the grave accent (*nighāta*).
[The form] was *abhavat*.

1. Regarding the mantra beginning with *ḍha*, the *Ṛgveda* (38) states: "The root *aśnu* means 'to pervade' (*vyāptau*). In the *leṭ* mood, there is the addition of *aṭ*. By transposition (*vyatyaya*), the active voice (*parasmaipada*) is used. The vowel *i* is elided according to the rule "and [the *i*] after this [root]" (*itaśca lopaḥ*). Then, by the rule "in place of *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*, the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions take precedence" (*iyaṅuvaṅbhyāṃ guṇavṛddhī bhavataḥ vipratiṣedhena*), the *guṇa* substitution occurs.

Who [is there] like a god among men, like one with horses, or who [has offered] trimmed sacrificial grass? The donor has advanced far with his dwellings; he has returned within and established his home.

Who [has approached] the one who goes to the gods, the one possessing horses, the people? Who [has approached] the one for whom the sacrificial grass has been spread? The donor has stepped forth further and further with his dwellings; he has established a dwelling that protects within. 7.
Who indeed, other than Brahmaṇaspati, could pervade—that is, encompass—the person who seeks the gods, who desires the deities?
Likewise, who else among the gods could prevail over the sacrificer who has trimmed the sacrificial grass—that is, who has prepared the *barhis* for the performance?
Who indeed, other than he, could overcome the sacrificer who has offered the oblation (*dāśvān*) with his domestic dwellings?

*Pṛcchīta*: from the root *pṛcī* in the sense of "contact. Because it belongs to the *rudhādi* class, there is *śnam*. By the rule *kṣasoralopaḥ*, the letter *a* is elided. It bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). Since the meaning of conjunction (*cārtha*) characterized by accumulation is seen in the phrase "and he slays the kings with his power" (*kṣatreṇa pṛcchīta rājabhir hanti*), the prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of accent) for the first finite verb occurs by the rule *cādilope vibhāṣā*. The word *hanti*—this second finite verb—is also not elided because it follows another finite verb (*tiṅ*). *Sukṣitim*: a beautiful dwelling (*kṣiti*) is *sukṣiti*. By the rule *manūkkin* etc., the final syllable of the latter member (*uttarapada*) has the acute accent. *Vartā*: from the roots *vṛt* ("to turn") or *vṛ* ("to choose") with the suffix *tṛc*; the absence of the augment *iṭ* is due to the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the rules prescribing augments. *Tarutā*: from the root *tṛ* in the sense of "swimming" or "crossing. By the rule *prasitaskamita* etc. (Pāṇini 7.2.34), the augment *uṭ* is prescribed after the suffix *tṛc*. It has the acute accent on the final syllable by the rule *citaḥ*. *Mahādhane*: that which is great and that which is a treasure (*dhana*) is *mahādhana*. By the rule *ātmahataḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.46), the vowel *ā* is substituted [for the final *a*]. By that word, the battle (*saṃgrāma*) consisting of such wealth is indicated. *Arbhe*: from the root *ṛ* in the sense of "going. By the rule *arti-bhyāṃ bhan* (Uṇādisūtra 3.432), the suffix *bhan* is added. Because it consists of a single syllable (*nisva*), it has the acute accent on the first syllable. || 21 ||

"Yaṃ rakṣanti" (whom they protect) is the sixth hymn, consisting of nine verses. Regarding it, the Anukramaṇī states: "Yaṃ rakṣanti—nine [verses]; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman [are the deities]; the third triplet is addressed to the Ādityas; it is in the Gāyatrī meter. The seer is Kaṇva, the son of Ghora.
These first three hymns consist of *gāyatrī* verses.
In the first and last *ṛc*s, the deities are Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman;
for the middle *ṛc*, "sugaḥ panthāḥ," the deities are the Ādityas.
The application is concluded.
That person whom the wise Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect— now, truly,
that man is not to be subdued.
The man whom the wise Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect—never indeed is that person subdued. ||1||

The *pracetasaḥ*—the gods such as Varuṇa and others who possess excellent wisdom (*prakṛṣṭajñāna*)—protect which sacrificer; that person, the sacrificer, is *nū cit*, very quickly indeed, *damyate*: he subdues, he destroys his enemies. Regarding *pracetasaḥ*: those whose consciousness (*cetas*) is preeminent (*prakṛṣṭa*). In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, there is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member. Regarding *nū cit*: the lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule "in the Ṛgveda, after *tu*, *nu*, *gha*, etc. Regarding *damyate*: from the root *dambhu* (to deceive/subdue). By metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*), the suffix *śyan* and the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) are employed.
Whom they protect with their very arms and guard from harm for mortals—
he thrives unharmed in every way.
Whom they carry across as if with their arms, who protect him from harm through his prayers—he prospers, unharmed, by means of all [the gods]. || 2 ||

Whichever sacrificer the gods, Varuṇa and the others, fill with riches—therein is the illustration: "by the arm itself. Just as one's own set of arms, having brought the required wealth, fills [the need], so it is here. Likewise, whichever mortal man, the sacrificer, they protect—that is, guard him—from *riṣas*, the injurer; that entire sacrificer, being *ariṣṭaḥ* (unharmed) by anyone, *edhate*, prospers. [Grammatical notes: *bāhutaiva*: *bāhutā* means "the state of being the arm" (*bāhutvam*). By this word expressing a state (*bhāva*), the physical arms and their functions are indicated. Alternatively, the suffix *tal* should be understood in the sense of a collection (*samūha*). According to the rule *liti*, the vowel preceding the suffix is acute. *piprati*: from the root *pṛ* in the sense of "protecting" or "filling. Some read it as *pṛ*. Due to its belonging to the *juhotyādi* class, there is reduplication (*ślu*). By the rule *atipiparatyośca*, the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes *i*. By the rule *abhyastānām ādiḥ*, the initial syllable is acute. *pānti*: There is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*) because of the subsequent *tiṅ* ending or because it begins a *pāda*. *riṣaḥ*: from the root *riṣ* in the sense of "injuring. By the rule *kip ca*, the suffix *kip* is applied. By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the case-ending is acute. *ariṣṭaḥ*: from the root *riṣ* in the sense of "injuring. By the rule *ekācaḥ*, there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*. The change to *ṣ* occurs via *brahmādi* (Pāṇini 8.3.105). In the negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), the original accent of the first member, being an indeclinable, prevails.

"300" refers to the [root] *as* (to be). There is the substitution of *ī* by the rule "ghumāsthā0. [In the form] *naśat*, the root *naś* has the meaning of moving. In the *leṭ* [mood], there is the addition of *aṭ*. By the rule "itaśca lopaḥ," there is the elision of the vowel *i*. || 22 ||

That mortal, unassailed, goes toward the jewel, toward all wealth, and toward his offspring by his own self. 6. He; the jewel; the mortal; wealth; all; offspring; and; by himself; toward; he goes; unassailed. 6.
O Ādityas, such a mortal—a human sacrificer—favored by you, being unassailed (astṛta) by anyone and unhurt, goes toward and attains *ratnam*, the delightful universal wealth (*viśvam vasu*);
and moreover, by himself (*tmanā*), he attains offspring (*tokam*) worthy of himself.
In the word *ātmanā*, the vowel *ā* is elided according to Pāṇini’s rule 6.4.141, which states that the initial *ā* of *ātman* is dropped in mantras. [The form is] *accha*.
The lengthening [of the vowel] is according to the rule *nipātasya ca*. [The word is] *astṛtaḥ*.
[It is derived from] the root *stṛñ* in the sense of "injuring."
*na stuto'stṛtaḥ*: [The word] *astṛtaḥ* [is derived from] *na stutaḥ*. [In this compound], the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the preceding member (*pūrvapada*) is retained.

How, O friends, shall we accomplish the hymn of praise for Mitra and Aryaman—the great refreshment of Varuṇa? 7. How? We shall accomplish. O friends. The hymn of praise. Of Mitra. Of Aryaman. The great. Refreshment. Of Varuṇa. 7.

"O friends"—the priests who have become companions. "The great, vast *psaras* (form)"—the form of the three [deities] beginning with Mitra. Therefore, in what manner, by what means, shall we accomplish (*rādhāma*) the hymn (*stoma*), the song of praise that corresponds to that? Regarding the word *kathā*: according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 5.3.26, *thā* is used after the interrogative *kim* to express manner; since it is designated as a case-ending (*vibhakti*) by the rule "those ending in *prāgdiśaḥ* are called case-endings," there is the substitution of *ka-* for *kim* by Sūtra 7.2.103. It bears the accent of a suffix (*pratyayasvara*). *rādhāma*: from the root *rādha* (or *sādha*) in the sense of "accomplishment. In the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, the suffix is elided by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). It receives the *nighāta* (suppression of accent) by the rule "a verb preceded by a non-verb is unaccented. *stomam*: from the root *ṭuñ* in the sense of "praising. The suffix *man* is added in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) by the rule beginning with *arti-stu-su-*. Because it has the marker *ni*, it is accented on the first syllable. *aryamṇaḥ*: in the genitive singular, the vowel *ā* is elided by the rule *alopo'naḥ*. The case-ending becomes accented by the rule regarding the "cessation of the acute accent" (*udāttanivṛttisvara*). *mahi*: from the root *maha* in the sense of "worship. The suffix *in* is added according to the Uṇādi rules. *psaraḥ*: from the root *psā* in the sense of "eating. That which eats (*psāti*) is *psaraḥ*, the form. The suffix *ḍa* is added according to the Uṇādi rules.

I shall not speak back to you who strike nor to you who curse, for you are seekers of the gods; with hymns of praise alone do I seek to win your favor. 8. I shall not speak back to you who strike, nor to you who curse, for you are seekers of the gods; with hymns of praise indeed do I seek to win your favor. 8.

O gods, Mitra and the others, I shall not speak back to you regarding such an enemy who strikes—that is, slays—the sacrificer who seeks the gods and desires them; out of fear of uttering evil words, I do not mention him. Likewise, I shall not speak back to you concerning that enemy who curses the sacrificer; the meaning is that you yourselves must deliberate and provide instruction.
As for me, however, I honor you on all sides with fair wealth alone.
*Ghanantaṃ*:
"He strikes" is *ghnan*;
by the rule beginning with *gamahana*, there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*).
In the word *hantṛ*, the substitution of *ku* (i.e., *t* becoming *ṭ*) occurs according to the rule *ho hanteḥ*; it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
[The word] *śapantam* is derived from the root *śapa* in the sense of "reviling" (*ākrośe*).
Because it is taught as having an initial vowel (adupadeśa), when the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains; thus, *voce*.
[The root] *brūñ* means "in distinct speech."
In the case of *luṅ* with *māṅ*, because of the rule *‘bruvo vaciḥ’* (Pāṇini Sūtra 2.4.53).

Regarding the word *vaci*: by the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.52), the suffix *kle* is replaced by *aṅ*. By the rule *vaca um*, the augment *um* is added. By the rule *na māḍyoge*, there is no addition of the augment *aṭ*. Regarding *devayantam*: [derived from] *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pāṇini 3.1.8). By the rule *na chandasyaputrasya*, the prohibition of the long vowel (*ītvapratiṣedha*) does not apply here. Regarding *sumnaiḥ*: from the root *mnā* in the sense of "repetition" (*abhyāse*). That which is well known or well bestowed is *sumnam*. By the rule *ātaścopasarge* (Pāṇini 3.1.136), the suffix *kapratyaya* is applied. By the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca*, the vowel *ā* is elided. Regarding *vivāse*: the root *vivāsati* has the meaning of "attending upon" or "serving" (*paricaraṇakarmā*) according to the Nighaṇṭu (3.5.10).

A wise man should indeed fear even one who gives, until he has completely laid down [the gift]. He should not long for ill-spoken words. || 9 || A wise man: *caturaḥ*. Indeed: *cit*. From one who gives: *dadamānāt*. Should fear: *bibhīyāt*. Until: *ā*. Having completely laid down: *nidhātoḥ*. Not: *na*. Ill-spoken words: *duruktāni*. He should long for: *spṛhayet*. || 9 ||
Regarding what was said—that one should not respond to someone who strikes or reviles—the reasoning for that is now stated:
"One should not long for ill-spoken words"; one should not desire wicked speech, but rather fear it.
In this regard, the entire remaining portion of the mantra serves as an illustration.
The word *cit* is used here in the sense of a simile.

Between two men playing dice, there may be a man who, while holding four dice (*kapadakān*) in his hand as they are being cast by another person, becomes apprehensive until the dice fall, wondering, "Will he win? Will he not win?
In this case, just as there is fear, so too should one understand the secret of Dharma regarding ill-spoken words.
Therefore, my intention is: "I shall not respond to one who strikes or reviles me.
Regarding this, the Nirukta states: "He holds four dice; thus, as one would fear a gambler, so too should one fear ill-spoken words; one should not long for ill-spoken words" (Nirukta 3.16).
*caturaḥ*: by the rule *caturaḥ śasi* (Pāṇini 6.1.167), the syllable preceding the case-ending is acute. *dadamānāt*.
In the root *dada* [meaning] ‘giving,’ the sense here is ‘holding. Because it is marked with the *pittva* designation, the suffix *śap* is unaccented (*anudātta*).
Because it is taught as having an initial vowel (adupadeśāt), the *śānac* suffix is unaccented due to the rule that *lasārvadhātuka* affixes are unaccented;
thus, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) alone remains. Example: *bibhīyāt*.
‘jibhī bhaye’ (the root *bhī* in the sense of fear).
Because it belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class, there is *śap*-elision;
[in the potential mood], the augment *yāsuṭ* is acute.
There is no *nighāta* because it begins with a *pāda*.
Regarding *nidhātaḥ*: from the root *dhā* preceded by the prefix *ni*, the suffix *tun* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule *sitanigami* (Uṇādisūtra 1.69).
The initial udātta accent occurs by way of transposition;
the *gati* accent prescribed by the rule “*tādau ca*” does not apply here because it is excluded by the rule “*atau*”.
[The word is] *duruktāya*.

By the rule *spṛhayepsitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.4.36), the designation of recipient (*saṃpradāna*) is applied; consequently, by the rule *caturthī saṃpradāne* (Pāṇini 2.3.13), the dative case is used. [The verb] *spṛhayet* [is derived from] *spṛha* [meaning] "desire" (*īpsā*).
The root *cur* belongs to the *cur-ādi* class.
Due to the status of the elision (*lopa*) as *sthānivadbhāva*, there is an absence of the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*).
The seventh hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with “saṃ pūpan,” is attributed to Kaṇva, is in the Gāyatrī meter, and has Pūṣan as its deity.
It is designated as such by the statement: “‘saṃ pūpan,’ ten verses; dedicated to Pūṣan.

According to the Smṛti, one should mutter this hymn when about to travel a long distance: “When about to travel a great distance or a dangerous path, [one should recite] ‘saṃ pūpan vacana’” (Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra 3.7.10). This is because it is so prescribed in the Sūtra.
In that context, the word "one should recite" (japet) is understood to carry over.

O Pūṣan, traverse our paths; O Son of Deliverance, remove our distress. O God, as our friend, speed us forward. O Pūṣan, traverse our paths; O Son of Deliverance, remove our distress. O God, as our friend, speed us forward.
1. Ca-pha: "It shall not be" [is] non-existent.
O Vpūṣan, nourisher of the world, O deity presiding over the earth, from the path of the wayfarer (vadhvanaḥ), lead us completely across (saṃ tira) to our desired destination.
Drive away (vi tira) the darkness (vaṃhaḥ)—the sin that is the cause of obstacles.
Pūṣan is further specified as *vvimuco napāt*, the grandson of the cloud that causes the release of water;
for *napāt* is a name for a son, as it is listed among the names for offspring in the Nirukta (2.2.13): "grandson (*napāt*) means progeny."
In another Vedic text, the origin of the earth from water is heard: "The fires are the earth.
Likewise, elsewhere too, the earth's essence being water is heard: "That which was the essence of the waters condensed; it became the earth.
Since a cloud is a bearer of water, the son of a cloud is indeed the son of water.
Nor should it be said that because the Earth is the daughter of the Cloud (*meghaputrī*), what concern does this have for Pūṣan? For the Earth itself is Pūṣan.
Thus, in another Śruti, the Brāhmaṇa portion of a certain mantra is known as follows: "Pūṣan protects the paths; this [Earth] indeed is Pūṣan.
And its etymological explanation is handed down elsewhere thus: "This indeed is Pūṣan, for she nourishes (*puṣyati*) everything here, whatever exists" (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14.4.2.25).
O divine Pūṣan, go before us; advance in front of us, be our leader—meaning, proceed ahead.
Vimuc’s son:
he is called *vimuṅ* because he releases water; *vimuṅ* is a cloud. [The suffix] *kip* is applied according to the rule “*kip ca*”.
A *napāt* is a son because he does not cause his family to fall (*na pātayati kulam*). The suffix *kvip* is applied to the root *pātayati* preceded by the negative particle *na*.
In accordance with the rule “*nabhrāṇnapāt...*” etc., there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) of the negative particle *na*.
In the case of *subāmantrita*, because it is treated as a subordinate member (*parāṅgavadbhāva*), the entire vocative compound takes the low accent (*sarvānudātta*) beginning with its first syllable.
[The word] *sakṣva* [is derived from the root] *pac*, meaning "to serve."
The *ātmanepada* ending occurs because the root is marked with the *anudātta* accent.

In the *loṭ* mood, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap* according to the rule "there is diversely [elision] in the Veda. Since the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are *anudātta* by the rule "the [suffixes] following *tās*, *ya*, and *sīyuṭ* are *anudātta*," the accent of the verbal root remains.
In *pra naḥ*, the *ṇ* replaces *n* according to the rule *upasargāddhasvam*. In *puraḥ*:
It has been said.
O Pūṣan, whatever malevolent wolf or ill-omened one plots against us,
strike him away from our path.
O Pūṣan, whatever malevolent wolf, ill-omened, lies in wait for us—strike him down from the path.

O Pūṣan, that adversary who points us out—commanding us, "One must go by this path"—that one, who is a *vṛka* (a wolf), meaning a striker or a plunderer of our wealth; who is *duḥśeva*, meaning difficult to serve or bringing ill-fortune—drive him away from the path; indeed, cast him down! Regarding *vṛka*: from the root *kuk-vṛk* in the sense of "seizing" (*ādadāne*). He is called *vṛka* because he "covers" (*vṛṇoti*) [his prey]. The suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule for roots ending in *ig*. It is acutely accented on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group. Regarding *duḥśeva*: he whose *śeva* (comfort/affection) is evil is *duḥśeva*. By the rule "in the Veda, the accentuation of the latter member is frequently [retained] even when the compound begins with *para*," the acute accent falls on the first syllable of the second member. Alternatively, *duḥśeva* means "he who is served with difficulty. Here, the letter *sa* is changed to *śa* through metathesis. The suffix *khal* is added according to the rule "after *īṣat*, *duḥ*, and *su*. By the accent of the *lit*-suffixes, the syllable preceding the suffix is acute. This results in the original accent of the second member of the compound being preserved. Regarding *ādidēśati*: from the root *diś* in the sense of "assigning" (*atisarjane*). In the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, there is the augment *aṭ*. By the rule "frequently in the Veda," there is the elision (*ślū*) of the *śap* (present marker). Due to the statement "it should be stated 'frequently in the Veda,'" the prohibition of *guṇa* for a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadha*) found in the rule "not for a reduplicated stem before a vowel" (*nābhyastasyāci*) does not apply here. Regarding *pathaḥ*: the case-ending is acute by the rule concerning the accent of the "cessation of the acute" (*udāttanivṛtti-svara*).
Drive far away that highwayman, the liar who plots against us with deceit.
Cast him out from the path of our journey.
Drive far away from our path that highwayman who speaks deceitfully and plots evil against us. 3.
Drive far away— toward a place extremely distant from the path of the son— that very one who possesses the aforementioned qualities,
who is an adversary obstructing the way, and who is a thief in the form of a sage.
One should not go toward a thief with the words "I am like a fool," nor [with the sounds] ca,
cha, ṇa, pa, ya, la, śa, sa, or na.

[The word *muṣīvān*] is so called because it is listed among its names as ‘*muṣīvān mlimlucaḥ*’ (Nirukta 3.24.11). [The word *huraścit*]: “[The one who is] a gatherer (*saṃcetāra*) of the deceits (*huraḥ*) of the Kautsyas, a waylayer (*paripanthinam*). The form ending in the suffix *-in* is a Vedic irregularity (*nipātita*) when the sense is that of a waylayer, according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 5.2.89: “*paripanthi-pariparṇau* are used in the Veda (*chandas*) when a waylayer (*paryavasthātṛ*) is to be expressed. *Muṣīvānam*: [The root] *muṣ* means “to steal. Stealing is *muṣiḥ*. The suffix *k* is added in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*) according to the Uṇādi rules. One who seeks after (*vanati*) or pursues (*saṃbhajate*) such stealing is a *muṣīvā*. [The root] *van* and *paṇ* mean “to seek after. The suffix *vic* is added according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.75: “It is seen [added] after other [roots] as well. The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.4.8: “In the place of a case-ending (*sarvanāmasthāna*), except in the vocative singular (*asaṃbuddhau*). The lengthening of the first member [of the compound] occurs according to the rule “it is seen after others as well. *Huraścitam*: [The root] *hṛ* means “deceit. An abstract action noun (*bhāva*) is formed with the suffix *k* according to the class beginning with *saṃpad*. By the rule “elision of *rā*,” the letter *ch* is elided. One who gathers (*cinoti*) deceits is *huraścit*. When *ci* takes the suffix *k*, there is the augment *tug*. There is no elision of the *k* by the rule “in a *tatpuruṣa* compound, before a *kṛt*-suffix, [the elision] is frequent” (*bahulam*). The accent is that of the original form of the final member of the compound. *Suteḥ*: [The root] *sū* means “to go. The suffix *kvic* is added according to the rule “*kvic* and *cau* are added in the sense of a name (*saṃjñāyām*). The acute accent (*udātta*) is on the final syllable by the rule “*citaḥ*. *Aja*: [The root] *aj* means “to move” and “to throw.”
Tread with your foot upon the burning heat of that malicious person, whoever he may be, who seeks to harm you.
O you, trample with your foot upon the burning heat of that two-footed one, whoever he may be, who utters evil against us. 4.
O Pūṣan, trample with your foot—that is, stand upon and tread down—the burning body of that thief, which causes torment to others.
Of what sort?
Of one who possesses the two [forms of theft]: both manifest seizure and secret seizure; and of one who proclaims his own evil, speaking of his own undesirable misfortune.
*Aghaśaṃsa* is a name for a thief, as it is listed among those names in the Nirukta (3.24.13): *mlimlucaḥ aghaśaṃsaḥ vṛkaḥ*. *Kasya cit* means "of someone," referring to an unspecified person.
*Dvāvī*:
one who possesses a pair (*dvaya*) is a *dvāvī*. The suffix *vini* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 5.2.122, *bahulaṃ chandasi*.
The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs according to the rule "it is also seen elsewhere.
Regarding *aghaśaṃsa*:
he whose mind’s desire (*śaṃsa*) is directed toward evil (*agha*), that is, toward sin (*pāpa*), is an *aghaśaṃsa*.
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [is maintained].
*Tapuṣim*:
it is called *tapuṣi* because one causes another to suffer by means of it.
The suffix *uṣiṇac* is [added] according to the *auṇādika* rules.
Due to the statement "in many cases" (*bahulavacanāt*), the letter *i* does not receive the designation *it*.
Because of the *nit*-designation, there is acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyudāttatvam*).
O Pūṣan, most wise one, we choose that aid of thine by which thou didst cause our fathers to prosper.
O Pūṣan, most wise Dasta, we choose that favor of yours by which you impelled the fathers. 5.

O wise one, O you who possess knowledge, O you who are worthy of being seen, or rather, O you who act for the sake of the virtuous— O Pūṣan, we choose, that is, we pray for from all sides, that protection of yours (*avaḥ*) which is such that by means of it you impelled (*acodayaḥ*), that is, set in motion, the ancestors such as Aṅgiras and others, who were in the bodies of *pitṛ*s. "That protection" is to be connected with the preceding clause.
*dasta*: [derived from] the roots *das* and *daṃś*, meaning "to bite" or "to see.
By the rule beginning with *sphāyitañca*, the suffix *rak* is applied.
The absence of the augment *num* is due to the non-constraint (*aniyatta*) of the self-instruction (*ātmanānuśāsana*).
Alternatively,
from the root *dasu* in the sense of "wasting away" (*upakṣaye*), with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) internalized, the suffix *rak* is applied as before.
*Mantu-maḥ*: [derived from] the root *man* in the sense of "knowing. By the rule *kaminajini* (Uṇādi-sūtra 1.72), etc., the suffix *tu* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
One who possesses knowledge (*jñāna*) is "possessed of knowledge" (*mantumān*). In the vocative case, according to the rule *matuvaso ruḥ*, the substitution of *ru* occurs.
[This results in] *acaudayaḥ*.
‘Cuda-saṃcodane’: it belongs to the *cur*-class (the ninth class).
O you who possess all good fortune, most richly endowed with golden axes, grant us wealth that is easy to win.
O most auspicious one for us all, you who possess the finest golden axe, bestow upon us well-gained riches. || 6 ||

O Viśvasaubhaga, you who possess all wealth—or rather, all good fortune—O Pūṣan, most abundantly armed with golden weapons, after our aforementioned prayer, make our riches—gold, gems, pearls, and so forth—*suṣaṇā*, that is, excellently endowed with the act of giving. Make them thus.
Now, regarding the word *adha*: the change of *atha* to *adha* is a Vedic (chāndasa) phenomenon; the lengthening [of the vowel] in the *saṃhitā* is according to the rule *nipātasya ca*.
Regarding *viśvasaubhaga*:
since the word *subhaga* is not included among the words beginning with *udātta* in the rule *subhaganmantre*, the suffix *añ* is applied.

Although the rule *hasrāgre-sindhante pūrvapadasya ca* would have required the vṛddhi of the final vowel of the second member (*uttarapada*), the commentary states that because all case-endings are optional in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the vṛddhi of the second member does not take place (Kāśikā 7.2.19).
He who possesses all auspicious fortunes is Viśvasaubhaga;
[this is] an *āmantrita-nighāta* (the enclitic accentuation of a vocative).
O you who possess the most excellent golden axe!
A golden axe;
because they possess this, they are called "those who possess the golden axe" (*hiraṇyavāśīmantaḥ*).
One who possesses the golden axe to the highest degree is "the most excellent possessor of the golden axe" (*hiraṇyavāśīmattamaḥ*).
The vocative is unaccented. *Suṣaṇā*:
[from] the roots *vana* and *ṣaṇa* in the sense of "gathering" or "bestowing."
They are called *suṣaṇāni* because they are easily enjoyed (*sukhena saṃbhajyante*). The suffix *khal* is applied by the rule *īṣadduḥsuṣu*;
the elision of the suffix *śe* occurs by the rule *śe chandasi*.

By the rule *liti*, the vowel preceding the suffix *lit* is udātta; furthermore, by the rule *kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svara*, the original accent of the final member of the compound is retained. [Thus: *kṛdhi*.
The root *ḍukuñ* means "to do.
According to the rule *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛmyabhchandasi*, the substitute *dhi* is applied for the suffix *hi*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is elision (*luk*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*).

Lead us beyond our enemies; make our paths easy to traverse and fair to travel. O Purishan, find wisdom for us here. (7) Lead us beyond our adversaries; make our ways easy to go and our paths fair. O Purishan, grant us insight here. (7)
O Pūṣan, lead those eternal enemies who seek to harm us beyond us, leading them elsewhere;
make us travelers upon a fair path, a beautiful road easy to traverse.
On this journey, O Pūṣan, perceive our *kratu*—our wisdom consisting of our protection.
"Saśvataḥ.
Regarding this, it is stated in the *Dhātuvṛtti* that some read "gluñja pastagatau" as including "saści" as well.
From this root, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied in the sense of the present tense (*laṭ*).

The elision of the suffix *śap* occurs by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 2.4.73). The acute accent (*udātta*) of the suffix *śatṛ* is due to the accent of the affix itself. The absence of the acute accent on the case-ending, as in "śatrūn," is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).

*Suga*: "Suga" means that which one goes well (*suṣṭhu gacchanti*) to; the suffix *ḍa* is applied to the root *gam* by the rule "after *su* and *dur*, [the suffix *ḍa* is used] in the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇe*)."
By the rule "supām suluk," the third case ending is replaced by the vowel *ā*; thus,
*supathā* means "by a beautiful path."
By the rule *na pūjanāt* (Pāṇini Sūtra 5.4.69), there is a prohibition against the application of a compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*).
By the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*, the acute accent (*udātta*) falls on the beginning of the second member of the compound;
however, by the rule *ṛtvādyaś ca*, the acute accent does not fall on the beginning of the second member here, because this is not a *bahuvrīhi* compound.
For there, the term "bahuvrīhi" continues to apply.
[The root] *kṛṇu* [is used];
[the root] *kṛvī* means "to injure" and "to do."
The suffix *u* is applied by the rule *dhinvikṛṇvyora ca*; the elision of *hi* occurs by the rule *utaśca pratyayāt*. [Thus we have] *vidaḥ*.
The root *vid* means "to know.
In the *leṭ* [subjunctive] mood, there is the augment *aṭ*. By the rule "there is elision of the *i* [of the suffix] after [a verbal root ending in] *it*," the *i* is elided.

Lead us toward good pasture; do not let a new fever afflict us on our journey. O Puru, find wisdom for us here. 8. Lead us toward good pasture; do not let a new fever afflict us on our journey. O Puru, find wisdom for us here. 8.
O Pūṣan, lead us toward a place abounding in excellent grass—that is, a region endowed with all kinds of vegetation; bring us to it from every side.
May there be no "new fever"—that is, no fresh distress—for the journey;
the meaning is: may no affliction whatsoever befall us as we travel on the path.
The rest has its meaning already explained.
*Suyavasaṃ*: A region in which the pasture (*yavasa*) is excellent is a *suyavasa* region.
The lengthening of the vowel in the first member of the compound is according to the rule *nipātasya ca*.

In accordance with the rule “*parādiś chandasi bahulam*,” the acute accent (*udātta*) should be understood as belonging to the beginning of the second member of the compound, or it may be seen as belonging to the *kravadi* group. Thus, *navajvāraḥ*;
[the root] *jvara* is used in the sense of “disease.”
The suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an action (*bhāva*).
This fever (*jvara*) is new, hence it is "new-fever" (*navajvara*).
By the rule beginning with "thā-thādi," the final syllable of the second member of the compound is acute-accented.
Be strong, be wide, and bestow; sharpen your teeth and fill your belly. O Pūṣan, find skill here for us. 9. Be strong. Be wide. Bestow. And. Sharpen. Fill. Your belly. O Pūṣan. Here. Skill. Find. 9.

O Pūṣan, be able (*śadhi*) to favor us; fill (*pṛdhi*) our house with wealth; furthermore, bestow (*pra yaṃsi*) whatever other thing is desired; sharpen (*śiśīhi*) us—meaning make us keen among all, that is, make us radiant; fill (*prāsi*) our belly with well-prepared food or Soma juice; the rest is as before. *Śadhi*: from the root *śak* (to be able). The suffix *hi* is used for the imperative (*loṭ*). By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is elision of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*). By the rule *hujhalbhyo hedhiḥ*, *hi* is replaced by *dhi*. Since *hi* is not included in the *apit* group, it is accented on its first syllable by the accent of the suffix. *pṛdhi*: from the root *pṛ* (to protect or to fill). By the rule *śruśṛpukṛvṛbhyaśchandasi*, *hi* is replaced by *dhi*. As before, there is elision of the suffix. By the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*, the vowel becomes *u*. By the rule *hali ca*, there is lengthening. Because it follows a finite verb (*tiṅ*), there is no suppression of accent (*nighāta*). *Yaṃsi*: from the root *yam* (to cease). Used in the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*) with the present suffix (*laṭ*). As before, there is elision of the suffix. There is suppression of accent (*nighāta*). *Śiśīhi*: from the root *śo* (to sharpen/thin). In the imperative, by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 7.4.78), there is *itva* (change to *i*) of the reduplicated syllable. By the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*, there is *ītva* (change to *ī*). The accent is that of the suffix. *Prāsi*: from the root *prā* (to fill). Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision of *śap*. Since the suffix *sip* is marked as *pit*, it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the root remains.

We do not revile Pūṣan; we praise him with well-spoken hymns. We implore the wondrous one for riches. 10. We do not revile Pūṣan; we praise him with well-spoken hymns. We implore the wondrous one for riches. 10.

We do not strike against the god Pūṣan, nor do we revile him; rather, with hymns (*sūkta*) belonging to the Veda, we praise him—we extol him everywhere. We beg for wealth, for riches, from the wondrous (*dasman*), the beautiful Pūṣan. Regarding *methāmasi*: the root *meth* is used in the senses of "to strike" and "to injure. In the present tense (*laṭ*), by the rule "the augment *i* is added before *masi*," the letter *i* is inserted before *mas*. Regarding *sūktaiḥ*: they are called *sūktas* because they well-praise and illuminate the deities. By the rule "the suffix *ka* is applied after a root ending in *k* or *ic* when forming a name," the suffix *ka* is used in the sense of the agent. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule beginning with "vacisvapi... etc. The accent is that of the *thāthādi* group. Alternatively, it is a past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*). By the rule "after a word denoting a good object of comparison, the suffix *ka* is applied," there is an acute accent on the final syllable of the compound. Regarding *gṛṇīmasi*: the root *gṛ* means "to sound. There is shortening according to the rule "the roots beginning with *pvā* take a short vowel. The suffix *masi* takes the augment *i*. Regarding *dasman*: the suffix *mak* is applied by the rule "the suffix *mak* is added to the roots *iṣ*, *yudh*, *iṣ*, *das*, *si*, *vyadh*, and *ūs*. [Verse 25]
The eighth hymn, consisting of nine verses, begins with "kadrudrāya.

Regarding this, it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "‘kadrudrāya’: nine verses; addressed to Rudra; the third verse is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa; another triplet is dedicated to Soma; the others are in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
The seer (ṛṣi) is Kaṇva, the son of Ghora.
The Gāyatrī is the metre;
“yāste prajāḥ” is another verse in the Anuṣṭubh metre;
Rudra is the deity.
The hymn beginning with “Just as Mitra” (*yathā no mitraḥ*) has Mitra and Varuṇa as its deities;
however, the other triplet beginning with “Upon us, O Soma” (*asme soma*) is dedicated to Soma alone.
In all rituals having Rudra as the deity, the worship of the directions (*dig-upasthāna*) should be performed with this hymn.

And thus it is stated in the Sūtra: “‘To which Rudra... for this Rudra, O father... to this Rudra with the firm bow’—this is the worship of the quarters in all sacrifices to Rudra” (Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra 4.1.21–22).

To Rudra, the wise, the most bountiful, the most powerful—let us speak what is most auspicious for his heart. 1. To whom? To Rudra. Who? To the wise one, to the most generous, to the most mighty. What shall we say? That which is most peaceful for the heart. 1.
1. [The letters] gha, cha, śa, sa, and va. 2. Ca, na, śa, ma, and they say [the letter] brū.

When, O Rudra—unto that deity of this name—shall we recite, or shall we chant, a hymn most *śaṃtama*, exceedingly productive of happiness? To what kind of one? To the *pracetase*, endowed with preeminent wisdom; to the *mīḷhuṣṭamāya*, the most bountiful, meaning the one who rains down desired objects; to the *tavīyase*, the most powerful; and to the *hṛde*, the one beloved within our hearts. *Kat*, *kadā*: the elision of the final syllable is due to Vedic license (*chāndasa*). *Rudrāya*: he causes all to weep at the time of the end, thus he is Rudra. The suffix *rak* is applied by the rule *rodeṇilukca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.179). *Pracetase*: from the root *citī* in the sense of perception; he perceives excellently, thus *pracetas*. By the rule *gatikārakayor api pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca*, the suffix *asuṇ* is applied and the first member retains its original accent. *Mīḷhuṣṭamāya*: he who has given excessively is *mīḷhuṣṭama*. This is a form ending in the suffix *asuṇ* established by the rule *dādhān sāhvān mīḍhāṃśca*. The substitution of *vasu* for *mīḍhvan* occurs by the rule *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*; the change of *v* to *p* occurs by the rule *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*. *Tabhyase*: *tan* is a Vedic root in the sense of increasing; he who has become exceedingly great is *tavīyān*. The suffix *īyasun* is applied by the rule *tubh chandasi*; the *tu* is elided by the rule *tur iḍāyyeṣu*; the elision of the *ī* of *īyasun* is due to Vedic license. It is acute-accented on the first syllable because of the *niṭ* designation. *Vocema*: from the root *vaca* in the sense of speaking; the suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*), becoming *aṅ*; the augment *um* is added by the rule *vaca um*. The vowel *e* is acute by the accent of the *yāsuṭ* augment. *Hṛde*: by the rule *padana* etc., the word *hṛdaya* is replaced by *hṛd*; the acute accent of the case-ending is by the rule *uḍiḍam* etc.

So that Aditi may grant us Rudra’s favor for our cattle, for our men, for our kine, and for our offspring. 2. So that Aditi may grant us Rudra’s favor for our cattle, for our men, for our kine, and for our offspring. 2.

May Aditi, the Earth, provide for us that Rudriya—the medicinal remedy related to Rudra—in such a manner that it may be effective; may she act accordingly. Furthermore, may she provide it in such a way that the Rudriya, beneficial specifically for our cattle—such as horses, buffaloes, and other livestock—as well as for our men and especially for the bovine species, becomes effective. Moreover, may she provide it in such a way that the Rudriya becomes effective for our offspring.

The connection of *bheṣaja* with Rudra is well-known from another mantra: “O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is auspicious and healing every day—that auspicious healing power of Rudra” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5.10.1).

Furthermore, the healing of cattle and other animals is clearly recorded elsewhere: “Healing for the cow, healing for the horse, healing for man, and then for us, excellent healing” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.8.6.1).
He did. [The root] *ḍukuñ* means "to do.
In the *laṅ* tense, there is an irregular substitution of *śap*.
Alternatively,
there is the augment *aṭ* in the *leṭ* [subjunctive] mood;
and by the rule "elision of the *it*" (*itaśca lopaḥ*), there is the elision of the vowel *i*.
Alternatively,

in the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, there is the substitution of *aṭ* for the *cli* suffix according to the rule “*kṛmṛdṛhibhyaśchandasi*” (Pāṇini 3.1.57). Then, there is the *guṇa* substitution according to the rule “*ṛdśo'ṅi guṇaḥ*” (Pāṇini 7.4.16).
In the first two alternatives, because the suffix is marked with *pittva*, it receives the acute accent (*udātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
In the third alternative, however, it is by way of exception (*vyatyaya*); due to its connection with *yad-vṛtta*, it does not receive the grave accent (*anighāta*).

In *paśve*, there is an absence of *guṇa* by virtue of the rule "gher ḍiti" (Pāṇini 7.3.111), because a grammatical operation conditioned by a specific technical designation (*saṃjñāpūrvaka*) is not necessarily constant; thus,
the *yaṇ* substitution takes place.
For *nṛbhyaḥ*:
by the rule *nṛ cānyatarasyām* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.184), there is an absence of the acute accent on the case-ending.
For *gave*.
The prohibition "na gobhansāvarṇa" applies to the case-ending accent that would otherwise have been obtained by the rule "sāvekācaḥ.
[Thus we have] *rudriyam*.
The suffix *gha* is applied after the word *rudra* in the sense of "belonging to him" (*tasyedam*).
So that Mitra and Varuṇa, so that Rudra may take heed of us, and so that all the gods, being of one accord, may take heed of us. (3)
May Mitra and Vahaga know us—that is, recognize us as objects of their favor—in whatever manner they do; and may Rudra also know us in that same way;
and may all the gods, being of one accord and equal joy, know us in the same way—so may it be.
1. "To the one who rains down desired objects" (ca-cha-na-pha-abhīṣṭakāmavarṣakāya) is the meaning. 2. "To the one [who protects] our horses, buffaloes, and other livestock" (ca-pha).

The remainder: Or rather, the two mantras containing the word *yathā* are connected with what precedes them, namely with *kadā vocema tathā* ("when may we speak thus?"). Regarding *ciketati*: from the root *kit* in the sense of "knowing. In the *leṭ* (subjunctive) mood, there is the augment *aṭ*. The prohibition of *guṇa* substitution by Pāṇini’s rule 7.3.80 (*nābhyastasya*) does not apply here, because of the statement: "It should be stated that [this rule] is optional in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). Furthermore, because it is a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, the initial vowel is udātta according to the rule *abhyastānām ādiḥ*. Regarding *sajopasaḥ*: from the root *juṣ* in the senses of "pleasure" and "service. They are *sajopas* because they enjoy (*juṣanti*) together (*samānam*). The substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-* occurs by the rule *samānasya chandasi*. Because the suffix *asun* has the marker *ni*, the initial vowel of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) is udātta; that very accent remains by the rule *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*.
We pray for that auspicious healing power of Rudra, the lord of songs, the lord of sacrifices, whose remedies are swift.
To Gāthapati, to Medhātithi, to Rudra, the one whose remedy is cooling—him we implore for that auspicious and healing well-being. 4.
Aiming toward Rudra, we pray for *śaṃyoḥ*—the well-known connection with the son of Bṛhaspati—and for *sūnṛtam*, the happiness that is beneficial to all creatures.
What kind of Rudra?

The lord of hymns (*gāthapati*), the protector of praise; the lord of sacrifice (*medhapati*), the protector of the ritual; and the one endowed with healing medicine in the form of bliss (*jalāṣabheṣaja*).
Or alternatively:
it is endowed with water, form, and medicinal herbs;
for water, when consecrated with mantras bearing the name of Rudra, becomes a medicinal herb.
Gāthapati: "Gāthā" is a name for speech, because it is listed among the synonyms for speech in the *Nirukta* (1.11.37), which states, "gāthā is a collection.
Gāthapati is thus the lord of the praise consisting of speech.
From the roots *kai*, *gai*, and *rai* [meaning] "to sound," the substitution of *ā* occurs by the rule *ādecaḥ*. The suffix *than* is applied by the rule *ḍupakṛṣipagātibhyasthan*.
The initial vowel is udātta by virtue of being a *nittva* [i.e., having an udātta accent on the first syllable of the suffix].
The shortening of the first member of the compound is according to the rule: "In names and in the Veda, the shortening of *ḍī* and *āp* occurs frequently.

Although the original accent of the first member would apply by the rule "In *pati*, when meaning sovereignty," the final syllable of the first member becomes udātta by the supplementary rule: "An addition to the list of *marud-vṛdha* and others is made for the Veda."
To the lord of wisdom;
as before;
the healer with cooling waters.
The root *jan* means "to appear.
From the sense "they are born" (*jāyante*), they are called *jāḥ*.
According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.101, "it is seen even in other cases," the suffix *ḍa* is applied even to the simple root due to the inclusion of the term *raśi*.
Lāṣaḥ: from the root *laṣ* in the sense of "desire" (*kānti*). Desire is longing (*abhilāṣa*).
The suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*).
That in which there is the desire (*lāṣa*) for water (*jala*) is "water-desire" (*jalāṣa*), meaning happiness.
Rudra is "the one whose medicine is the form of water-desire" (*jalāṣabheṣajaḥ*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member prevails.
In the word *śaṃyoḥ*,
the suffix *yuṣ* is added in the sense of the superlative by Pāṇini’s rule 5.2.138, *kaṃśaṃbhyāṃ yus*.

In the word *siti* (Vaiśeṣika Sūtra 1.4.16), by virtue of its designation as a *pada*, there is the substitution of an *anusvāra* for the nasal and its subsequent assimilation (*parasavarṇa*). This is the accent of a suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
He who shines like the bright sun, gleaming like gold—
the Vasu, the most excellent among the gods.
He who shines like the bright sun, like gold; the most excellent Vasu among the gods. 5.
Rudra, who is like the sun—bright and possessing the solar fire—and who shines like gold;
just as gold is a source of delight for all living beings, so too is Rudra.
Furthermore, he is the most excellent among all the gods and the *vasu*, the cause of their dwelling.

The root *ruc* occurs [in the sense] "to shine" and "to please. Because it is taught as having an *a*-vowel (*adupadeśa*), the suffix *la-sārvadhātuka* is unaccented, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
"Śreṣṭhaḥ" means "more praiseworthy.
From the word "praśasya," when the suffix *iṣṭhan* is applied, there is the substitution of "śra" according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.3.60: "praśasyasya śraḥ."
By virtue of the *nittva* [rule], it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.
*Vasu*:
he causes all to dwell, thus he is *vasu*.

The root *vas* means "to dwell. From this root, with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) implied, the suffix *up* is applied according to the rule "śṛ-stṛ-ñji-hi," etc. Due to the continued application of the term "nit," the word is accented on its first syllable.
The *dhāyyā* verse is "ābhimarutte 'śaṃ naḥ karati.
Furthermore, it is prescribed in the section [beginning with] "atha yathemam" in the Sūtra: "vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase śaṃ naḥ karayate" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 5.20).

May he grant well-being to our horse, an easy path to our ram and ewe, to our men and women, and to our cattle. 6. May he grant well-being to us; may he grant an easy path to the horse, to the ram, to the ewe, to the men, to the women, and to the cow. 6.
"May the God make a good path—easily traversable—and happiness for our kinsmen, such as those beginning with the *arvat* [horse];
for the *arvat*, that is, for the horse.
The word *arvat* is a name for a horse, as it is listed among its names in the Nirukta (1.14.3): 'The *arvat* is a prize-winning steed (*vājī*').'"
"To the ram" means to a male of the ram species; "to the ewe" means to a female of that same species; "to men" means to males; "to women" means to females; "to the cow" means to the bovine species.
He performs (*karati*).
[The root] *ḍukuñ* means "to act. There is an irregular substitution for the *śap* suffix.
Regarding *arvate*: it is called *arvan* because it goes (*arti gacchati*). The suffix *vanip* is applied according to the rule "it is seen [to be used] after other roots as well."
In the singular dative case, by the rule "arvaṇas tṛ maghonaś ca," there is the substitution of *tṛ* for the *n* [of *arvan*].
Since the suffixes *vanip* and *puṣ* are marked with *p*, they are unaccented (*anudātta*);
thus, the accent belongs to the verbal root.
For *meṣa*:
[the root] *miṣ* in the sense of "rivalry" (*spardhā*).
The suffix *ac* is applied according to the rule beginning with *pac*, because of the statement: "Words such as *devasena*, *meṣa*, and others are to be seen among the *pac*-class."
For *meṣī*: the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 4.1.63, *jāter astrīviṣayād ayopadhāt*; it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In the singular dative case, there is an absence of the augment *āṭ* because the rule prescribing it is not mandatory (*anitya*).
There is a circumflex accent (*svarita*) by the rule "after a vowel that is either acute (*udātta*) or circumflex (*svarita*), the following non-acute (*anudātta*) vowel becomes circumflex.
However, the rule "after a vowel with an acute accent preceded by a consonant" does not apply here, because of the statement: "all rules are optional in the Vedic language (*chandas*)."
In *nṛbhyaḥ*, the prohibition of the acute accent on the case-ending— which would otherwise apply by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*— is effected by the rule *nṛ cānyatarasyām*. [Similarly,] *nāribhyaḥ*.
The suffix *ṅīn* is applied because of the inclusion [of the word] among the *śārṅgarava*-class in the rule *nṛnarayor vṛddhiñ ca* (Pāṇini 4.1.73, Gaṇapāṭha).
Due to its being marked with *ṇ*, it is udātta on the first syllable. [Thus:
*gave*.
The rule "na godhansāvavarṇa" is a prohibition of the acute accent on the case-ending.
O Soma, bestow upon us the glory of a hundred men—great renown and abundant manly strength. ||7||
O Soma, bestow upon us—upon us—abundant prosperity sufficient for a hundred men; establish it in us with excellence.
Likewise, bestow upon us great, mighty renown, endowed with abundant strength, and food.
In *asme*, the form *śe* is the substitute for the locative case according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*. [The same applies to] *nṛṇām*.
The prohibition of lengthening by the rule *nṛ ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.6) applies here.
By the rule *nāmyatarasyām*, the word *nāman* optionally receives the udātta accent.
The words beginning with *mahī* have already been explained.
May those who obstruct our Soma, may the enemies, not deceive us. O Indu, grant us a share in the prize. 8.
May those who obstruct the Soma—those who exclude themselves from the sacrifice—never harm us;
likewise, may our enemies never harm us.
O Indu, O Soma, bestow upon us strength or its domain; favor us in every way.
*Somaparibādhaḥ*: those who obstruct the *soma* are such [beings]. The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "kvip ca."
The word *arātayaḥ* has the original accent of the final member of the compound due to the rule *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*. [It is derived from] the root *rā* in the sense of "giving."
The suffix *kvin* is used in the sense of the agent (*kartari*) due to the word "variously" (*bahulam*) in the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*;
or else,
the suffix *kvic* is used by the rule *kiccakau ca saṃjñāyām*.
In a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), the initial member, being an indeclinable (*avyaya*), retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
[The word] *juhuranta* [is derived from the root] *hṛ* with the prefix *pra*, meaning "to perform" or "to execute."
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition.
In the *laṅ* [aorist], there is *ślu*-elision because it belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class.
By the rule "there is diversity in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*, Pāṇini 7.1.103), due to the mention of "diversity," there is also the substitution of *u* for the vowel *i*.
The doubling [of the *bh*] and the substitution of *valādi* [for *jha*] follow.

According to the statement, "All rules are optional in the Veda," when the substitution of *at* by the rule *adabhyastāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.4) does not occur, the substitution of *anta* by the rule *jho'ntaḥ* applies.
By the rule *na mādyoge*, the absence of *at* is established.

Those progeny of yours, O Soma, which belong to the immortal, in the highest abode of the Cosmic Order (ṛta)—O Soma, as the head, as the navel, as the longing one, you know them as they adorn themselves. 9. Those progeny of yours, O Soma, which belong to the immortal, in the highest abode of the Cosmic Order—O Soma, as the head, as the navel, as the longing one, you know them as they adorn themselves. 9.

O Soma, those progeny which are related to you, or those who offer praise—those progeny—you, as the head (*mūrdhā*), the one occupying the position of the head, should desire (*venaḥ*) [them] in the *nābhi*, the sacrificial hall endowed with structural integrity. Of what kind are you? Of the immortal (*amṛtasya*), free from death; of the Truth (*ṛtasya*) established in the highest station (*parasmindhāmani*). O Soma, know (*vedaḥ*) the progeny who adorn (*ābhūṣantīḥ*) you on all sides. *dhāman*: By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, there is elision of the locative case ending. *nābhi*: From the root *ṇaha* (to bind).
