By the rule *naho bhaśca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 4.565), the suffix *ip* is added in the sense of the object. Due to its *jittva* quality, it has the acute accent on the first syllable. By *supāṃ suluk*, there is the substitution of *ḍā* for the locative case ending. *venaḥ*: The root *venati* means "to desire" (Nirukta 2.6.4). In the *leṭ* mood, with the suffix *sip*, there is the augment *aṭ*. By the rule *tiṅatiṅaḥ*, there is the *nighāta* (suppression) of the accent. *ābhūṣantīḥ*: From the root *bhūpa* (to adorn), belonging to the *bhvādi* class. The suffix *śap* is unaccented because it is marked with *pittva*; the suffix *śatṛ* also lacks accent due to the accent of the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes. The root itself has the acute accent on the first syllable. In the compound, the original accent of the final member (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*) prevails. *vedaḥ*: From the root *vida* (to know). In the *leṭ* mood, with the suffix *sip*, there is the augment *aṭ*. [Note: The commentary concludes with the verse number 27 and section 8.]

In the ninth section (anuvāka), there are seven hymns (*sūkta*). Among them, the first hymn, consisting of fourteen verses, begins with "agne vivasvat. Regarding this, the index (*anukramaṇikā*) states: "For the hymn beginning with 'agne,' Praskaṇva Kāṇva [composed] an Āgneya hymn in Paṅkti meter; however, the first two verses are *pragātha*, and they also belong to the Dawn (*uṣas*)."
The seer is Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva.
Here, the even-numbered verses (second and fourth) are *sanobṛhatī*s;
the odd-numbered verses (first and third) are *anuṣṭubh*-like *bṛhatī*s.
The entire hymn is dedicated to Agni, as is the following one.
The first two are dedicated to the Aśvins and to Uṣas respectively.
This hymn is used in the morning litany (prātaranuvāka) during the rite for Agni, when the meter is Bṛhatī, and in the Śastra for the Aśvins.
In the section beginning with "Now, of this night," it is sūtra-ed: "O Agni, O Vivasvat, O friends, you... (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13).
In the Vājapeya sacrifice, at the Āgnimāruta [laud], the first Pragātha is an Anuṣṭubh.

In the section beginning with "By means of the Vājapeya," it is sūtra-ed: "If they should chant in the Citravatī verses, then 'The bright one for us,' 'May he rise up,' and 'O Vivasvat, the dawns' are the Stotriya and Anurūpa verses of the Agniṣṭoma-sāman" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 9.9).
In the case of a shift in the *paryāyas*, the *pragātha* "āśvinā yakṣi," etc., is the *stotriya* for the *āśvina-śastra*.
This is prescribed in the section beginning with "yadi paryāyān abhiyuñjet" by the sūtra: "āśvināyakṣi triṣṭubho 'gne vivasvad upasaḥ" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 6.6).

O Agni, immortal one, bring hither today from the radiant Dawn the wondrous gift for the donor, O Jātavedas, the gods who awaken at the break of day. O Agni, from the radiant Dawn, O immortal one, bring hither the wondrous gift for the donor; O Jātavedas, you yourself, bring today the gods who awaken at the break of day.

O Agni, bring from the presence of the goddess Uṣas the gift of wealth to the donor, the sacrificer who has offered the oblation; having brought it, cause him to attain it. This Agni is further specified as *amartya*, the immortal, and *jātavedas*, the knower of all that is born.
1. The phrase "by the accent of the root" (*dhātusvareṇa*) does not exist [in this context]. [Pāṇini] Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.2.44. First Chapter, 311.

Regarding this very word, Yāska explains: "Jātavedas—why? Because he knows (*veda*) what is born (*jātāni*), or because they know him (*enaṃ viduḥ*) when things are born; or because he is found (*vidyate*) at every birth; or because his wealth (*vit*) is born, or his knowledge (*prajñāna*) is born. As for the fact that once born he found (*avindata*) cattle, that is the Jātavedas-nature of Jātavedas," according to the Brāhmaṇa. And: "Therefore all cattle approach Agni" (Nirukta 7.19). What kind of *rādhas* (wealth/gift)? "Vivasvata"—endowed with a distinguished dwelling (*viśiṣṭanivāsopetam*). "Citra"—of various kinds. Furthermore: "And on this day, bring hither (*ā vaha*) the gods who are awakened at dawn (*upa-budhaḥ*), those awakened at the time of *uṣas*. *Vivasvata*: "Vivaḥ" is the act of illuminating (*vivāsanam*). From the root *vas* (to dwell), preceded by *vi*, with the sense of causation internalized, the suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule for *saṃpad-ādi* formations. The suffix *matup* is added in the sense of "possessing that" (*tasyāsmin*). By the rule *madhupadhāyāḥ*, there is the substitution of *v*. Since the suffix *matup* is used here in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*), the *pañcamī* (ablative) case ending is absent, and thus the substitution of *ru* does not occur. It is acutely accented on the first syllable because it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* class. *Rādhas*: From the roots *rādha* and *sādha* meaning "to accomplish. That by which one accomplishes is *rādhas*, i.e., wealth. The suffix *asun* is applied in the instrumental sense. It is acutely accented on the first syllable because of the *nic* augment. *Dāśuṣe*: From the root *dāś* meaning "to give. The form *dāśvān* is a conventional (*nipātita*) formation ending in the suffix *kamu*. In the singular dative, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*. There is the substitution of *ṣ* by the rule *śāsivasi*. *Jātavedas*: He who knows (*veti*) what is born (*jātāni*) is Jātavedas. The suffix *asun* is applied by the rule *gatikārakayor api pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca*. Alternatively, *veda* is a name for wealth; he whose wealth is born is such [a one]. This is a vocative pause. *Vaha*: In the *saṃhitā* text, there is lengthening by the rule *ayo'tasmin*. *Devān*: In the *saṃhitā*, the *n* is replaced by *r* by the rule *dīrghādiṭi samānapāde*. The vowel *ā* becomes nasalized by the rule *āto'ṭi nityam*. *Upabudhaḥ*: Those who awaken at dawn (*upasi budhyante*) are *upabudhaḥ*. From the root *budh* meaning "to understand/awaken. The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *kvip ca*. The absence of the substitution of *u* for *r* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). The accent is that of the original base of the second member of the compound.
For you are the beloved messenger, the bearer of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of the sacrifices.
Being impelled by the Aśvins and Uṣas, bestow upon us great heroic power and lofty renown.
For you are the beloved messenger, the bearer of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of sacrifices; united with the Aśvins and Uṣas, bestow upon us great heroic power and high renown. 2.
O Agni, you are one who is cherished and endowed with divine, specific qualities; you are "juṣṭaḥ," meaning served or honored;
you are the "dūtaḥ" of the gods, the bearer of news; the "havyavāhanaḥ," the carrier of the oblation; and the "rathīḥ" of the sacrifices and seasons, standing as the very chariot itself.
And thus another mantra has been explained by the Brāhmaṇa itself: "He says, 'The charioteer of the sacrifices,' for this is indeed the chariot of the gods" (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.5.9.2).
And another Brāhmaṇa states: "He says, 'The charioteer of the sacrifices,' for having become a chariot, he carries the oblation to the gods.

Being such [a charioteer], having become united with the two deities, the Aśvins, and with the deity Uṣas, bestow upon us—place within us—'great' (abundant) 'glory' (food), which is endowed with excellent heroic power.
*Juṣṭaḥ*. [The root] *juṣī* [is used] in the senses of "pleasure" and "service. By the rule *nityaṃ mantre* (Pāṇini 6.1.210), it has an udātta accent on the first syllable.
In the case of *asi*, there is elision of *s* by the rule "atāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.4.50). Furthermore, by the rule "hi ca," there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* accent.
Havyavāhana:

he is called Havyavāhana because he carries the oblation (*havya*). The suffix *ṇyu* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.66: "The suffix *ṇyu* is used after the root *vah* when preceded by *havya*, provided it does not occur within a *pāda*."
The substitution of *y* for [the final consonant] is applied.
Since it belongs to the *jaś*-class, when the initial udātta accent is applied, the natural accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the second member of the compound prevails.
*agne*.
In words such as *pāda*, there is the absence of the acute accent on the first syllable and the absence of the lack of svarita (i.e., they are udātta).
In *rathīḥ*,
the suffix *ī* is added to the word *ratha* in the sense of the same meaning (*svārthika*).

Regarding *adhvarāṇām*: since there is no *dhvara* (obstacle/fault) [in them], it is a *bahuvrīhi* compound; by the rule *anansubhyām*, the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. Regarding *suvīryam*.
In the word *vīravīryau*, the acute accent (*udātta*) falls on the first syllable of the second member of the compound according to the rule [Pāṇini 6.2.114].
In *asme*, the form *śe* is the substitute for the locative case ending according to the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
1. By the Brāhmaṇa Ca-pha himself.
The Ṛgveda.
Today we choose as our messenger Agni, the Vasu, beloved by many—
the one whose banner is smoke, whose face is radiant, the glory of the sacrifice at the break of dawn.
Today we choose as our messenger Agni, the Vasu, who is beloved by many, whose banner is smoke, who is radiant in splendor, at the break of days, the glory of the sacrifices and the rites. 3.
On this day, we choose—that is, we pray for—Agni.

Of what sort? As a messenger (*dūtam*), a bearer of news; as a dweller (*vasum*), the cause of habitation; as one dear to many (*puru-priyam*); as having smoke as his banner (*dhūmaketum*), possessed of a smoke-sign; and as radiant (*bhrājat-īkam*), adorned with celebrated luster.
"Bhārajajīkaḥ prasiddhabhāḥ" (Nirukta 6.4)—such is the statement of Yāska.
At the dawns, during the times of the break of day, [he bestows] upon the discerning sacrificers the splendor of a bridegroom, one who serves the sacrifice. Now...
The lengthening [of the vowel] is by the rule "nipātasya ca.
He who is dear to many is *puruṣpriyaḥ*. The final acute accent (*antodāttatva*) is by the rule "samāsasya."
Regarding *dhūmaketu*: by the rule "iṣiyudhīndhi" (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.142), the word *dhūma* ends in the suffix *map*, is oxytone,
and in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, it retains its original accent as the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratva*).
*bhrājajīkam*: [This is derived from] the root *ṛj* in the sense of "going," "bathing," "earning," or "acquiring. By the rule *ṛjeśca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.462), the suffix *īkan* is applied.
Because the status of being a *kit* suffix is carried over, there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution.

*Bhāsaḥ* means "of light"; *kajīkaḥ* is derived from *prājiyatā*. Regarding the accentuation, the rule "In the case of *bhārajada*, there is an addition [to the list] for *dvirodha*, *āsādi*, and so forth in the Vedic language" (*chandasi*) prescribes that the first syllable of the preceding member (*pūrvapada*) is udātta.
Alternatively:
In which there is the acquisition of light;
[this is] a *bahuvrīhi* compound with the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratva*).
In the *vyuṣṭis*.
The root *ucchī* means "to dawn" (*vivāsa*),
which signifies "avoiding" (*varjana*).
Those times of dawn are called *vyuṣṭayaḥ* because they are specifically "dawned upon," meaning they are distinguished by being freed from darkness.
The suffix *ktin* is used in the sense of the object (*karman*). By the rule beginning with "titutra," there is a prohibition of the *it*-augment.
By the rule beginning with "vaśra," *patva* (the substitution of *p*) occurs, and subsequently *ṣutva* (the substitution of *ṣ*).
In the case of *tādau ca*, the preceding member retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
Following the substitution of *yaṇ*, the subsequent unaccented vowel becomes circumflex (*svarita*) by the rule "udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ. [Thus we have] *adhvaraśriyam*.
He resorts to the *adhvara* (sacrifice), thus he is *adhvaraśrīḥ*.

The suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *kvip ca* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.215); due to its connection with that suffix, there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution) and the vowel is lengthened. In the second case singular, the substitute *iyaṅ* is applied by the rule *aci śnudhātubhruvām* (Pāṇini 6.4.77).
I praise Agni Jātavedas at the break of dawn— the most excellent, the youngest guest, well-invoked, and beloved by the person who offers oblations— so that he may go toward the gods.

The most excellent, the youngest, the guest, well-invoked, beloved by the person who offers oblations—to him, Agni Jātavedas, I offer praise at the break of dawn, so that he may go forth toward the gods. 4.
At the dawns, during the times of morning, I praise Agni, the god, for his strength—so that he may go forth toward and encounter all the other gods.

Of what nature is he? Most excellent, being preeminently praiseworthy; most youthful; a guest capable of constant movement; well-invoked, being the proper locus for the oblation from every side; beloved and pleasing to the person who gives the sacrificial offering; and Jātavedas, the knower of all that is born.
*yaviṣṭham*:

from the word *yuva*, when the suffix *iṣṭhan* is added, there is the substitution of *yaṇ* according to the rule "sthūladūra... etc., the elision of the following [vowel], and the *guṇa* strengthening of the preceding [vowel].
The substitution of *ava* [for *upa*].
Due to the *nit* designation, there is acute accent on the first syllable.
[The word] *atithim*.
The suffix *ithin* is applied according to [Uṇādisūtra 4.442], "ataḥ sātatya-gamane ṛtambajñi," etc.
Due to its being marked with *ṇ*, there is acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable.
It is well-sacrificed (*svāhuta*).
The root *hu* is used in the sense of "giving" and "offering.
That in which one is summoned is called *āhūta*.

Regarding the word *su*, by the rule *suḥ pūjāyām* (Pāṇini Sūtra 1.4.94), it receives the designation of *karmapravacanīya*; thus, by the rule *svatī pūjāyām* (Pāṇini Mahābhāṣya 2.2.18.4), a compound is formed.

The first member of the compound retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) because it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). Nor does the rule "the accent of a preverb (*gati*) or a kāraka [retains its original accent] before a *kṛt*-suffix" apply here, because this word *su-* has its designation as a *gati* superseded [by the designation *praśasta*].
"I praise you, O immortal one, the food of the universe."
O Agni, worthy of the sacrificial feast, you who carry the oblations, protect us with your immortal self as the most excellent sacrificer.
I shall praise you—O Agni, immortal food of the universe, protector, immortal one worthy of sacrifice, most excellent sacrificer, bearer of oblations. 5.

O *amṛta* (deathless), O *bhojana* (sustainer) of the entire world, O *havyavāhana* (carrier of oblations), O *miyedhya* (worthy of sacrifice)—O Agni of such a nature, I, the performer of the rite, shall praise you, the *trātāram* (protector) of the universe, the *amṛta* (immortal), the *yajiṣṭham* (most excellent sacrificer). I shall praise (*stuviṣyāmi*). [The root] *huñ* means "to praise. There is an augment *ḍ* by way of metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*). When the augment is unaccented, the accent falls on the suffix. *Bhojana*: He causes one to enjoy the fruit of action; thus, *bhojanaḥ*. The suffix *lyu* is applied according to the rule for roots beginning with *nand* etc. *Trātāram*: From the root *traiṅ* meaning "to protect. By the rule *ādecaḥ*, there is the substitution of *ā*. In the formation of the agentive suffix *tṛc*, there is a prohibition of the *it* augment by the rule *ekāca upadeśe*. *Amṛtam*: By the rule *najo jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*, the final syllable of the compound is udātta. *Miyedhya*: The augment *iy* is a Vedic (*chāndasa*) feature. *Yajiṣṭham*: From the word *yaṣṭṛ*, the suffix *iṣṭhan* is added by the rule *tuchi chandasi*. By the rule *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*, there is the elision of the suffix *tu*. 24.
O youngest one, be a bringer of good praise to the singer; O honey-tongued one, well-invoked with oblations, extending the life of Praskaṇva, pay homage to the divine host.
Be well-disposed toward the one who praises you, O youngest one, honey-tongued and well-invoked. Prolonging the life of Praskaṇva so that he may live, pay homage to the divine host. 6.

O most youthful one (*yaviṣṭhya*), you who are easy to praise (*suśaṃsa*)—meaning you are well worthy of being praised—whose tongue is honey-sweet (*madhujihva*), meaning whose flame is intoxicating, and who are well-invoked (*svāhuta*), being offered oblations directly toward you: take heed (*bodhi*)! Be aware of our intention. Furthermore, for the sake of the life (*jīvase*) of Praskaṇva—the great seer, son of Kaṇva, named after him—as Yāska states: "Praskaṇva: the son of Kaṇva, originating from Kaṇva" (Nirukta 3.17)—prolonging (*pratiran*) his lifespan, pay homage (*namasya*) and honor the divine folk (*daivyaṃ janaṃ*). *Suśaṃsaḥ*: From the root *śaṃsu* (to praise), the suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*). He whose praise (*śaṃsaḥ*) is beautiful is *suśaṃsaḥ*. The acute accent on the final syllable of the second member follows the rule "āyudāttaṃ yacchāndasam. *Bodhi*: From the root *budh* (to understand). The form is the imperative (*loṭ*) with the ending *-hi*. By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is elision of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*). By "huślu-bhyo hedhiḥ," *hi* is replaced by *dhi*. Since the prohibition of the *pit* designation is optional in the Veda, the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel occurs. The elision of other letters in the root is a Vedic feature. *Gṛṇate*: From the root *gṛ* (to sound). The present participle suffix (*śatṛ*) is applied. By "ṛdha-ādibhyaḥ śā," the suffix *śā* is added. By "ābhyastayorātaḥ," the long *ā* is elided. The acute accent of the case-ending follows "śataranumaḥ. *Yaviṣṭhya*: This has been explained previously. *Praskaṇvasya*: "Prakṛti" means origin. He whose origin is from Kaṇva is *praskaṇvaḥ*. By the rule "praskaṇvahariścandrāvṛṣī" (Pāṇini 6.1.153), the augment *suṭ* is prescribed. In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first member retains its original accent. *Pratiran*: The prefix-less root *tṛ* here has the sense of "increasing. *Namasya*: By the rule "namovarivaścitrahaḥ kyac" (Pāṇini 3.1.19), the suffix *kyac* is added in the sense of honoring. The accent belongs to the suffix. The lengthening in the *saṃhitā* is according to "anyeṣām api dṛśyate. *Daivyam*: By the rule "devādyañ" (Pāṇini 4.1.85), the suffix *yañ* is added in the sense of "belonging to that" (*tasyedam*), as it falls under the *prāgdīvyatīya* category. Ka, 41.

The people indeed kindle you, the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest; so, O Agni, much-invoked and wise, bring hither the gods swiftly to this place. (7) hotāram viśvavedasam saṃ hi tvā viśa indhate | sa ā vaha puruhūta pracetaso'gne devā~ iha dravata || 7 || The people indeed kindle you, the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest; so, O Agni, much-invoked and wise, bring hither the gods swiftly to this place. (7)
The people—the subjects—indeed kindle thoroughly their own Agni, the Hotṛ who establishes the sacrifice, the all-knowing Viśvavedas.

O Agni, invoked by many (Puruhūta), you, being wise, bring hither swiftly to this rite the gods endowed with supreme knowledge; cause them to arrive here. "Dravata" is a word for speed, as it is listed among those names in the Nirukta (2.15.3): "dravata oṣam."
Viśvavedasam:
he is called Viśvavedas because he knows all things (viśvāni vetti). This is formed with the suffix *asun*.
In *marudvṛdhādi* and similar compounds, there is udātta accent on the final syllable of the first member;
or alternatively,
*veda* is a name for wealth.
He who possesses all the Vedas is "Viśvavedāḥ.
O Agni, you are the "patiḥ" (lord) and protector of the "adhvarāḥ" (sacrifices) belonging to the "viśām" (people); for you are indeed the "dūtaḥ" (messenger), the bearer of offerings to the gods.

O Agni, bring hither—causing them to come toward us—the gods who are "awakened at dawn" (uparbudhaḥ), meaning those awakened at the time of morning, and who are "seers of heaven" (svardṛśaḥ), meaning those who behold the sun; bring them on this very day for the drinking of Soma (somapītaye), that is, for the purpose of consuming the Soma juice.
*asi*: there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent by the rule "hi ca. *somapītaye*.
The root *pā* means "to drink.

By the rule *myāgāpāpaco bhāve* (Pāṇini 3.2.9), the suffix *kin* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*). Then, by the rule *ghumāsthā...* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), the substitution of *ī* occurs.
The drinking of Soma;
the accentuation of the first member of the compound remains as it was originally due to its inclusion in the *dāsībhārādi* group.
[The word] *svardṛśaḥ*.
He who eats and moves well is the Sun (Svar-ādityaḥ).
From this root, the suffix *vic* is applied according to the rule "it is seen [to occur] after other roots as well.
Those who behold him are the "beholders of heaven" (svardṛśaḥ).
The suffix *kip* [is applied] after the word *ki*; it retains the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the final member of the compound, as prescribed by the rule *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*.
O Agni, rich in light, you have shone through the ancient dawns, visible to all;
you are the protector in the settlements, the domestic priest among men at the sacrifices.

O Agni, rich in light, you have shone following the former dawns; you are visible to all. You are the protector among the villages, the one appointed as high priest; you are the friend of men in the sacrifices. 10.

O Agni, O Vibhāvasu—possessing the wealth of a distinguished light—you who are visible to all (*viśvadarśata*), you have shone forth (*dīdertha*) following the former dawns, that is, with reference to the times of dawn that have passed.
As such, you are the protector (*avitā*) in the villages (*grāmeṣu*), the places where people dwell.

In the sacrifices (*yajñeṣu*), among the rites to be performed, you are the human *purohita*, stationed in the eastern direction of the altar; you are beneficial to the men who are officiating as priests.
*dīdertha*. *dīdeti* is a Vedic form;
it has the meaning of "shining."
Due to the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the grammatical injunction, there is an absence of the augment *iṭ*.

Because of the statement, "In the section on reduplication, it should be stated that in the Veda it is optional" (*dvivaṃcanaprakaraṇe chandasi veti vaktavyam*, Kāśikā 6.1.8.1), there is an absence of reduplication.
[Thus we have] *viśvadarśataḥ*.
He is worthy of being seen by all.
The suffix *atac* is applied to the root *dṛś* by the rule beginning with *bhṛmṛdṛśi* (Pāṇini 3.2.161).
Due to its inclusion in the *marudvṛdhādi* group, the final syllable of the first member of the compound is udātta (Pāṇini 6.2.106.2).
The word *purohita* [is derived from] the word *pura*. According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 5.3.39, “*pūrvādharādavarāṇāmasi puradhavaścaiṣām*,” it ends in the suffix *asi*.
Thus, the term *puraḥ* is used.

Because it is an indeclinable by the rule *taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ* (Pāṇini 1.1.38), and because the designation *gati* applies by the rule *puro’vyayam* (Pāṇini 1.4.60), there is a *gati-samāsa*; and in that *gati-samāsa*, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛti-svara*) applies by the rule *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pāṇini 6.2.49).
O Agni, we establish you as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest, the officiating Ṛtvij—
like Manu, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger.
O Agni, we establish you as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest, the officiating ṛtvij—just as Manu did—O God, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger. 11.
O Agni, just as a god places [the sacrificial fire] in the region of men according to the human way, so do we establish you here; we set you down. Of what nature are you?

You are the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the producer of the rite; the Hotṛ priest, the officiant who sacrifices during the seasons such as spring; the far-sighted one, endowed with supreme knowledge; the swift one, the destroyer of the vigor of enemies; the messenger of the gods, acting in the capacity of a messenger; the immortal, free from death.
The word *manuṣ* ends in the *uṇādi* suffix *asip*.
The suffix *vati* is applied according to Pāṇini’s rule 5.1.115: “When there is equality with that [in respect] to an action, the suffix *vati* is used.
Because it possesses the quality of being like iron (*ayasa-tva*), there is no shortening [of the vowel].
We meditate upon [thee].
[The root] *dhā* (from *ḍudhāñ*) means "to hold" and "to nourish. [This is used] in the optative (*liṅ*).

The elision of the vowel *a* [in *jīra*] is a Vedic archaism (*chāndasa*). Regarding *jīram*: *ju* is a root found in the *Sūtra* collection; the suffix *rap* is applied according to *Uṇādi-sūtra* 2.181, *jorī ca*. Kātyāyana states: "In the case of the suffix *rak*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of *jy*, resulting in *jīra*" (Pāṇini 1.1.4.6).
O Agni, whose splendor is like that of Mitra among the gods, you go as their domestic priest and as a messenger close at hand; your flames, O Agni, flash forth like the roaring waves of the ocean.
O Agni, you who possess the glory of Mitra among the gods, who are the domestic priest and the intimate envoy, as you go along, your flames shine like the thundering waves of the Sindhu river. 12.

O Agni, when you—possessing great splendor (*mitramahas*), the worshiper of friends (*mitrāṇām pūjaka*)—are established as the domestic priest (*purohita*) in the eastern direction of the altar, acting as an intermediary (*antara*) among the divine folk, and perform the office of a messenger (*dūtyam*) for the gods, then your flames (*arcayaḥ*) shine forth brilliantly.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
just as the waves (*ūrmayaḥ*) of the ocean, endowed with a resonant roar (*prasvanitāsaḥ*), shine forth.
*Mitramahaḥ*: [The root] *maha* means "to worship. He is worshipped (*mahyate*) by friends (*mitraiḥ*), that is, he is honored; thus, he is *mitramahāḥ*.
The suffix *asun* is derived from the *auṇādika* [list].
[In the word] *yāsi*,
there is no *anighāta* (lack of suppression of accent) due to its connection with *yad-vṛtta*.
*Dūtaryam* means the business of a messenger (*dūta*). The suffix *ya* is applied according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 4.4.120: *dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī*.

Because of the statement, “In the Vedic language (*chandas*), all rules are optional,” there is the occurrence of the circumflex accent (*svarita*) by the rule *titsvaritam* when the acute accent (*udātta*) prescribed by *yato ’nāvaḥ* does not take effect.
[The result is] *prasvanitāsaḥ*. [The roots] *syamu*, *svana*, and *dhvana* mean "to sound."
The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*). Those whose sound is excellent are called *prasvanitāsaḥ*; here, the augment *asun* is added.
Here, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member of the compound prevails.
Regarding *ūrmayaḥ*: the suffix *map* is applied according to *arnerucca* (Uṇādisūtra 4.484).
Hear us, O you whose ear is keen, together with the gods who carry the oblation and travel in unison;
let Mitra, Aryaman, and those who journey at dawn sit upon the sacred grass at our sacrifice.
Listen, O you of listening ears! With the fires, with the gods, O Agni, together with those who travel at dawn, let Mitra and Aryaman sit upon the sacrificial grass at the morning sacrifice. 13.
O Agni, you who possess ears capable of hearing, listen with your ears; hear our speech.

Let Mitra the god, Aryaman, and all the other gods who travel at dawn—those who go to the place of sacrifice in the morning—sit down together with them all, with you, the Āhavanīya fire, and with the other gods who share the same path, for the sake of the sacrifice (*adhvara*) upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). Let them sit.
Listen!
The root *śru* means "to hear. By the rule beginning with *śrṛṇu*, the substitute *hedi* is applied [for the imperative suffix].
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is elision (*luk*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*). *Śrutkarṇaḥ*:
that which hears is *śrut*.
In the word *kṛpī*, there is the addition of the augment *tug*.
One whose ears (*karṇau*) have heard (*śrutau*) is *śrutkarṇaḥ*. By means of fires (*vahnibhiḥ*).
The root *vah* is used in the sense of "carrying.
The suffix *ni* is applied according to the rule *vahi-śri-yu-śru-glaha-ava-ribhyo niḥ*. Because the suffix is marked with *n*, it is *ādyudātta* (accented on the first syllable).
They are "sayāvānaḥ" because they go together;
the root *yā* means "to reach."

By the rule *āto manin-*, the suffix *vanip* is applied; the accentuation follows the rule for the original tone of the final member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). Thus: *prātaryāvāṇaḥ*.
As before, the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] occurs by the rule *prātipadikāntanumvibhaktiṣu ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.11).

1. Ca-na-pha-śa-sa: At dawn, at the time of morning, may the Maruts, the givers of good gifts, whose tongue is Agni and who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), hear this hymn of praise. May Varuṇa, whose vow is firm, drink the Soma; [O Indra,] join yourself with the Aśvins and Uṣas.

Listen to our hymn, O Maruts, you bounteous givers, whose tongue is Agni and who increase the cosmic order (ṛta). Let them drink the Soma; let Varuṇa, the upholder of the sacred law, drink it, along with the Aśvins and Uṣas. Release [the waters]! 14.

May the Maruts, the gods, hear our hymn of praise. Of what nature are they? They are the "givers of good gifts," excellent bestowers of fruit; they are those among whom Agni is the "tongue," meaning that Agni stands as the primary leader within them.
The increasers of *ṛta*, that is, the strengtheners of the true sacrifice;
likewise, may the god Varuṇa, whose vows are firm and who has undertaken his ritual duties, drink the Soma together with the two gods, the Aśvins, and with the deity Uṣas— O bounteous givers!
In the sense of "giving" (*sudāñ dāne*),
the suffix *nu* is applied by the rule *dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.312) to form the word *dānu*,
which begins with the vowel *ā*.
For the gods, wise from the beginning, are prompt to listen for the sake of the donor; O you who possess ruddy horses, lover of songs, bring those thirty-three gods here.
For the gods, the wise ones from of old, are indeed prompt to hear the one who offers oblations. O you whose horses are ruddy, O lover of songs, bring those thirty-three hither. 2.
O Agni, the wise gods, possessed of distinguished insight, are indeed *śruṣṭīvantas*— that is, they are responsive to the sacrificer who has offered oblations;
for *śruṣṭi* is the granting of the fruit [of sacrifice],
and they are surely the recipients thereof.

O Agni, lover of songs (*girvaṇas*), who are worthy of being sought after through hymns and praises, you who are accompanied by the horses named Rohita—bring hither those thirty-three gods numbered by this count. Yāska [states]: "The god is called *girvaṇas* because they seek him with songs" (*Nirukta* 6.14). Bring them here.
*Śruṣṭīvān*. *Śruṣṭi* has the sense of "impelling.
The suffix *kvip* is used here in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
They obtain and enjoy favor; thus they are called *śruṣṭīvānaḥ*. [This is according to Pāṇini 3.2.75:
"Also after other [roots]..."

The Mahikerus—the Priyamedhas, seers endowed with beloved sacrifice—invoked Agni for protection (*ūtaye*). How so? Shining (*rājantam*) with a bright flame (*śucinā śociṣā*) in the midst of the *adhvaras*, that is, the sacrifices. Regarding the word *mahikeravaḥ*: the root *maha* means "to honor"; the suffix *ina* is added according to the *uṇādi* rules. The root *kṛ* (in the form *ḍukṛñ*) means "to do"; the suffix *uṇ* is applied by the rule *kṛvāpāji*. Thus, they are those whose *kāravaḥ* (singers) are *mahayaḥ* (great). The substitution of *e* for the vowel *ā* is Vedic (*chāndasa*). In this *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent remains on the first member. Regarding *priyamedhāḥ*: those whose *medhaḥ* (wisdom/sacrifice) is *priyaḥ* (beloved). Regarding *āhūtapata*: from the root *hve* (in the form *hem*), meaning "to contend" or "to call. In the *luṅ* tense with the *sic* suffix, there is a *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) because of the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. There is the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatvam*). By the rule *halaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.2), there is lengthening. Finally, by the rule *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*.
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, you who are worthy of praise, truly hear these songs by which the sons of Kaṇva invoke you for protection.
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, O Excellent One, listen well to these songs by which the sons of Kaṇva call upon you for protection. 5.

O you who are invoked with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), being summoned by the *ghṛta*, listen well—listen attentively—to these songs (*giraḥ*) offered by us, which are words in the form of hymns that bestow ancient fruits. O son of the great seer Kaṇva, listen to those words with which they call upon you for protection, for the sake of their own preservation.
*Ghṛtāhavana*:
that in which one is invoked with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) is *ghṛtāhavana*.
The suffix *lyuṭ* is used here in the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇa*).
The first syllable of the vocative is udātta.
In the word *śrudhi*, the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs according to the rule *śru-śṛṇu-pṛ-kṛ-vṛ-bhyaś chandasi*.
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is the elision (luk) of the verbal suffix (vikaraṇa).
In the Aśvamedha sacrifice, at the offering to Pūṣan, the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) for the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation is "O you of most wonderful fame" (*tvāṃ citraśravastama*).

This is prescribed in the section beginning with "Desiring to obtain all desires" (*sarvān kāmānāpsyan*), in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (10.6): "O you of most wonderful fame... that which was most pleasing, that [was offered] to Agni."
All living beings invoke you, O most renowned in glory,
the flame-haired one, for your great love and to carry their oblations.
All living beings invoke you, whose fame is most wonderful—the one with flaming hair—to carry their oblations for the sake of that which is much beloved. 6.

O Agni, most renowned for your manifold forms, exceedingly dear to many, and the delighter of numerous sacrificers—O you whose hair is flame, endowed with locks of radiant light—all living beings, that is, your progeny, the sacrificers, invoke you in order to carry the oblation, to convey the sacrificial offering.
How are you?
You are possessed of hair in the form of blazing light.
And so the Vājasaneyins record: "The rays of this kindled [fire] are like its hair, as if it were grieving."
*Citraśravastama*. *Śrava* is a name for food. He whose fame (*śravas*) is wonderful (*citra*) is *Citraśravas*.
*Citraśravastama* means "most wonderfully famous."
*Citraśravastamaḥ* means "possessing exceedingly wonderful fame";
it has the accent of a vocative.
*Śociṣkeśam*.

The root *śuc* means "to shine. The suffix *is* is applied according to *Uṇādi Sūtra* 2.255: "The suffix *is* occurs after [roots ending in] *arc*, *śuc*, *hu*, *sap*, *pā*, etc. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [is maintained].
[The suffix] *habhyām*.

Because the act of offering (*havana-kriyā*) is to be attained, the fourth case (*caturthī*) is used due to its status as a recipient (*saṃpradāna*), according to the rule "the term *kriyā* (action) must be included [in the definition of *saṃpradāna*]". [The form] *voḷahave* [is derived from] the root *vah*, meaning "to convey."
In accordance with the rule *tum-arthe śeṣen*, the suffix *taven* is applied.
After the substitutions of *ṭha* for *tha*, *dha* for *dha*, *ṭu* for *thu*, and the elision of *ḍha* have been performed,
the vowel *a* is replaced by *o* according to the rule *sahi-vahoḥ id-varṇasya* (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.112).
The word *niṣṭhā* has an udātta accent on its first syllable.
The inspired poets have established you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ priest and the officiating minister at the celestial rites— the best finder of wealth, with ears that hear, most far-reaching.

The inspired singers have established you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ priest, the officiating minister, the greatest finder of wealth, the one with the most attentive ears, and the most far-reaching in the sacrifices of heaven. 7.
O Agni, the inspired ones (*viprāḥ*), the wise, have established you in the *diviṣṭi* sacrifices; that is, they have placed you there. Of what nature are you?

You are the *hotṛ*, the invoker, the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*) who is habituated to sacrificing during the ritual seasons (*ṛtu*). You are the most excellent finder of wealth (*vasuvittama*), the one who brings forth riches in the highest degree, and the one with ears that hear (*śrutkarṇa*).
O Son of Strength,
O Truthful One, seat here today upon the sacred grass the divine host that comes at dawn, for the drinking of Soma, O Vasu.
O you who move at dawn, O you who are made of strength, O true one, for the drinking of Soma, seat here today upon the sacred grass the divine host, O Vasu! 9.

O Agni, who art produced by force, who hast crushed the stingy ones that yield no fruit, and who art the cause of our dwelling—here today, on this day of the sacrifice, seat upon the sacrificial grass (barhis) the gods who come at dawn for the drinking of Soma, the divine host, and any other assembly of deities, and cause them to reach the sacrifice.
*prātaryāvṇaḥ*: by the rule *śasi alopo 'naḥ*, there is the elision of the vowel *a*. *sahaskṛta*.
*Saha* is strength (*bala*), because by means of it one endures (*sahate*) or overcomes (*abhibhavati*). That which is performed by that [strength] is *sahaskṛtaḥ*.

The absence of the elision (*aluk-abhāvaḥ*) of the third case ending, as in *sahaḥ-kṛtaḥ*, is due to Vedic usage (*chāndasaḥ*), according to Pāṇini’s rule 6.3.1: "The elision of the third case ending does not occur after *bhojas*, *sahas*, *ambhas*, or *tamas*."
Worship first with joint invocations the divine host that comes hither;
this is the Soma of the liberal giver—drink it, for it has been pressed beyond the day.
O Agni, worship the divine host with joint invocations, bringing them hitherward. O bounteous ones, this is the Soma; drink it, which has been prepared for you beyond the day. 10.
O Agni, with joint invocations together with other gods, worship—that is, sacrifice to—the divine folk, the living beings who are of the nature of deities, turning them hitherward toward you.
O gods, bestowers of excellent fruits, this Soma stands before you for your sake;
drink that Soma!
Of what kind is it? It is called *tiroahnya*, which is the name for that Soma which was praised on the preceding day but is offered on the following day.
*Daivyaṃ*:
by the rule "devayajñau," the suffix *yaj* is applied according to the *prāgdīvyatīya* group.
*Yakṣva*.
In the imperative (*loṭ*), there is elision of the suffix *śap* by the rule "often in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*). The absence of the accent of the affix is a Vedic peculiarity (*chāndasa*).

Because the word *agne*, occurring at the beginning of a quarter-verse (*pāda*), is treated as non-existent according to the rule "an antecedent vocative is as if non-existent" (*āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat*), there is no suppression of the accent (*nighāta*) by the rule "the verb [is unaccented] after another verb" (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*).
Regarding the term *sahūtibhiḥ*: those whose invocation (*hūti*) or calling is the same are *sahūtayaḥ*. The substitution of *samāna* for *saha* is according to the rule "samānasya chandasi."
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member prevails. *Pāta*: from the root *pā* (to drink).
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is the elision (luk) of the suffix śap; thus, *tiroahnyam*. That which occurs on the day (*ahani*) is called *ahyam*.

In the case of the word *bhava*, because it is formed by the suffix *cha* according to the rule *bhave chandasi*, the elision of the *ṭi* portion does not occur by the rule *naṣtaddhite*; this is due to the restriction *aṣṭakhoreva* (Pāṇini 6.4.145).
Once the designation *bha* is established, the elision of the vowel *a* occurs by the rule *alopo'naḥ*.

Regarding the rule *‘ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ’* (Pāṇini 6.4.168), which prescribes the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*), it is not applied here because all such rules are optional in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
Thus, we have *tirohito ’hyaḥ* and *tiroahnyaḥ*. In these cases, the preservation of the original form is governed by the rule *‘prakṛtyāntaḥpādam’*.
The initial member of the compound retains its original accent when it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*).

The third hymn, consisting of fifteen verses beginning with “eṣāṃ uṣāḥ,” is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Praskaṇva. This and the following [hymns] are dedicated to the Aśvins and composed in the Gāyatrī meter.
Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: “eṣo pañconāśvinaṃ tu gāyatram.”
This hymn is used at the Prātaranuvāka, during the Āśvina sacrifice, with the Gāyatrī metre, and in the Āśvina Śastra; it is prescribed by the rule:
“Now, for the Āśvina [Śastra], this [is the hymn] beginning with ‘uṣāḥ’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.15).
Ka. 41 322 Rigveda

This unprecedented Dawn shines forth, the beloved of heaven. I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a lofty hymn. 1. This—Dawn—unprecedented, shines forth, the beloved of heaven; I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a great [hymn]. 1.

"This very one who is being beheld by us, the beloved who is the cause of joy for all—she is not unprecedented (apūrvyā), meaning she did not exist previously during times such as midnight; rather, the goddess Uṣas, having come from the sky (divaḥ), now dawns (vyucchati), that is, she dispels the darkness.
O Aśvins, I praise you both (vām) with vast (bṛhat) and abundant hymns.
I praise.
In the case of self-praise,
according to the rule "the substitutes for *tiṅ* [endings] are *tiṅ* [endings]," the first-person singular ending is replaced by the second-person singular ending.
Or alternatively:
In the third person singular of the subjunctive (*leṭ*), the suffix *sip* is applied according to the rule "the suffix *sip* is frequently used in the subjunctive.

O you two skillful ones, whose mother is the Sindhu, who further the thoughts of wealth, O gods, finders of riches through our prayer! 2. yā | dasrā | sindhumātārā | manotarā | rayīṇām | dhiyā | devā | vasuvidā || 2 ||
The connection with the preceding verse is as follows: "I praise those two gods, both Aśvins, who possess the qualities about to be described.
Of what nature are they? They are "dasrā," meaning beautiful to behold, and "sindhumātarā," meaning having the ocean as their mother.
Although the Sun and Moon alone are born from the ocean, nevertheless, according to the view of some, the Aśvins possess that same nature because they are of their form.

They are "the furtherers of thoughts" (*manottarā*), meaning those who carry one across by means of the mind; "by wisdom" (*dhiyā*), meaning by ritual action; and "finders of wealth" (*vasuvidā*), meaning those who cause one to obtain a place of dwelling.
[The term] *manottarā*...
"Manasā tarataḥ" means "crossing by means of the mind," thus it is *manottarā*.
From the root *tṛ* (to cross), with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it, the suffix *ap* is applied according to the rule *ṛdorap*.
When the final *s* of the preceding word [manas] becomes *h*, the substitution of *u* for *o* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
Of riches;
the word *nāma* has an acute accent (*udātta*) by the rule "optionally after a prefix" (*anāmy-atarasyām*).
By wisdom (*dhiyā*).
The acute accent on the case ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*.
[The term] *vasuvidā* means "one who finds (*vindate*) the *vasūni*, i.e., places of residence."

The word *kipca* contains the suffix *kip*. "Your lofty steeds carry you along upon the ancient surface of the earth, when your chariot flies with its winged horses. (3) They carry you, O lofty ones, upon the ancient surface of the earth, when your chariot flies with its winged horses. (3)
O Aśvins, when your chariot flies—that is, moves—upon the *viṣṭap*, the celestial world praised by various hymns (*jūrṇāyām*), then your lofty praises (*kakuhāsaḥ*) are uttered by us;
they are being proclaimed.
[In the word *vacyante*,] the substitution of *vac* for the root *brū* occurs according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 2.4.53: *bruvo vaciḥ*.
There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *vacisvapi* etc.

Since the phrase *vā chandasi* ("optionally in the Vedic") is understood in the rule *saṃprasāraṇācca*, the substitution of the preceding vowel (*parapūrvatva*) is optional; therefore, the *yaṇ* substitution occurs. The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

*Kakuhāsaḥ*: According to the lexicon, "the word *kakubha* is known to denote both faith (*śraddhā*) and preeminence (*pradhāna*). By the word *kakubha*, which expresses preeminence, its corresponding hymns of praise (*stuti*) are indicated through metaphorical indication (*lakṣaṇā*). The form *hattvam* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
By the rule "ājeserasuk," the suffix *asuk* is applied.
[The root] *jṛ* is used in the sense of "wasting away" (*vayohānau*). Thus, [the form] *jūrṇāyām*.
In this context, the meaning is for the purpose of praise, because the verbal roots have a single meaning.

Regarding the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ* by the rule "after a root ending in *nyu*, there is no *iṭ* before a suffix marked with *k*. The substitution of *u* for *a* occurs according to the rule "diversely in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
The vowel lengthening [is applied] by the rule *hali ca* (Pāṇini 6.3.111).
The status of being a *niṣṭhā* suffix is established by *radābhyām* (Pāṇini 8.2.42). The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
By means of the birds (*vibhiḥ*).
[The root] *vi* is used in the sense of "going" and so forth.
They go, they move—thus they are called *vayaḥ* (birds).
Horses;
the suffix *ḍit* is derived from the *uṇādi* [list];
let it fall.
The root *pat* means "to go.
In the *leṭ* mood, there is the augment *āṭ*. By the rule "there is elision of the *i* [of *it*] after [a verbal suffix]," the *i* is elided.

Through the oblation, the lover of the waters, the filler of the vessel, the protector of men, the father of the dwelling, the one who observes all people. 4. Through the oblation; the lover; of the waters; he drinks; the filler; of men; the father; of the dwelling; the observer. 4.
The two Aśvins are the gods; Vapā-jāraḥ is the Sun, the consumer of waters through his own heat. Vapipat, by means of the oblation (havis) given by us, satisfies the gods.
It should be understood that the Sun’s quality of being a "filler" (pūraka) results from the offering of oblations once the Sun has risen.
Therefore, the meaning is: "At the time of sunrise, you two must come."

What kind of *jāra* is he? He is the *parpuri*: by the aforementioned sequence, one whose nature is filling (*pūraṇa-svabhāva*); the sower (*vapitṛ*), meaning a protector; and the *vacarṣaṇi*, meaning a beholder of action (*karman*). Regarding this, the *Nirukta* states: "The *parpuri* is the one who causes the oblation (*havis*) to decay (*jarayitṛ*) or the one who drinks (*pibati*); there are Vedic citations for both *pṛṇāti* [to fill] and *prīṇāti* [to please]; he is the father (*pitṛ*) because he protects (*cāyitṛ*) the performed action; thus he is the Sun" (*Nirukta* 5.24).
Jāra: He who causes to age is jāra;
[it refers to] the sun (āditya).
The word *dāra* is derived from the root *dṛ* with the suffix *ghañ*, as prescribed by the rule *dārajārau kartari ṇiluka ca* (Pāṇini 3.3.20.4).
By the rule *karṣātvataḥ*, it bears an udātta accent on the final syllable.
[The word] *apām*.
In the word *uḍidam*, the case ending is acute (*udātta*). [The root] *pṛ* [is used] in the sense of protecting and filling.
Because *juhoty-ādi* [verbs] take *śap*, there is *ślu*-elision;
by the rule “*artipiparyośca*,” the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is shortened;
and by the rule “*anudātte ca*,” the beginning of the reduplicated stem (*abhyasta*) receives the acute accent (*udātta*).
In *parpuri*,

the suffix *kin* is applied according to the rule "ādyamahan. Although the status of *kit* is already established by its being a *liṅ* suffix, the absence of *guṇa* substitution— by virtue of the rule "ṛcchatyṛtām" (Pāṇini 7.4.11)— is secured through the force of the explicit inclusion of the letter *k*.
By the rule "udoṣṭhyapūrvasya," there is the substitution of *u*;
by the rule "nisvādādyudāttatvam," it has the udātta accent on the first syllable.

You are the opener of our prayers, O Nāsatyas, you whose words are esteemed; drink of the Soma with boldness! 5. Opener; of you two; of the prayers; O Nāsatyas; you whose words are esteemed; drink; of the Soma; with boldness. 5.

O Aśvins, you who are praised with words of devotion, you two who are the beloved objects of our hymns—O Vanaspatya [or O you two who are true to the forest], drink that Soma which is the *ādāra* (the stimulator) of your *matīnām* (devout thoughts). What kind of Soma? *Dharṣṇuyā*: one that is bold or impetuous; that is to say, intense due to its quality of producing exhilaration. Regarding the words: *Ādāraḥ*: From the root *dṛ* in the sense of "to pay heed" (*ādare*). That which causes heedfulness is *ādāraḥ*. The suffix *ghañ* is applied according to the rule "dārajārau kartari ṇiluka," and the final syllable of the compound is accented by the rule *thāthādinā*. *Matīnām*: The word *nāman* is optionally accented according to the rule "nāmanpatarasyām. *Matavacasā*: Those two whose speech (*vacas*) consists of thought (*mata*) in the form of praise. The vowel *ā* replaces the case-ending according to "supāṃ suluk. *Pātam*: From the root *pā* in the sense of "drinking. Due to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," the *śap* suffix is elided, and the substitution *pibādeśaḥ* does not occur according to the rule "pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartishayasahacara. *Somasya*: Because of the rule "kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam," the object becomes a recipient (*saṃpradāna*), and thus the genitive is used in the sense of the dative. *Dharṣṇuyā*: The case-ending is replaced by *yāc* according to "supāṃ suluk. 33. Translation complete.
O Aśvins, grant us that nourishing food which bestows light and dispels the darkness. ||6|| O Aśvins, grant us that nourishing food which bestows light and dispels the darkness. ||6||

O Aśvins, may that food—rich in light, endowed with the splendor of essence and potency, and possessing the radiance of form—carry us across; may it lead us to the heroes. Having caused the darkness of poverty to vanish and be destroyed, grant such food to us, O you two, and bestow it upon us.
The root *pṛ* [is used] in the sense of protecting (*pālana*) and filling (*pūraṇa*).
From the causative form (*pyantāt*), in the *luṅ* tense with the *caṅ* suffix, there is the elision of the *ṇi*.

The [rules concerning] the substitution of *upadhā* vowels, doubling (*dvirbhāva*), the retention of the first consonant (*halādiśeṣa*), and the lengthening of vowels (*sandhāvevadīrghāḥ*) apply; furthermore, "in the Veda, these occur diversely even without the application [of specific rules]."

The absence of *aṭ* [augment]. By the rule "caṅanyatarasyām" (Pāṇini 6.1.218), when the penultimate vowel of the root is to be acute, there is instead an acute accent on the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). There is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) by the rule "yadvṛttānnityam. In *asme*: the substitution of *śe* for the dative plural ending is according to "supāṃ suluk... In *rāsāthām*: the root is *rā* in the sense of "giving. This is the aorist (*luṅ*) in the sense of a Vedic prayer (*prārthanā*), with the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) by transposition. For the suffix *kleḥ*, there is *sic*. The prohibition of *iṭ* is by the rule "ekācaḥ. As before, there is the absence of *aṭ*. The *nighāta* is by the rule "tiṅaṅatiṅaḥ."

Come to us in the ship of our prayers, so that we may reach the further shore; O Aśvins, harness your chariot! 7. Come to us in the ship of our thoughts, so that we may go to the further shore; O Aśvins, yoke your chariot! 7.

O Aśvins, come toward us from the midst of the ocean with your ship as the means of travel, in order to reach the further shore of our thoughts and hymns—to go to the end—by means of your vessel. To come hither, yoke your chariot; make it ready for the journey. Regarding *nāvā*: the acute accent on the case-ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. Regarding *gantave*: the suffix *-taven* is used in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) by the rule *tumarthe sesen*; it is acutely accented on the first syllable because it is marked with the *ni*-sign. Regarding *yujñāthām*: from the root *yujir* (to yoke) in the imperative (*loṭ*), second person dual, *āthām* ending; *śam* is substituted for the root vowel because it belongs to the *rudhādi* class; the *a* is elided by the rule *bhasoralopaḥ*; the accent is that of the suffix.
The drop of Soma has, through inspired thought, yoked for you both the broad oar of heaven and the chariot at the crossing-place of the rivers. || 8 ||

O Aśvins, yours is a vessel—a boat serving as the means of travel—that is broader than even the wide heaven; it exists at the landing-place of the rivers, that is, the oceans. And your chariot exists upon the earth for the purpose of moving.
The drops of Soma have been yoked by *dhi*, by the ritual action directed toward you.
*Aritram*: [derived from] the root *ṛ* "to go. The suffix *itra* is applied in the sense of an instrument according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.2.184: *atilaghūsūkhanasahacara itraḥ*.
The accent is that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
In *divaḥ*,
the case-ending is udātta by the rule "aḍiḍam."
Regarding *tīrtha*: [it is derived from] the root *tṛ* in the sense of "floating" or "crossing over. By the rule *pātṛdāvaciricisicimyasthak* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.164), the suffix *thak* is applied.
The substitution of *i* for *e* occurs by the rule "ṛta iddhātoḥ"; the lengthening occurs by the rule "hali ca. [Thus:
*yuyuje*.
In the case of the *liṭ* [perfect tense], there is the substitution of *re* for *irec* by the rule "irayo re" (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.76).

O Kaṇvas, the drops from heaven are the treasure at the place of the rivers; where will you deposit your own Vṛtra? 9. From heaven, O Kaṇvas, the drops [flow] as wealth to the place of the rivers; where will you two intend to place your own Vṛtra? 9.
They are the Kaṇvas, the sons of Kaṇva;
or alternatively,
the wise officiating priests.
The ellipsis is "Ask the Aśvins for help. How so? That is explained:
from the sky (*divaḥ*), that is, from the celestial realm, the *indavas*—the rays of the sun—have become manifest.

In the place—the intermediate space—of the rivers, which are of the nature of flowing and take the form of rain, the light of the dawn has appeared as a treasure (vasu) that serves as the cause for the dwelling of ourselves and others; this is the sense of the ellipsis.
At this moment, where (kuha) do you two intend to place your own Vṛtra, your own form?
The intended meaning is that it must be shown here upon arrival.
*Kuha*: By the rule *vā ha ca chandasi* (Pāṇini 5.3.13), the suffix *hapratyaya* is added to the word *kim* in the sense of the locative case.
By the rule *ku tiṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.104), *kim* becomes *ku*.
*dhitsathaḥ*. [The root] *dhā* (in the form *dhudhāñ*) means "to hold" and "to nourish.
According to Pāṇini Sūtra 7.4.54, *sani mīmāghurabhalabhaśakapatapadāmaca iḥ*, there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel *ā*.
By the rule "atra lopo'bhyāsasya" (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.4.58), there is the elision of the reduplicated syllable (abhyāsalopa).
By the rule "saḥ syārdhadhātuke" (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.4.49), the letter *s* is replaced by *n*.

Light has become *ūṃ*; for the ray, gold has become *ūṃ*. Facing the suns, the dark one has looked out with his tongue. 10. It became; *ūṃ*; light; *ūṃ*; for the ray; gold; toward; by the suns; he looked out; with his tongue; the dark one. 10.
The light of the sun indeed appeared for the sake of the ray during the time of dawn;
and the sun became like gold through his own rising.
And Agni, becoming black himself as he entered the sun by means of his own brilliance, shone forth with his own tongue, that is, with his flame.
Therefore, the meaning is that this is the time for the two Aśvins to come forth.
It became [so].
There is a prohibition of the *guṇa* substitution by the rule "abhūsṛyomiddhi.
With respect to gold.
The prefix *prati* is designated as a *karmapravacanīya* by the rule *pratiḥ pratinidhipratidānayoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.4.92).
[When joined with a *karmapravacanīya*, the second case ending is used] according to the rule *karmapravacanīyayukte dvitīyā*.

Wearing [their garments], O you two who are auspicious to men, come hither for the drinking of Soma with a song, like unto Manu. *vavasānā* | *vivasvati* | *somasya* | *pītyā* | *girā* | *manuṣvat* | *śambhū* (i.e., *śam-bhū*) | *ā* | *gatam* || 13 ||

O Aśvins, who are the source of happiness for those who have meditated upon you, come hither—come for the sake of drinking the Soma and for the sake of our song of praise—to Vivasvat, who is like Manu, who honors you, and who is devoted to your service, you two who take delight in dwelling with him. Come!
*vavasānā*:
[derived from] the root *vas* ‘to dwell’;
by Pāṇini-sūtra 3.2.129, *tācchīlyavayovacana*, the suffix *cānaś* is applied in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlya*).
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is the elision (ślau) of the suffix śap;
by the rule "anyeṣām api dṛśyate," there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (abhyāsa) in the saṃhitā.
The vowel *ā* [in *pītyā*] is a substitute for the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
The word-final acute accent (*antodāttatva*) is applied by the rule *citaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.163).
[The form is] *pītyā*.
The root *pā* is used in the sense of drinking; the suffix *ktin* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) according to the rule "sthā-gā-pā-pacaḥ bhāve";
and by the rule "ghu-mā-sthā-," the substitution of *ī* for *ā* occurs.
The final udātta accent occurs by way of transposition.
Third [chapter].
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
I bow to that Great Lord Vidyātīrtha, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire universe from the Vedas.
Now begins the fourth chapter of the first Aṣṭaka.
"Ayaṃ nāma" is the fourth hymn of the ninth Anuvāka, consisting of ten verses. Regarding this, it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: "Ayaṃ [daśa], in Prāgātha meter."
Because of the established rule, "The seer [is named] after another [person] from whom he received [the hymn]," the seer is Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva.
Likewise, since it was stated previously that "But the [hymn] addressed to the Aśvins," by the technical convention of naming the deity, this hymn also has the Aśvins as its deities.
By this very same convention, both this and the subsequent [hymn] are *pragāthas*.
Therefore, the odd-numbered verses, beginning with the first syllable of the third line, belong to the *brahman* [meter];
the even-numbered verses, beginning with the second and fourth syllables, belong to the *satobṛhatī*.
This hymn is used in the *prātaranuvāka* during the *āśvina* ritual when the meter is *bārhata*.
In the section beginning with "Now, the [hymns] for the Aśvins," it is stated in the Sūtra: "'imā u vām ayaṃ vām'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.15).
This hymn is also used in the Āśvina-śastra, as indicated by the rule: "according to the procedure of the Prātaranuvāka" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.5).
This most honey-sweet Soma has been pressed for you, O increasers of Truth;
drink it, O Aśvins, as it passes through the day, and grant clarified butter and treasures to the donor.

This most honey-sweet Soma has been pressed for you, O increasers of Truth; drink it, O Aśvins, which was prepared on the day before yesterday, along with clarified butter and treasures for the donor. 1.

O Aśvins, you two who increase the *ṛta*—that is, the truth or the sacrifice—this Soma here before you has been pressed, that is, extracted. Of what nature is it? It is most sweet, possessing an excellence of sweetness.
"Drink that Soma which was pressed on the previous day, which has now become invisible;
bestow delightful riches upon the donor, the sacrificer who has offered the oblation."
*vām*: By the rule *yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayorvānāvau* (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.1.20), the substitute *vām* is applied for the genitive dual;
and this [substitute] is unaccented (*anudātta*).
*Madhumattamaḥ*: [The root] *man* means "to know. That which is known (*manyate*) is *madhu*.
In the word *phalipāṭinam* and so forth, the suffix *u* is applied. Due to the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule "nit," there is acute accent (*ādyudāttatva*) on the first syllable.
There is a substitution of the letter *dh* for the final [consonant].

"Madhumattamaḥ" means "most rich in honey" (atiśayena madhumān). Because the suffix *man* is treated as having the *pit* designation, its inherent acute accent (*udātta*) remains; thus, only the word-accent (*padasvara*) is left. [The term] "ṛtāvṛdhā" [is explained as follows].
From the root *vṛdh*, with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it, the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule "kvip ca.
The lengthening of the first member of the compound is justified by the rule "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate.
Thus, [the word] *tiroahnyam* is formed.
*Ahyaḥ* means "the state of a snake" (*ahi-bhavaḥ*). The suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *bhave chandasi*.
Due to the restriction in the rule *ahyasyoreva* (Pāṇini 6.4.145), there is no elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant) by the rule *nastaddhite*.

According to the rule "all rules are optional in the Vedic language" (*sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante*), there is an absence of *prakṛtibhāva* by the rule "ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.168); consequently, by the rule "alopo 'naḥ," there is the elision of the letter *a*.
Thus, *tiro'hyaḥ* becomes *tiro'hnyaḥ*.

Since *tiras* is a particle (*nipāta*) meaning "disappearance" according to the rule "tiro 'ntardhau" (Pāṇini 1.4.71), it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*); therefore, in this *prādi*-compound, the original accent of the preceding member (*anyapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*) applies.
The word *dāśuṣe* [is derived from the root *dāś*] with the suffix *kasun*, being an irregularly formed (*nipātita*) word according to the rule "dāśvān sāhvān" etc.
In the singular dative case, the semivowel is vocalized (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam."
The substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*] occurs by the rule "śāsivasi-ghasīnāṃ ca."

Come hither, O Aśvins, on your three-seated, triple-wheeled, and well-adorned chariot. The Kaṇvas offer prayers to you at the sacrifice; graciously hear their invocation. 2. On your three-seated, triple-wheeled, and well-adorned chariot, come hither, O Aśvins. The Kaṇvas offer prayers to you at the sacrifice; graciously hear their invocation. 2.

O Aśvins, come hither on your chariot which has three seats, which is elevated within and adorned with various bindings, which is threefold—possessing unimpeded motion as it traverses the three worlds—and which is well-fashioned, endowed with beautiful color.
The wise Kaṇvas, sons of Kaṇva, or the officiating priests, prepare for you both at the sacrifice a *brahman*—either a hymn in the form of a mantra or food in the form of an oblation.
Hear well, with great attention, the invocation of those Kaṇvas.
With the triple-seated chariot.
[Rigveda 1.4.2] (Bandhana 33)

O Viśvavedasā, you two possessors of all knowledge, standing upon the *barhis*—the sacrificial grass situated in three places in the form of three enclosures (*kakṣyā*)—you two sprinkle the sacrifice with sweet juice; that is, you desire to pour it. O Aśvins, for your sake, those who have pressed the Soma, who have arrived at the dwelling, and who wear golden ornaments, call upon both of you.
[The word] *tridhasthe*.
The sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is called *tridhastha* because it stands together in three places;
the suffix *ka* is applied by the rule *supi sthaḥ*,
and the vowel *ā* is elided by the rule *āno lopa iṭi ca*.
The substitution of *sadh* for the word *saha* occurs according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.3.96: *sadha mādasthayośchandasi*. Thus, [we have] *madhvā*.
The absence of the augment *num* is due to the fact that the rules governing augments (*āgamānuśāsana*) are not universally obligatory (*anitya*).

In the case of *jasi ca*, by the rule "In the Vedic language, there is optionally [the absence of the substitution] for *jas* and the following [cases]" (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.3.109.1), there is also the absence of the substitution of *nā*.
[Thus we have] *mimikṣatam*.
[The root] *miha* means "to sprinkle."

By the rule *sani ekācaḥ*, there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*. Because the suffix *san* is marked with the *k* indicator by the rule *halantācca*, there is an absence of the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*). Then, the rules for the elision of the remaining consonants of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsahalādiśeṣau*) apply.
Ḍhvakkvavapatvāni.
Sutasomāḥ. Those by whom Soma has been pressed.
The accent of a bahuvrīhi compound [is on the final syllable].
*abhidyuḥ*:
*dyu* is a name for "day."
By that [word], its related illumination (*prakāśa*) is indicated.

[The compound] *abhigatā dhūm* [is formed] according to the rule: "Words such as *adhi*, etc., when used in the sense of having crossed over and so forth, form a compound with a word in the second case" (Pāṇini Sūtra 2.2.18.4). Thus, it is a compound.
The original accent of the first member of the compound remains [in *avyaya-pūrvapada*].
O Aśvins, with those aids by which you protected Kaṇva at the sacrifices, with those protect us today, O lords of splendor; drink [the Soma], O you who increase immortality. 5.
With those aids by which you two, O Aśvins, protected Kaṇva, with those protect us well, O Lords of Splendor! Drink the Soma, O you who increase the Truth. 5.

O Aśvins, you two—by those desired aids and protections with which you protected the great seer Kaṇva—O lords of splendor (*śubhaspatī*), guardians of beautiful deeds, protect us, the performers [of sacrifice], well with those very protections.
The rest is clear.
[The word is] *abhiṣṭibhiḥ*.
They are called *abhiṣṭayaḥ* because they are directed toward (*abhimukhya*) [the goal]; that is, the fruits (*phalāni*). [The root] *iṣu* means "to desire.
By the rule "the suffix *ktin* [is used] in the sense of the object" (*karmaṇi ktin*), and by the rule beginning with "*tina-tr*" etc., there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*.
The substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) is applied by the rule *emanādiṣu chandasi pararūpaṃ vaktavyam* (Pāṇini 6.1.94.6).
By the rule *tādau ca*, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the prefix (*gati*) is maintained.
According to the *Phitsūtra* 81, *upasargā abhir varjyam*, the word *abhi* has its final syllable accented (*antodātta*).
Śubhaspatī:
[The root] *śubh* means "to shine.
[The suffix] *kip* is applied according to the rule "and *kip*."
By the rule "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra," the *visarjanīya* is replaced by *s*.

Because of the rule "subāmantrita," the sixth-case ending undergoes *parāṅvad-bhāva*; consequently, the entire compound consisting of the genitive case and the vocative takes the universal low pitch (*sarvānudātta*) as prescribed in the eighth chapter [of Pāṇini's grammar].
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, bearing wealth on your chariot, bring nourishment to Sudās;
bestow upon us riches from the ocean or from heaven—riches desired by many.

O Aśvins, you who are the destroyers of distress, bringing wealth upon your chariot, bring nourishment and riches to Sudās. Whether from the ocean or from heaven, bestow upon us that which is desired by many.

The two Aśvins, the wonder-workers (*dastrā*) who are beautiful to behold, carrying wealth upon their chariot for King Sudās—the son of Pijavana, endowed with excellent giving—brought to him nourishing food (*pṛkṣaḥ*).
[They brought it] from the ocean, that is, from the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*);
"ocean" is a name for the intermediate space.
Because it is listed among its names in [the Nirukta] as "The ocean is the sacrifice" (Ni. 1.3.15);
and furthermore, having brought down from heaven—that is, from the celestial realm—the wealth (*rayi*) which is "much-desired," i.e., coveted by many, "bestow it upon us," establish it within us.

*Sudāḥ* means "one who gives well"; [the suffix] *asu* is applied, and by the rule for the accentuation of the original form of the final member (*kud-uttarapada-prakṛtisvaratvam*), it bears its own accent. *Divas pari*.
By the rule "pañcamyāḥ parāvadhyarthe" (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.3.51), the *visarjanīya* is changed to *s*. [Thus we have] *puruspṛham*. [The root] *spṛh* [is used] in the sense of desiring (*īpsā*).
The root *spṛh* belongs to the *cur*-class and ends in *a*. [The term] *puruspṛhaḥ* means "desired by many";
it is formed with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of the object (*karman*).

Therefore, because of the status of the elision as *sthānivat*, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel. Since the first syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is acute by the rule *jittvareṇa*, that very accent remains by the rule *kuduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*.
"Whether you two are in the distance, O Nāsatyas, or whether you are among the Turvaśas, come hither on your well-rolling chariot together with the rays of the sun. (7)
Whether you two, O Nāsatyas, are far away, or whether you are present here among the Turvaśas.

In *bahulam*, there is the elision of the *ṅe* case-ending. In *pṛñcantā*, [the root] *pṛcī* means "to join. In the present participle (*śatṛ*), the suffix *am* is added because it belongs to the *rutra*-class; then, by the rule *bhaloralopaḥ*, the vowel *a* is elided. The accent is that of the suffix. In *mukte*, by the rule *sukarmapāpa* (Pāṇini 3.2.89), the suffix *kri* is applied to the root *kṛ* in the sense of past time; then, by the rule *hrasvasya piti* (Pāṇini 6.1.71), the augment *tuk* is added. In *mudānave*: he whose giving (*dāna*) is excellent (*sudānu*). The word *dāna* ends in the suffix *nu* and is acutely accented on the first syllable. By the rule *ādyudāttaṃ cchandasi*, in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the first syllable of the second member is acutely accented. In *sīdantam*, [the root] *pad* means "to dissolve," "to go," or "to sink down."
Therefore, O Nāsatyas, come with that chariot of sun-like brilliance,
with which you have ever brought wealth to the donor for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Therefore, O Nāsatyas, come hither on your chariot with its sun-bright skin, whereby you have constantly brought wealth to the donor for the drinking of the sweet Soma. 9.
O Nāsatyas, [come] with sun-like skin, with the mantra of the sun, with the rays of the sun...

[to] the *sadas*. That in which they sit is the *sadas*. Because of the suffix *asun* and the *niṅ* augment, it has the udātta accent on the first syllable. *Papṛkṣuḥ*: from the root *pā* (to drink); in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), there is the elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule "elision of *ā* before *iṭ*" (*āto lopa iṭi ca*). It takes the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). By the rule "also when *hi* follows" (*hi ca*), there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent. ||2||

The fifth hymn, consisting of sixteen verses beginning with "saha vāmena," has Praskaṇva as its seer. Because it belongs to the Bṛhatī class, the even-numbered verses are Anuṣṭubh-Bṛhatīs, while the odd-numbered verses are Satobṛhatīs.
The deity is Uṣas.
According to the Anukramaṇikā, "Together with the sixteenth [verse], it is the Upastha.
This hymn belongs to the Prātaranuvāka, in the Upastha section, during the Ṛtu sacrifice, in the Bārhata metre.
In the section titled "Then the Upastha," it is stated in the Sūtra: "The Bārhata [sūkta] begins with 'pratyu adṛśi maha vāmene'ti" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.14).
Likewise, this sūkta is also used in the Āśvina-śastra, because it is extended [to that context] by the rule "according to the method of the Prātaranuvāka" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.5).
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, shine forth together with the left [side], together with great splendor, O radiant one; O goddess, bestowing wealth, shine forth with riches.
O Dawn, daughter of heaven, shine forth upon us with your left [side]—you who are radiant with great splendor, O Goddess, rich in gifts. 1.
"O daughter of Heaven," O daughter of the deity Yū, "O Dawn," O goddess of the time of dawn, "shine forth for us," bring about the break of day "with wealth.
O "radiant one," O goddess Dawn, shine forth "with great splendor," that is, with abundant food.
O "goddess," you who are "munificent," being endowed with the habit of giving, shine forth "with riches," that is, with wealth characterized by cattle.
Uccha! ‘Ucchī’ means to dawn. O daughter of heaven!

Regarding the rule *āmantrita-parāṅgavat-svare* [Pāṇini 8.1.72], because of the statement *param api chandasi* [Pāṇini 2.1.2.6], when *divaḥ* functions as a prior member of a compound, the entire vocative group receives the sixth case accentuation (*sarvānudātta*) according to *āmantritasya ca* [Pāṇini 8.1.19]. In *bṛhatā*,
the case-ending is accented by the rule *brahma-mahat-osya-saṃkhyānam* [Pāṇini 6.2.39].
*vibhāvari*: [derived from] *bhā* in the sense of "shining" (*dīptau*); the suffix *vanip* is applied according to the rule *āto maninkvanivvanipaśca*.
By the rule "vano ra ca," the suffix *ṅīp* is applied; through its conjunction, the letter *n* is replaced by *r*. In the vocative case, there is shortening [of the vowel], resulting in *dāsvatī*.
The root *dāś* means "to give. The suffix *asun* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*), resulting in *dāś*. That which possesses this [quality] is called *dāsvatī*.
The substitution of *v* for *matup* occurs by the rule *mādupadhāyāḥ*;
the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added by the rule *ugitaśca*.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, bestowing all wealth, they hasten forth abundantly to shine. O Dawn, raise up for me the bounteous gifts of the wealthy patrons.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, bestowing all things well-finding, they hasten forth abundantly to shine. O Uṣas, raise up for me the true songs; bring hither the bounty of the liberal patrons.

Aśvāvatī: possessed of many horses; Gomatī: endowed with many cows; Viśvasuvidah: excellent bestowers of all wealth; O subordinate deities, you have arrived—*cyavanta* meaning "you have reached"—abundantly (*bhūri*) for the sake of *vastave*, that is, for the dwelling of living beings. O Daughter of Heaven! (1. ḍha)

O Goddess Uṣas, "utter" (*udīraya*)—that is, speak—"truthful words" (*sūnṛtāḥ*), meaning pleasant and beneficial speech, "for me" (*mām*), directed toward me. "Impel" (*coda*)—that is, send forth—the "wealth" (*rāghaḥ*) belonging to the "munificent ones" (*maghonām*), those who possess riches, for our sake. Now, regarding *āvatīḥ*: by the rule *mantre somāścendriyaviśvadevasya matau* (Pāṇini 6.3.131), there is lengthening of the first member of the compound. Furthermore, because the optional prohibition of the *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha* (substitution of the preceding vowel with its homogeneous long) is stated by the rule *vā chandasi*, the *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha* is applied here. Regarding *cyavanta*: from the root *cyuṅ* (to move). In the *laṅ* tense, the augment *aṭ* is absent due to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge'pi*. Regarding *vastave*: from the root *vas* (to dwell). The suffix *taven* is added in the sense of the infinitive marker *tumun* by the rule *tumarthe sesen*. Because it has the *niṭ* designation, it is accented on the first syllable. Regarding *īraya*: from the root *īra* (to go and to shake). The causative suffix *ṇic* is added in the sense of "causing to do. Regarding *coda*: from the root *cuda* (to impel). It belongs to the *curādi* class. In the *loṭ* tense, the *śap* is replaced by *ślu* by the rule *chandasyubhayathā*. Since it is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the *ṇi* is elided by the rule *ṇeraniṭi*. Because the *śap* is *pit*, it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains. There is no suppression (*nighāta*) because it does not stand at the beginning of a *pāda*. Regarding *maghonām*: in the genitive plural, the *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization of the semivowel) occurs by the rule *śrayuvamaghonāmataddhite*.
The goddess Uṣas has shone forth and now shines on high; she is the quickener of chariots, for those who have placed themselves within her advances are like those seeking glory upon the ocean.

She has dwelt; she has shone forth; may the goddess shine forth now—she who is swift for chariots, for those who have placed themselves within her movements like those seeking glory upon the ocean. 3.

The goddess Uṣas has shone forth; she made her dwelling in the past—that is, she brought about the dawn—and indeed, even now, she shines forth; she brings about the dawn. Of what nature is this goddess?
"Of the chariots"—the *jīrā* is the impeller, for at the time of dawn, chariots are indeed set in motion.
"In the arrivals," that is, in the comings of this Dawn, "those chariots which have been prepared," meaning they become readied; the connection with the preceding phrase is "of those chariots.
This is an illustration regarding the impelling of chariots.
‘Desirous of fame’ (śravasyavaḥ) means ‘desiring wealth. Just as they propel boats by mooring them in the midst of the ocean, so [he] dwelt.
[The root] *vas* is used in the sense of ‘dwelling.’
By the rule *nalī 'limbabhyāsasyobhayeṣām'* (Pāṇini 6.1.17), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable.
By the accent of the suffix (*lisvara*), the syllable preceding the suffix is acute (*udātta*). [Thus:
*ucchāt*.
The augment *āṬ* is added by the rule *leṭo ’ḍāṭau*; the vowel *i* is elided by the rule *itaś ca lopaḥ*;
and the suffix *śap* is applied because [the root] belongs to the *tud*-class.
Since the suffix is added due to the sense of "coming" (*āgamana*), it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

Because the word *uṣāḥ* belongs to a different sentence, this [word *jīrā*] does not undergo the enclitic accent (*nighāta*) with respect to it, according to the rule: "The enclitic accent, as well as the substitutes for *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, must be stated within the same sentence" (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.1.18). [The word is] *jīrā*.
The verbal root *ju* is a Vedic root meaning "to go.
By the rule *'jorī ca'* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.181), the suffix *khap* is applied.
[This refers to] her.
In the rule "idam-anvādeśe," the substitute *aś* is unaccented;
since the case ending is also unaccented due to the substitution of *m*, the entire word is unaccented.
[This applies] in the sense of "conducts" (*ācaraṇeṣu*).
