O you of bold mind (*dhṛṣanmanas*), O Indra whose mind subdues enemies, you who exist at the limit—on the upper region—of this pervasive atmosphere (*vyoman*) and of the world (*rajas*), you who are born of your own power (*svabhūyojāḥ*), you have made the earth, the terrestrial world, for our protection.
Furthermore, you have become the counterpart, the representative, of the strength of the powerful.
Likewise, one should go well to the forest.
"Āpaḥ" is a name for the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). One who has encompassed (*paribhūḥ*) the world of the intermediate space (*antarikṣaloka*) and the world of heaven (*dyuloka*).
The verb *bhavati* preceded by *pari* has the sense of "appropriating. You obtain this.
In the word *uḍidam*, the case ending is acute (*udātta*).
Regarding *vyomanaḥ*: the root *ava* has the sense of "going," according to the lexicon which states, "ava [is used] in the senses of protection, going, and beauty."
It is called *vyoma* because it moves (*gacchati*) through and pervades (*vyāpnoti*) with distinction;
or else,
it is called *vyoma* because it specially protects (*avati*) living beings by bestowing growth (*vṛddhi*).
The suffix *manin* is applied according to the rule "it is seen even after other [roots]";
by the rule "jvara-tvara," etc., there is the substitution of *ūt* for the penultimate vowel and the letter *v*,
and then *guṇa*.
The original accent of the first member [of the compound] applies because it belongs to the class beginning with *dāsībhāra*.
Alternatively,
the suffix *manin* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).

In the compound *vividhomrakṣaṇam*, which is a *bahuvrīhi* meaning "that in which there is manifold protection (*om-rakṣaṇam*)," the accentuation of the original form of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratvam*) applies.

Upon the substitution of the semi-vowel (*yaṇ-ādeśe*), the following unaccented vowel becomes circumflex (*svarita*) according to the rule: "After an acute (*udātta*) or circumflex (*svarita*) [vowel], the *yaṇ* [substitute] [causes the following unaccented vowel to become circumflex]."
*Svaḥ*.
[The word *su* is] derived from the root *at* with the suffix *vic*, according to the rule "it is seen after other roots as well.
Then, by the rule "after an indeclinable, the case-suffixes *āp* and *sup* are elided" (Pāṇini 2.4.82), there is the elision (*luk*) of the *sup* suffix.
The *svarita* accent is applied according to the rule: “The *nyaṅ* vowel and the *svarita* [are so called]” (Phiṭ-sūtra 74).

In the *marutvatīya* śastra of the *bhūtāgni-ekāha*, before the hymn from which the *nivid* is drawn, this verse beginning with “Thou hast become the image of the earth” (*tvaṃ bhuvaḥ pratimānaṃ*) is to be recited.
He has formulated this very point in the Sūtra: “The recitation has been explained by [the rules for] the Bṛhaspatisava: ‘Thou hast become the image of the earth’” (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 9.5).
You are the counterpart of the earth; you have become the lord of the vast, lofty hero.
You have filled the entire mid-air with your greatness. Truly, indeed, no one is your equal.
You are the counterpart of the earth; you have become the lord of the vast, lofty hero.
With your greatness, you have filled the entire mid-air. Truly, indeed, there is no other like you. 13.

O Indra, you are the counterpart— the representative— of the earth, of the vast and expansive ground. The meaning is that just as the world of earth is great and possesses inconceivable power, so too are you.
Likewise, regarding *ṛṣvavīra*:
"heroes" (*vīrāḥ*) are the gods, so called because they act as heroes (*vīrayanti*), that is, they become courageous.
He for whom the heroes have been made visible is thus described.
You have become the lord and protector of that vast, exalted, and expanded heavenly world.

Likewise, by your greatness, you have truly and completely filled the entire intermediate space—the atmosphere existing between heaven and earth—with your majesty. Therefore, it is the absolute truth that there is no other whatsoever who is equal to you.
*bhuvaḥ*: from the root *bhū* in the *leṭ* mood with the suffix *sip*, there is the augment *aṭ* and the substitution of *u*.
Of *pṛthivyāḥ*: the case-ending is acute according to the rule “*udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt*”. Of *bṛhataḥ*.
The acute accent of the case-ending is due to the rule "bṛhanmahatorluksaṃkhyānam. Regarding *bhūḥ*:
since the Vedic usage permits the *luṅ* (aorist) tense even for the present, there is an absence of the augment *aṭ* according to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge'pi."
*aprāḥ*. [The root] *prā* means "to fill"; it belongs to the second (*adādi*) class.
In the *laṅ* [past tense], there is the substitution of *aṭ*.
In the word *mahitvā*, the third case ending is replaced by *ḍā* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
*tvāvān*:

The suffix *vatup* is applied in the sense of similarity by the rule *yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam* (Pāṇini 5.2.39, vārttika). By the rule *pratyayottarapadayośca*, the form *tvā* replaces the portion ending in *map* of the stem *yusmad*.

The substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel] occurs by the rule *ā sarvanāmnaḥ*. Since the affix is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the nominal stem (*prātipadika*) alone remains.

Neither heaven and earth reached the extent of his expansion, nor did the rivers reach the end of his mid-world; nor indeed his own rain when he fights in his exhilaration—alone, you have performed all other things in succession. Neither heaven and earth reached the extent of his expansion, nor did the rivers reach the end of his mid-world; nor indeed his own rain when he fights in his exhilaration—alone, you have performed all other things in succession. 14.
The expanse (*vyacas*) of that Indra, which pervades heaven and earth, could not be reached by them; they were unable to attain it.
Likewise, above the *rajas*—the intermediate space—the flowing waters (*sindhavaḥ*) did not reach the end or limit of that Indra’s splendor.

Moreover, when he was exhilarated by the intoxication of drinking Soma, Vṛtra and the others could not reach the limit of the strength of this Indra as he fought his own rain—that is, as he engaged in battle against Vṛtra and the rest.
Therefore, O Indra, you alone have drawn toward yourself (*ānupak*)—that is, made dependent upon yourself—the entire universe (*viśvam*), the whole collection of beings other than yourself;
the sense is that the entirety of the world of beings has become subject to you.
*dyāvāpṛthivī*:
heaven (*dyauḥ*) and earth (*pṛthivī*).
By the rule *divo dyāvā* (Pāṇini 6.3.29), the substitute *dyāvā* is prescribed and is marked as having an acute accent on its first syllable.
The word *pṛthivī*, by the rule *pṛthivī-śabdaḥ pitr-ādibhyaś-ca*, ends in the suffix *ṅīṣ* and is oxytone (accented on the final syllable).

In a *devatā-dvandva* compound, by the rule *devatā-dvandve ca*, there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛti-svara*) of both members. Because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) in the rule *apṛthivī-rūpa-manthiṣu*, the prohibition contained in the rule *nottarapade 'nudāttādau* does not apply.

*vyacaḥ*. Because of the rule "the root *vyac* is treated as belonging to the *kuṭādi* class when *manas* follows" (*Kāśikā* 1.2.1.1), there is an absence of *ṅittva*, and consequently an absence of *saṃprasāraṇa*. [The form] is *ānuśuḥ*.
The *parasmaipada* ending is used through a transposition (*vyatyaya*) from the root *abh*.
By the rule *ata ādeḥ*, the vowel *ā* is substituted for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).
And by the rule *abhnoteśca*, the augment *nuṭ* is added.

The Maruts sang their praise here in this very battle; all the gods rejoiced after you, O Indra, when with your bold weapon you struck down Vṛtra face to face. 15. They sang their praise; here; the Maruts; in this; in the battle; all; the gods; rejoiced; after; you; of Vṛtra; when; with the bold; weapon; down; you; O Indra; face to face; struck. 15.
"O Indra, here in this battle, the Maruts have praised you; strike, O Blessed One, slay, and display your heroism!"—with these words they honored him.
In each and every battle, or indeed in every conflict, all the Viśvedevas—that is, all the Maruts endowed with qualities such as generosity—rejoiced after you, bringing you joy in succession.
Or alternatively:
After your gift, they too became intoxicated. O Indra, when— *yat* meaning *yadā* (when)— you, with the *dhṛṣṭi*, that is, the *astri* (spear) which pierces enemies,
or rather with the *vadha*, the weapon for striking, namely the *vajra* (thunderbolt)...

Furthermore, the preeminence of the *vajra* is traditionally taught in the Brāhmaṇa: "This [sacrificial post] is indeed a *vajra*; it should be made eight-cornered, for the *vajra* is eight-cornered" (AiB 2.1).
With that *vajra*, you struck Vṛtra's face—that is, his mouth—or rather, his nose, which is the cause of breathing; you utterly destroyed his vital breaths.
*Ārcan*. The root *arca*, meaning "to worship," belongs to the Bhvādigaṇa.
The augment *āṬ* is acute.
Regarding the form *sasmin*:
the substitution of *sa-* prescribed by Pāṇini’s rule *tadoḥ saḥ sāvanantyayoḥ* (7.2.106) should be understood as applying to the locative case (*saptamī*) by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
Alternatively,
one should understand that there is an elision of the vowel in the word *sarvasmin*; thus it becomes *devāsaḥ*.
*Ājserasuk*:
*ānam ānanam*;
the elision of the vowel is Vedic (*chāndasa*).
Or rather:
*ana* means breath;
it is breathed (*anyate*).
1. Ḍa: And likewise.
2. Ḍa: Only one. 3. Ḍha: Followed by *sa*.

*Ānaṃ* means the nose (*ghrāṇam*). The suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). By the rule *karpānvataḥ*, there is an udātta accent on the final syllable. *Jaghanyaḥ*: from the root *hana* in the sense of "to kill" or "to go. In the *thali* suffix, by the rule *upadeśe'tvataḥ*, there is a prohibition of the substitution of *it*. By the rule *abhyāsācca*, the *ha* following the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes *gha*. By the accent of the *liṭ* (perfect tense), the syllable preceding the suffix is udātta. || 14 ||
The third hymn, consisting of eleven verses beginning with “nyū ṣu,” has its tenth and eleventh verses in the Triṣṭubh meter;
the remaining nine are in the Jagatī meter.
Samba is the seer;
Indra is the deity.
Thus it has been stated in the Anukramaṇī: “In the [hymn] beginning with ‘nyū’, there are eleven verses, and the last two are in the Triṣṭubh meter.”
This is the *sūkta* for the recitation (*śastra*) of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin during the first round (*paryāya*) of the Atirātra sacrifice.
Accordingly, the Teacher [Āśvalāyana] laid it down in his sūtra: "‘nyūṣu vācamapsu dhūtasya harivaḥ piba’ is the *yājyā* [verse]" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.4).
We bring forth our speech and our songs to the Great One, to Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat;
for even now he has found treasure as if among those who sleep.
You are the opener of the stall for the horse, O Indra, the opener of the stall for the cow, the opener of the stall for the fodder; you are the powerful Lord of wealth.
O man, you who from of old have touched the song of praise, we, as friends for our friends, now sing this hymn to you.

Thou art the door to the swift steed; O Indra, thou art the door to the cow, the door to the pasture, the lord of wealth, the powerful master. O heroes, from of old you have been the seekers of the hymn; as a friend to your friends, we now sing this praise to you. 2.

O Indra, you are the giver of the doors for the swift steed; likewise, you are the giver of the doors for the cow and the like; likewise, you are the giver of the doors for the *yarva*—the species of grain such as barley and the rest. You are the lord (*inaḥ*), the master, the protector of all, and the ruler of wealth (*vasu*) which is the cause of dwelling. O leader of men (*śikṣā-nara*), you are the guide of giving (*śikṣā*); the root *śikṣ* has the meaning of "giving" (Nirukta 3.10.8). You are ancient (*pradivaḥ*), one in whom days have passed from of old. You are the non-withdrawer of desires (*akāmarśanaḥ*); one who draws away or destroys desires is a *kāmarśanaḥ*, and you are not such, hence *akāmarśanaḥ*. [The compound follows] the accentuation rule where the first member retains its original accent. [O Lord of] the oblation (*havi*).
In the Vedic language (cchandasi), [the suffix] *a* occurs [after the genitive];
thus, *tvāyataḥ*.
He desires you for himself (*tvām ātmana icchati*).
By the rule "supa ātmanaḥ kyac," and by the rule "pratyayottarapadayośca," there is the substitution of *tvā* for the portion ending in *m* (maparyanta). The form *āśvam* is Vedic.
From a root ending in *kyac*, the suffix *śatṛ* is substituted for *laṭ*.

Since that [suffix] has an *adupadeśa* (a low-pitched vowel in its original enunciation), it is unaccented by the accent rule for *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes. However, by the statement "It should be stated that the accent of a single substitute (*ekādeśasvara*) is established as internal" (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.2.6.1), once that [single-substitute accent] is established, the acute accent of the case-ending beginning with *ac* (i.e., *ām*) is applied by the rule "śaturanumaḥ... (Pāṇini 6.1.173).
*Kāmam*: [This is derived] from the root *kam* in the sense of "desire" (*kāntau*). The suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*).

Although the rule *karṣātvataḥ* would have required the final syllable to be accented (*antodātta*), the word is instead acutely accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) because it is listed among the *vṛṣādi* group.
*unathiḥ*. [The root] *un* in the sense of "abandoning" (*parihāṇe*), belonging to the *curādi* group.
In the case of *luṅ*, by the rule *niśridrustubhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.48), the substitution of *caṅ* for *cli* is prohibited by the rule *nonayatidhvanayati* etc.
(Pāṇini 3.1.51). Furthermore, by the rule *hyantakṣaṇa* etc. (Pāṇini 7.2.5), the *vṛddhi* [vowel lengthening] in *sic* is prohibited.
With these songs and with these drops, O Aśvins, warding off the lack of understanding with cattle;
with Indra and with the drops, may we subdue the Dasyu and, free from enmity, grasp the nourishment.

With these [Soma drops], with these [Soma drops], being well-disposed; with these [Soma drops], subduing the lack of understanding; with cattle, with horses, with Indra, overcoming the Dasyu with [our] Soma drops; free from hatred, may we together seize the nourishment. 4.

O Indra, being pleased by these radiant oblations (*havis*) offered by us, by these soma-drops (*indu*) present before you, and by the *soma* juices, turn away our lack of wisdom—that is, poverty—by means of cattle (animals given by you), by wealth consisting of horses, and by bestowing auspicious thoughts; O Lord, become one whose mind is gracious toward us.

With the drops (*indu*)—the Soma juices offered by us—Indra, being pleased, shall destroy (*dayantaḥ*) the Dasyu, the enemy who oppresses; thus becoming *yutadveṣasaḥ*, those whose enemies are driven away, we shall *saṃ rabhemahi*—that is, we shall take hold together with the food (*iṣā*) granted by Indra;
the meaning is that we shall come together.
*Sumnaḥ*: one whose mind (*manas*) is beautiful (*śobhana*).
The acute accent on the first syllable of the second member of the compound is according to the rule *somana-sī aloma-upasī*.

*nirundhānaḥ* [is used] in the sense of "obstructing. The root *rudh* (in the form *rudhir*) means "to obstruct"; because it is marked with the *svarita* accent, the *ātmanepada* (middle voice) ending is applied.

By the rule "śvasorallopaḥ," there is elision of the vowel *a*. By the rule "citaḥ," there is the udātta accent on the final syllable. [In the case of a compound ending in *kruddha*,] there is the preservation of the original accent of the second member (*uttarapada-prakṛtisvaratva*).
Non-insight:
insight is to be contemplated; it is sovereignty.
Non-insight is that which is not insight.
The initial member of the compound retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) because it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). The genitive case is prohibited by the rule *na lokāvyaya* (Pāṇini 2.3.69).
[The vocative] *aśvinā*.
The term *aśvin* means "possessing horses"; it is formed by adding the possessive suffix *ini* to *aśva*.

O Indra, may we obtain wealth together with nourishment; may we obtain it with strengths, with many-glittering, youthful riches; may we obtain it through divine providence that is full of heroic vigor, preeminent in cattle, and rich in horses.

O Indra, may we grasp wealth; may we grasp nourishment; may we grasp abundant, glittering spoils and glorious riches; may we grasp divine providence, which is full of heroic vigor, preeminent in cattle, and rich in horses. 5.
O Indra, may we be united with you through wealth;
may we be united with food;
and likewise may we be united with strengths.
With what kinds of strengths?
With those that are *puruścandra*, delighting many; with those that are *abhidyubhiḥ*, shining on all sides.
Furthermore, may we unite with your divine *pramati*, your excellent intelligence.
Of what kind? "Possessing heroic vigor" (vīraśuṣmayā). She is so called because she possesses *śuṣma*, which is strength (*bala*) that is especially capable of destroying enemies.
ᳵGo-agrayā.

She is so described because she has cows (*gāvaḥ*) right at the front (*agre*), that is, in the very presence of her worshippers (*stotṛbhyaḥ*), for the purpose of giving. [In *aśvāvatyā*] "by means of one possessing horses" (*aśvape-tayā*). [In *rāyā*] the accentuation of the case-ending is by the rule "aḍiḍam," etc. [In *puruṣannaiḥ*] the augment *suṭ* is applied by the rule "hasvācchandrottarapade mantre"; the letter *ś* arises through the substitution of *ścutva*; it bears the accent of the compound. [In *abhidyubhiḥ*] "those whose splendor (*dyauḥ*) has reached upward. Here the word *div* indicates brilliance (*dīpti*). It bears the original accent of the first member of the compound, as it begins with an indeclinable. [In *devyā*] the accentuation of the case-ending is by the rule "udāttayaṇaḥ. [In *pramatyā*] the original accent of the prefix (*gati*) is maintained by the rule "tādau ca niti. In the two following [words], being *bahuvrīhi* compounds, there is the original accent of the first member. In *goagrayā*, the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāvaḥ*) occurs by the rule "sarvatra vibhāṣā goḥ" (Pāṇini 6.1.122). [In *aśvāvatyā*] the lengthening of the vowel occurs before the suffix *matup* by the rule "mantre somāśvendriya... (Pāṇini 6.3.131). || 15 ||
Those exhilarations have gladdened you, those virile powers, O Lord of Beings, and those Soma juices in the slayings of Vṛtra.
When for Kāru, who had spread the sacrificial grass, you irresistibly struck down ten thousand Vṛtras, you brought them low.

Those exhilarating draughts have gladdened you; those manly powers of yours, O Lord of the Hundredfold, in the slayings of Vṛtra, when for the singer who spreads the sacred grass, you, irresistible, struck down ten thousand Vṛtras. 6.

O Lord of the hundred, O protector of the good, Indra—when the slayings of Vṛtra, the acts of killing Vṛtra, served as the occasion, those aforementioned exhilarating Maruts gladdened you, they made you rejoice and attain joy. Those aforementioned oblations belonging to you, the showerer (vṛṣṇi)—the sacrificial offerings such as the *caru* and the *puroḍāśa*—gladdened you.
And those well-known Soma juices also gladdened you.

Whenever you, being irresistible by enemies, struck down—that is, slew—the ten thousand countless *vṛtra*s (obstructing calamities) for the singer who offers praise, for the sacrificer who provides the sacred grass (*barhis*), then [the result follows];
this is how it connects with the preceding.
*vṛṣṇyā*:
the elision of the *śi* suffix occurs by the rule "in the Veda, [the suffix *śi*] is frequently [elided].
*barhayaḥ*.

The root *barhayati* has the meaning "to injure" (*hiṃsākarmā*; Nirukta 2.19.30). In the *laṅ* [aorist], the absence of the augment *aṭ* is due to the rule "in the Veda, [the augment] is frequently absent even when there is no connection with *mā*" (*bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge’pi*). Since the *śap* [present marker] is *pit*, it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the *ṇic* suffix alone remains.
That which, due to its connection with a metrical foot, does not undergo elision [of the initial vowel].

You come upon battle after battle with boldness; you shall destroy fort after fort with your might. When, O Indra, through your friendship with Namya, you struck down the guileful one named Namuci in the distance.

With battle, for battle, you come hither; indeed, you go forth with boldness. You strike down this stronghold after stronghold with your might, O Indra, when, through friendship, you struck down from afar the guileful one named Namuci with your bow. ||7||

O Indra, with boldness, you go toward the battle—the conflict connected with war—of the enemies as their subduer; that is, you always possess the nature of a warrior. The particle *gha* is for the purpose of completing the meter.

With your might and power, you utterly destroy this city before us— the city of the enemies, the Asuras— along with their fortresses. O Indra, by means of your thunderbolt, which is capable of bending the enemy, acting as your companion and ally, you struck down the guileful Asura known by the name Namuci in a distant land, because you completely annihilated him.
Therefore, the meaning is that you yourself are praised in this manner.
By *yudhā*; [the root] *yudh* means "to fight. The suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule beginning with *saṃpadādi*.
The acute accent on the case-ending is due to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*.
[In the word] *eṣi*,
[the root is] *iṇ* "to go."
Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision of the *śap* suffix.
[The form is] *dhṛṣṇuyā*.

‘*Jiṣṇuḥ*’: by the rule *trasigṛdhṛdhṛṣikṣipaḥ knuḥ*, the suffix *knu* is applied; due to its *kit*-status, there is no *guṇa* substitution. By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the case ending *su* is replaced by *ā*. By the rule *citaḥ*, it has an acute accent (*udātta*) on the final syllable. *Purā*: from the root *pṛ* in the sense of “protecting” or “filling”; he fulfills the desires of kings. By the rule *kvip ca*, the suffix *kvip* is added. By the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*, the vowel *u* is substituted for the *ṛ*. By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the case ending is acute. *Haṃsi*: from the root *han* in the present tense (*laṭ*), with the second person singular ending (*sip*); because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision of *śap*. By the rule *naścāpadāntasya jhali*, an *anusvāra* is inserted. *Namnyā*: from the root *ṇamu* in the sense of “bending. An *auṇādika* suffix *ina* is added. By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the third case ending is replaced by *ā*; the *ṭi*-portion is elided. *Satyā*: because of the prohibition of the *ghisamjñā* designation by the rule *śeṣo dhyasakhi*, there is no substitution of *nā* (for the feminine), and thus the *yaṇ* substitution occurs. *Namucim*: he does not release the battle with Indra; hence *namuciḥ*. An *auṇādika* suffix *ki* is added. By the rule *nabhrāṇnapāt* etc., the negative particle *nañ* retains its original form (*prakṛtibhāva*). Since *nañ* is neither a verb nor a *kāraka*, the rule for the accent of the second member of a compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*) does not apply, and thus the accent remains on the first member, which is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). *Māyinam*: because the word *māyā* is listed among the *vrīhyādi* group, the possessive suffix *ini* is added.
You struck down Karañja and Pūṛṇaya with the most brilliant path of Atithigva;
you shattered the hundred forts of Vaḍgada, O irresistible one, for Ṛjiśvan whose wealth was purified.
You slew Karañja and Pūrṇaya with your most brilliant power on the path of Atithigva; you shattered the hundred fortresses of Vaḍgada, while Ṛjiśvan drove away those who were hemmed in.

O Indra, you slew the asura known as Karañja and also the asura named Pūrṇaya for the sake of King Atithigva; you struck them down with your most brilliant, exceedingly radiant, and skillful weapon, the *vartanī*.
Likewise, you slew Ananuda—an *anuda* being one who follows (*anu*) and cuts (*dyati*) or shatters from behind, that is, a pursuer or follower.

Such as you are, alone and without followers, O Ṛjiśvan, you shattered—that is, you split apart—the hundreds, by the hundreds, of cities belonging to the Asura named Vaḍgada, which had been completely besieged by the king named Ṛjiśvan.

*vadhīḥ*: from the root *han*, in the *laṅ* tense with the suffix *sip*, there is the substitution of *vadha* by the rule "in the *luṅ* [and other tenses]" (*luṅi ca*). Because that substitute ends in the vowel *a*, there is no *vṛddhi* strengthening (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.3.35).
For this very reason, because it consists of more than one vowel (*anekāctvāt*), there is no prohibition of the augment *iṭ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.10).
By the rule "iṭa īṭi," there is the elision of the suffix *sic*. [The form is] *tejaṣṭhayā*.

From the word *tejas*, the suffix *vini* is applied in the sense of possession according to the rule *asmāyāmedhā*. From that [form *tejovin*], when the superlative suffix *iṣṭhan* is added, the *vini* is elided by the rule *vinmator luk*.
Then, the final *ṭi* is dropped by the rule *ṭeḥ*.
By virtue of being a feminine noun ending in *ū*, it has the udātta accent on its first syllable.
*Vartanī*: it is called *vartanī* because one is turned or impelled by it (*vṛyate preryate 'nayā*).
The suffix *lyuṭ* is applied in the sense of instrument (*karaṇe*).
Because it is marked with the indicator *ṭi*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added according to Pāṇini Sūtra 4.1.15.
By the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.39), the case ending undergoes substitution by the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*).
The final udātta accent occurs due to a metrical inversion. He split; the root *bhid* means "to cleave."
In the case of the third person singular (*sip*) of the present tense (*laṭ*), *śnam* is added because [the root] belongs to the *rudhādi* class.
By the rule *itaś ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *i*.
By the rule *halṅyābbhyaḥ*, there is the elision of the suffix *s*.
Ananudaḥ. [The root] *dā* means "to cut. By the rule *ādeca upadeśe'śiti*, there is the substitution of *ā*.
The suffix *ka* is applied by the rule *ātaścopasarge*.
In the *bahuvrīhi* compound *anudaḥ* (meaning "one who has no *ud*" [to give]), the final syllable of the second member is udātta according to the rule *nañsubhyām*.
The long vowel in the *saṃhitā* reading is a Vedic (*chāndasa*) irregularity.
"Pariṣpūtāḥ" [means] "completely purified.
[The root] "pū" is used in the sense of "impelling" (or "purifying").
The suffix *niṣṭhā* is applied in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*).
In the phrase "gatiranantaraḥ," the word *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
1. The *ḍha* and *na* case endings are udātta.
Ṛgveda 4.38.1:
"O King of Men, you [conquered] these who had approached with Suśravas, the twice-ten kinsman."
He, the renowned one, crushed ninety-nine thousand six hundred with his chariot wheel, making them difficult to traverse on foot.

O King of Men, you, the renowned one, with your chariot wheel, crushed the sixty thousand, ninety-nine [thousand], and two times ten [thousand] of these who had approached the friendless Suśravas—[you who were] twice [as strong]. You struck them down where they could not stand. 9.

O Indra, you who are renowned and famous from all sides—[you who defeated] those who had approached for battle with King Suśravas, known by that name, who was without kin (abandhu) and without allies, [and who were led by him]—those lords of the people (janarāja), the rulers of the various territories;
specifically, sixty thousand, ninety-nine thousand, and nine hundred [followers] of those kings. (The number of the followers of those kings is stated by means of the "sixty" and so forth.)

With such a wheel—belonging to the king, having such a number of followers, with chariots and chariot-connections, difficult to traverse, and by means of a difficult-to-traverse path (meaning: one that cannot be reached by enemies)—you overturned them; you brought them down.
The meaning is that you came to the aid of Suśravas while he was praising you for the sake of his old age, and thus you conquered his enemies.
Janarāja:
Due to the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the rule regarding the formation of compound endings (*paribhāṣā* 84), there is an absence of the suffix *ṭac* [as prescribed by Pāṇini 5.4.91].
The word *rājan* is derived from the root *rājṛ* "to shine" with the suffix *kanin*, and is thus acutely accented on its first syllable (*ādyudātta*).
By the rule *kruduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratva* (the accent of the final member of a compound with *kruddha* remaining as the original accent), that very [accent] remains.
In *abandhunā*,
the final syllable of the second member is udātta by the rule *nañsubhyām*.
*Sūśravasā*: one whose *śravaḥ*—that is, food—is beautiful (*śobhana*).
The acute accent on the first syllable of the second member of the compound is according to the rule: "In the Veda, a word ending in *vyac* has the acute accent on its first syllable."

*upajagmuḥ*: from the root *gam*, the *liṭ* (perfect) affix *kvasu* is applied; when the *śas* case-ending follows, it receives the designation *bha*, and by the rule "there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the vowel in *vasu*," vocalization occurs.
The state of having another vowel preceding [the *s*] occurs;
by the rule "gamahana," etc., there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*),
and by the rule "śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca," the status of being a word-final (*padatva*) is established.
By the rule that the original accent of the final member of a compound with *kruddha* remains, the accent of *ksīra* alone is retained.
*Rathyā*:
this belongs to a chariot (*ratha*), thus it is *rathyam*.
The suffix *yat* is applied by Pāṇini’s rule *rathādyat* (4.3.121).
By the rule *yato ’nāvaḥ*, the initial syllable is acute-accented (*ādyudātta*).
The vowel *ā* of the case-ending is substituted by *supāṃ suluk* (7.1.39).
*Duṣpadā*: [derived from] the root *pada* meaning "to go," with the suffix *khal* applied according to the rule *īṣadduḥsuṣu*.
By the rule "liti," the vowel preceding the suffix *lit* is udātta. As before, the case-ending becomes *ā*.
[The verb form is] *avṛṇak*.

The root *vṛj* in the sense of "avoiding" belongs to the *raudhādika* class. In the *laṅ* (imperfect) tense, in the second person singular, there is elision of the *s* by the rule "after vowels ending in *hal*, the *si* [is elided]."
The substitution of *k* for *c* occurs by the rule "coḥ kuḥ" (Pāṇini 8.2.30).
You protected Suśravas with your aids; O Indra, you protected Tūrvayāṇa with your succors.
You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king for his conquest.
You protected Suśravas with your aids, and Tūrvayāṇa with your protections, O Indra. You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king for his service. 10.
O Indra, you protected Suśravas—the king previously mentioned—by means of your aids (*ūtibhiḥ*), that is, by your own protections.

Likewise, you protected the king named Tūrvayāṇa through your single guardians (*trāmabhiḥ*). Furthermore, for the sake of this great and youthful Suśravas, you brought the three kings, Kutsa and the others, under his control so that they might be subdued (*arandhayaḥ*).
Yāska [states] in the Nirukta (6.32): "The Ṛṣi is so called because he has attained mastery."
By means of the *trai* [roots]; from the root *traiṅ* in the sense of "protecting" (*pālane*); the substitution of *ā* [for *e*] occurs according to the rule *ādecaḥ*.
The suffix *manin* is applied by the rule *āto manin*; it has the udātta accent on the first syllable because it belongs to the *ni* class. [Thus formed is] *arandhanāyaḥ*.
It performs the act of cooking or subjugation; thus, "randhanayati.
The suffix *ṇic* is applied according to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.26 (*tatkaroti*).

Due to the status of being treated like the primary nominal stem (*iṣṭavadbhāva*) according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.155 (*iṣṭavarṇau prātipadikasya*), there is the elision of the final syllable (*ṭilopa*).
In the *laṅ* [tense], the long vowel [of the root] occurs before the *sip* suffix due to Vedic usage.

O Indra, may we be your most auspicious friends, you who protect the gods. We shall praise you, and through you, possessing excellent heroes, may we extend our life-span further and further. (11) O Indra, those who are your friends, the guardians of the gods—may we be the most auspicious among them. We shall praise you; through you, being rich in heroic sons, may we attain a longer life, extending it even further. (11)

O Indra, we who are here at the conclusion of the sacrifice, protected by the gods (*devagopāḥ*), being your friends—dear to you like true companions—and therefore most auspicious (*śivatamāḥ*), have become exceedingly blessed; as such, even after the completion of the sacrifice, we shall praise you.
Praised by us, may we—possessing excellent heroes, that is, having noble sons—and maintaining a life that is exceedingly long and most pre-eminent, continue to exist for a very extended duration.
*Devagopāḥ*:
those for whom the gods are protectors (*devā gopā yeṣām*).
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada*) is retained.
I have not made it my own.
[The root] *as* means "to exist" (*bhuvi*).
It is used in the sense of the *luṅ* (aorist) tense.

The word *bhāvaḥ* [indicates the formation]. Regarding *pṛtsu*: by the rule “*padādiṣu māṃsṛtsnūnām upasaṃkhyānam*” (Pāṇini 6.1.63.1), there is the substitution of *pu* for the word *pṛtanā*. Regarding *parīṇaśe*: the root *naś* has the sense of “to perish. The suffix *ken* is applied according to the rule “*kṛśyārthe tavaiken*. Because of its initial *ni*, it is udātta-accented. By the rule “*nipātasya ca*,” there is lengthening of the first member [of the compound]. Regarding *nacaḥ*: the nominative case is used in the sense of the accusative. Regarding *rorvat*: from the root *ru* meaning “sound,” after the elision of *ya* (in *ruy*), the present participle suffix *śatṛ* is added. By the statement “*adādivacca*,” there is elision of *śap*. Due to the *ṅittva* of *śatṛ*, there is an absence of *guṇa* and the substitution of *uvaṅ*. By the rule “*nābhyastāc chatuḥ*,” there is a prohibition of the augment *num*. By the rule “*abhyastānām ādiḥ*,” there is udātta-accent on the first syllable. Regarding *kathā*: by the rule “*thā hatau ca chandasi*,” the suffix *thā* is added to the word *kim* to express manner. When that [suffix] receives the designation of a case-ending, there is the substitution of *ka* for *kim* according to the rule “*kimaḥ kaḥ*” (Pāṇini 7.2.103). Regarding *ārata*: from the root *ṛ* meaning “to go,” the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied by the rule “*samo gamyucchi0*. Since this is Vedic usage, the present tense *laṭ* is employed; due to being of the *adādi* class, there is elision of *śap*. There is the substitution of *at* for *jha*, and the augment *āṭ* with subsequent *vṛddhi*.
O Arci, praise Indra, magnifying him who hears you— the powerful Śakra, possessed of might and power— who,
as a bull with his bold strength, subdues both heaven and earth by his virility.

O Arcī, praise Indra, magnifying him who hears you—the powerful one, possessed of might, endowed with wisdom—who, as a bull through his virile power, subdues both heaven and earth by his bold strength. ||2||

O Adhvaryu, sing praise to Indra, who is possessed of power (*aśākine*), endowed with strength (*śaktiyuktāya*), wise (*aśacīvate*), and capable (*aśakrāya*). Worship such an Indra in this manner. Furthermore, while magnifying—that is, honoring—Indra, who hears the hymns and recognizes that "this praise is appropriate," extol him directly; offer your song of praise to him face-to-face. That Indra, by means of his bold (*dhṛṣṇunā*) and conquering might (*śavasā*), thoroughly subdues both *rodasī*, heaven and earth.
Yāska [states] that *ṛñjati* means “the act of adorning” (Nirukta 6.21).

That Indra is “a bull (*vṛṣā*), capable of pouring forth”; he is “bull-like (*vṛṣavat*)” by virtue of this very capacity for pouring; he is “the bull (*vṛṣabha*), the showerer of desires,” or else, “the showerer of the waters of rain.”
*arca*. Since the root *śap* is marked with *pittva*, it is anudātta; thus, the accent of the verbal root remains. There is lengthening by the rule "aco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.3.135).
Śākine;
śāktiḥ means śākaḥ. [The root] śaklū [is used] in the sense of power (śakti).
The suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*).
The suffix *ini* expresses possession (*mattvarthīya*).
Because the object (*karman*) is treated as a recipient (*saṃpradāna*) according to the rule “the mention of action must be made,” the dative case is employed.
"Abhiṣṭuhi. [This is derived from] the root *stu*, where due to its being of the *adādi* class, there is elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix;
and by the rule "upasargāt sunoti," there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*.
In *dhunā dhuḥ*, the change to *dhu* occurs by the rule [Pāṇini 8.2.29].
In *vṛṣṭvā*,
the vowel *ā* replaces the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk* [Pāṇini 7.1.39].
They cook.
[The roots] *ṛji* and *bhṛjī* mean "to roast.
Because they are marked with the indicatory letter *iṭ*, the augment *num* is applied.
When the suffix *śap* is applicable, *ś* occurs by way of substitution.
The flame is for the great heaven, a hymn for the Sun, whose sovereignty is firm—of him who is bold and more bold than the bold.
Or rather, the Asura has been made vast by his own power; for he is a bull, a chariot drawn by two bay steeds, standing before us.

A ray [of light] unto heaven; a lofty hymn of praise to the Sun, whose own dominion is firm—[the hymn] of him who is bold, of daring mind, and of great renown. By his might, the Asura has made his citadels; he is a bull, a chariot drawn by two bay steeds. For such indeed is he. 3.
O singer, [sing] "to the radiant, to the great Indra" the *śūrya*.
*Śūrya* is a name for happiness; that which is conducive to it is *śūrya*.

"Utter such speech characterized by praise for that Indra, the bold one who overcomes his enemies, whose own dominion (*svakṣatram*) is [as follows]... [Note: *kīdṛśam* (of what sort) refers to the description of his dominion.]

The mind is powerful; it becomes bold and courageous. For he is indeed Indra, the one of great luster (*bṛhacchavas*), possessed of abundant fame, the *asura*—the dispeller of enemies. Or rather, *asu* means breath or strength; he possesses that, thus he is *asura*. Or again, *asu* refers to the vital breaths (*prāṇa*), by which the waters are indicated, according to the Vedic text: "The waters are indeed the vital breaths" (*Tai. Brā.* 3.2.5.2). He who bestows (*rāti*) those [waters] is the *asura*. By his greatness (*barhaṇā*), he is the destroyer of enemies. Accompanied by the two bay horses (*haribhyām*), he is placed at the front, honored, the bull (*vṛṣabha*) who showers down desires, the chariot (*ratha*) whose nature is to speed. [Grammatical notes: Regarding *śūnyam*: the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of "good in that place. Since "all rules are optional in the Veda," the rule "the acute accent falls on the first syllable after *yata*" (*yato'nāvaḥ*) does not apply; instead, by the rule "the third [accent] is circumflex" (*tisvaritam*), it has a circumflex accent. Regarding *dhṛpataḥ*: from the root *dhiṣ* in the sense of "boldness. There is an irregular substitution for the suffix *śa*. In the word *śatru-namaḥ*, the case ending is acute. Regarding *bṛhacchavas*: "he whose fame (*śravaḥ*) is great (*bṛhat*). In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent of the first member remains. Regarding *asuraḥ*: from the root *asu* in the sense of "to cast. The suffix *uran* is added by the rule *aseraran* (*Uṇādi Sūtra* 1.42). Because of the *niṣ* [prefix], the acute accent falls on the first syllable. Regarding *barhaṇā*: the case ending is replaced by *ā* by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. Regarding *puraḥ*: formed with the suffix *asi* by the rule *pūrvādhara-* etc.; it is oxytone (acute on the final syllable).
You shook the ridge of the vast heaven; with your own boldness, you shattered Śambara.
When, through your daring, you struck down the hundredfold offspring of the deceitful Vṛndi with your exhilarating bolt, you cast it into the womb of the earth.

You stirred up the ridge of the vast heaven; you yourself boldly shattered Śambara when, with your exhilarating [Soma], you boldly hurled the whetted, stone-edged thunderbolt at the sorcerers and their hosts. 4.
O Indra, you caused the lofty, high region of the great heaven—the celestial world—to tremble;
by your own self, as the subduer of enemies, you yourself struck down and slew the Asura named Śambara.
This was when you, in order to conquer the arrogant enemies who had become soft, [acted].
Or rather:

[O Indra], you who possess a *vṛnda*—a multitude—of *māyins*, deceitful Asuras, [are] joined with a mind that is *mandinā*—joyful—and *dhṛpatā*—attaining boldness; [with such a mind], take hold with your hand of the *śitām*—sharpened—*garbhastim*.
Or rather:
*garbhastí-* is a name for a ray. You desire to hurl that [thunderbolt]—the *aśanī*, the *vajra*—which possesses such rays, in order to conquer those Asuras who have been struck down (*pṛt*).
The meaning is: "you impel them toward those [waters].
At that time, the phrase "you stir up the ridge of the vast heaven" connects with what precedes it.
You stir them up.
The root *kup* means to be angry. From the causative (*ṣyant*) form, in the *laṅ* tense, there is an absence of the augment *aṭ*, according to the rule:
“In the Veda, the augment *aṭ* is frequently absent even when not joined with *māṅ*.”
By oneself; the elision of the vowel *ā* occurs according to the rule "in mantras, the *ā* of *ātman* when it begins with [a word] starting with *ā*.
O you who are firm!
The elision of the third case ending occurs by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. [The form] *śitām* [is derived from] the root *śo*, meaning "to thin" (*tanūkaraṇe*).
In the case of the suffix *niṣṭhā*, there is the substitution of *i* for [the final vowel] by Pāṇini’s rule 7.4.41: *aśācchor anyatarasyām*.
[Thus we have] *pṛtyaṃsi*.
From the word *pratāna*, [the suffix] *kyac* is applied by the rule *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*.
In the word *kyaccarapratanasya*, there is elision of the final vowel; it bears the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
"When you cast down upon the head of the snorting Śuṣṇa—even though he was a roaring leader of hosts—"
With a forward-striving mind, full of power, whatever you shall do— even if it be something difficult— who can restrain you?

When you strike down upon the head of the snorting one, roaring at the woods of even the arrogant Śuṣṇa— with a forward-striving mind, full of power— whatever you shall do even today, who can restrain you?

O Indra, you, roaring with clouds and making your purpose heard while breathing within the atmosphere— he who breathes is the wind (*śvasana*)— you, from the mass (*vṛndinaḥ*) of his rays, bring the fruits and other things to a state of softness; even of *Śuṣṇa*, the dryer of fluids,
you cause the forests (*vanā*) that have grown upon his head— that is, in the upper region— to fall down, since you bend them down.
The meaning is that you cause [them] to reach.
Water rained down by the wind and the rays of the sun is established once again above the sun;
it is this very act of establishing it that is figuratively attributed to Indra.
"By one who goes forward with excellence;
that is to say, by one who is not turned away.
By the powerful one."
Because it is listed among the words for the act of slaying in the sense that "it destroys," *barhaṇā* means the injury of enemies; [the term refers to you] as one possessed of such power.

Being thus endowed with such a mind, since even now (*adyā cit*), at the time of the cosmic order (*dharma-kāle*), you establish the terrestrial juices above the sun and cause them to rain down during the rainy season—because you perform this, for that reason, no one (*kaḥ*) stands over (*pari*) you; the meaning is that there is no one at all.
Therefore, the sense is that you alone are the most excellent of all.
[The verb] *vṛṇakṣi* [is used];
[the root] *vṛjī* means "to avoid" or "to exclude."
It belongs to the *raudhādika* class.
Because the suffix *sip* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*) prevails.
Due to its connection with a word ending in *yat*, it does not lose its accent (*anighāta*).
By means of *prācīnena*. From the root *añj* preceded by *pra*, the suffix *kin* is applied according to the rule "ṛtvig-" etc.;
the elision of the nasal *n* occurs by the rule "aniditām".
In the rule "vibhāṣāñjer adikṣipriyām," the suffix *kha* is applied in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*). The substitution of *īn* for *kha* occurs;
then, by the rule "acaḥ," there is the elision of the vowel *a*, and by the rule "cau," there is the lengthening of the vowel.
Because the suffix -kha is *satiśiṣṭa* (remaining when others have been elided), the vowel *ī* in its substitute is acute by virtue of the rule *upadeśivadbhāva*. [In the word] *adyā cit*,
there is lengthening according to the rule *nipātasya ca*.
*kṛṇavaḥ*. [The root] *kṛvi* [is used] in the senses of "injuring" (*hiṃsā*) and "doing" (*karaṇa*).
Due to its being marked with the *it*-augment, the *num* augment is applied.
In *leṭi* and *sipi*, there is the augment *aṭ*.
By the rule "dhinivṛṇvyora ca," the suffix *up* is applied, and the letter *v* is replaced by the letter *a*.
When the *a* of that suffix is elided, due to the status of being a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*), the *guṇa* substitution for a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) does not occur.
There are the *guṇa* and *avādeśa* substitutions.
Regarding the low-pitched (*anudātta*) accent of the augment (*āgama*), the accent of the *vikaraṇa* suffix applies.
On this point, it is stated in the *Nirukta*: "The bard (*vandī*) praises (*vandate*); [the root] *mand* pertains to the state of being dull."
"You uncover [the waters] on the head of Śravasana, who makes a sound; you dry up the clouds of Śuṣṇa and Āditya, crying out, 'The forests,' or perhaps 'The riches'" (Nirukta 5.15–16).
In the case where it means "riches," it should be explained as "the riches of the cloud.
You protected Narya and Turvaśa when they were in need; you, O Śatakratu, [protected] Turvīti and Vyaya.
You [protected] this chariot in the contest for booty; you shattered ninety-nine fortresses.
You protected Narya Turvaśa; you [protected] Yadu and Turvīti, O Śatakratu. You [protected] the chariot and Etaśa in the contest for booty; you shattered ninety-nine forts. 6.
O Indra, you protected—that is, you guarded—those three kings, Narya and the others.

Likewise, O Śatakratu (possessor of a hundred powers), whether meaning "one of manifold deeds" or "one of manifold knowledge," you indeed protected the king named Turvīti, who was born of the Vyaya clan.
Furthermore, when a battle had to be fought for the sake of wealth, you protected this one named Etaśa, whose nature is speed, in his chariot. This is the sense.
Alternatively, it should be construed as follows: he protected the chariot of the aforementioned kings,
as well as Etaśa— the name of a horse—
and the horse Etaśa itself.
Likewise, you shattered—that is, you destroyed—the ninety-nine cities of Śambara; that is, those numbering ninety-nine (nine more than ninety).
[And] Etaśa:
he is called Etaśa because he goes (*eti*).
The root *iṇ* means "to go.
By the rule *iṇ-manta-śānta-śunau* (Uṇādi-sūtra 3.429), the suffix *taśan* is applied.
There is *guṇa* substitution.
Regarding *kṛlye*: this is a phonetic modification (*varṇavikāra*) of the word *kartavye*, due to its belonging to the *pṛṣodarādi* class.

1. *ca-tadavasthāpanamindraḥ*; *na-tādṛgavasthāpanamindraḥ*; *sa-tadeva sthāpanamindraḥ*. 2. *ḍha-na-sa-varṣesīti*. 3. *ḍha-yadetat*. 4. *śa-vandinaḥ*; here. 5. *ta-tha-da-dha-sa-turvīti*: [it refers to] one named Turvīti. 6. *ca-cha-pha-raṃhaṇasvabhāvam etaśam*: *etaśa* is the name of a seer (*ṛṣi*).

Truly, that king, the lord of the virtuous, the person who offers oblations, shall hear [us]—he who fulfills the command; or he who welcomes our hymns with bounty, for him the giver makes the lower regions of heaven overflow. He indeed, the king, the lord of the virtuous, shall hear, the person who offers oblations, who fulfills the command; or he who welcomes our hymns with bounty—the giver makes the lower regions of heaven overflow for him.
That person is indeed born as a leader, shining like a king, a lord of the virtuous, and a protector of the good; as a sacrificer, he causes himself to prosper.
He who, having offered oblations to Indra, attains—that is, pervades—Indra’s instruction or, alternatively, his praise, while being one to whom the host of offerings has been presented.

Whether they be *ukthas* or *śastras*, he who as a praiser (*stotṛ*) recites them together with the abundant food characterized by the oblation (*havir-lakṣaṇa*), does so for the purpose of bringing [Indra] face to face; he recites them for that praiser. To him, the praiser, may Indra—the granter of desired fruits (*dānuḥ*)—[drive] the clouds, one after another.

*Upara* is a name for a cloud; and it has been etymologically explained by Yāska himself: "It is called *upara* because it is a solid mass (*upala*); or because living beings perish within it, or because the waters have ceased (*uparatāḥ*) therein" (Nirukta 2.21).
He causes those clouds to swell—that is, he moistens or milks them—from the vicinity of heaven.
In the word *satpatiḥ*, there is a long vowel [substitution] according to the rule beginning with "ṛci tunugha" (Pāṇini 6.3.133).
The Lord of the good is the "Satpati.
[In this compound], by the rule "patyāvaiśvarye," there is the preservation of the original accent of the first member.
[He is] the one who hears.

From the root *du* (meaning "to go" and "to increase"), in the present tense, after the suffix *ṇic*, when *luṅ* is applied and *cli* is replaced by *caṅ*, the substitution of *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs—overriding even the internal operations such as *vṛddhi* on the basis of the rule "the application of *saṃprasāraṇa* and that which depends upon *saṃprasāraṇa* is stronger" (Pāṇini Mañjarī 6.1.17.2). Thus, by the rule "also in the case of *ṇi*, *śvi*, and *ślī*" (Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.31), *saṃprasāraṇa* takes place.

Because a grammatical operation conditioned by a specific technical name (*saṃjñā*) is not necessarily permanent, there is an absence of *vṛddhi*, and consequently, reduplication and the subsequent steps follow.
The substitution [of -ya] is prescribed.
In *rātahavya*,
there is the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member in a *bahuvrīhi* compound.

Regarding *śāsam*: from the root *śās* in the sense of "instruction" (*anuśiṣṭau*), with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*), the rule "karṣātvataḥ" would normally result in an udātta accent on the final syllable; however, by means of metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*), there is an udātta accent on the first syllable.
Alternatively, it should be regarded as belonging to the *vṛṣādi* group.
For it has been stated that this is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class of words).
Alternatively,
from the root *śaṃs* in the sense of "praising," with the suffix *ghañ*, there is the elision of the nasal (*n*) by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*).
*invati*. [The root] *ivi* means "to pervade.
Since the suffix *śap* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal root remains.
Because of its connection with the syllable *yad*, there is no suppression (*anighāta*).
He recites (*abhigṛṇāti*).
[The root] *gṛ* [is used] in the sense of "sound."
It belongs to the *kry-ādi* class.
By the rule "the short vowel for roots beginning with *pv-ādi*," there is shortening.
Since the suffix *tip* is marked with *p*, it is unaccented (*anudātta*), and thus the accent of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa-svara*) prevails.
As before, there is an absence of elision (*nighāta*).
In *uparāḥ*, the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding sound (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*) replaces the case ending *śas* according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
It swells (*pinvate*). [The root] *piv* (in the form *mibi ṇivi*) means "to sprinkle" (*secane*).
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyayena*).

Unequaled is your dominion, unequalled is your wisdom; may those who offer oblations be foremost through their skillful action. O Indra, those who, as givers, increase your great dominion, your enduring power, and your virility—[may they be foremost]. 8. Unequaled is your dominion, unequalled is your wisdom; may those who offer oblations be foremost through their skillful action. O Indra, those who, as givers, increase your great dominion, your enduring power, and your virility—[may they be foremost]. 8.
Indra’s sovereignty and power are not equal to anyone else's;
that is to say, they are supreme over all.
Likewise, his wisdom and intellect are not equal to anyone else's intellect.
The meaning is that it takes every object as its domain. *Ime* is a pronoun (*sarvanāman*) having the same sense as the word *ete*.
May these *somapās*, the drinkers of soma—the sacrificers—prosper through their *apas*, their ritual actions. May they flourish.

O Indra, those who have given oblations to you increase—make grow—the great (*mahi*), vast (*vratatu*) power (*kṣatra*), the mighty (*sthavira*), massive (*sthūla*), fully developed (*pravṛddha*) virility (*vṛṣṇya*, i.e., manly strength) of yours; that is, they cause it to flourish.
Or alternatively:
[they increase the power] of you, the giver, who has bestowed the fruit of the sacrifice upon the sacrificers.
The phrase "The Rigveda is yours" is to be supplied [to complete the sense].
Not so; because it is a pronoun (*sarvanāman*), the *śī* substitution occurs for the nominative plural suffix *jas* (Pāṇini 7.1.17), resulting in a *guṇa* vowel.

Although the rule "The [words] *tva*, *sama*, *sima*, and *nema* are unaccented" (Phitsūtra 78) would result in all syllables being unaccented (*anudātta*), the initial syllable is instead acute (*udātta*) by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*).
*dadupaḥ*.
[This is derived from] *dadāti* with the suffix *kasu* in the perfect tense (*liṭ*).
The substitution of *śas* for *jas* occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
According to the rule "vowel-substitution (saṃprasāraṇa) and that which depends upon vowel-substitution are stronger," the vowel-substitution occurs prior to the addition of the augment *iṭ*.
Then, by the rule "and [the substitution of] *ṣ* for the [finals] of *śās*, *vas*, *ghas*, and *si*," the substitution of *ṣ* occurs. [Finally,] there is the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).
*Mahi*: the suffix *in* is added after the root *maha-rauṇādi*. *Sthaviram*.
By the rule *ajiraśiśira-* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.53), the root *sthā* is irregularly formed with the suffix *kirac*.
These abundant [soma-draughts], milked from the mountain, are for you—the vessels and chalices that are the drinking-vessels of Indra.
Flow forth; satisfy their desire, and then bestow wealth upon the mind.
9 | For you indeed are these many [soma juices], pressed by the stones, seated in the vessels, the cups drunk by Indra; they have released the obstruction of the waters,
the waters of rain.
The word *dharuṇa* signifies a stream.
Darkness, which obstructs the streams, stood [there].
This very meaning is made explicit.
Within the bellies—the abdominal regions—of Vṛtra, the asura who obstructed the three worlds, there were mountains;
thus, because the cloud was covered by Vṛtra in the form of darkness, it is said that even the rainwater was obstructed.
He [Indra] drove away these aforementioned rivers.

By the etymological derivation "nayaḥ" from "nadana" (flowing), the word *nadī* denotes waters. Indra causes those waters—which were placed (*hitāḥ*), that is, obstructed, by Vṛtra, the *vatriṇā* (the enveloper)—to flow forth; they are *viśvāḥ* (all-pervading) and *anuṣṭhāḥ* (standing in succession).
Such waters Indra *abhijinnate*, that is, he brings them down toward the *pravaṇeṣu* (sloping) low-lying regions of the earth.
Regarding *vatriṇā*: from the root *vṛ* in the sense of "obstructing" (*varaṇe*), the suffix *kip* is applied according to the rule *āhagamahanajanakhanaghasaḥ kic*.
Due to its being a nominal stem (*liṅga*), reduplication and other such operations apply.
The substitution of *yaṇ* [occurs]; it has the accent of a suffix;
[the word] is *anuṣṭhāḥ*.
The suffix *ka* is applied to the root *sthā* by the rule *ātaścopasarge*;
the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs by the rule *upasargātsunoti*. [Thus] *jinnate*.
The Ātmanepada ending is used by way of transposition from the root *han* in the sense of "going. By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 2.4.73), the suffix *śap* is replaced by *śru*.
Furthermore, by the rule "artipipartyośca, bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pāṇini 7.4.77–78), the vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is shortened.
May he bestow upon me increasing glory, great dominion, and powerful strength, O Indra, conqueror of men!
Protect our patrons and guard our wise leaders; and grant us wealth, along with offspring and nourishment.
Bestow upon us increasing splendor; O Indra, protect our great dominion, which overcomes men and is most powerful.
Guard our wealthy patrons and protect the wise leaders. Grant us wealth for the sake of noble offspring and for sustenance.
O Indra, you—place splendor and fame upon us; bestow it upon us. Of what kind? He says: "Increasing our welfare."
"Śam" means pacification.

When there is the pacification of diseases, that which increases [thereby]—such [is it]. Likewise, "mahi" means great; "janāṣāṭ" means the overcomer of enemy persons; "tavyam" means increased; and "kṣatram" means power. The word "adhi dhā" (place upon) is to be understood as the ellipsis.
Furthermore, O Indra, having made us wealthy with riches, protect and preserve us;
likewise, guard and protect our wise patrons and others as well.
Thus, for the sake of wealth, for noble offspring, and for food, establish us in these things.

*dhāḥ*. By the rule *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*, the *luṅ* (aorist) is used in the sense of a prayer (*prārthanā*). By the rule *gātisthā0*, there is the elision (*luk*) of *sic*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasyamādyoge ’pi*, there is the absence of the augment *aṭ*.
*asme*: by the rule *supāṃ suluk...* (Pāṇini 7.1.39), the locative case ending of the pronoun *asmad* is replaced by *śe*. *janāṣāṭ*.
He who overcomes people is *janāṣāṭ*. The suffix *ṇvi* is applied according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 3.2.63 (*chandasi sahaḥ*), and the vowel *a* is lengthened by the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ*.
The substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*] is according to Pāṇini Sūtra 8.3.56: *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*.
The lengthening of the vowel in the preceding word is by the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*.
[The suffix] *tavya* [is applied].
The verbal root *tṛ* in the sense of "increase" is a Vedic (sautra) root.
By the rule *aco yat*, the suffix *yat* is applied.
Following the rule *dhātostannimittasyaiva* (Pāṇini 6.1.80), there is the substitution of *av* for *ṝ* due to the presence of the suffix.
The word *anāvaḥ* has its accent on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*) because of the rule "from *anāvaḥ*.
[The root] *rakṣ* [is used];
"to protect" (*pālana*) is the meaning of *rakṣ*.
Since the root *śap* is marked with *pittva*, it is unaccented; thus, the accent belongs to the verbal root.
The lengthening occurs by the rule *aco 'ntyādi ṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.143) [corrected to *aco 'ntyādi ṭi*], which applies here as *aco 'ti tiṅaḥ*.
[The form is] *maghonaḥ*.
In the case of *śru-yava-maghonām at-taddhite*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) before the suffix *śas*.
[The form] *pāhi* [is derived from the root *pā*]; because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix.
Because *heḥ* lacks the *apit* designation, its own accent remains.
As for *maghonaḥ*, because it occurs within another sentence (*vākyāntaragatatvāt*), there is no *nighāta*.
[The form is] *svapatyai*.
She whose offspring are beautiful is thus described.
The final syllable of the compound is accented by the rule *namsumyām*.

Regarding the absence of the augment *yāṭ* in the case of *āp* [ending] before the nominative plural suffix *jas*, as indicated by the statement “in the Vedic language, the forms are stated explicitly,” the *vṛddhi* substitution occurs according to the rule *vṛddhireci*.
1. Not sent by me.
2. To Śobhanaputra. Verse 49.
The fifth hymn, consisting of eight verses beginning with “divaścid asya,” is the seer Savya’s composition; it is addressed to Indra and is in the Jagatī meter.

Thus it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: “divaścid asya... for it is Jagatī. Because of the word “hi” (for), according to the technical rule regarding *tu* and other particles, the two subsequent hymns are also in the Jagatī meter.
This hymn is used in the Maitrāvaruṇa’s śastra during the first paryāya of the Atirātra sacrifice.
It is stated in the Sūtra: “‘divaścid asya’ is the paryāsa, and ‘sa no nabhyebhiḥ’ as well” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 6.4).
This hymn is also used in the Niṣkevalya śastra on the Viṣuvat day.
And it is prescribed in the Sūtra: “One should recite the six subsequent [verses] beginning with *divaścidasya*” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 8.6).

Furthermore, this is prescribed for the Niṣkevalya [laud] on the second Chandoma day of the Daśarātra sacrifice, which includes the root [of the ritual]: “*tvaṃ mahā~ indra yo ha divaścidasya*, *tvaṃ mahā~ indra tubhyam*—this is the Niṣkevalya” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 8.7).
Even from heaven his vastness has spread abroad; neither the great earth can equal Indra.
Terrifying and mighty, like a scorching heat, he sharpens his thunderbolt for brilliance, like a bull.

Even from heaven his vast extent has spread abroad; even the great earth cannot equal Indra. Terrifying and mighty, a scorcher of the people, he whets his thunderbolt for brilliance, like a bull sharpening its horns.
The vastness, the breadth, and the power of that Indra have spread out even beyond the sky,
the realm of light; even the earth, by its greatness and magnitude, does not equal Indra—
the ground itself cannot be a counterpart to Indra.
The meaning is that he is even greater than that.

*Bhīmaḥ* means terrifying to his enemies; *tuvivimān* means possessed of wisdom or strength; for the sake of *carṣaṇibhyaḥ*, i.e., for the benefit of men who offer praise, he is *ātapaḥ*, one who causes heat or affliction against his enemies on all sides.
Being such, that Indra *vajram*—the weapon characterized by its power to strike (*varjanaśīla*)—*tejase* for the sake of sharpness, *śiśīte*: he sharpens it, he makes it keen.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
just as a bull (*vṛṣabha*), possessing a desirable gait (*vananīya-gati*), sharpens its horns for the sake of combat, so too [is it here].
*divaḥ*:
the vowel of the case-ending is udātta by the rule "usiṅam". *varimā*.
From the word *uru*, the suffix *iman* is applied according to the rule for the *pṛṣodarādi* group;
by the rule beginning with “*priyasthira*,” the substitution of *vara* for the word *uru* occurs.
He spread out;
"pratha" means "to become manifest. By his greatness (maha).
The elision of the vowel is Vedic;
or alternatively,
the suffix *kan* is applied to the root *mahi* according to the rules of the *auṇādika* [unadi] list.
It is accented on the final syllable by the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*).

In the third case singular, there is the elision of the vowel *a* according to the rule *alopo’naḥ*. The accent of the case-ending is then applied by the rule concerning the "accent of the cessation of an acute" (*udāttanivṛttisvara*).
Regarding *prati*: according to the rule “*prati* [is used] in the senses of representation (*pratinidhi*) and exchange (*pratidāna*),” it functions as a *karmapravacanīya*.
Consequently, by the rule “when joined with a *karmapravacanīya*” (Pāṇini 2.3.8), the word *indra* takes the second case ending.
The ablative case [which might be expected] by the rule *pratinidhi-pratidāne ca yasmāt* (Pāṇini 2.3.11) does not occur here because of its Vedic character (*chāndasatvāt*).
[The word] *bhīmaḥ* [is derived] from the root *bhi* in the sense of "fear" (*bhiya*), with the suffix *mak* added according to the rule *bhiyaḥ puk ca* (Uṇādi-sūtra 1.145).
‘Bhīma is that from which one fears,’ says Yāska (Nirukta 1.20).
[It is] heat;
it is called *tapas* because it heats (*tapati*).
The suffix *ac* is applied after the root *pac* etc. (Pāṇini 3.1.134).
By the rule beginning with *thā-tha* (Pāṇini 6.2.144), there is udātta accent on the final syllable of the compound. [He] sharpens.
The root *śo* means "to thin.
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
By the rule "in the Veda [there is] diversity," the suffix *śru* replaces the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*).
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the substitution of *i* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) occurs. By the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*, the substitution of *ī* occurs.

Furthermore, even though the following *l*-suffix is not preceded by a vowel, the accentuation of the initial syllable of the reduplicated form (*abhyasta*) is applied by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*) according to Pāṇini 6.1.189.

*Vaṃsagaḥ*: From the root *vana-paṇa* in the sense of "to enjoy" (*saṃbhakti*), the suffix *sap* is added according to the *uṇādi* rules in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*). Thus, *vaṃsagaḥ* means "one who goes to what is to be enjoyed" (*vananīya*)—that is, one who approaches the forest.

The suffix *ḍa* is applied to the root *gam* by the rule *anyatrāpi dṛśyate* (Pāṇini 3.2.48). Because it begins with *divodāsa* and similar words, there is udātta accent on the first syllable of the preceding member.
1. The two [syllables] ḍha and ca. 2. The greatness of sa. 3. The power of ḍha and sa.
Like the ocean, he, the lord of the sea, receives with his vast expanses those who have approached him from every side.
Indra, like a bull, yearns for the drinking of Soma; having pressed it, that warrior is glorified by his might.

Like the ocean, he, the lord of the sea, receives those who have come from afar with his vast expanses; Indra, for the drinking of the Soma, acts like a bull. From the pressing, that warrior is glorified by his might. || 2 ||
"Indra, belonging to the ocean (*samudriya*).
Because waters flow forth from it, the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*) is called "the ocean" (*samudra*). That which exists therein is "belonging to the ocean" (*samudriya*).

Being thus, with his own *vvarīmabhiḥ*—that is, his *saṃvaraṇaiḥ* (coverings), or alternatively, his *uruvaiḥ* (wide-spreading)—he *viśritāḥ* (pervaded) the *vnadhaḥ*, the rivers, the waters that produce sound and were obstructed by Vṛtra; he *vvarṇavāt* (held back), as if against the ocean. The sense is that having taken them for himself, he rained them down.
And that Indra, for the drinking of Soma, acts like a bull (*vṛṣāyate*); he behaves like a bull;
the meaning is that he exists filled with exhilaration.
Likewise, that Indra is *vyudha*.
"Irajyasi" means "you rule. The root *irajyati* has the sense of sovereignty.
That Indra, the deity, having surpassed [all] by his heroic power (*vīryeṇa*), became widely celebrated—that is, he was thoroughly known by us with preeminence.
And that fierce Indra, fierce himself, was appointed as the domestic priest by the gods and stationed in front for every single purposeful action, such as the slaying of Vṛtra.
Of *dharma*s:
from the root *dhṛ* in the sense of "holding" (*dhāraṇe*),
the suffix *manin* is applied in the active sense (*kartari*) according to the rule "it is seen [that this suffix is applied] after other roots as well."
The initial udātta accent is due to the *nittva* [of the suffix].
*Irājyasi*:
from the root *iraj*, meaning "to envy."
In the visible [state], there is one [form] in sovereignty; however, according to Kaṇva and others, it is from the suffix *yat*,
[expressing] through heroism.
The root *śūra-vīra* means "valiant" (*vikrānta*). It belongs to the *nū* class [of roots]. The suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *aco yat*.
There is elision of the suffix *ṇi*.

Because of the rule "In a *bahuvrīhi*, [the first syllable of] *vīra* and *vīrya* are also [acute]" (*vīravīryau ca*), which prescribes acute accent on the initial syllable of the final member, the rule "That which ends in *yat* [is acute], except for *nau*" (*yato 'nāvaḥ*) does not apply; thus, there is no acute accent on the initial syllable by that rule. Consequently, the rule "The suffix *ti* is circumflex" (*titsvaritam*) applies. For if that were the case, since the result would already be established by the rule "In the Veda, [the first syllable of] a word ending in *vyac* is acute" (*ādyudāttaṃ vyacchandasī*), the separate mention of *vīrya* in the former rule would be redundant. Therefore, [the objection] is incorrect.
The deity (*devatā*) is simply the god (*deva*). The suffix *tal* is added in the sense of the base word itself according to Pāṇini’s rule 5.4.27: *devāt tall*.
In the word *cekité*, the preceding syllable has the udātta accent due to the suffix *iti*. [The root is] *kita* in the sense of "knowing."
From this root *cikidya*, ending in *yaṅ*, in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*) in the passive sense, there is the elision of *at* and the elision of *yal*.
[Thus we have] *purohitaḥ*.

Regarding the word *puraḥ*, which ends in the suffix *asi*: by the rule "A taddhita suffix that does not take all case-endings [is called an indeclinable]," it is an indeclinable; consequently, by the rule "An indeclinable [preceded by a preposition is] a gati," it receives the designation *gati*. Then, by the rule "A *gati* [is unaccented when followed by a verb] that is not separated [by another word]," the first member retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
Thus he, possessing such power, is celebrated with reverent words by those who proclaim his noble majesty among the people.
He becomes a desirable bull, a lovely bull; when Maghavan stirs the lowing of the milch-cows, he is a bull through his earthly might.

He alone is celebrated among the people by those who offer homage; proclaiming his own noble power among men, the Bull becomes the desired object of their longing. When the Maghavan impels the lowing cows with his strength, he becomes the Bull upon the earth. 4.

He, that very Indra, is praised with speech—meaning he is lauded by the ṛṣis who, desiring words, offer worship with reverence and hymns in the forest or the wilderness. Or rather, he desires for himself the word, which is praise. And that Indra, proclaiming his own power (*indriya*) among his people, conducts himself beautifully.
Furthermore, he is the bull (*vṛṣā*), the fulfiller of desires; he is the desirable one, the inspirer of the one who intends to sacrifice and wishes to bestow gifts.
The sense is that he generates a longing for the sacrifice among men who desire to offer it.
He is the bull, the showerer of oblations (*havir-varṣayitā*).
The meaning is "he has offered the oblation.

Maghavan means "possessing wealth. Such a sacrificer, endowed with *kṣema*—that is, protection provided by Indra—when he impels (*invati*) his speech (*dhenām*), characterized as praise, [then he attains his goal].
"In that case, he becomes willing"—this connects with what precedes.
Or alternatively:
Maghavan, the bull Indra, because he pervades (*invati*)—that is, extends through—the *dhenām*, the praise performed by the sacrificers—with a mind that effects stability (*kṣema*).
Therefore, the word "tasmāt" (therefore) should be supplied.

*namasyubhiḥ*: the suffix *kyac* is applied in the sense of worship according to the rule “*namo-varivasas-kardhyeṣu kṛñaḥ*” (*Pāṇini 3.1.19*), and the suffix *up* is added according to the rule “*kyāc chandasi*” (*Pāṇini 3.2.170*).
He desires speech; he wishes to speak.
The wise sages make him one who desires to speak; they cause him to wish to speak.
In the case of the root *vac*, when the suffix *ya* is added in the sense of the object (*karmaṇi*), there is the elision of the vowel *a* and the elision of the *y*.
Alternatively,
the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs through the addition of the suffix *vyat* to the root *vac*.
*Prabruvāṇaḥ*: from the root *brū*,
meaning “to speak clearly,” with the suffix *śānac* substituted for the present tense marker *laṭ*.
Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix.
Due to the doubling of the *śānac* suffix, there is an absence of *guṇa*, resulting in *uvaṅ*. By the rule regarding the accent of *ciṇ*, it is udātta on the final syllable.
*Indriya*.

*Indriya* is the mark (*liṅga*) of Indra. According to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.2.93—"The suffix *ghañ* is applied to the word *indra* in the senses of 'mark' (*liṅga*) and so forth, [yielding] *indriyam*, meaning 'Indra's mark,' 'seen by Indra,' 'created by Indra,' 'beloved by Indra,' or 'given by Indra'"—the suffix *ghañ* is prescribed after the word *indra* in these senses such as 'mark.'
Therefore, there is the acute accent on the final syllable.
[The root] *invati* [is used];
[the root] *ivi* means "to pervade."
Since the root *śap* is marked with *pittva*, it is unaccented; thus, the accent of the verbal root remains.
However, because of its connection with the particle *yat*, it does not undergo elision of the accent (*anighāta*).
1. Ḍha means "to hold. From this [root]:

He alone makes the great days and the battles easy for himself by his own power, through your strength, for the sake of the people. And then indeed they place their trust in the radiant one; for Indra, who repeatedly hurls the thunderbolt, he increases his vigor. 5. He alone makes the great days and the battles easy for himself by his own power, through your strength, for the sake of the people. And then indeed they place their trust in the radiant one; for Indra, who repeatedly hurls the thunderbolt, he increases his vigor. 5.

He, that very Indra, the warrior, with his purifying vigor and strength, performs— does he perform— for the sake of the people who offer praise, great deeds at the great encounters, that is, in great battles.
When Indra hurls down, again and again, his weapon— the thunderbolt that is the means for striking down— at the sacrifices,
then immediately thereafter all people place their *śraddhā* in the radiant and blazing Indra.
*Śrat* is a name for truth.
Everyone agrees that what is said—that Indra is powerful—is indeed true. Mahārṇava!

The meaning is "he has done. [Regarding] *kṛtrimā*: from the root *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of "making," the suffix *kti* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) by Pāṇini 3.3.88 (*dvitaḥ ktiḥ*). By Pāṇini 4.4.20 (*traimśrityam*), the suffix *ap* is added in the sense of "accomplished" (*nirvṛtta*). Since that suffix is marked with *p*, it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the suffix *kti* alone remains. The elision of the *śel* suffix is according to Pāṇini 6.1.70 (*śeṣchandasi bahulam*). [Regarding] *kṣamayā*: from the root *kṣampū* in the sense of "endurance" (*sahana*). It is called *kṣamā* because it endures the afflictions caused by living beings. The suffix *aṅ* is applied by Pāṇini 3.3.104 (*piñjidādibhyo'ṅ*). Then the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is added. There is a transposition (*vyatyaya*) resulting in the elision of the penultimate vowel of the root. The accent on the case-ending is Vedic. Alternatively, this root has the meaning "to overcome"; since "enduring" (*sahana*) has the sense of "overcoming" (*abhibhava*) as in the root *vaha*, the *uṇādi* suffix *manin* is applied to it. There is a transposition resulting in the feminine gender (*ṅīliṅatā*). Although the suffix *ṅīp* is prohibited by Pāṇini 4.1.11 (*manaḥ*), the suffix *ḍāp* is applied by Pāṇini 4.1.13 (*ḍābubhābhyāmanyatarasyām*). There is the elision of the *ṭi* portion. [The form is] *vṛdhānaḥ*.

*ketāḥ*: [This is derived from] the root *kit* with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of an object (*karman*). Due to the *jittva* (the presence of *j*), it is acute-accented on the first syllable (*ādyudātta*). *Dambhuvanti*: [From the root] *dambh* in the sense of "to deceive. Because it belongs to the *svādi* group, the suffix *śnu* is applied. Since that suffix has the marker *ṭ*, there is the elision of the nasal (*n*) by the rule *aniditām*. Because the preceding element is a *saṃyoga* (a conjunct consonant), the substitution of *yaṇ* [for *u*] does not occur by the rule *huśruvoḥ*; instead, the substitution of *uvaṅ* occurs by the rule *aci śnudhātu...*. *Bhūrnayaḥ*: [From the root] *bhṛ* in the sense of "supporting. In lists such as *ghṛṇiḥ pṛśniḥ*, a word ending in the suffix *nip* is derived from this root as a *nipātana* (irregular formation). There is the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* and lengthening. Alternatively, [it is derived] from *bhṛ* in the sense of "fear" (*bhaye*) with the suffix *kin* in the agentive sense (*kartari*) by the rule *kṛtlyuṭo bahulam*. By the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*, there is the substitution of *u* for *ṛ*. By the rule *hali ca*, there is lengthening. Because of the rule *ṛkāratvādibhyaḥ kinniṣṭhāvadbhyati* (Pāṇini 8.2.44, vārttika 1), which treats *kin* like the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*), there is the substitution of *n* for *ṇ*. Due to the *nittva* (the presence of *n* as an indicatory letter), it is acute-accented on the first syllable.
Thou carriest in thy hands wealth that is never exhausted; O Indra, renowned one, thou hast taken up the thunderbolt in thy body.
Like things enclosed by makers yet unenclosed, thy bodily forms, O Indra, are many according to the cosmic orders.

You bear inexhaustible wealth in your two hands; you, the famous one, have placed invincible power within your body. Like things both covered and uncovered by makers, O Indra, your many vital powers reside within your person.
O Indra, you bear in your hands—that is, you hold for the sake of giving to your worshippers—an inexhaustible (*aprakṣitam*) treasure (*vasu*).
Likewise, you, the renowned one, maintain in your own body (*tanvi*) an invincible (*apāḷaham*) power (*sahas*).
Your bodies are encompassed (*āvṛtāsaḥ*) by the deeds performed through strength, which consist of the slaying of Vṛtra and other demons by those who act as your agents.
All actions performed by the vital force remain enveloping this body;
in this regard, there is an illustration:
"Like the warp-threads."
*Avataḥ* is a name for a well. Just as wells are covered over by creatures who have entered them to draw water, so it is here.
Because this is so, O *Indra*, many *ṛtavaḥ*—that is, ritual acts—are performed within your bodies.
*Aprakṣita*:
the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) is formed from the root *kṣi* in the sense of "destruction" (*kṣaye*).
