these walls of the well are heating me, that is, they are thoroughly afflicting me on all sides.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"Like co-wives.
Those who have one common husband are co-wives; just as they cause distress to that single husband from all sides.
Or they afflict one another.

O Śatakratu, O Indra of manifold deeds or manifold wisdom, the mental agonies (*ādhyaḥ*)—produced by sacrifices, gifts, and other rites that have not been accomplished—devour and consume in various ways me, your praiser.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
4. Like four mice, 4. like rats—like genitals sewn by a weaver and smeared with the essence of food, they devour the threads.
Or rather, by the word *śiś* (genitals), the organ of generation itself is meant.
It exists in the tail by way of metaphorical designation;
the meaning is that, just as they throw their own tails into vessels of ghee, oil, and so forth, and then, having pulled them upward, they gnaw and lick them,
even so do the greedy ones devour me.
And this, O Indra, is not right for you toward your praiser;
therefore, lift me up from this well.
The rest is the same.
Regarding this, the Nirukta states: "These ribs, like co-wives, torment me on all sides from the side of the pit;
they gnaw at the sinews like rats at the threads of a seat.
Or perhaps it is the naming of one's own command."
"They pierce the phalli," so [it says] in Nirukta 4.6.
*sapatnīḥ*. According to Pāṇini’s rule 4.1.35, *nityaṃ sapatnyādiṣu*, the word *pati* undergoes the substitution of the nasalized form *na* [as *patnī*],
followed by the feminine suffix *ṅīp*.

In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), the long vowel of the same quality as the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam*) is applied according to the rule *vā chandasi*. [The root] *mṛṣ* [is used]; [the root] *suṣ* [is used] in the sense of stealing (*steye*).
The lengthening [of the vowel] is Vedic;
thus Yāska says: ‘*Mūṣaḥ* means *mūṣikāḥ* (mice);
and *mūṣikāḥ* [is derived] from the root *muṣ* (to steal), and *mūṣaḥ* is also from this very same [root]’ (Nirukta 4.5).
The root *śiṣ* (variant:

*ṣṇā*) is used in the sense of purification (*śauce*). The suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule: "The suffix *ka* is prescribed in the sense of the *ghañ* [suffix] for the roots *sthā*, *snā*, *pā*, *vyadh*, *han*, and *yudh*. Thus, [the word *śiśna* is formed].
The letter *śa* arises from the corruption of the color [of the phoneme] *sa*.

1. According to the rule “it should be stated that for roots beginning with *kṛ*, two [forms] occur before *ke*” (Kātyāyana-vārttika on Pāṇini 6.1.12.1), there is reduplication. 1. By the rule “frequently in the Veda” (*bahulaṃ chandasi*), the short *i* is substituted for the reduplicated syllable.
Those seven rays which are yonder—therein my kinship is extended.
Trita, the wise one, knows that; he, the singer, utters it for the sake of kinship. Heaven and Earth have witnessed this for me.
These seven rays—therein my navel is extended. Trita, the meditative one, knows that; he utters his cry for kinship. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me! 9.

1. Those standing at his side; 2. *kṣa*—they strike one another, and likewise *ṭha*—likewise; 3. *ca-dha-dha-mā*—me; 4. *kṣa-sa-lisāni*. Those seven rays of the sun which exist in the heavenly world—in them, existing internally in the form of the seven vital breaths (*prāṇas*), my navel is stretched out, that is, connected.
The seer points to himself in the third person.

"Trita," the one who has overcome ignorance through the sacred bathing-place (tīrtha), "the son of the waters," the seer (ṛṣi), "knows"—that is, he understands—"that aforementioned event; no other [does].
Although he knows it, "he utters praise" (*rebhati*) to those rays of light as they move toward the well (*kūpa*), calling out to them.
The rest is the same.
*Ātātā*.
This is derived from the root *tan* (to extend) with the suffix *ni* in the sense of the object (*karman*).
By the rule beginning with "anudāttopadeśa," there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*).

In the phrase "gatiranantaraḥ," the word *gati* (a verbal prefix) retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). Regarding *jāmi*: it is a term for the act of going (*gamana-karman*), as it means "that which goes" (*jamati*).
*Jāmi* means that which goes;
the suffix *iṇ* is added according to the *uṇādi* rules.
Its state is *tattva*.
*rebhati*. The root *rebh*, meaning "to sound," belongs to the *bhūvādi* class.
These five eyes which stand in the midst of the great heaven—worthy of being proclaimed among the gods—they have turned toward one another; hear this from me, O Heaven and Earth!
These, those five bulls who stood in the midst of the great heaven—now, toward the gods, they have turned together to that which is to be proclaimed. Mark this for me, O Heaven and Earth! 10.
"Oxen" means those who sprinkle, who rain down desires. "Five."
The five deities are those set forth by the half-verse: "And may Indra, his quality, his back, his purpose, and the knower of the truth grant us delight" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.107.3).
Alternatively, they are the five numbered as fire, wind, sun, moon, and lightning.
And so says the Śāṭyāyanaka: "These indeed are the five lights which shine in the worlds:
fire on earth, wind in the intermediate space, the sun in heaven, the moon in the stars, and lightning in the waters. "In the stars" means in the world of the stars.
"In the waters" means in the waters contained within the clouds.

This is likewise recorded in the Taittirīya: "Agni is in the earth, Vāyu in the intermediate space, Sūrya in heaven, Candramas in the quarters, and the stars in their own world" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 1.20.1).

"Those five gods who stand—remain—sit—in the midst of the great, vast heaven (*maho divaḥ*), they, moving together toward me simultaneously, come quickly to my praiseworthy and fitting hymn of praise among the gods (*devatrā*); those gods accept my service.
Thereafter, being satisfied, they turn back (*ni vavṛtuḥ*). The rest is the same."
*ukṣaṇaḥ*: by the rule "vā pappūrvasya nigame," there is an absence of lengthening of the penultimate vowel. *devatrā*.

In the phrase "devamanuṣya" and so forth, the suffix *tra* is used in the sense of the locative case. [The word] *pravācya* is derived from the root *vac* by means of the suffix *yat*, according to the rule *aco yat*.
There is the elision of the suffix *ṇi* by the rule "ṇeraniṭi.

When the acute accent on the first syllable is applied by the rule "yato'nāvaḥ," the original accentuation of the final member of the compound (*kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*) prevails. [Thus we have] *sandhrīcīnāḥ*.
Those who go together are *sadhryañcaḥ*; they themselves are *sandhrīcīnāḥ*.
[The form] *sadhryañcaḥ* is derived from the root *añc-* preceded by the prefix *saha-*, with the suffix *kvip* according to the rule beginning with "ṛtvig-" and so forth.
The elision of the *n* is by the rule "aniditām" (Pāṇini 6.4.24).
The substitution of "sadhi" for "saha" is by the rule "sahasya sadhiḥ" (Pāṇini 6.3.95).
The suffix "vap" is added in the sense of the word itself (svārthe) by the rule "vibhāṣāpteradikṣiprām" (Pāṇini 5.2.18).

*vavṛtuḥ* [is derived from] *vṛt* in the sense of "turning. Since the rule "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*" (in Vedic usage, the *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* suffixes may be used for all tenses) applies, the *liṭ* suffix is employed here to denote the present tense.
The *parasmaipada* ending occurs by way of transposition;
the lengthening of the reduplicated syllable in the *saṃhitā* follows from the rule "it is also seen in other cases."
These well-winged ones sit in the midst of the ascent of heaven;
they ward off the wide wolf as he crosses the flowing waters. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
These well-winged ones sit in the midst of the ascent of heaven; they drive away the wolf as he crosses the flowing waters. Mark this for me, O Heaven and Earth! 11.
1. *kṣa*—he cognizes;
2. *kṣa-na-sa*—and it does not exist;
3. *kṣa-ṭha-sa*—those who accept [it].
Suparṇas:
this is a name for the rays;
they have beautiful flight.
These are the rays of the sun;
they abide and move in the expanse of the sky and the intermediate region, which is the ascent of all that obstructs.
Those rays of the sun drive away, restrain, and ward off the wolf from the path—that is, from the way leading to the forest-dwelling place.
Of what sort?
Crossing over, that is, traversing, the many— that is, the great— waters.
Before Trita fell into the well, a certain large wild beast dwelling in the forest arrived, desiring to cross the great river and intending to devour him.
However, upon seeing the rays of the sun, it turned back, thinking, "This is not the right moment.
Therefore, it is said that the rays ward off the wolf.
According to Yāska’s view, however, *āpaḥ* is a name for the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*).
On the banks of the *yahvatī*, the rays of the sun restrain the wolf—the moon—as it crosses the great intermediate space by way of the twelvefold path, that is, by its own course.
For during the day, the moon, being obstructed by the rays of the sun, is seen to be devoid of luster.
Therefore, the meaning is that they render it lusterless. Regarding "ārodhane":
it is called *ārodhana* because by means of it one ascends (*āruhyate*) or is drawn up (*ābhriyate*).
The suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*).
They drive away (*sedhanti*);
[the root] *pidhu* means "to go."
This [suffix] should also be understood as having the sense of *ni-pūrva* (preceded by *ni*). For example:
*pathaḥ*. In the singular ablative case, there is the elision of the *ṭi* [portion] according to the rule "abhasya ṭerlopaḥ."
The accentuation of the case-ending is due to the *udāttanivṛtti-svara* (the accent resulting from the removal of the acute accent).
According to the view of Yāska, however, the ablative (*pañcamī*) is used by way of substitution for the instrumental sense (*tṛtīyārthe*). [The word is] *yahvatīḥ*.
The word *iti* is a name for "greatness.
From this [root], the suffix *kvip* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.2.178 (*sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ*) for the sense of habitual action (*ācārārtha*).
Thereafter, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied in place of the present tense marker (*laṭ*).
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "ugitaśca.
Due to the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the rules governing augments (*āgama*), there is an absence of the *num* augment.
Consequently, the designation "nadī" (feminine noun) does not apply here by the rule "śatrunumaḥ," as it would otherwise do through transference (*vyatyaya*).

O Gods, that which is new, worthy of praise, beneficial, and excellent to proclaim—[that] the rivers flow according to the *ṛta*, and Sūrya has spread out the truth. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me! 12. New. That. Worthy of praise. Beneficial. O Gods. Excellent to proclaim. The *ṛta*. They flow. The rivers. Truth. He has spread. Sūrya. Take note. Of this. For me. O Heaven and Earth. 12.
O gods, that divine power of yours— newer than the new, praiseworthy, worthy of hymns, laudable, and easy for the officiating priests to proclaim— is thus placed within you as a beneficial force.
Therefore, by your power, the rivers—those streams whose nature is to flow—send forth the *ṛta*, the water;
that is to say, they flow truly and without ceasing.
Likewise, the Sun spreads out, extends, his own light which is ever-present as truth.
The rest is the same.

*Supravācanam*. From the root *vac* in the sense of "speaking," with the causative suffix (*ṇic*), the suffix *yuc* is applied in the sense of the abstract noun (*bhāve*) according to the rule "it is seen after other roots as well."
They offer.
By the rule "sip is frequently used for leṭ," the suffix *sip* is applied;
there is *guṇa* substitution.
He stretched it out; according to the rule "it is also seen in other cases," there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable in the *saṃhitā* [text].

O Agni, that which is worthy of praise and kinship among the gods is yours. As such, being well-impelled like a man, worship the gods for us, you who are most wise. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this from me. O Agni, that which is worthy of praise and kinship among the gods is yours. As such, being well-impelled like a man, worship the gods for us, you who are most wise. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this from me.
1. These [rays] belong to you. 2. By means of that which consists of twelve parts, and by means of that which consists of twelve rays;
O Agni, yours is the praiseworthy, celebrated, and attainable power.
A *āpi* is a kinsman; the state of being such is *bāndhava*. This kinship exists—that is, it is found—among the gods, Indra and others who are endowed with qualities such as generosity.

Therefore, O most wise one (*viduṣṭara*), being seated (*satta*) at our sacrifice, worship (*yakṣi*) those gods, Indra and the others, according to the rule of the scriptures with oblations; honor them.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
"like a man" (*manuṣvat*).
Just as it is in the sacrifice of the Manus, so it is here;
the rest is as before.
Āpya. From the root *ā-plu* in the sense of "pervasion," the suffix *i* is applied according to the rule *aca iḥ* after this causative (*ṣyan*) form.
The suffix *vyañ* is applied because [the word] belongs to the *brāhmaṇa*-class and so forth.
[Thus we have] *sattaḥ*. By the rule "nasatta-niṣattam" (Pāṇini 8.2.61), there is no substitution of the nasal (*ṇatva*) for the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix.
The elision of the syllable *ni* should be understood as a Vedic (chāndasa) phenomenon. [In the word] *manuṣya*,
the suffix *us* is applied to the root *man* according to the rules of the Uṇādi class.

In this case, the suffix *vati* is used in the sense of the ablative case according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.1.116 (*tatra tasyeva*). According to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.4.18.3 (*nabho'astromanuṣāṃ vyupasaṃkhyānam*), because it is a state (*bhāva*), there is an absence of *pada*-status; consequently, there is an absence of the substitution of *ra* and so forth. [Thus,] *yakṣi*.

By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is the elision (luk) of the suffix śap; by the rules for the substitution of *vaś* and so forth, there is the substitution of *kutva* and *patva*. Thus: *viduṣṭaraḥ*.

From the word *vidvas*, with the suffix *tarap* added, the status of being a *bha*-stem applies by virtue of the rule *ayasmayādīni chandasi*. Consequently, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *vamoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*. Furthermore, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs according to the rule *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*.

Seated as the Hotṛ priest among men, Agni, the most wise one, goes toward the gods; the god, the sage among the gods, prepares the oblations. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me. 14. Seated: as the Hotṛ. Among men: from among men. Toward the gods: approaching the gods. The most wise one: the most knowing. Agni: the fire-god. Prepares the oblations: makes the offerings ready. The god: the divine one. Among the gods: in the midst of the deities. The sage: the wise one. Take note of this: acknowledge this. For me: on my behalf. O Heaven and Earth: the two worlds. 14.

Seated at our sacrifice like Manu, the Hotṛ—the invoker of the gods, the most wise, the god endowed with the qualities of generosity and other virtues, and the most intelligent among all the gods such as Indra—may Agni, being thus, bring those gods toward us and properly present our offerings according to the rule of the scriptures; the particle *ā* here denotes a limit, meaning "in accordance with the scriptural injunction. May he impel them [to partake].
The rest is the same.
*suṣūdati*. [The root] *ṣūd* means "to flow.
The augment *aṭ* is applied in the *leṭ* tense.
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," the suffix *śap* is replaced by *śru*, resulting in *medhiraḥ*.

The possessive suffix *iran* is added in the sense of possession according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.2.109.3: "The suffixes *in* and *irañ* should be stated after the words *medhā* and *aryā*. Thus, [the form] is derived.

Brahmā and Varuṇa perform [this act]; we implore him who knows the way. He unfolds the thought within the heart; may the manly one be born. O Heaven and Earth, know this truth of mine. 15. Brahmā. Performs. Varuṇa. Him, the knower of the way. Him. We implore. Apart. Unfolds. With the heart. The thought. Manly. May he be born. Truth. Know. Mine. Of this. O Heaven and Earth. 15.

We pray to that Varuṇa, the god who is the warder-off of what is undesirable, who performs the act of protecting—that is, the work consisting of the preservation of sacred prayer (*brahman*)—who is the finder of the path (*gātuvid*), the one who causes us to attain the way that wards off suffering; we entreat such a Varuṇa for our desired fruit.
1. *ksa-sa-syat* is well-known in the Vedic scriptures (*śruti*).
2. The substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs according to the rule *ta-śa-sa-śca*.

3. Of those who are not protected from *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *aniṣṭa*; 4. Of one who protects against suffering through *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *sa*, and who does not ward off suffering through *na*.

*Īmahe* is a term for the act of sacrificing. To that Varuṇa, this our singer, with his *hṛdā*—that is, with his heart (*hṛdayena*)—unfolds, reveals, and makes manifest the *mati*, meaning the praise worthy of reflection; that is to say, he utters it. May this Varuṇa, who is to be praised as ever new, cause our *ṛta* (truth/ritual order) to be born; may he become ever new for us. *Brahma*: The lengthening [of the vowel] is according to the rule *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (Pāṇini 6.3.137), which applies to the *saṃhitā*. *Gātuvidam*: From the root *vid* in the sense of "obtaining" (*lābhe*). The suffix *kvip* is applied with the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) implied. *Īmahe*: From the root *īṅ* in the sense of "going. The elision of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*) occurs by the rule *bahulam chandasi* (Pāṇini 2.4.73). *Hadā*: By the rule beginning with *paṭhana* (Vārttika on Pāṇini 6.1.63), the word *hṛdaya* is replaced by *hadā*. 22. Translation complete.
That path which belongs to the Sun in heaven has been made manifest; O gods, he cannot be overstepped. O mortals, you do not see it; O Heaven and Earth, bear witness to this for me!
That path which the Āditya has made in heaven to be proclaimed—that, O gods, one cannot overstep; you mortals do not see it. Mark this for me, O Heaven and Earth! 16.
The path: that which leads to the eternal.
Or rather, it is the path for the practitioners who go to the world of Brahman (*brahmaloka*).

According to the Śruti: "They go, free from passion, through the gate of the sun" (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.2.11). Such is this Āditya, who has been made—that is, fashioned—in the sky, the world of heaven, in a manner that is worthy of proclamation, meaning he exists in such a way that he is visible to all living beings.

O gods, this very Āditya cannot be transgressed even by you; it is impossible for you to overstep him, because your own life depends upon him. For it is when the sun exists that the seasons, beginning with spring, are produced.
Sacrifices are performed at the proper times,
and your livelihood depends upon those sacrifices;
therefore, this [observance] must not be transgressed by you either.

And thus, O mortals—O evil-doing men—you do not see that sun of great majesty; you do not know the sun. This is a reproach directed at Ekata and Dvita for having thrown [him] into the well and departed:
"I alone am the seer of the mantra; I know that sun, whereas you two, O evildoers, do not know it."
*Panthāḥ*. [Derived from] the root *pat* in the sense of "going. By the rule *patestha ca*, the suffix *ini* is applied.

In the form *pathimathyṛbhukṣām*, there is the substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel]; in *pathi* [and others], by the rule *inotsarvanāmasthāne* (Pāṇini 7.1.86), the substitution of *at* occurs for the vowel *i*;
and by the rule *tho nyaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.87).
The initial acute accent [of *pathin*] is due to the rule "pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne. *Pravācyam*:
from the root *vac* with the causative suffix (*ṇic*), the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of the abstract action (bhāva) by the rule "aco yat."
The word *anāvaḥ* has its initial syllable udātta (accented) because of the rule beginning with "yato 'nāvaḥ. Regarding the root *kram*: it means "to step" (*pādavikṣepe*).
In the expression *kṛthārthe tavaikena*, the suffix *ken* is applied; because it is marked with the *ni*-indicator, it bears the acute accent on its first syllable.
Trita, cast down into the well, called upon the gods for help;
Bṛhaspati heard that, making wide room from afar, and [said]: "May this wealth of his be mine, O Heaven and Earth."
Trita, cast down into the well, calls upon the gods for help. Bṛhaspati heard that, while making wide space from the narrowness. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me! 17.
1. kṣa-vartate | 2. ḍha-atikrame yuṣmābhiḥ | 3. kṣa-ṭa-ṭhana-sa-yūyam |
The seer named Trita, who was cast down and placed in a well, calls upon the gods with hymns for their protection—that is, he invokes them.
Bṛhaspati, the god known as Gṛtsa, the protector of the great gods, heard that call of Trita; having heard it, what did he do?
Having rescued [us] from this narrow distress, from this pit-fall of the nature of sin, he makes for us a wide and beautiful expanse.

*havate*: from the root *hve* (to call), in the present tense (*laṭ*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule "there is much [irregularity] in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*); then the substitution of *śap*, guṇa, and the ā-deśa [apply].
For protection (*ūtaye*). By the rule "uti-yūti" etc., the suffix *ktin* is acute-accented.
Bṛhaspati.
The elision of the *su* suffix occurs because the term is listed among the *pāraskara*-type words in Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.1.157 (*tadbṛhatoḥ karapayoḥ*).
Furthermore, by the rule "both [members] in *vanaspati*-type compounds," both the preceding and following members simultaneously retain their original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
[This is from the word] *aṃhūraṇāt*.
The root *ahi* means "to go.
Because it is marked with the *it*-sign (*idit*), the augment *num* is added.
According to the rule *kharjipiñvādivya urolacau* (Uṇādisūtra 4.530), the suffix *ura* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).

Because it has the state of being the cause for the non-occurrence of suffering, the suffix *na*—characterized by the rule *pāmādi* (Pāṇini 5.2.100)—is used here in the sense of possession (*matvarthīya*), meaning "that which possesses this [state].
Alternatively, both forms are derived from the root *han* preceded by the prefix *ā*.

For Aruṇa, the one who shines forth, has indeed seen me once as I was traveling on my path; having perceived it, he rises up, and then he ascends the ridge of the mountain. This wealth of his, the gift of Rudra, has been found by me.

The ruddy one—has not the wolf once beheld him as he went along his path? Having perceived him, she indeed slinks away like one who has been struck on her back. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me! 18.
A reddish-brown, crimson-colored wolf, a wild dog, indeed once—on one occasion—saw me as I was going along the path;
for "hi" is used here as a verse-filler.
And having observed me, desiring to seize me, it sprang up.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
it is like a carpenter who, having suffered pain in his back from the act of carving, turns upward in order to alleviate that pain. It is just like that.
"O Heaven and Earth, know this sorrow of mine.
Alternatively,
"vṛka" refers to the moon, which has its light fully revealed.
Aruṇa, shining and illuminating the entire world, the maker of months— producing specific divisions of time such as the year by means of the month and half-month—
he, the Moon, because the knowledge of the division of lunar days depends upon the movement of the Moon,
beheld the host of constellations moving along the path of the sky.
The particle *hi* is used here for emphasis.
By saying "he saw only the cluster of stars and not me fallen into the well," his disregard is highlighted;
[the implication being] that had he seen me, he would have rescued me from the well.
Having observed the host of stars and seen them, it rises;
it rises together with whichever constellation it is joined to.
The meaning is that it does not approach me.
The rest is as before.
Regarding this, Yāska considers *māsakṛt* to be a single word, whereas Śākalya considers it two words. In that latter view, the meaning is as follows:
he repeatedly beheld his own wives, the stars beginning with Aśvinī, who had become the daughters of Dakṣa Prajāpati.
"He looks at me only once; having looked once, he leaps up.
He goes upwards together with the stars.
He does not pull me out of the well."
Therefore, this is improper:
O Heaven and Earth, you two must know this account of mine.

Regarding this, the Nirukta states: "The wolf (*vṛka*) is the moon, because its light is spread out (*vivṛta-jyotiṣka*), or its light is transformed (*vikṛta-jyotiṣka*), or its light is powerful (*vikrānta-jyotiṣka*). Aruṇa is the illuminator; he is the maker of months, for the moon is the maker of both months and half-months.

Just as it sees the host of stars as they move, it overtakes them, having observed each one with which it is about to be joined. And the moon is a carpenter and one afflicted with back disease" (Nirukta 5.20–21).
*Sakṛt*:
This is derived as an indeclinable (*nipātita*) used for counting the repetition of an action, according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 5.4.19: *ekasya sakṛcca*.
*Vṛkaḥ*.

1. *Vṛñ*: [The root] designated as *kṣa-sa*. 2. *Kṣa-duḥkhāprasi-hetubhūtā*: That which has become the cause for the non-manifestation of suffering. 3. *Kṣa-sa-aruṇaḥ*: Aruṇa; reddish in color. 4. *Kṣa-sma*: "Not existing. 5. *Kṣa-ṭha-ṭha- 'he... jānītam'*: "O... know! does not exist. 6. *Kṣa-sa-pathā*: By way of the path, i.e., through the path of the sky (*ākāśamārgeṇa*). 7. *Kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-tadbhāryāḥ*: His wives. 8. *Kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-punaḥpaśyamānāḥ sakṛdeva paśyati*: While looking again and again, he sees it only once. 9. *Kṣa-sa-ārocamānaḥ*: Shining brightly. Ka. 82

In *varaṇe* [the suffix] *kam* is applied by the rule *sūtrabhūṣisūpimubhyaḥ kin* (Uṇādi Sūtra 3.321). *Jihīte*: from the root *ohāṅ* in the sense of "going," belonging to the *juhotyādi* class; the change of the reduplicated syllable to *i* occurs by the rule *bhṛjāmit*. *Nicātya*: from the root *cāy* in the senses of "worship" and "listening"; here, because roots have a single meaning, it means "seeing. By the rule *samāse'napūrve kvo lyap*, the suffix *lyap* is substituted for *kva*. *Pṛṣṭāmayī*: from the root *spṛś* in the sense of "touching"; that by which one is touched is *spṛṣṭiḥ*. The elision of the vowel is Vedic (*chāndasa*). *Pṛṣṭāmayas* becomes *pṛṣṭāmayaḥ*; that which possesses this is *pṛṣṭāmayī*.

Through this hymn of praise, may we, accompanied by Indra and with all our heroes, prevail in the assembly. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that. 19. Through this hymn of praise—may we, accompanied by Indra, prevail in the assembly with all our heroes. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that. 19.

By means of this *āṅgūṣa*—that is, by means of this hymn worthy of proclamation, acting as the cause—we, accompanied by Indra—the Lord who bestows grace—and possessed of all heroes, that is, endowed with all sons, grandsons, and so forth, may we overcome our enemies in the *vṛjana*, in battle.
May Mitra and the other gods honor—that is, protect—this very speech of ours. The word *uta* is used for the purpose of including the deities.
Regarding this, Yāska says: "Āṅgūṣa means praise, a hymn, a proclamation.
By means of this hymn, may we be possessed of Indra" (Nirukta 5.11).
[The word is] *enā*.
By the rule *dvitīyāṭaussvenaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.34), the form *idam* is replaced by *enā* in the third case (*tṛtīyā*).
By the rule *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39), there is the substitution of *ā* for the case-ending. Due to the accent of the *cit* suffix, it has an udātta accent on the final syllable.
By means of *āṅgūṣa*. [The word is derived] from the root *ghuṣ* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of the object (*karman*).
The absence of the elision of the letter *ḍ* after *āṅ* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
The substitution of *gṛ* for the sound *ghoṣa* occurs because it belongs to the class beginning with *pṛṣodara*.
By the rule *tāthādi*, the final syllable of the compound is udātta.
[May we] be.
In the optative (*liṅ*) of the root *ās* used in the sense of a request, there is the elision of the vowel *a* according to the rule *bha-sor-alopaḥ*.
Then, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs according to the rule *upasargād āṭa-dhātryo 'sti-y-ac-paraḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.87).
In the fifteenth section, there are ten hymns.
Among them, the first hymn, consisting of seven verses, begins with "indram."
Here the sequence is stated: "Indra, Mitra, and Varuṇa, ending in Triṣṭubh. Since [the previous seer] continues by implication, Kutsa is the seer;
however, because Trita is not specifically distinguished there, he is merely an alternative for that same [seer] and does not continue.
One verse is a *triṣṭubh*;
the remaining verses are *jagatīs* according to the technical rule regarding those ending in *triṣṭubh*.
It has been stated that the deity is the Viśvedevas.
The application [of the mantra] is indicated by its internal mark (*laiṅgika*).

We invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, the host of Maruts, and Aditi for our protection. Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are bounteous givers, deliver us completely from all distress. Indram | Mitram | Varuṇam | Agnim | ūtaye | Mārutam | Śardhaḥ | Aditim | havāmahe | Ratham | na | durgāt | Vasavaḥ | sudānavaḥ | Viśvasmāt | naḥ | aṃhasaḥ | niḥ | pipartana || 1 ||
For protection (*ūtaye*) and preservation (*rakṣaṇāya*), we invoke (*havāmahe*) Indra and the rest, as well as the Marut host (*mārutam śardhaḥ*), that is, the assembly of Maruts and their power.

The Vasus—the dwellers (*nivāsayitāraḥ*)—Indra and the others, who are givers of good gifts (*sudānavaḥ*), [deliver us] from all (*viśvasmāt*) distress (*aṃhasaḥ*), that is, from sin. 1. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha*: "niśāmanam" means seeing (*darśanam*).
2. *kṣa*: elision of the letter *s*.
3. Kṣa-ṭa-ṭha: The word "uta" does not exist [in this context] as a conjunction of deities;
4. because of the continued application (anuvartana) of kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-sa;
5. kṣa: we call [it].

6. *kṣa-he vasavaḥ* (O Vasus, come hither!). 7. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-he-sudānavaḥ* (O bounteous givers, come hither!). *naḥ* means "us"; *niṣpipartana* means "deliver us" or "protect us. Here is the illustration: *rathaṃ na durgāt*—just as charioteers protect a chariot from a difficult place, a place that is hard to traverse and prone to destruction, so [should you protect us]. Regarding *pipartana*: some say the root is *pṛ*. By the rule *loṭī tasanasanathanāśca*, the suffix *tana* is substituted for *ta*. Because the suffix is not marked with *ṅ*, there is *guṇa* strengthening. By the rule *artipiparyośca*, the vowel of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) becomes *i*.
O Ādityas, come for our complete well-being; O gods, be bringers of prosperity in the battles against Vṛtra.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are liberal givers, deliver us from all distress.

O Ādityas, come hither for our complete well-being; O gods, be our benefactors in the battles against Vṛtra. Like a chariot from a difficult path, O Vasus, you who are bounteous givers, deliver us from every distress. 2.

O Ādityas, sons of Aditi, you gods—come hither! Come to provide assistance for us in battle, for the sake of *sarvatāti*, that is, for the expansion [of our power] through all heroic men; the meaning is: come to grant us aid in the fight.
Moreover, in the battles against Vṛtra—
this is a name for combat—
be bringers of well-being (*śambhavaḥ*), that is, be those who cause happiness to arise in the midst of conflicts.
The suffix *śap* is elided by the rule "gameloṭi bahulaṃ chandasi."
May the Pitṛs, worthy of high praise, and the two goddesses, mothers of the gods and increasers of cosmic order, protect us.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O bounteous Vasus, deliver us from every distress.

May our fathers, who are worthy of praise, and the two goddesses, the mothers of the gods, who increase the cosmic order (ṛta), rescue us from every distress, just as the bounteous Vasus rescue a chariot from a difficult path. 3.
May our fathers, beginning with Abhiprātārin, protect us—that is, guard us.
Of what kind are they?
They are "supravācanāḥ," meaning they can be easily praised or extolled.

Moreover, O Son of the Gods, since all the gods are as sons to you, may those two who increase the *ṛta*—that is, truth or sacrifice—the divine Dyāvāpṛthivī (Heaven and Earth) endowed with qualities such as divinity, protect us;
the rest is the same.
The word *devī* [is formed] with the long vowel of the same quality as the preceding sound (*pūrvasavarṇadīrghatva*) according to the rule *vā chandasi*. [The term is] *ṛtāvṛdhā*.
The suffix *kvip* is applied to the root *vṛdh*, with the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it;
the vowel *ā* [in the form *vṛdhā*] results from the substitution of the case-ending according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
We implore Narāśaṃsa, the prize-winner, with offerings, and Pūṣan, the ruler of heroes, with blessings.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you bounteous givers, deliver us from all distress.

We implore Narāśaṃsa, the vigorous one, who seeks the prize, and Pūṣan, the lord of heroes, with our prayers for blessings here. O bounteous Vasus, deliver us from distress, as one delivers a chariot from a difficult path, and rescue us from every misfortune. 4.

1. In the manuscripts *kṣa*, *ṭa*, and *ṭha*, the word "devāḥ" is absent. 2. *kṣa*: "bhavata. The rest has been explained elsewhere. 3. In *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *sa*, after the rule "luk," there is the additional note: "By the rule beginning with *anudāttapadeśa*, there is the elision of the nasal [of the root]. [The form is] *bhūta*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the elision of the suffix *śap*. 4. *kṣa*: "Endowed with qualities such as giving (*dāna*). 5. *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*: "Protect! The remainder [of the commentary] is: "I praise here, at this time, *narāśaṃsam*—worthy of being praised by men—and *vājinam*, the possessor of horses, while *vājayan*, i.e., inciting, or rather, inflaming [him]."

Likewise, with well-performed hymns that serve as the means, we entreat—that is, we pray for our desired object—the god Pūṣan, the nourisher, who is "kṣayadvīra," exceedingly powerful, and in whom all heroes find their fulfillment.
[We praise] Narāśaṃsa.
According to the rule "ubhe vanaspatyādipu," there is the simultaneous preservation of the original accents of both members of the compound.
The word *nara-* ends in the suffix *-ap* according to the rule *ṛdorap*, and is udātta on its first syllable;
the lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by way of a nipātana (irregular derivation).
The word *śam-* ends in the suffix *-ghañ* and is udātta on its first syllable.
*vājayan*: from the root *vraj* (in the sense of "to go") with the suffix *ṇic*.
*Kṣayadvīram*:
[derived from] the root *kṣi* in the sense of "perishing" (*kṣaye*), with the suffix *śatṛ* applied to the present tense (*laṭ*).

When the suffix *śap* is to be applied, there is a substitution by transposition (*vyatyaya*) for *ś*. Because of the rule "in Vedic usage, both ways," this [suffix] is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka*, and thus lacks the *ṅit* designation; consequently, *guṇa* and the replacement by *āy* occur.
Since it is taught with an *a*-vowel (*adupadeśa*), the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are unaccented, and the accent falls on the *vikaraṇa*.

By the rule "ato guṇe," there is substitution of the single substitute form (pararūpa); then, by the rule "ekādeśa udāttena," this single substitute becomes udātta. [The word] *kṣayantavīraḥ* means "in which heroes dwell. In this bahuvrīhi compound, the original accent of the first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛtisvaratva*) applies.
O Bṛhaspati, make this path easy for us today; we pray for that health and well-being which Manu ordained for you.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you who are liberal givers, deliver us from all distress.

O Bṛhaspati, always make for us a path that is easy to traverse; we implore you for that which is beneficial and brings peace and prosperity, as ordained by Manu. Like a chariot from a difficult road, O Vasus, you who are bounteous givers, deliver us from every distress. 5.

O Bṛhaspati, always (*sadamit*) grant us (*naḥ*) easy passage— this is a name for happiness— and make it well-being. Moreover, that which belongs to you (*te*), the pacification (*śam*) of diseases that require calming, and the warding off (*yoḥ*) of fears that must be separated from us, is beneficial to Manu— that is, established by Manu, the Brahman.
Or rather:
we pray for— that is, we request— that which is such a pacification and protection as is favorable to human beings.
*Sugama* means that which is easily understood (*suṣṭhu gamyate 'smin*). It is formed by adding the suffix *ḍa* to the root *gam* according to the rule *suduror adhikaraṇe*.

The two words *śam* and *yoḥ* have been explained by Yāska in this way: “the allaying of diseases and the warding off of fears” (Nirukta 4.21). *Manuhitam*: the suffix *usi* is added to the root *man* according to the Uṇādi rules.
By the rule "the third case retains its original accent when used as the first member of a compound," the first member retains its natural accent.
Kutsa, the seer, has invoked Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of power, for protection from distress.
O Vasus, bounteous givers, rescue us from all affliction, as one rescues a chariot from a difficult pass.

Kutsa, the seer, called upon Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of power, when he was held down in the pit for help. O bounteous Vasus, rescue us from every distress, as one rescues a chariot from a difficult path. || 6 ||

*Kāṭeḥ* is the name of a well. Into that well *nibaॉḻahaḥ*, meaning "cast down," the seer *Kutsa* called upon *Indra* for protection (*ūtaye*). How [did he call]? As the slayer of Vṛtras (*vṛtrahaṇam*), the destroyer of enemies; as the Lord of Might (*śacīpatim*). *Śacī* is a name for action; thus, it means the protector of all actions. Or else, the husband of the goddess Śacī. In the compound *śacīpatiḥ*, both members retain their original accent because the word is listed among those beginning with *vanaspati*. The word *śacī*, ending in the feminine suffix *kīn*, is udātta on its first syllable according to the *śāṅgarava*-class. Regarding *nibaॉḻahaḥ*: the root *bāh* means "exertion. 3. *nipātitaḥ* (emended from *nipātitaḥ*) 4. *āhvayati* (emended from *ahūta āhvayati*) 5. *sma* (emended from *sma*) 6. *śacyā* (emended from *śacyā*) 7. *devyāḥ* (emended from *devyāḥ*) 8. *bāha* (emended from *bāha*) 9. *prayatne* (emended from *prayatne*)
1. *sa-kṣiyanti* (they dwell). 2. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha*—from the root *kṣi* (to perish/dwell). 3. *kṣa-sa*—struck down. 4. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha*—he challenged. 5. *kṣa-sa*—of the goddess Śacī.
Due to the influence of the prefix *ni*, it functions in the sense of "falling.
In the form *nihāya*, there is an absence of the augment *iṭ* according to the rule "the teaching regarding augments is not absolute" (*anityamāgamaśāsanam*).

[The forms] *kṣubdha*, *svānta*, and so forth; or alternatively, in rules such as *kṣubdhasvānta* (Pāṇini 7.2.18), the absence of the augment *iṭ* is prescribed by way of irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in the sense of "intense" (*bhṛśa*).
And here, the word *bāḍham* functions by implication in the sense of a very intense falling. By the rule *gatiranantaraḥ*, the preceding verb retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*).
[The form] *ahnat*.
By the rule *lipisicihśca* (Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.53), there is the substitution of *aṅ* for *cli* in the *luṅ* tense;
by the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *ā*.
May the divine Aditi protect us; may the protector among the gods save us, never failing.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that favor.
May the goddess Aditi protect us; may the god, the savior, protect us without ceasing. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that. 7.

May Aditi—the divine mother of the gods, endowed with virtues such as generosity, indivisible (aditi) or undepressed—protect us thoroughly (ni pātu) together with her own sons, the gods who are likewise endowed with virtues such as generosity.
May the radiant god Savitṛ, the protector and guardian of all, protect us (trāyatām), remaining vigilant and watchful in guarding us.
May Mitra and the other five deities honor (mamahantām) that which we have prayed for by means of this hymn.
"May he protect.
The root *trai* (in the sense of "protecting") belongs to the Bhūvādigaṇa.
*Aprayucchan*. [The root] *yuccha* means "to be negligent. From this, the suffix *śatṛ* is applied to the present tense (*laṭ*).
In a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), the initial member that is an indeclinable (*avyaya*) retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*).
The second hymn, consisting of three verses beginning with "yajño devānām," is the seer Kutsa's composition; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and is addressed to the Viśvedevas.
This is indicated by the Anukramaṇī entry: "yajñaṣṭum.
Its application is determined by its internal characteristics (liṅga).
The sacrifice approaches the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious.
May your benevolence turn hitherward toward us—that which is the best finder of wide space even from distress.
The sacrifice goes toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious. May your benevolence turn hitherward, for it is the best finder of wide space even from distress. ||1||
Our sacrifice attains the favor—the happiness—of the gods, Indra and the others.
Moreover, O Ādityas, may you be gracious toward us, bringing us comfort.
Likewise, may your auspicious thought—that benevolent mind intent upon favor—turn hither, directed toward us.
May that wisdom, which bestows ample wealth (*varivas*) even upon a man who has fallen into distress or poverty—
*varivas* being a name for wealth—
be ours. It is the one that causes the attainment of wealth in the highest degree.
The meaning is: "May this very wisdom continue to protect us."
"Be [there].

According to the rule "an initial vocative is treated as non-existent," since the vocative *ādityāsaḥ* occurring at the beginning of the quarter-verse (*pāda*) is treated as non-existent, this [subsequent vocative] stands at the beginning of the quarter-verse; therefore, because of the condition "not at the beginning of a quarter-verse," [the rule does not apply]. (Note:
*kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-na-sa* [variants] read: "provided it possesses the sense of intensity").
2. Following the word *pratyeti* in the *kṣa* recension, there is the phrase *pratigacchati*.

The meaning is that [the sacrifice] goes toward the heavenly world (*dyuloka*; *kṣa*: *svargaloka*) in order to produce a face [for us]. Alternatively, the additional reading is: "May the sacrifice belonging to the gods (*devānām*), which is [denoted by] *yaḥ* (*kṣa*: *yo'tha*), attain (*pratyeti*; *kṣa*: *prati*) or reach (*prāpnoti*; *kṣa*: *prāpnoti*) our well-being (*sumnaṃ sukham*)."
3. She is intent on bestowing grace upon her devotees.

Thus, due to the exclusion (*paryudāsa*), there is an absence of the *nighāta* (unaccented) rule. *mṛḍayantaḥ*: from the root *mṛḍ* [meaning] "to gladden," with the suffix *pyant*, the present participle suffix *śatṛ* is added; then *śap*. By the rule *chandasyubhayathā*, the *śatṛ* is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix; consequently, because it is taught as beginning with *a* (*adupadeśāt*), the *lasārvadhātuka* accent does not apply, and the accent of the *śatṛ* itself remains. *vavṛtyāt*: from the root *vṛt* [meaning] "to turn"; in the *liṅ* (optative), the *parasmaipada* ending is used by transposition (*vyatyaya*). By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the *śap* is replaced by *plu*. *aṃhoḥ*: from the root *ahi* [meaning] "to go"; because it is marked with *idit*, the augment *num* is added, and the *uṇādi* suffix *upratyaya* is applied. *varivovittarā*: from the root *vid* [meaning] "to obtain," with the causative sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*) implied, the suffix *krip* is added; then the comparative suffix *tarap* is applied. *asat*: from the root *as* [meaning] "to be"; in the *leṭ* (subjunctive), the augment *aṭ* is added.

May the gods come to us with their protection, being praised by the *sāmans* of the Aṅgirases; may Indra with his powers, the Maruts with the Maruts, and Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter. upa naḥ devā avasā gamantu aṅgirasāṃ sāmabhiḥ stūyamānāḥ | indra indriyairmaruto marudbhirādityairna āditiḥ śarma yaṃsat || 2 ||

May all the gods, who are endowed with qualities such as generosity (*dāna*), and who are possessed of protection (*avasa*) or the food (*anna*) that must be given to us, come toward us—their worshippers—and approach us. In what manner? Being praised by the *sāmans* (chanted mantras) belonging to the *ṛṣis* known as the Aṅgirases.
Furthermore, [may they come] through Indra and his powers (*indriyas*).
This is the name of wealth.
Let them come with their own kinsmen—the riches that are to be given to us—and let them come with honor.

Likewise, let the forty-nine great gods, who consist of seven groups and are measured as "such-like and other-like" and so forth, come with the Maruts—the winds existing as their own constituent parts in the form of prāṇa, apāna, and the rest—and let them come with honor.
Likewise, may Aditi— the indivisible or non-depressed mother of the gods— along with her own sons, the Ādityas, grant (yaṃsat) us (naḥ) protection (śarma), that is, happiness.
[The verb form] *gamantu* is used in the imperative (*loṭ*), with the elision of the suffix *śap* according to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi."

The remainder [of the rule] is "chandasyubhayathā" (Vedic usage allows for both [treatments]). Because it is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, there is no doubling [of the consonant]; and by the rule "gamahana," etc., there is no elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*).
[Thus we have] *yaṃsat*.
[The root] *yam* means "to cease."
The suffix *sip* is applied in the *leṭ* [subjunctive] mood;
thus, by the rule “*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*,” the suffix *sip* occurs.

May Indra grant us that; may Varuṇa grant that; may Agni grant that; may Aryaman grant that; may Savitṛ grant us that favor. May Mitra and Varuṇa grant us that; may Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant it. 3.
Whatever food is being sought by us—
"cana" is a name for food— may Indra bestow (*dhāt*), that is, grant (*dadhātu*), such food (*canaḥ*) to us (*naḥ*).
In this same way, the application should be understood for "tad varuṇaḥ" and so forth as well.
The meaning is: "May Mitra and the others honor—that is, protect—this food of ours which has been given by Mitra and the others."

*Canas*: [derived from] *cāy*, meaning "to worship" or "to know. According to the Unādi Sūtra 4.639, *cāy-ṛse hrasvaśca*, the suffix *asun* is applied with the augment *nuṭ* and the shortening of the root vowel.
There is elision of the *val* (the suffix *val*).
Due to its being marked with the *ni*-sign, it has the acute accent on the first syllable.
[The form] is *dhāt*.
In the Vedic language, by the rule "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ," the *luṅ* (aorist) is used for the sense of prayer (*prārthanā*). By the rule "gātisthā," there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic*.
1. In the *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha* recensions, "stotṛn" is absent.
2. In the *ṭha-u-sa* recensions, it says "prayacchatu.
The third hymn, consisting of thirteen verses beginning with "ya indrāgnī," is the *ṛṣi*-verse of Kutsa; it is in the *triṣṭubh* meter and is addressed to Indra and Agni (*aindrāgna*).
And thus it has been introduced [in the Anukramaṇī]: "The [hymn] beginning with 'ya indrāgnī sasāna' is addressed to Indra and Agni.
The application [of the mantra] is based on its indicative mark (liṅga).
O Indra and Agni, with that most wondrous chariot of yours which surveys all living beings, come hither, you who stand upon that excellent vehicle; then drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, your most wondrous chariot surveys all living beings. Come hither with that well-rolling chariot, you who stand upon it; then drink of the pressed soma.

O Indra and Agni, most wonderful—that chariot belonging to you two which surveys all beings, all created things; that is to say, because it is made of gold and adorned with jewels, it illuminates the entire world with its own splendors. Come hither with that chariot and come to our sacrifice.
Is it then by turns?
No, he says;
"with a common chariot," meaning you two have mounted a single chariot together and have arrived simultaneously, not by turns.
Now, immediately upon your arrival, drink the Soma of the Soma pressed by the officiating priests for your son—either that which is characterized as your own portion or a part thereof.
For you two: the dual form of the genitive case *vām* is substituted according to Pāṇini’s rule *yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthī* (8.1.20).
The state of being entirely unaccented [is indicated].
He sees;
[the root] *cakṣiṅ* [is used] in the sense of "distinct speech."
Here, for the sake of clarity:
due to its belonging to the *adādi* class, there is elision of the *śap* suffix;
and by the rule "the first member of a conjunct [is elided] after *s* or *k*," there is elision of the *k*.

By the rule *tāsyanudāttet*, since the *lasārvadhātuka* suffix is unaccented, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains. By the rule *yadvṛttānnityam*, there is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of the accent).
[The word is] *saratham*.
This is both *samāna* (equal) and a *ratha* (chariot), hence *saratha*.
[The form] *samānaḥ* becomes *samāvaḥ* by the rule *samānasya chandasi*;
[the accentuation] of the initial syllable of the second member is by the rule *parādiś chandasi bahulam*.

*tasthivāṃsā*: [derived from] the root *sthā* (to stand) with the suffix *kasu*, which is the substitute for the perfect tense marker (*liṭ*). The root *chā* is used in the sense of the cessation of motion.
The dual ending [is applied]. By the rules "śapūrvāḥ khayah" and "vasvekājādvasām," the augment *iṭ* is added.

The elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by the rule “*āto lopa iṭi ca*” (Pāṇini 6.4.64). The form *ākāraḥ* is derived by the rule “*supāṃ suluk pūrvasavarṇāccheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ*” (Pāṇini 7.1.39). [Thus,] *somasya*.
The word "kriyā" (action) must be supplied; since the object [of the action] functions as the recipient (sampradāna), the genitive case is used in the sense of the dative.
As vast as this entire world exists— broad in its extension and deep in its magnitude—
so much let this Soma be for your drinking, O Indra and Agni, according to your will.
As far as this entire world exists—vast in its extent, deep in its breadth—so much let this Soma be for your drinking, O Indra and Agni, sufficient for your minds.

This entire world, this whole moving universe—whatever exists and whatever its extent may be—[is encompassed by you]. Of what nature is it? It is *uruvyacāḥ*: wide-reaching, meaning all-pervading. Likewise, it is profound with *varimatā* (vastness), that is, with a greatness more extensive than the broad expanse. O Indra and Agni, let the Soma be of such a measure for you two to drink; let that Soma be sufficient for your mind, for the sake of your internal organ (*manas*). Regarding *uruvyacāḥ*: from the root *vyac*, in the sense of "making wide" (*vyājīkaraṇe*), with the suffix *asun*.

1. All classes of beings beginning with *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *sa*. 2. *Kṣa* and *sa* remained established. 3. But not *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *na*. 4. Of the son of *ṛtvigbha* and *rabhi*. 5. And the chariot [beginning] with *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *ra*. 6. As much as the measure (*yāvat-parimāṇam*). 7. This Soma [beginning] with *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*, and *sa*. Regarding the form [of the word *soma*]: by the rule "In the case of the root *vyac*, [the suffix *kvip* is applied] when *ku*, *tra*, etc., follow, provided there is no *manas*," there is an absence of *saṃprasāraṇa* due to the absence of *kit*-status. When the elision (*luk*) of the nominative suffix *su* would have occurred by the rule "The [nominative] *su* is elided after a neuter [stem]" (Pāṇini 7.1.23), the substitution of *ḍā* occurs by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*) according to the rule "The *su*, *luk*, etc., of case-endings."
*Varimatā*:
By the rule *pṛthv-ādibhya imanij vā*, the suffix *iman* is added to the word *uras* in the sense of "its state" (*tasya bhāvaḥ*).
According to the rule *priyasthira-ityādinā*, the word *uras* undergoes the substitution *vara*.
Furthermore, the arising of an abstract suffix (bhāvapratyaya) here is Vedic;
the elision of the third case ending is according to the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
Alternatively:
The augment *tuṭ* in the third [case ending] is Vedic; thus it is *tāvān*. That is its measure (*tat-parimāṇam asya*).
By the rule *yattadetebhyaḥ parimāṇe vatup* (Pāṇini 5.2.39), [the suffix] *vatup* is applied;
by the rule *ā sarvanāmnaḥ*, the substitution of *ā* occurs. Thus: *pātave*.
In the word *pā*, [the root] *pā* means "drinking. The suffix *tavn* is applied according to the rule *tumarthe śeṣeṇa*;
because it contains the augment *niṣṭhā*, it is accented on the first syllable.
*aram*.
According to the rule *vālamūlalaghvalaṅgulīnāṃ vā lo ramāpadyata iti vaktavyam* (Pāṇini-mañjarī 8.2.18), there is an optional substitution of *l* for *r*;
thus [the form] *yuvabhyām* [is derived].

Due to the irregularity (vyatyaya), in the absence of the substitution of *ā*, there is the elision of the letter *d* according to the rule "elision of the suffix when nothing remains" (*aśeṣe lopaḥ*).

For you two have made for yourselves a common, auspicious name; you two are united and are slayers of Vṛtra. O Indra and Agni, you who possess common horses, having sat down together, O bulls, pour forth the rain of the bull Soma. 3. *cakrāthe*—for you have made; *hi*—indeed; *sadhryak*—common; *nāma*—name; *bhadram*—auspicious; *saṃśrīcīnā*—united; *vṛtrahaṇau*—O slayers of Vṛtra; *uta*—and; *sthaḥ*—you two are; *tau*—those two; *indrāgnī*—O Indra and Agni; *sadhryaśvā*—possessing common horses; *niṣadyā*—having sat down; *vṛṣṇaḥ*—of the bull; *somasya*—of Soma; *vṛṣaṇā*—O bulls; *ā*—forth; *vṛṣethām*—pour ye.

O Indra and Agni, you two have made for yourselves a single, auspicious, and beautiful name, "Indra and Agni," which is joined together and directed toward greatness. Moreover, O slayers of Vṛtra, destroyers of the Asura Vṛtra, you two are united and moving together for the sake of slaying Vṛtra.

"Indeed, because it is so, therefore, O *vṛṣaṇā*, you two showerers of desires, Indra and Agni, being *sadhryañcau*, joined together, having *ni-padya*, sat down upon the sacrificial altar (*vedī*), do you both *ā-vṛṣethām*, pour down—that is, pour into your own bellies—the portion belonging to yourselves of the *vṛṣṇaḥ*, the showering Soma."
*Sadhryak*: From the root *yant* (to go) with the prefix *saha*, the suffix *kvin* is applied according to the rule beginning with “*ṛtvig-etc.*”;
the elision of the nasal is by the rule “*aniditām*.”
Regarding the form *sahasya sadhiḥ*:
according to the rule *adrisyornodāttanipātanaṃ kṛtsvaranivṛttyartham* (Pāṇini 6.3.95.1), the substitute *sadhi* is accented on its final syllable.
Upon the application of the *yaṇ*-substitution, the resulting vowel becomes *svarita* by the rule *udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*.

*Sadhrīcīnā*: The suffix *mva* is added in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*) by the rule *vibhāṣāñjer adikstriyām*. The substitution of *āj* for the case-ending is applied by the rule *supāṃ suluk*.
*vṛtrahaṇau*: in the *saṃhitā* stage, when the substitution of *āv* occurs, there is the elision of *v* according to the rule *lopaḥ śākalyasya*. *vṛṣethām*.
The root *vṛṣ* means "to sprinkle.
Here, by way of grammatical anomaly (*vyatyaya*), the suffix *śa* is applied, as well as the middle voice (*ātmanepada*).

When the fires are kindled, you two, O Agni and Indra, having anointed yourselves, with ladles extended and spreading the sacrificial grass—O Indra and Agni, come hither for our well-being, as the sharp Soma has been poured by those who have prepared it. samiddheṣv agniṣv āñjānā yata-srucau barhir oṃ iti tistīrāṇā tīvraḥ somaḥ pariṣiktebhir arvāg indrāgnī saumanasāya yātam. 4. When the fires are kindled, anointing [yourselves], with ladles held out, spreading the sacred grass (barhis)—O Indra and Agni, come hither with a gracious mind, for the sharp Soma has been poured by those who have sprinkled it. 4.

When the fires—the Gārhapatya and others—have been properly kindled through the ritual addition of fuel and other rites, and while the two priests, the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ, have offered oblations with clarified butter using ladles from which the fluid flows, and have subsequently spread the *barhis* grass upon the sacrificial altar for the sake of the sacrifice, having thus become such as they are;
then, O Indra and Agni, [be present] with those sharp, swift, and intoxicating [soma-draughts].

"O you two who have been anointed with *soma* juices poured all around from the *parivīka* vessels, the cups, and so forth—come hither, toward us, for the sake of goodwill, that is to say, for our favor. Regarding the word *ānajānā*: the root *añj* (in the sense of manifestation, sprinkling, and motion) takes the suffix *kānac* after the perfect tense (*liṭ*). There is elision of the nasal according to the rule "aniditām...". In the case of reduplication, the initial vowel is lengthened by the rule "ata ādeḥ". Although the rule "tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ" applies only to roots with two consonants, here the augment *nuṭ* is applied by transposition even though the root has only one consonant. Regarding *tistirāṇā*: the root *stṛñ* (in the sense of covering). The suffix *kānac* is applied as before. The change to *i* occurs by the rule "ṛta iddhātoḥ". In the case of reduplication, the rule "śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ" applies. In all instances, the case-ending is replaced by *ā* by the rule "supāṃ suluk...". Because the word is marked with the *cit* indicator, it is oxytone (accented on the final syllable).
Whatever heroic deeds you two, Indra and Agni, have performed, whatever forms and powers you possess,
and whatever ancient, auspicious friendships you have— by means of these, drink of the pressed soma. 5.
O Indra and Agni, those heroic deeds which you two have performed, those forms and powers as well—by virtue of those ancient and auspicious friendships of yours, drink of the pressed Soma. 5.
O Indra and Agni, those heroic deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra which you two have performed, and those forms—cows, horses, and other classes of beings—which you have manifested;
for by Indra and Agni the entire world is created.
Indra, in the form of the sun, produces rain through the oblations mixed with sacrifice.
From rain all living beings arise;

moreover, you two have performed those deeds consisting of the bestowing of rain and so forth, which are the "virile acts" (*vṛṣṇyāni*) born of rain. Likewise, there exist those "ancient," long-standing, and "auspicious," beautiful friendships (*sakhittvāni*) belonging to you two.
Accompanied by all of those [gods], may you two drink the pressed Soma, the soma that has been extracted; for the sake of friendship—
friendship being the state of a friend.
In the word *sakhyaḥ*, the suffix *ya* is applied; the elision of the *śi* case-ending occurs by the rule *śe chandasi bahulam*. [The form is] *tebhiḥ*.

In the word *bhīmā*, the absence of the *aim* suffix is due to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. The acute accent (*udātta*) on the case-ending, which would have been required by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, is prohibited by the rule *na gośvansāvavarṇa*.
Since this Soma, which was first chosen by you both when you were invited by us against the Asuras—
that very thought and faith with which you have come— drink of this pressed Soma.
Since this Soma, which you first chose for yourselves, has been offered by us to the Asuras, come indeed toward that true faith; then drink of the pressed Soma. 6.

O Indra and Agni, at the very commencement of the rite, choosing and honoring you both, I said: "When I shall lead forth the Soma with the *arvan* [steed]. Having spoken thus, regarding that faith (*śraddhā*)—the utterance made with excessive reverence according to the purpose of our friendship—come hither indeed; do not remain away.
Then, immediately upon your arrival, drink the pressed Soma.
That being so, this *soma* of ours becomes especially worthy of being offered (*vihavya*) by the *asuras*—that is, by the officiating priests who cast the oblations; otherwise, it would be useless.
Therefore, the meaning is: "O Indra and Agni, come!
[The word] *vṛṇānaḥ*.
The root *vṛñ* means "to gather" (*saṃbhakti*).
From the present tense marker (*laṭ*), the suffix *śānac* is applied.
By the rule "1. kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-kṛnāṃ tāmurki," [the substitution of *tām* for the *śānac* occurs].

In *ka* 83, there is the elision of the vowel *ā* according to the rule *ābhyastayorātaḥ*. [The word] *asuraiḥ*: from the root *asu* in the sense of "to throw" (*kṣepaṇe*), with the suffix *uran* by the *uṇādi-sūtra* 1.42 (*aseran*). *vihavyaḥ*: from the root *hve* in the sense of "giving and eating" (*dānādanayoḥ*), with the suffix *yat* by the rule *aco yat*; there is *guṇa* substitution; the substitution of *av* occurs by the rule *dhātostanimittasyaiva*; and the acute accent on the first syllable occurs by the rule *yato'nāvaḥ*. It has the original accent of the final member of a *kṛt*-derived compound.

O Indra and Agni, when you rejoice in your own dwelling, or when you, O worshipful ones, [rejoice] in sacred prayers or in the kingdom—from there, O bulls, come hither; drink of the pressed soma. 7. When, O Indra and Agni, you rejoice in your own home, or when, O worshipful ones, [you rejoice] in sacred prayers or in the kingdom—from there, O bulls, come hither; drink of the pressed soma. 7.
O worshipful Indra and Agni, worthy of sacrifice, if you rejoice in your own dwelling, in your own home, the place of your residence;
or if you rejoice upon coming to another Brahmin sacrificer to accept the oblation;
or if you rejoice upon coming to provide assistance in battle for a king, a Kṣatriya.
Therefore, from all this place around, O Indra and Agni, you two showerers of desires (*vṛṣaṇau*), come indeed;
do not remain indifferent.
The rest is as before.
*Madathaḥ*:
[derived from] *madī* in the sense of "joy";
the *śap* suffix is applied by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*).
*Yajatrā*:
By the rule *‘aminakṣa’* etc., the suffix *atran* is applied to the root *yaj* in the sense of the object (*karman*). The vowel *ā* of the case-ending is substituted by *supāṃ suluk* etc.

O Indra and Agni, whether you are among the Yadus, the Turvaśas, the Druhyus, the Anus, or the Purus—from there, O mighty ones, come hither; drink of the pressed soma. 8. Whether, O Indra and Agni, [you are] among the Yadus, among the Turvaśas, whether among the Druhyus, the Anus, or the Purus—you are present—come from there, O bulls, for indeed; then drink of the pressed soma. 8.

In this context, *yaduṣu* and the following five are names of human tribes. O Indra and Agni, if you two abide among the Yadus—those restrained men who are non-violent—or if you abide among the Turvaśas—those violent men; [then come to us].
Whether they exist among those malicious men who desire to harm others and seek to cause them distress,
or among living beings (*anuṣu*)— that is, among all sentient creatures who possess consciousness and are endowed with life—
for the lives of others are indeed fruitless due to their lack of knowledge and absence of spiritual practice.
If [the offerings] are for you among them;
likewise, if they are for you among other people who are to be satisfied by their desires;
therefore, O Indra and Agni, you who rain down desires, come from every place.
Drink the Soma that has been pressed immediately thereafter.
Regarding the Yadus: from the root *yam*, meaning "to cease" or "to restrain. They are called Yadus because by means of them the senses (*indriyāṇi*) are restrained (*niyamyante*).
In the word *yameduk*, the suffix *kup* is applied and there is the augment *duk*;
by the rule beginning with *anudāttaupadeśa*, the nasal (*anunāsika*) is elided.
[The word occurs] among the Turvaśas.
The root *turv* has the meaning "to injure. The suffix *aś* is derived according to the *Uṇādi* rules. [Thus it forms] *duhuṣu*.
The root *duh* is used in the sense of "desiring to kill.
The suffix *kip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule for *saṃpad* and so forth.
Thus, they desire to go to the supreme state beyond suffering (*duhaṃ*).
The suffix *kyac* is applied according to the rule “*chandasi parecchāyām api*” (in Vedic usage, *kyac* is used even for the desire of another).
The suffix *up* is applied according to the rule “*kyāc chandasi*” (after a word ending in *kyac*, the suffix *up* occurs in Vedic usage).
[The form is] *anuṣu*.
1. *hu*—in the sense of giving and eating;
2. *kṣa-ṭa*—now, immediately thereafter; 3.
*a-sa*—this (*sa-idam*) follows after the word "pibatam" (*drink ye*); this is the explanation according to the view of Naru for the sake of the meaning.
In the historical perspective, however, it should be understood that [the term refers] to the subjects related to the five kings, Turvaśa and the others, who were the sons of Śaryāti;
this is the additional point.

In the root *ana* meaning "to breathe," the suffix *u* occurs even after this root due to the word *bahulam* (variously), as prescribed by the rule *anaśra* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.8). Because of the continued application of the term *nit*, the word is udātta-accented on its first syllable. Regarding *purū*: in the root *pūrī* meaning "to fill," those who are filled (*pūryante*) are called *pūravaḥ*; the suffix *u* here is an *auṇādika* (irregular) formation.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are on this lowest earth, on the middle one, or on the highest,
come hither from there, O bulls, and drink of this pressed soma juice.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the lowest earth, in the middle, or in the highest, even from there, O mighty ones, come hither; then drink of the pressed soma. 9.
"O Indra and Agni, if you two are present on this lowest earth, on this most proximate ground;
or if you are in the middle earth, in the intermediate world (antarikṣa)—
here the word 'earth' (pṛthivī) refers to all three worlds."
As it is said: “He who dwells on the second or the third earth by name” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.2.12.1).
And furthermore: “Whether they dwell on the highest, most excellent, or far-removed earth—that is, in the heavenly world—from all such places, O two showerers [of benefits], come hither!”
"Immediately upon your arrival, drink the pressed Soma."
In the word *avamasyām*: by the rule *ṅe-ryai-yāt*, the augment *syāt* is added after the word *avama*. The same applies in the subsequent cases as well.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are on the highest earth, the middle one, or even the lowest, come hither from there, O bulls;
drink of this pressed soma juice.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the highest heaven, in the middle region, or in the lowest earth—come hither from there, O showerers of blessings; drink then of the pressed Soma. 10.
This is to be explained as before;
however, this much is the distinction:
previously it was stated that they should come as far as Indra and Agni in the three worlds beginning with Bhūmi.
Now, while you are proceeding through the lower succession among yourselves in the three worlds, it is entreated that you two—Indra and Agni—should come as far as [that point].
O Indra and Agni, whatever [soma] is in heaven, whatever on earth, whatever on the mountains, in the plants, or in the waters—from there, O bulls, come hither; drink of this pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in heaven, or on earth, or among the mountains, in the plants, or in the waters—from there, O bulls, come hither; drink of this pressed soma.
1. From *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-sarvasmāt* onwards, the [explanation] is the same.
66. The Ṛgveda [Bha. 1. a. 7. va. 28]:
O Indra and Agni, if you two are in the sky, in the heavenly world (*divi*).
Whether you are on the earth in the world of mortals, or on mountains such as Meru, or in clouds; likewise,
whether you are in plants such as sesame, beans, and rice, or in the waters, acting as benefactors— if you are there,
O you two who rain down desires, come from all those places!
And having arrived, drink the pressed Soma.
In *pṛthivyām*,
the acute accent (*udātta*) of the case-ending is due to the rule "udāttayaṇaḥ. In *oṣadhīṣu* [the same applies].
They are called *oṣadhayaḥ* because "the raw (*pāka*) seed-syllable (*opaḥ*) is placed within them.

The suffix *kvip* is applied according to the rule "after a verbal root, when the object or the locus [is to be expressed]. Due to their inclusion in the *dāsībhāra-* group, the original accent of the first member of the compound is retained.
And that [word] is udātta on the first syllable because it ends in a consonant;
furthermore, there is lengthening by the rule "opadheśca vibhaktāvaprathamāyām" (Pāṇini 6.1.172).
O Indra and Agni, when you rejoice according to your own nature at the rising of the sun and in the midst of heaven,
come hither from there, O bulls, and drink of the pressed soma.

O Indra and Agni, when you have risen in the midst of the sky by the power of your own nature, rejoice there. From that place, O Indra and Agni, seeking with my mind better wealth—whether kinsmen or those born of the same lineage—I have fashioned for you this hymn that strives for booty; for no other youthful protector exists for me.

For, seeking what is better with my mind, I have not offered oblations to others, whether they be kinsmen or even my own people; no other youthful providence exists for me. Therefore, I have fashioned for you two this prayer that strives for strength. 1.

O Indra and Agni, desiring and longing for wealth that is excellent and praiseworthy, I—through my mind and intellect—have pervaded both my kinsmen (*jñāsaḥ*) and also my relatives (*sajātān*), those born of the same origin who are distinct from my kinsmen; for they indeed become the givers of wealth.
I have sought you two alone as my kin and my friends through my thought and understanding.
You two are the ones who bestow riches.
Moreover, O young man and young woman, there is no other superior intellect (*pramati*) bestowed upon me by anyone else;
this superior intellect which is mine was given by you two alone.
He is such [a person].

*Apadhya* means "having struck down" (*tanmīta*). Alternatively, *uta vā gha syālāt api ca syālāt* means "even from a brother-in-law," for he is close by virtue of association; so say the Maitrāyaṇīyas. Or, *syālā-jānāvanatīni* [is the derivation]. *Lājāḥ* [are so called] from the root *lāja* ("to fry"); the form is from the root *syai* ("to flow"). *Śarpa* means "eating and blowing," from the roots *śṛṇāti* ("to destroy") or *śasati* ("to sharpen"). Now, with the offering of Soma, O Indra and Agni, I generate for you two a hymn (*stoma*) that is newer than the new, like the nave of a wheel. (Nirukta 6.9). Regarding *aśvam*: from the root *śru* ("to hear"), in the imperfect (*laṅ*), first person singular, there is the elision of the suffixal augment (*vikaraṇa*) according to the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. *Bhūridāvattarā*: from the root *ḍudāñ* ("to give"). By the rule *āto manin-kvanib-vanipaśca*, the suffix *vanip* is added. One who gives much is *bhūridāvā*; one who gives even more is *bhūridāvattaraḥ*. By the rule *bhūridābhastuḍkavyaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.17.2), the suffix *tud* is added after the comparative suffix *tarap*. There is elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*) due to the designation of the word as a *pada*. The vowel *ā* replaces the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk...* (Pāṇini 7.1.39). *Gha*: in the *saṃhitā* text, lengthening occurs by the rule *ṛci tunudha...* (Pāṇini 6.3.133). *Atha*: by the rule *nipātasya ca* (Pāṇini 6.3.136). *Prayanī*: from the root *yama* ("to cease"). In the suffix *ktin*, [the form is derived]. *Anu*... [text fragment].

For you two, O Indra and Agni, the goddess Dhiṣaṇā presses the Soma for exhilaration, grasping it firmly. O Aśvins, you of auspicious hands and fair arms, wash it in the waters, mingling it with honey.

For you two, O Indra and Agni, the goddess Dhiṣaṇā, desiring [you], presses the Soma for exhilaration. O Aśvins, you of auspicious hands and fair arms, hasten hither; mix [the draught] with honey in the waters. 4.

O Indra and Agni, for your exhilaration and for your sustenance, the divine, radiant, and longing *dhiṣaṇā*— that is, Speech in the form of sacred mantra, desiring you both— presses the Soma. Or rather,
the radiant *dhiṣaṇā*, namely the pressing-skin, desiring your exhilaration, presses the Soma.
By means of the pressing-stones (*prāvabhiḥ*), he is the performer of the pressing (*abhiṣava*) therein;
[the two] Aśvins are those possessing horses, with auspicious hands—that is, with beautiful arms—and with fair palms (*supāṇī*).
The *pāṇi* is the portion of the hand above the wrist (*maṇibandha*).
Śobhanapāṇi:
For an animal sacrifice to Indra and Agni, the *Ṛgveda* verse "pra carṣaṇibhyaḥ" is the *yājyā* for the *havis*.

In the section titled "Of Offerings" (*pradānānām*), it is sūtra-ed: "May the divine Savitṛ, rich in jewels, come forward for the people in the calls to battle" (*pra carṣaṇibhyaḥ pṛtanāhaveṣvā devo yātu savitā suratnaḥ*; Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7).
You two surpass all people in the calls to battle; you exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness;
you surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty—O Indra and Agni, you are superior to all other beings.

You two surpass all people in the calls of battle; you surpass both the earth and the heavens; you surpass the rivers and the mountains by your greatness. O Indra and Agni, you both exceed all other beings. 6.

When there are invocations for the sake of protection in battles, in conflicts, and in challenges, O Indra and Agni, you two have come; by your greatness (*mahitvā*), you both surpass (*pravrīricāthe*) all human beings—meaning you are superior to all. Here, due to the influence of the prefix (*upasarga*), the verbal root expresses a meaning contrary to its own primary sense, as in "forgetting" (*prasmaraṇa*) or "setting out" (*prasthāna*). Likewise, you both surpass even the entire earth (*pṛthivyāḥ*).
The same applies to words such as these:
*sindhavaḥ* means waters characterized by flowing;
*girayaḥ* means mountains.
Moreover, O Indra and Agni, you two surpass all beings—all created things—and even those that are beyond them; you remain superior.
*pṛtanāhavaḥ* (3):
[The word *hava* is derived from the root *hve* with the suffix *ap*, by the rule *bhāve'nupasargasya*; there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
By transposition (*vyatyaya*), since the accent of the initial syllable of the root does not occur, the accent of the original form of the final member (*anuttarapadaprakṛtisvara*) applies.]
*riricāthe*.
[The root] *ric* [is used] in the sense of "emptying" (*virecana*).
The suffix *liṭ* is applied while the rule "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*" (Pāṇini 3.4.6) remains in force.
Or rather, by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," the *śru* suffix replaces the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*) in the present tense (*laṭ*); thus,
*mahitvā*.
In the word *mahaḥ* [in the phrase] *pṛtanāyām*, the suffix *indra* is applied according to the *augādika* group. Its abstract state (*bhāva*) is greatness (*mahattvam*).
The form *surāṃ sulka* is a substitute for the third case ending.
Regarding the very same animal sacrifice mentioned previously, the verse "ā bharataṃ" is the invitatory formula (*anuvākyā*) for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "ā bharataṃ śikṣataṃ vajrabāhū ubhā vāmindrāgnī āhuvadhyai" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7).
Bring hither and bestow [wealth], O you whose arms wield the thunderbolt; O Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers!
These indeed are the rays of the Sun, by which our two parents attained companionship.

Bring hither! Bestow [your gifts]! O you with thunderbolt-arms (*vajrabāhū*), Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers (*śacībhiḥ*). Now these are your rays of the sun, by which you were united as parents. 7.

O Indra and Agni, you whose arms are like vajras and whose hands hold vajras, bring wealth for our sake; having brought it, bestow it upon us—you whose function is the act of giving—and furthermore, favor us, your worshippers, with your own powers (*śacībhiḥ*), which is a term for ritual actions.
1. "sa-'yāni" does not exist;
2. "sa-tāny api" [does not exist]; 3. "sa-'pṛtanāhavaḥ" does not exist.
O you two, protect us with your deeds.
Furthermore, by those rays and those flames of Indra in his solar form, our ancestors— our forefathers— attained the state of the seven thousand, that is, they went to the world of Brahmā.
For it is by the path beginning with light that the meditators go to the world of Brahman;
and thus it is heard in scripture: "They pass into the light, from the light into the day" (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 5.10.1).
Or alternatively:
Those very rays by which they attained union and reached your essence—
those rays are indeed these ones being invoked by us now.
Those rays that belong to Indra in his solar aspect are the same as those of Agni.
And thus it is heard in scripture: "The sun indeed enters into fire at evening; therefore, fire is seen as the ray of the sun" (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2.1.2.9).
Therefore, by the praise of the sun's rays, the praise of both Indra and Agni is established.
Bharata.
The term *hyamahorbhaḥ* indicates the substitution of *bha*.
"Training" (*śikṣaṇam*);
[the root] *śikṣa* means "to take up effort."

When the sarvadhatuka suffix is unaccented due to the rule *adupadeśāl-laghūpadhāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.186), the *śap* affix is also unaccented because it is marked with *p*. Thus, the accent of the verbal root (*dhātusvara*) remains. Furthermore, because the *tiṅ* suffix follows, there is no elision of the *śi* augment.
The root is *āp* in the sense of "pervasion" (*vyāptau*). From this root,
with the word *sa* as an upapada, the suffix *tvan* is applied according to the rule "kṛtyārthe tavaiken" (Pāṇini 3.4.14).
The change of the verbal root [dhā] to *dhī* occurs because it belongs to the class beginning with *pṛṣodara*;
or alternatively,
[it is derived from] the root *pap* in the sense of "measuring."
In the case of "insarvadhānubhyaḥ," there is the substitution of *in* for *map*, the state of being seventh [case], and the addition of *ām*.
The root *ama* is used in the senses of "going" (*gati*) and "taking" (*ādāna*).

In the *laṅ* tense, the augment *āṭ* is added, which is accented acute (*udātta*). Due to the rule "after that which contains *yat*" (*yadvṛttāt*), there is an absence of the *nighāta* (non-accentuation).
