O Purandara, you who are trained and hold the thunderbolt in your hand—O Indra and Agni, protect us in the battles! May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that favor. Purandara; śikṣitaṃ (the trained); vajrahastā (O you two with thunderbolts in your hands); asmān (us); indrāgnī (O Indra and Agni); avatam (protect); bharaiṣu (in the battles); tat (that); naḥ (for us); mitraḥ (Mitra); varuṇaḥ (Varuṇa); māmahantām (may they grant); aditiḥ (Aditi); sindhuḥ (Sindhu); pṛthivī (Earth); uta (and); dyauḥ (Heaven). || 8 ||
O Indra and Agni, you who hold the thunderbolt in hand, grasping the vajra with your hands, you who shatter the cities of the Asuras—teach us and bestow upon us the wealth we desire.
Furthermore, protect and guard us in battles and conflicts.
May Mitra and the others honor and celebrate that which has been prayed for by means of this hymn.
*Puraṃdara*:
[The suffix] *kvac* is applied by the rule "apūḥsarvayordārisahoḥ" (Pāṇini 3.2.41).
The form *am* is established by the specific grammatical injunction (*nipātana*) "vācyamapuraṃdarau ca" (Pāṇini 6.3.69).
The vowel *ā* [in place of the case-ending] is by the rule "supāṃ suluk" (Pāṇini 7.1.39).
The fifth hymn, consisting of nine verses beginning with "tataṃ me," is the seer Kutsa's composition; its deities are the Ṛbhus.
The fifth and ninth verses are *triṣṭubh*s, while the remaining verses are *jagatī*s.
And thus it has been set forth in the Anukramaṇī: "The fifth [verse] is indeed *navāva*, while at the end there are two *triṣṭubh*s."
This verse, "idam ārcam," is the insertion point for the *nivid* in the *vaiśvadeva* *śastra* on the fourth day of the *abhiplava* period.
It is prescribed in the section beginning with "tṛtīyasya" in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (7.7): "'tataṃ me apa' is the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra]."

The work was stretched out by me; that same work is being stretched out again. The sweetest prayer is recited for the sake of the hymn. This ocean here belongs to all the gods; O Ṛbhus, drink together of that which has been consecrated with "svāhā. *tatam* | *me* | *apaḥ* | *tat* | *ūm* | *tāyate* | *punar* | *svādiṣṭhā* | *dhītiḥ* | *ucathāya* | *śasyate* | *ayam* | *samudraḥ* | *iha* | *viśvadaivyaḥ* | *svāhākṛtasya* | *sam* | *ūm* | *tṛṣṇuta* | *ṛbhavaḥ* || 1 ||

1. Not attaining the state of being inherent in *kṣa*, they attained the state of being inherent in *sa*. 2. The prohibition of the elision (*nighāta*) of *kṣa*. 3. [The mantra] *kṣa-ṭa-hastaiḥ*. 4. May *kṣa*, those friends of his, and others protect [me].
O *Ṛbhus*, by me—that is, by me—the *ap-* [work], namely the ritual action consisting of the *agniṣṭoma* and other forms, was extended (*tataṃ*) and performed extensively in the past.
That very same thing (*tat*) is now again extended (*tāyate*), meaning it is performed once more.

In this regard, that which is most sweet (*svādiṣṭhā*) and most excellently offered (*svāhutāmā*), being exceedingly pleasing, is praised and recited as a hymn (*ucathāya*) for the sake of praise. Furthermore, in this sacrifice, the Soma juice—which has the nature of overflowing (*samudran-śīlaḥ*)—has been prepared so as to be sufficient for all the gods.
By drinking that Soma which has been consecrated with the cry of *svāhā* and poured forth, may you both be thoroughly satisfied (*samutṛpṇutaḥ*).
*Tatam* [is derived from] the root *tanu*, meaning "to expand. In the formation of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*), there is a prohibition of the suffix *it* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*.
The elision of the nasal [in *apaḥ*] occurs by the rule beginning with *anudāttopadeśa*. [The form] *apaḥ*:
[the root] *āp* in the sense of pervading (*vyāptau*).
In the formation of the word *āpaḥ* from the verbal root meaning "to act" (*karman*), the vowel is shortened by the rule *hrasvo nud vā*. [Thus] *tan* + *asun* results in *tāp*,
and by the rule *tanoter yaki* (Pāṇini 6.4.44), the substitution of *ā* for *a* occurs, yielding *tāyate*.
*Svādiṣṭhā*: From the word *svādiṣṭha*, the suffix *iṣṭhan* is added in the sense of superlative degree (*ātiśāyanika*). By the rule *ṭeḥ*, there is the elision of the final phoneme *ṭ*.
For the sake of speech (*ucathāya*). [The root] *vac* means "to speak. The suffix *atha* belongs to the *augādika* group.
By the rule *vacisvapi* etc., there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). [Thus] *samudraḥ*.
[The root] *undī* means "to moisten."
The suffix *rak* is applied by the rule *sphāyitañci*, etc.;
the elision of the nasal is by the rule *aniditām*.
[The form is] *viśvebhyaḥ*.
*devāhoṃ bhāgaḥ* means "the portion for the gods.
The suffix *ya* is applied according to the rule *chandasi ca*.
*viśve* means "all" those who are in this Soma.

In the case of a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by the rule *viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*, there is acute accent on the final syllable of the first member even when it is not a proper name (*asaṃjñāyām*), due to an irregularity (*vyatyaya*). In *svāhākṛtasya*,

because the word *svāhā* is a *gati* by virtue of its upward direction (*ūrdhvāditva*), according to Pāṇini 1.4.61, the rule *gatiranantaraḥ* applies, resulting in the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.
*tṛpṇutaḥ* [is derived from] *tṛp*, meaning "to please"; [the suffix] *kṣu* is applied after roots beginning with *svā*.
By the rule "ṛbhavaḥ," there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) in the *saṃhitā* as "ṛtvijaḥ."
When they desired to come hither with their efforts— the Apākās, the horses, and some of my companions—
the sons of Sudhanvan came by the abundance of their journey to the house of the liberal Savitṛ.
When you came from afar, seeking food, O sons of Śvā, some of you turned back; yet you, O sons of Sudhanvan, by the abundance of your wandering, arrived at the house of the liberal Savitṛ. 2.

O Ṛbhus, you who were once distant but have now attained mature knowledge—wise ones belonging to a former time, my *āpayaḥ*, meaning those who lead me [to the goal] and are my kinsmen—whoever among you, desiring *ābhogyaṃ* Soma, that is, the Soma fit for enjoyment, went forth (*pra etana*) at that time, having gone to the forest to practice austerity;
for the Ṛbhus are the sons of Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa.
As it has been stated by Yāska: "Ṛbhu, Viśvāvasu, and Vāja—these were the three sons of Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa" (Nirukta 11.16).
Kutsa was also an Āṅgirasa; therefore, he said, "These are my kinsmen.

O Saudhanvanas, sons of Sudhanvan, by the abundance—that is, the great quantity—of the austerity (tapas) accumulated through your conduct at that time, you went to the sacrificial hall of the donor who had offered oblations, of Savitṛ, the sacrificer performing the pressing of Soma. Having obtained Soma through your austerity and having drunk it, you departed.
Or else:

They reached the dwelling place—the residence—of Savitṛ, who had bestowed the drinking of Soma upon the Ṛbhus at the morning libations and other rites when they were brought near by Agni and the others; having been served [Soma] by the one who gives (dāśuṣaḥ), they arrived at the third libation.
All of this is recorded in the *Aitareya Brāhmaṇa* (3.30) and elsewhere, beginning with the statement: "He recites the *Ārbhava* [Śastra]."
It is called *ābhogaya*. *Ābhoga* means enjoyment (*bhoga*) on all sides (*ā*).
That day is *ābhogaya*.
Regarding the rule *chandasi ca*:
the absence of elision (*lopa*) in the word *yasya* is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndasa*).
By means of transposition (*vyatyaya*), the accentuation of the syllable preceding the suffix is acute.
Alternatively, from the root *uj* preceded by the prefix *ā*, there is the suffix *ip* in the sense of the object, belonging to the *uṇādi* group, and the substitution of *ku* for *u*.
By transposition (*vyatyaya*), there is *guṇa* [vowel strengthening].
aitana | [from] the root *i* in the sense of "going," in the *laṅ* tense, second person plural.

1. *kṣa*: for the purpose of praising (*stutyāya*) and for the purpose of seeking you (*yuṣmad-ruṣaṇāya*). 2. *kṣa*: the suffix *rak*. 3. *sa*: for the purpose of drinking that (*tat-pānāya*). 4. *kṣa*: the suffix *yap*; *ṭa*: the suffix *yaḥ*. 5. *kṣa*: the suffix *ayap*; *ṭa*: the suffix *ghap*.

In the case of the plural number, *tā* is substituted for *yasya*. By the rule "tas-an-as-n-ath-na-śa," *tan* is substituted for that [suffix]. There is the augment *āṭ* and *vṛddhi*. Thus: *āpayaḥ*. From the root *ā-pṛ*, the *i*-affix is added according to the *uṇādi* rules. *Bhūmanā*: from the word *bahu*, the suffix *imanij* is applied by the rule governing the *pṛthu* group. By the rule "there is elision of *bahu* and *bhū* replaces *bahu*," there is the elision of the vowel *i* and the substitution of *bhū* for *na-hu*. Because a grammatical operation conditioned by a specific technical name (*saṃjñā*) is not necessarily permanent, there is no elision [of the final *u*]. "May Savitṛ impel you toward immortality, which is unassailable, as you have reached the end of your allotted lifespan."
They made that single drinking-vessel of the Soma-drinker fourfold.

Savitar bestowed immortality upon you when you came proclaiming [it], that which is not to be hidden. That very chalice, the drinking-vessel of the Asura, though it was one, you made into four. We [have done so]. 3.
O Ṛbhus, at that time, Savitṛ, the god who impels all, bestowed upon you immortality— the state of divinity— meaning he directed it toward you and gave it to you.

This was when, in the age of Vamana, which is free from concealment, you were united with the *dhṛtayas* (stabilizing powers) to be performed, and you became worthy of the sacrificial oblation through your labors.

Regarding this, the Nirukta states: "Having performed their tasks, the mortals who were the R̥bhus, the sons of Sudhanvan—being wise and swift carriers—attained immortality; they were united within the year through their steadfast labors. Or [the word] *surasyānāḥ* means 'possessing divine wisdom. There were three sons of Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, known as Dhṛti, Bhuvana, and Vāta" (Nirukta 11.16).
*viṣṭī*. [The forms] *viplū* [in the sense of] pervasion (*vyāptau*) and *snātvā* etc. (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.1.49) result in the substitution of the long vowel *ī* for the suffix *ktvā*.
*śamī*: by *supāṃ suluk* (Pāṇini 7.1.39), there is elision (*luk*) of the case-ending of *śamī*. *ānaśuḥ*.
11. *aś* [is used] in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*). 12. By way of transposition (*vyatyaya*), the Parasmaipada ending is employed. 13.
And by the rule "abhoteśca" (Pāṇini 7.2.35), the augment *nuṭ* is added after the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). 14. Thus [the form is derived].
*Apracyuta*.
15. *Pracī* in the sense of contact.
16. The *laṅ* [suffix] in the passive voice (*karman*).
Like a field, the Ṛbhus measured out with fervor the single vessel that was gaping open;
they, being praised, seeking a likeness, and desiring glory among the immortals, strove for it as if striving for half [of the prize].
Like a field, the R̥bhus, being praised, gathered together with their tool that single, gaping vessel; seeking glory among the immortals, they approached it as if begging for a share.

1. Praised by the officiating priests standing nearby; 2. the *ṛbhus*; 3. the one who was "straining" (*jehamānam*), making an effort toward the act of offering; 4. "one," without a companion; 5. the vessel, the means of drinking—the *camasa* cup fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ with a measuring rod; 6. like a field, that is, like the earth; 7. with a "sharpener," a sharp weapon, in the form of four *camasa* cups, in order to make [it]; 8. three times; 9. they "measured" (*mamur*), that is, they performed a specific measurement. Desiring what? 10.
"The comparison," the excellent food characterized by Soma which serves as the standard for all; 11. "not desiring," that is, not begging [for it].
He explains this very point:
12 "Among the immortals," that is, among the gods who are free from death; 13 "desiring glory," meaning desiring food characterized by oblations;
14 "desiring," that is, longing for the drinking of Soma together with the gods.
The meaning is that they fashioned a square seat for the sake of great gain.
The root *māṅ* (in the sense of measuring and sound) is [the basis]. 15. *māṅ* means "to measure" and "to sound. 16.
The *parasmaipada* ending is used by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). Regarding *tejanena*:
according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.4.57, *aṇo’pragṛhyāsyānāsikaḥ*, the nasalization (*ānunāsikya*) of the vowel *a* occurs by way of transposition before a non-final position (*anavasāne*).
There is *prakṛtibhāva* (absence of sandhi) due to the inclusion in the group beginning with *īṣā-akṣa*.
[The form] *jehamānam* [is derived from the root] *veha* or *jeha*, meaning "effort" (*prayatna*). 19–20.
It belongs to the *bhū* class (*bhauvādika*).
Because it is marked with an indicatory vowel *a* (anudāttet), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used.
[The word is] *upastutāḥ*.
21. *gatiranantaraḥ* (Pāṇini 6.2.49): by this rule, the word *gati* retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvaratva*). 22. *upamam*. 23. *māṅ māne* (Dhātupāṭha 2.56). 24. [End of section].
The suffix *ka* is applied by the rule "ātaścopasarge" (Pāṇini 3.2.3). [Thus we have] *icchamānāḥ*.
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by way of metrical transposition (*vyatyaya*).
With inspired thought, let us offer to the heroes of the mid-air our wisdom like clarified butter from a ladle;
for the *Ṛbhus*, who by their skillful crossing followed this father’s path, have won the prize and reached the realm of heaven.

We offer our inspired thought to the heroes of the mid-air, like clarified butter with the ladle. The Rbhus, who by their wisdom followed the swift power of this Father, have ascended to the realm of heaven for the sake of booty.
1. Belonging to the *antarikṣa*, that is, to the intermediate region (*antarikṣaloka*), which occupies the middle place; 2. for the *nṛ* (men), that is, for the *ṛbhus*, the leaders of the sacrifice.
For the *ṛbhus* are indeed the leaders of the sacrifice;
it was by means of that [sacrifice] that they attained the status of gods.
Alternatively,
[they are] for the leaders of the intermediate world;
these are recited in the middle station.

From such [beings], as with a ladle—that is, as with a pure ladle—one offers the oblation (havis) consisting of clarified butter (ghṛta), characterized by its flowing nature, into the intermediate space (ākṣa); that is, into the middle station (madhyamasthāna).

We offer oblations (*juhvāma*). The long vowel *ā* is used in the sense of a limit (*maryādā*); that is, we offer according to the scriptures. In this very way, we perform our mental resolve (*manīṣā*), praise, and discernment (*vijñāna*) through knowledge (*vedana*). This is the remainder of the sense. Furthermore, those *Ṛbhus* who, having become rays of the sun, attained (*saśrire*) the "crossings" (*taraṇitvāni*)—the skillful means of crossing—of this Sun, the protector of the entire world; for it is said: "The rays of the Sun are also called *Ṛbhus*. Those *Ṛbhus* ascended to the "dust" (*rajaḥ*) of heaven. The word *rajas* denotes the worlds. They reached the food characterized by Soma (*vāja*) belonging to the shining heavenly world through sacrificial acts such as giving, and other divine deeds such as the fashioning of the four ladles (*camasa*). [Grammatical notes: In *suceva*, the case-ending is acute according to the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. In *juhvāma*: the root *hu* means "to give" or "to eat"; in the imperative (*loṭ*), the augment *āṭ* is added to the first person plural by the rule *āḍuttamasya picca*. In *vijñānā*: from the root *vid* "to know," the suffix *mani* is added by the *Uṇādi* rules; there is no elision of the *n* because of the rule *na saṃyogānmantāt*. In *taraṇitvā*: from the root *tṛ* "to swim" or "to cross," the suffix *ani* is added in the sense of the agent by the rule *atisabhṛdhṛdhamyasyavitṛbhyo'niḥ*; the state of that is *taraṇitva*. The *ś* is elided by the rule *śelopaśchandasi bahulam*. In *saśrire*: some read *saśri* in the root list *gluñcapastañjagatau*; the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) occurs by transposition. The absence of reduplication follows the statement: "In the section on reduplication, it should be stated that in Vedic usage it is optional. The accent falls on the syllable following *ira* due to the rule *śrisvādannodāttatvam*. There is a prohibition of the *nighāta* (anudātta) accent by the rule *yadvṛttānnityam*. In *aruhan*: from the root *ruh* "to grow" or "to appear"; in the *luṅ* tense, *aṭ* replaces *cli* by the rule *kṛsṛdṛhahibhyaśchandasi*. In *divaḥ*: the case-ending is acute by the rule *aḍidamityādinā*. In *rajaḥ*: from the root *rañj* "to color"; that which colors is *rajas*, i.e., the world. As it is said: "The worlds are called *rajāṃsi*" (Nirukta 4.19). The suffix *asun* is added in the locative sense by the *Uṇādi* rules. The elision of *n* occurs by the rule *rajakarajanarajaḥsupasaṃkhyānam*. The genitive case ending is elided by the rule *supāṃ suluk...*.]
Like the R̥bhus, O Indra, you have become newer through your power; you have become a piercer with your strengths and your riches.
O Gods, through your protection on this dear day, may we overcome the attacks of those who seek to harm us.

Indra is our most recent [kinsman] by his power; R̥bhu is the bestower of wealth through his riches and treasures. O gods, by your protection on this beloved day, may we overcome the hostile attacks of those who do not press the Soma.
R̥bhu, Vibhvan, and Vāja were the three sons of Sudhanvan.
Among them, by virtue of his power and strength, R̥bhu is the most recent, the newer, and the more excellent. He is our Indra, the Supreme Lord;
the meaning is that he is our protector.
Alternatively, Indra himself is praised here as "Ṛbhu" through the etymological derivation provided by the Nairuktas, namely "one of wide radiance" (*urubhānī*).

Furthermore, with the *vājais*—that is, with other *vājais* (strengths or foods) to be granted to us—and with the *vasubhis*, the causes of our dwelling, may he be *ṛbhuḥ vasuḥ*: the dweller who provides us with a home; and for that very reason, may he be *tṛdiḥ*: the bestower of those foods and riches.
The latter half-verse is addressed directly:

O gods, endowed with qualities such as generosity—O Ṛbhus and others—on a day connected with you, joined with protection (*avas*), dear and favorable to us, may we stand against the armies (*pṛtsutīḥ*) of those enemies who do not press the soma and who oppose the sacrificer who does press it.
*Navīyān*:
from the word *nava*, the suffix *īyasun* is added in the sense of comparative excellence. *Vājebhiḥ*.
By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the substitution of *aim* for *bhis* does not occur.
[The word] *vasuḥ*:
from the root *vas* "to dwell."
From this [root], with the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*) included, the suffix *u* is applied by [Pāṇini 3.2.174] *pṛstvastināhe*.
Due to the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of the term "beginning with *ni*," the word is udātta-accented on its first syllable. Thus, *tṛdiḥ*.
The root *tṛd* means "to give. By the rule *āhagamahan*, the suffix *kvip* is applied.
Because it has the nature of a *liṅ* (injunctive), reduplication and so forth occur.
The elision of the vowel *ā* occurs by the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pāṇini 6.4.64).

1. *kṣa-sa* [becomes] the rays of the sun (*sūryasya raśmibhūtāḥ*). 2. By those [suffixes] taught after *sa-vedas*. 3. By *kṣa-na-samuc* [there is] *dva*. 4. In the case of giving and not giving (*a-dānādānayoḥ*). 5. *kṣa-sa-manin*. 6. *a-ṭa*: "It does not exist for us" (*asmākam nāsti*). 7. *na-ta-da-dha-pha-śa-ga*: "The Ṛbhus. 8. *a-ṭa-ga*: "In the beloved, may we overcome" (*priye'bhi abhibhavema*). 9. *kṣa-ṭa-sa-īyasun*. By the rule "of the final *ṭi*" (*ṭeriti*), there is elision of the *ṭi*.
O Ṛbhus, you fashioned the cow from the hide; O sons of Sudhanvan, you joined the mother again with a calf.
You, the men, performing noble deeds, made your parents young and vigorous.

O R̥bhus, you fashioned a cow from the hide; you reunited the mother with her calf once more. Thus, O sons of Sudhanvan, men of skillful workmanship, you made your parents young and vigorous again. || 8 ||
The cow of a certain person died.
Seeing the calf of that cow, the seer praised Ṛbhu.
The Ṛbhus fashioned another cow similar to it, covered it with its hide, and joined it together with that calf.
This meaning is established in the first half [of the verse]:
"O Ṛbhus, you [were fashioned] from the hide—that is, by means of the hide, the skin;
the genitive case is used in the sense of the instrumental."
"You milked the cow until she was completely drained, you made her exhausted and joined her [with the calf];
thereafter, you reunited that mother-cow with the calf—you made them meet, so to speak.

Furthermore, O Saudhanvanas, sons of Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, O R̥bhus, leaders of the sacrifice, through *svapastyā*—that is, by the desire for noble deeds, namely by the performance of sacrifices, gifts, and other such acts."
You made the parents—the father and mother—who were exhausted, worn out, and aged, young again, endowed with renewed youth; you performed this deed.
The root *piś* is used in the sense of "dividing" (*avayava*);
it belongs to the Taudādi class.
The augment *num* is applied by the rule *śeṣāt* for roots such as *muc*.
*Saudhanvanāsaḥ*:
the sons of Sudhanvan are the Saudhanvanas.
By [Pāṇini’s rule] *an* (Pā. Sū. 6.4.167), there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*).
By [the rule] *ājaserasuk*, and by *āmantritasya ca*, there is the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable.
*svapastyā*:
"Excellent water" is *svapaḥ*;
the desire for that is *svapasyā*.

The suffix *kyac* is applied after the word *sup* (nominal stems) when expressing the self (*ātman*). According to the rule *apratyayāt*, the suffix *akāra* is added in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*). Thus, *jivṛtsā*.
The root *jṛ* is used in the sense of "loss of vitality" (*vayohāni*).
By the rule *jṛdhāstṛjādyabhyaḥ kvin* (Uṇādi Sūtra 4.494), the suffix *kvin* is applied.
Then, by the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ*, the vowel *ṛ* is changed to *i*.
There is a transposition of the places of the letters *repha* and *va*.
Due to the frequentative nature of the rule (*bahulavacanāt*), the lengthening occurs by the application of *Pāṇini 6.3.63* (*halaśca*).
The initial udātta accent is applied by *Pāṇini 6.2.49* (*nistvādyaudāttatvam*).
*yuvānā*: the vowel *ā* is the replacement for the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. *pitarā*.
*Pitā* and *mātā* form the compound *pitarau*.
By the rule *pitā mātrā* (Pāṇini 1.2.70), *pitā* remains [as the single substitute]. As before, the case-ending is replaced by the vowel *ā*.
*akṛṇotana*.
[The root] *kṛvī* belongs to both the classes *hiṃsā* (injury) and *karaṇa* (doing).
Due to its being marked with *it*, there is the insertion of *num*.

The suffix *u* is applied by the rule *dhanvi-kṛṣṇy-or-a-ca*; simultaneously with that, the letter *v* is replaced by *a*. When the subsequent *a* is elided, because of its status as a *sthānivadbhāva*, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel. For the middle plural form *ta* of the *laṅ* tense, the substitute *tan* is applied by the rule *tasa-nasana-thānaś-ca*.
Because it possesses the nature of *pit*, it lacks the quality of being *ṅit*, and therefore it is unaccented (*anudātta*).
With strengths, O Indra, bestow upon us wonderful wealth in the winning of booty;
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
With strengths, O Indra, who possess the *Ṛbhus*, aid us in the winning of booty; bestow upon us wonderful wealth. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
O Indra, accompanied by the Ṛbhus— namely Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, and Vāja— all three being designated here by the term "Ṛbhu" through figurative usage—

you, joined with them, in the "vājasāti"— that is, upon the occasion of the acquisition or distribution of "vāja," meaning food— do "viddhi" us, that is, pervade us with "vājebhiḥ," meaning foods. Or alternatively:
"Vājasātā" is the name of a mantra.
O Vājasāta, through the *vājebhiḥ*—that is, by means of the *ṛbhūs* who are endowed with vigor (*vāja*)—know us in battle; protect us.
Furthermore, bestow (*ā darṣi*) upon us wonderful (*citra*) and praiseworthy (*cāyanīya*) wealth (*rādhas*); that is, exert yourself to give it to us.
In the third pressing, [the verse] "With the Ṛbhus at the winning of booty" (Ṛgveda 1.111.1) is not present.

Because Indra is present [in Mitra], there is a praise of Indra by way of association. "That which has been requested by us—our own—that may Mitra and the others honor (*mamahaṃtām*), that is, revere. In the word *vājasātau*: the root *vana* and *ṣaṇa* mean "to gather" (*saṃbhakti*). The suffix *kvin* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*). By the rule *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ*, the vowel substitution (*ātvam*) occurs. Thus, it means "that in which there is a gathering (*sāti*) of strengths (*vāja*). In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the accent remains on the first member (*pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*). In *avidbhi*: the root *viṣ* means "to pervade" (*vyāptau*). The suffix *hi* is the substitute for the imperative (*loṭ*). By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the *śap* suffix is elided. By the rule *huślavyo herdhiḥ*, *dhi* replaces *hi*. By the rule *hutvajaśve*, and because of the inclusion of the word *dṛś* in the rule *chandasyapi dṛśyante* (Pāṇini 6.4.73), the augment *aṭ* is added to the imperative (*loṭ*). Alternatively, from the root *ava* in the imperative, by the frequentative statement (*bahulavacanāt*) in the rule *siddhabahulaṃ leṭi*, the *sip* suffix is used. Because it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the augment *iṭ* is added. [The doubling of the *d*] is by the rule *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*.
“Yuvata.

Here, by virtue of its semantic force, the word *yuvan* denotes merely the state of being young (*yuvatva*) as the basis for its application (*pravṛttinimitta*). [The suffix *matup* is added] according to the rule “*tadasminn asti*” (Pāṇini 5.2.94), resulting in *yuvata*.
The elision of phonemes is according to Vedic usage.
Fashion for our sacrifice, O Ṛbhus, food accompanied by wealth, for sacred law and skill, together with offspring;
so that we may dwell with a clan consisting entirely of heroes, you shall bestow upon our host your own inherent power.

For our sacrifice, fashion skillful vital strength; for holy order and wisdom, fashion food accompanied by noble offspring, so that we may dwell with a clan consisting entirely of heroes. Grant that excellent Indra-power to our host.
O Ṛbhus, for our sacrifice—for the purpose of the sacrifice—fashion, produce on all sides, the *vayas* (food characterized by oblations) accompanied by *ṛbhu* (extensive manifestation).
This very point is further explained:
[fashion it] for *ṛtu* (our ritual action) and for *dakṣa* (strength).
The dative case is used for that purpose.

For the sake of both these [purposes], [the text says]: "We invoke the lord of the *ṛbhus*, Indra, who is accompanied by excellent offspring characterized by sons, grandsons, and so forth, for our protection; [we invoke] the *ṛbhus*, the *vājas*, and the Maruts for the drinking of Soma."
May both Mitra and Varuṇa, and now the Aśvins, impel us toward gain, toward prayer, and toward victory.

I invoke R̥bhukṣan, Indra, for our protection; I call upon the R̥bhus, the Vājas, and the Maruts to drink the Soma. May both Mitra and Varuṇa, and now the Aśvins, impel us toward gain, toward prayer, and toward victory. ||4||

To Ṛbhukṣan—this is great knowledge. I invoke, I call upon, the great Indra. For what purpose? For protection (*ūtaye*). Likewise, [I invoke] the Ṛbhus and Vājas. Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, and Vāja are the three sons of Sudhanvan; therein, by means of the words denoting the first and the last, the middle one is also implied. Therefore, all three are expressed by the two terms. As it has been said by Yāska: "The plural number is used for the first and the last, but not for the middle" (Nirukta 11.16). Such Ṛbhus and Maruts I invoke for the drinking of Soma, for the sake of consuming the Soma. Likewise, both [the pairs] in their dual form.

The root *śo* means "to thin" (*tanūkaraṇe*). By the rule "in the Veda [the suffix] is frequently [omitted]," there is the elision (*ślu*) of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*). By the rule "it is a substitute," there is the substitution of *āśvam*. There is reduplication (*dvirbhāva*). Upon the shortening [of the vowel], by the rule "in the Veda [it is] frequently [short]," there is the shortening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Thus: *aviṣṭu*. From the root *av* in the imperative (*loṭ*), by the inclusion of the word "frequently" in the rule "the suffix *sip* is frequently [used] in the subjunctive (*leṭ*"), there is the suffix *sip*. There is the addition of the augment *iṭ*. Thus: *paṣṭuve*. || 32 ||
‘Īḷe’ is the seventh hymn, consisting of twenty-five verses.
It is the seerly composition (ārṣam) of Kutsa, the descendant of Aṅgiras.
The twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth verses are *triṣṭubh*s; the remaining twenty-three are *jagatī*s.
The first quarter-verse belongs to Heaven and Earth;
the second belongs to Agni;
the remainder of the hymn belongs to the Aśvins.

And thus it has been enumerated: "I praise the Aśvins; the first two quarters have five syllables more [than the norm], while the others have deities indicated by their internal marks (liṅga); they are Triṣṭubhs.
This hymn is also used in the Pravargya and the Abhiṣava rites.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "‘O Heaven and Earth, you are indeed stones’" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.6).
Furthermore, this hymn is used in the Prātaranuvāka of the Āśvina sacrifice when the metre is Jāgata.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "‘We have gone to the great ones... O Heaven and Earth, you two have helped us’—this is the Jāgata [hymn]" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.15).
This [rule] applies also to the *āśvina-śastra* because of the extension (*atideśa*) stated as "according to the principle of the *prātaranuvāka*" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 6.5).
Likewise, in the *asoyāma*, there are four *atiriktottha* [hymns];
among them, this hymn occurs in the *atiriktottha* of the Acchāvāka.
In the section titled "He whose cattle," it is sūtra-ed: "I praise both Heaven and Earth, even now" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 9.11).
I praise Heaven and Earth for their primordial thought; I praise Agni, the radiant heat, for our journey’s fulfillment.
O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith you quickened Kāra for his share of the prize, come hither to us with those very protections.

I praise Heaven and Earth for their primordial wisdom; Agni, the radiant heat, for our journey and for the sacrifice. With those aids wherewith you quicken the singer for the sake of the Soma-portion—O Aśvins, come hither with those very protections! 1.
I praise—that is, I laud—the two, Heaven and Earth.
For what purpose?
For "prior perception," that is, for the sake of making known [the arrival] of the Aśvins beforehand.
For they are indeed close to the Aśvins.
Or rather:
"I praise Dyāvāpṛthivī as the two Aśvins for the sake of first perception"—that is, for the awakening of our own hymn of praise even before the hymns of others.
And so it has been said: "Some [say] those two are the Aśvins, [others] heaven and earth" (Nirukta 12.1).

Furthermore, the sense is: "In every journey—that is, upon the arrival of the Aśvins—I praise Agni, who has been established in the form of an invocation for the sake of sacrifice, that is, for the purpose of his own ritual service.
Of what nature is this Agni?
"Bring the *gharma* vessel, blazing with the *pravargya* rite, and therefore endowed with beautiful luster;
O Aśvins, bring it!
This is the name of the battle."
In battle, for the sake of a share—that is, for the portion belonging to you—to be taken as victory, they come with those aids and protections;
"kāram" [is used here], for the learned state that the word *kāra* denotes a conch shell; they engage in the combat.
"O you two who grant success, you who cause the sound-making conch to resound, fill it with your mouths; with those such protections (ūtībhīḥ),
along with them— 'u' being used as a conjunction—
come well even to us who are unequal."
*Īḷe*. [The root] *īḍ* means "to praise. *Iḍ* is the first person singular form.

Because it belongs to the *adādi* class, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*. Due to its being unaccented (*anudātta*), the *lasārvadhātuka* suffixes are also unaccented, and thus the accent of the verbal root remains. [The compound] *dyāvāpṛthivī*.
"Cauśca" means "and pṛthivī.

In the form "dyāvā" (from "divo dyāvā"), the substitute "dyāvā" is prescribed as having the udātta accent on its first syllable. The word "pṛthivī," ending in a long vowel, has the udātta accent on its final syllable.
In the case of a dual compound of deities (*devatā-dvandva*), there is the preservation of the original accent of both members (*ubhayapada-prakṛti-svaratva*).

Because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) by the rule "not [in the case of] *apṛthivī*," the prohibition stated in "not when the second member begins with an unaccented vowel" (*nottarapade 'nudāttādau*) does not apply.
By the rule "optionally in the Veda" (*vā chandasi*), the long vowel resulting from the homogeneous combination of the preceding vowel (*pūrvasavarṇa-dīrghatva*) is applied.
*pūrvacittaye* | [The root] *cit* means "to perceive" (*saṃjñāna*).
From this [root], with the sense of "containing within" (*antarbhāvita*)—
1. Even in the case of the *kṣa* and *ṭa* [consonants], there is the *antaryāma*.

*vyāṃt*: The suffix *ki* is applied after the root *vi-āp* because it belongs to the *marud-vṛdha* group; thus, there is udātta accent on the final syllable of the first member (*pūrvapada*). *surucam*: From the root *ruc* meaning "to shine" and "to be beautiful," the suffix *ki* is applied in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) according to the rule for *saṃpad-ādi* compounds. It means "one who possesses beautiful luster. By the rule *nañ-subhyām*, the final syllable of the second member (*uttarapada*) is udātta. *yāman*: From the root *yā* meaning "to go" or "to reach," the suffix *manin* is applied in the sense of an abstract noun (*bhāve*) by the rule *āto manin-kvanib-vanic-aś-ca*, based on the general statement *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*. *kāram*: That by which something is done is called *kāra*; the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). By the rule *karṣāvataḥ*, the final syllable is udātta. *jinvatha*: From the root *jivi* meaning "to please. Here, filling (*āpūraṇa*) is indicated as the cause of pleasure. For a person becomes pleased when filled with wealth. The suffix *tumun* is used because it denotes an action intended for another (*idistvāt*). It belongs to the *bhūvādika* class. Due to the *pit*-nature of the *śap* affix, it is *anudātta*. Since the verbal suffix (*tiṅ*) has an *adupadeśa* (a vowel as its upadeśa), the accent of the root remains by the rule regarding *lasārvadhātuka* accents. There is no prohibition of the *nighāta* (elision of accent) by the rule *yadvṛttādanityam*, for it is stated therein that the operation is desired even when there is an intervention (Kāśikā 8.1.66). *ūṣu*: Lengthening occurs by the rule *ikaḥ suji*.

O leaders, you two Aśvins, endowed with the power (*majman*) born from drinking the divine (*divya*), celestial (*divi-bhava*), and heaven-born nectar (*amṛta*)—Soma—you two rule over the governance, the instruction, and the training of all those *viśas*, the subjects, in whatever worlds they dwell. This is an act of sovereignty: you are capable, you possess the power [to do so].
Or rather:

by *majmanā*, through your own extraordinary power, you two rule (*kṣayathaḥ*)—that is, you possess sovereignty—over the granting (*praśāsane*) and bestowing (*pradāne*) of the nectar (*amṛta*) existing in heaven for the sake of the people (*viśām*), that is, for all creatures.

Moreover, with those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*), that is, protections, you two caused (*pinvathaḥ*) the barren cow (*asvām dhenum*)—meaning a cow incapable of bearing young—to swell with milk for the sage Śayu; the sense is that you filled her with milk.
"With those aids," and so forth, as before.
*Asvam*. [The root] *ṣūk* [is used] in the sense of "the release of the embryo of living beings."
*Savana* means "giving birth.
The suffix *kip* is used here in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) according to the rule for *saṃpad-ādi*.
That in which there is no *sū* (giver of birth) is called *asuḥ*.
By the rule "nambubhyām," the final syllable of the compound is udātta (acute-accented).
In the case of the nominative singular ending *am*, the substitution of *yaṇ* occurs according to the rule "oḥ supi.
By the rule "udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ," the following anudātta (non-acute) vowel becomes svarita (circumflex-accented).
*pinvathaḥ*. [The root] *pivi* means "to sprinkle.
Because it is marked with the *idit* designation, the augment *num* is applied.
[The root *aj*] belongs to the *bhū* class (*bhauvādika*).
With those aids by which the all-pervading one, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, the twice-born, the swift, the crosser, and the far-reaching one desires to move;
with those aids by which Trimantu became far-seeing—with those aids, O Aśvins, come hither.

With those [powers] by which Parijman, the son of Tanaya, and Dvimātṛ, swift and far-reaching, desire to overcome; with those by which Trimantu became far-seeing—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither! 4.
Vāyu, the one who moves everywhere, [is the father] of Tanaya, his own son, Agni.
For Agni is born when he is kindled by Vāyu, which exists as the vyāna breath.
And thus it is heard in scripture: "Now, that which is the junction of prāṇa and apāna is vyāna."

Therefore, regarding other vigorous actions, it is said: "As the fire, when fanned by the wind, runs forth from its source, so he makes the drawing of that bow, the filling of the quiver, and the shooting of arrows" (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 1.3.3; 5).
Alternatively, his status as the son of Agni arises from his birth from Vāyu at the Pṛṣṭhya and other rites.
And it is handed down in scripture: "From wind, fire" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 8.1).
Thus, being endowed with *majman*, that is, with strength, Agni—the son—is the "double-mothered," the creator of two worlds.
Fire has the earth as its locus, while wind has the intermediate space as its locus.
When both are joined together, it is logical that they both act as the progenitor;
or alternatively,
"having two mothers" (*dvimātṛ*) is an epithet of the son.
By the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the genitive case ending is replaced by *su*.
"Of the two-mothered" (*dvimātṛkasya*) means one who is born from two kindling-sticks (*araṇi*).

O Aśvins, such a Vāyu, through those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*)—meaning protective supports acting as causes—becomes a "crosser" (*taraṇiḥ*), one who crosses exceedingly and moves swiftly, among those who run in the four directions; he "prevails" (*vibhūpati*), meaning he becomes pervasive.
Or rather:
he especially adorns everything.

Moreover, Kakṣīvān—the knower of the three (trimantuḥ), who has acquired knowledge regarding the three types of sacrifices, namely the *pākayajña*, *haviryajña*, and *somayajña*—became possessed of distinguished knowledge (*vicakṣaṇaḥ*) through those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*) belonging to you.
With all those aids, come hither,

O Aśvins! *Parijmā* [is derived] from the root *aja* preceded by *pari*, meaning "to go" or "to cast," and is formed as an irregular (*nipātana*) word according to the rule beginning with *śru-bṛkṣan*.
In *turṣu*,
[the root] *tṛ* [is used in the sense of] "floating" and "crossing. The substitution of *u* for *ṛ* occurs by the rule "frequently in the Veda" (*bahulaṃ chandasi*).
The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule "hali ca.
Alternatively,
[the form is derived] from the root *svar* with the suffix *kvip*.
By the rule *jvaratvara* etc., there is the substitution of *uṭ* for the vowel and the following consonant.
By the rule *sāvekācaḥ*, the case-ending receives the udātta accent.
[He] rules as a sovereign (*vibhūpati*).
In the *leṭ* [subjunctive] mood of the root *bhū*, there is the augment *aṭ*.
By the rule "the suffix *sip* is frequently used in the *leṭ*," the suffix *sip* is applied.
Alternatively:
The root *bhūṣ* means "to adorn";
it belongs to the *bhvādi* class.
[The word] *vicakṣaṇaḥ*.

The suffix *yuc* is applied by the rule "anudāttetaśca halādeḥ. 1. *kṣa*: of one born in heaven; 2. *kṣa*: the creator, the Sun; 3. *kṣa*: from both [factors] combined; 4. *kṣa*: the substitution of *da*.

"Without these [aids], you two did not gladden [us]; you two satisfied us. This will be made clear in another mantra, beginning with "The Aśvins indeed gladdened Bhujyu in the ocean" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.116.3). Furthermore, "with those aids by which you gladden—that is, satisfy—Karkandhu and Varvya," who were being oppressed by the Asuras. The rest is understood. Regarding *jasamānam*: the root *jasu* means "to injure"; although the suffix *yak* would have been expected, there is a metrical substitution (*vyatyaya*) for *śap*. Regarding *āraṇe*: from the root *at* preceded by *ā*, the suffix *lyuṭ* is applied. *Jijinvadhuḥ*: the root *jici* means "to please"; this is the form in the perfect tense (*liṭ*) with the ending *athus*.
With those aids by which you helped Śucanti, the winner of wealth, the praiser, the swift one who follows the heat;
with those by which you protected Pṛśnigu and Purukutsa—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.

With those [powers] by which you made *Śucanti*, the winner of wealth (*dhana-sā*), the one with a good assembly (*su-saṃsad*), and *Tasa*—who was like a heated vessel (*gharma*) full of nourishment (*omyāvat*)—[prosperous] for Atri; and with those [powers], O Ashvins, you two showerers of desires (*vṛṣaṇā*), by which skillful acts (*śacībhiḥ*) or insights (*prajñābhiḥ*), you made the lame sage named Paravṛj free from lameness;
and likewise, by which aids (*yābhir utibhiḥ*) you brought about for the blind sage Aśva the sight (*cakṣase*) so that he might see clearly with his eyes.
And by those aids with which you two caused Śr̥ṇa—who had deformed knees—to go forth to seek the Seven Seers;
and furthermore, by those aids with which you released Vartikā, the female of a bird resembling a sparrow, who was seized and cast before a wolf, freeing her from the mouth of the wolf.

According to Yāska’s interpretation, however, it should be construed thus: "by those [aids] with which you liberated that Vartikā—the Dawn who returns day after day—from the wolf, namely the Sun, whose light is spread abroad."
Come with all these protections, you who are without equal.
*vṛṣaṇā* | [The root] *vṛṣ* [is used] in the sense of "to sprinkle. [The suffix] *kanin* [is applied] according to the rule *yuṣi...* etc.
*Mīḷha* is a name for wealth.
O lords of abundant wealth, in battle, by means of those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*), you made him capable of going toward the one who was not yet born.
And this will be made clear in the verse: "For his footstep cuts through the enemy like a leaf" (*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.116.15).
And with those aids by which you protected the seer named Vaśa— the son of Aśva, known as Aśvya, the impeller of praise—
come to us also with all those protections.
"Preṇim. [The root] "preṇu" is used in the senses of motion, impelling, and joining.
The suffix *i* is added according to the *Uṇādi* rules.
With those aids by which, O bounteous ones, the vessel of honey flowed for the merchant Dīrghaśravas, son of Uśij,
and with those by which you protected Kukṣīvant the singer— come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent succors.

With those [aiding hands], O bounteous givers, with which you caused the honey-cask to flow for the merchant Auśija Dīrghaśravas, and with which you protected Kukṣīvant the singer—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent aids! 11.

Uśij was the name of Dīrghatamas’s wife; her son, named Dīrghaśravas, engaged in trade for the sake of his livelihood by means of working with gold. He praised the Aśvins for the sake of [recovering] his wealth, and those two Aśvins impelled the cloud.
This meaning is set forth in the first half [of the verse]:

O "Sudānū," you two Aśvins of beautiful bounty, by means of those aids (*ūti*) of yours which served as the cause, the cloud (*kośa*)—that is, the rain-cloud—flowed forth *madhu*, the rain-water endowed with sweetness; the sense is that through your favor, the desired rain came to pass. Furthermore, by means of those same aids, you protected the singer Kakṣīvān, the son of Uśij, who bears this name.
With all those aids, come to us as well.
Kakṣīvant: *kakṣyā* means a girth-rope; he who possesses such a thing is Kakṣīvant. Thus equipped is Kakṣīvant.
The substitution of *v* for the suffix *matup* in the forms *āsandīvat*, *adhīvát*, *cakrīvat*, and *kakṣīvat* occurs by virtue of this grammatical rule (*nipātana*);
there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).
With those [powers] by which you crushed the Rasa with its flood of waters, by which you turned back the chariot for victory,
and by which you brought forth Triśoka’s cows— come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids.

With those [aids] by which you two crushed the Rasā with a flood of water; with those by which you protected the chariot for victory; with those by which Triśoka drove forth the cows—O Aśvins, come hither with those excellent aids! 12.

"Rasā is a river; it comes from the root *ras*, meaning 'to sound'," says Yāska (Nirukta 11.25). O Aśvins, by those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*) acting as causes, you two filled with water (*udaḥ*) the river Rasā—which was devoid of water—by causing its banks to overflow with a flood (*kṣodasā*). Likewise, by those [aids], you [filled] your own chariot (*ratham*), which was "unfailing" (*anaśam*) and endowed with wealth, in order to conquer (*jiṣe*).

1. [The word] *kṣa* has this designation (*saṃjñā*). 2. *kṣa*: by means of those [suffixes], as previously stated. 3. *kṣa-ṭa*: that which is designated as *uśija*. 4. *kṣa-ṭa*: the term "Aśvinau" does not exist [here]. 5. *kṣa-ṭa-sa*: for Dīrghaśravas, who is of celebrated fame (*prathitayaśas*). 6. *kṣa-ṭa-sa*: and there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*).

With your aids, come to us, O you who are most swift to arrive. And with those aids by which Triśoka, the seer and son of Kaṇva, drove forth the stolen cows from the presence of the Asuras—come to us with all those aids. Regarding *kṣodasā*: the root *kṣudir* means "to crush. The suffix *asun* is added according to the Uṇādi rules, resulting in *kṣodaḥ*. For the instrumental singular, the rule *supāṃ supo bhavanti* prescribes the substitution of *śas*. By the rule beginning with *pahan*, the word *udaka* becomes *udan*. In the technical designation *bha*, the rule *alopo'naḥ* causes the elision of the vowel *a*. Regarding *pipinvathuḥ*: the root *pivi* means "to sprinkle. Because it is marked with *it*, the augment *num* is added. Regarding *jiṣe*: the root *ji* means "to conquer. The suffix *kse* is applied in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) by the rule *tumarthe sesena*. Regarding *udājata*: the root *aja* means "to move" or "to throw."

With those aids wherewith you go around the sun in the distance, wherewith you protected Mandhātṛ in the contests for lordship over the fields, wherewith you protected the sage Bharadvāja—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids, indeed! 13. With those [aids] wherewith you go around the sun in the far distance; wherewith you protected Mandhātṛ in the lordships of the fields; wherewith you protected the inspired singer Bharadvāja—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither, yes, come! 13.
O Aśvins, with those aids by which you go around— that is, you protect— the Sun, who was situated in the distance, in a far-off place, the Āditya enveloped by Svarbhānu in the form of darkness,
and likewise [you protected] the seer Mandhātṛ in the contests for fields;
for "field-lord" (kṣetrapati) means the lord or master of fields.
Protect us in the rites connected with that;
moreover, with those aids by which you protected the wise Bharadvāja, the seer, preeminently through the granting of food—
come to us as well for our protection, accompanied by all those aids.
In the case of *kṣetrapatya*,
since [the group] beginning with *brāhmaṇa* is an *ākṛtigaṇa*, the suffix *vyañ* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*).

With those aids wherewith you protected the great Atithigva, Kaśoju, and Divodāsa in the slaying of Śambara; with those wherewith you protected Trasadasyu at the breaking of the forts—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us. yābhir mahām atithigvam kaśojuvam divodāsam śambarahatye āvatam | yābhiḥ purubhidyai trasadasyum āvatam tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā ā gatam || 14 || With those [aids] by which you protected the great Atithigva, Kaśoju, and Divodāsa in the slaying of Śambara; with those by which you protected Trasadasyu for the breaking of the forts—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither. || 14 ||

He [the Aśvin] [delivered] the great Divodāsa— named thus— the son of Atithigva (who is to be approached by guests), the possessor of swift horses, one who goes to enter the waters for fear of the Asura, such a royal seer, during the slaying of Śambara; for "śambara" means a weapon, and the Asura is so called because he is equipped with that.

When his slaughter had become the object [of your action], you protected him with those aids; moreover, with those aids, you protected Trasadasyu— the son of Purukutsa and the seer named thus— during the *pūrbhidyā*, that battle in which cities (*pur*) are broken down.
"By them," and so forth, as before.

*mahāṃ*: [the form] *mahāntam* has undergone a Vedic elision of the vowel. 1. *kṣa-ṭa-sa-agamayatamam*: *ava* here has the sense of "going. 2. *kṣa-sa-asuraiḥ apahatāḥ*. 3. *ṭa-tadvānasuraḥ śambaraḥ*. 4. *kṣa-ṭa-badhe*. 5. *kṣa-ṭa-sa-yuvāṃ arakṣatam*. 6. *kṣa-ṭa-puraḥ*. 7. *kṣa-ṭa-rājarṣim*. 8. *kṣa-samānam*. (Kaṇḍikā 86)
*Kaṣojuvam*. *Kaśaḥ* is a name for water;
[it is derived from] the root *kaś*, meaning "to move" or "to instruct."
Because it impels various waters, it is called *kaṣojuḥ*;
*ju* means a mantra, that is to say, a root.
The suffix *kvip* and the lengthening [of the vowel] are applied by the rule *kvivaci* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.215),
resulting in *divodāsam*.
The absence of elision (*aluk*) is established by the rule *divaśca dāse pañcamyā alug vaktavyaḥ* (Kāśikā on Pāṇini 6.3.21.5).

The acute accent on the first syllable of the preceding member [in *divodāsa*] is due to the rule "There is an addition [to the list] for *divodāsa* and others in the Vedic language" (Pāṇini 6.2.91.1).

In *śambarahantye*, the suffix *kyap* is applied to the root *han* in the sense of an abstract state (bhāva) by the rule "And *t* [is substituted] for *han*" (Pāṇini 3.3.96); furthermore, through that [suffix], there is the substitution of the final *t* for the root.
The original accent of the final member of a compound ending in *kruddha* [is retained].

With those aids by which you protected Vṛtra when he was drinking, Upastuta, Kali, and Vittajani when he sought your favor; with those by which you helped Vyashva and Pṛthi—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent aids! 15 With those [aids]... Vṛtra... drinking... Upastuta... Kali... with those... Vittajani... seeking favor... with those... Vyashva... and... Pṛthi... you protected... with those... indeed... well... aids... O Aśvins... come hither! 15
O Aśvins, with those aids by which you protected Vatra—the son of Vikhanas—this Ṛṣi known as Saṃjña, who was drinking especially the earthly essence;
how was he?
He was "upastuta," being properly praised by those standing nearby.
Likewise, with those aids by which you protected (duvasyathaḥ) the sage named Kali when he had acquired wealth and a wife;
and also (uta), with those aids by which you protected (āvatam) the royal seer named Pṛthī, who was deprived of his horses (vyaśva)—
the rest is as before.
*vipipānam*:
from the root *pā* in the sense of "drinking";
the suffix *cānaś* is used here in the sense of habitual action (*tācchīlika*).
By the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is *ślu* (elision) of the suffix *śap*;
by the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," there is shortening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Thus: *upastutam*.
There is a completion of the action through hymns of praise;
by the rule *pravr̥ddhādi* (Pāṇini 6.2.147), there is the acute accent on the final syllable of the compound.
[He is] *vittajāni*.
He by whom a wife has been obtained is called "vittajāyaḥ. The compound-final suffix *niṅ* is substituted [for the final vowel of] "jāyā" according to Pāṇini Sūtra 5.4.134.
The *y* is elided by the rule "lopo vyor vali."
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member [is maintained]. For example: *vyaśva*. That from which the horse has departed is called *vyaśva*.
When the first member of the compound is acute by virtue of the accent of the *bahuvrīhi*, the following unaccented vowel becomes circumflex (*svarita*) according to the rule "udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ."

With those aids wherewith, O Heroes, you sought a path for Śayu, wherewith for Atri, and wherewith of old you found the way for Manu; with those wherewith you sped to Śara and drove [the chariot] for Syūmaraśmi—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us! 16. With those [aids], O Heroes, for Śayu; with those for Atri; with those of old for Manu, you sought a path; with those you sped to Śara; you drove [the chariot] for Syūmaraśmi—with those, indeed, with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither! 16.

Those two leaders, the Aśvins, in former times (*purā*), at an earlier period, by means of those aids (*ūtibhiḥ*) with which you desired—meaning, you performed—for the seer named Śayu a path (*gātum*) characterized by the exit from suffering;
what was that?
[It is understood] by implication.

1. *kṣa* is elided before *ṭa*, *sa*, and *vainya*. 2. There is elision of *ta*, *da*, *śa*, and *ya*. 3. When the preceding member ends in *kṣa*, it is not *anudātta*. 4. For *kṣa*, there is no *kim*. *ca*, *ṭa*, *sa*, and *sāmarthya* [apply]. This is demonstrated in the Ṛgveda verse (1.116.22): "O Nāsatyas, by your powers (*śacībhiḥ*), you [acted] as if for one lying down. Likewise, in the case of Agni—the seer who was being tormented by the Asuras in the hundred-gated mechanical prison—[the gods] sought, through those aids (*yābhiḥ ūtibhiḥ*) which they desired, a path (*gātu*) characterized by the cooling of the heat-causing fire with cold water, serving as the cause for the departure of suffering.
And this is well known from such passages as, "With snow you two warded off the burning heat of fire" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.116.8).

Likewise, for the sake of the king named Manu, by means of those aids (*ūtayaḥ*), you two created a path (*gātum*) consisting of the sowing of grains such as barley and so forth—a path that serves as the cause for the departure from poverty.
And thus says another mantra: "O Aśvins, sowing barley with the wolf" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.117.21).

Moreover, "to Syūmaraśmi"—one whose rays (raśmi) are woven (syūta) or bound together; to the seer named thus—"with those aids" (ūtibhiḥ), [you two] "drove forth" (ājatam)—the arrows (śārīḥ). *Śara* is a specific kind of bamboo;
the arrows are modifications thereof—[you drove them] against the enemies.
"By those aids," and so forth, as before.
*Narāḥ* [is derived from] the root *nṛ* in the sense of "leading" (*naye*),
with the suffix *ap* according to the rule *ṛdorap*.
The vowel *ā* is the substitution for the case-ending by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. [The form] *śayeve* [is derived from] *śīṅ*, meaning "to sleep."
The suffix *up* is applied according to the rule *bhṛmṛśītṛcari-* (Uṇādi Sūtra 1.7) and so forth. [The word] *īṣadhuḥ* [is derived from] the root *iṣu* in the sense of "desire" (*icchā*).

In the case of the *liṭ* [perfect] suffix *athus*, because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) by the rule "non-homogeneous" (*asavarṇa*, Pāṇini 6.4.78), there is no substitution of *iyaṅ* for the reduplicated syllable; instead, there is a long vowel by way of *savarṇadīrgha*. Thus, from the root *śṛ*, we have *śārīḥ*.
For the sense of modification (*vikāra*), the suffix *ac* is applied after the word *śara* by the rule "beginning with an unaccented vowel" (*anudātādi*).
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ*. [Thus we have] *syūmaraśmi*. [The root] *ṣivu* means "to weave" (*tantu-santāne*).
The suffix *man* is an *uṇādi* suffix [added] to the root *mīv*.
By the rule *cchoḥ śūḍ*, *ūṭ* is substituted.
In a *bahuvrīhi* compound, there is the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the first member.

With those [powers] by which Paṭharvā, exerting himself for the sake of Jaṭhara’s belly, shone like a fire kindled and piled up—those with which you protected Śaryāta in the great contest for wealth—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us. 17. With those [powers] by which Paṭharvā, exerting himself for the sake of Jaṭhara’s belly, shone like a fire kindled and piled up—those with which you protected Śaryāta in the great contest for wealth—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us. 17.
Regarding the word *jaṭhara*, Yāska states: "The Aśvins [produced] the *jaṭhara*; *jaṭhara* means the belly (*udara*), for that which has been eaten (*jagdha*) is contained within it" (Nirukta 4.7).
Being endowed with strength, he who was nourished by the *jaṭhara*—the body—[acted]. The king-sage named Paṭharvan produced this;
this is a name for battle.
In battle, you shone forth on all sides with those aids belonging to you;
there is an illustration for this:
like the fire piled with wood, kindled and set ablaze by the officiating priests in the sacrificial hall.
The meaning is: "just as fire shines, so too [is it]. Furthermore, regarding the statement, "Śaryāta Mānava, contending with Indra in the *mahādhana*"—this is a name for a battle.
With those aids (*ūti*) by which you protect (*avathaḥ*, i.e., *rakṣathaḥ*) us in battle when we are endowed with great wealth—
this and more has already been explained.
He shone; *dīdeti* is a Vedic form meaning "to shine.
He was born.
The root *aja* is used in the senses of "going" (*gati*) and "throwing" (*kṣepaṇa*).
The form [Aja] is derived from the sense "they throw arrows into this," using the suffix *manin* in the locative sense (*adhikaraṇe*), according to the *uṇādi* rules.

Due to the statement, "In the case of an affix beginning with a consonant (*valādi*) that is not a verbal root (*adhātuka*), the substitution of *vī* for *i* is optionally desired" (Kāśikā 2.4.56.2), there is an absence of the *vī* substitution.
The elision of the locative case ending is by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. [Thus we have] *mahādhane*. The form *āram* is derived from *ātman* by the rule *ātmahataḥ*.

1. From the vicinity of *kṣat* (destruction) and *ameḥ* (fire). 2. Characterized by the cooling (*śītīkaraṇa*) of *kṣaya* (decay). 3. Serving as the cause for the departure of *kṣata* (wound) and *dāridrya* (poverty). 4. Continuous (*saṃtataḥ*) from *kṣa*. 5. The suffix *manin* [is applied] to *kṣata*. 6. Produced by pieces of wood (*kāṣṭhaiḥ*).
O Aśvins, with those aids by which you two, O Aṅgiras, went forth with your mind and reached the opening of the cow-pen;
with those aids by which you turned toward the heroic Manu with nourishment—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors!

With those [aids] by which, O Aṅgiras, you two discerned with your mind and went to the forefront in the wide expanse of the flood of cattle; with those aids by which you turned the heroic Manu toward nourishment—with those very excellent succors, O Aśvins, come hither! 18.
The vocative "O Aṅgiras" stands outside the sentence;
by means of it, having addressed himself, the seer impels [himself] toward praise:
"O Aṅgiras, you who are born of the lineage of the Aṅgirases, praise the two Aśvins!"
O Aśvins, being pleased by the hymn worthy of contemplation through the mind, you two— by means of those aids (*ūti*)— thoroughly delight the worshippers;
or rather,
you delight them by means of the mind itself as the instrument.

Likewise, when there was the opening—the disclosure and revealing of the cave-door—of the "cow-flood" (go-arṇasaḥ), that is, the wealth in the form of cattle hidden by the Paṇis in a cave, with those aids (*ūtībhiḥ*) you two went forth ahead of all the gods; moreover, with those aids you two thoroughly protected the heroic and valiant Manu with food and with a weapon of the appropriate kind upon the earth.
With all those aids, come to us as well!
*Nirapyatha* is a form resulting from the transposition of the syllables of *niramayatha*. It means "in the opening."
In the word *grahavṛhaniśrigama*, the suffix *ap* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*).
The acute accent on the final syllable of the compound is determined by the rule *thāthādisvareṇa* (Pāṇini 6.2.144).
With those aids by which you brought wives for Vimada, or with which you bestowed the ruddy cows,
and with which you carried Sudās to godly prosperity— with those very aids come hither, O Aśvins!

With those [horses] by which you carried Patnī to Vimada, or with which you instructed Aruṇī against evil, and with which you brought divine favor to Sudās—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither! 19.
O Aśvins, with those aids of yours by which you brought the wives—the daughters of Purumitra—to Vimada, the seer of that name;
[the word] *agha* is a filler for the verse.
Likewise, with those aids by which you bestowed—directly toward us—the ruddy, reddish-colored, ascending cows, which had not been taught [to come].

Likewise, by those aids (*ūti*) with which you two brought—i.e., caused to reach—the highly praised wealth worthy of the gods (*sudevya*) to King Sudās, the son of Pijavana, who was a giver of auspicious gifts;
"by those [aids]," and so forth, has already been explained.
*patnīḥ*:
*amo* [the suffix *am*] is replaced by *śas* by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). *nyūhathuḥ*.
The root *vah* is used in the sense of "carrying.
Before the suffix *aghus*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) because it belongs to the *yajādi* class;
then follows reduplication and so forth.
Regarding Sudāsa: he is called Sudāsa because he gives beautifully (*śobhanam dadāti*);
[the suffix] *asun* is applied.
*Sudevyam*:
[The suffix] *yat* is applied because it begins with a numeral (Pāṇini 4.3.54).
It bears the *svarita* accent according to the rule "the first syllable is *svarita*" (*tisvaritam*).

1. Born of the lineage of Kṣa-Aṅgīras. 2. By means of that which has become the cause (Ṭa). 3. The wife of Kṣa. 4. Kṣa is for the purpose of filling the meter. 5. Kṣa-Ṭa: moreover. 6. Kṣa-Ṭa: Sudevyam means "relating to Sudeva"; Sudeva is one whose god (deva) is excellent (su). That which exists there [in him] is Sudeva; that which exists relating to him is Sudevyam.

With those aids by which you become sources of well-being for the donor, with which you protect Bhujyu, and with which [you protected] Adrigu; O Aśvins, come hither with those excellent succors, [aiding] Omyāvatī, Subharā, and Ṛtastubh. 20. With those [aids] by which you become sources of well-being (śantātī) for the donor; with which you protect Bhujyu; with which [you protected] Adrigu; [aiding] Omyāvatī, Subharā, and Ṛtastubh—O Aśvins, come hither with those excellent succors (ūtībhiḥ). 20.
O Aśvins, you become the bestowers of well-being through your aids for the sacrificer who has offered oblations;
and by those very aids, you protected Bhujyu, the son of Tugra,
as well as Vadriya.
Adrigu is the pacifier of the gods;
for the Śruti declares, "Both Adrigu and Apāpa are the two pacifiers of the gods" (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.6.6.4).
Moreover, he is Vṛtastubha.

With those [powers] by which you quicken the hero who fights for cattle in the protection of men, at the winning of land and of offspring; with those by which you protect the chariots and the horses—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither! 22. With those [powers]... the hero... who fights for cattle... in the protection of men... at the winning of land and of offspring... with those... you protect the chariots... and the horses... with those... excellent aids... O Aśvins... come hither! 22.

O Aśvins, with those aids by which you quicken—that is, gladden and protect—the man who fights for cattle, meaning one engaged in battle concerning cattle, the leader of the sacrifice, the patron (yajamāna), in a battle to be endured by men (nṛpāhe);
likewise [with those aids] for the field consisting of houses and the like;
and the word *tanaya* signifies wealth.
With those aids by which you protect the sacrificer for the sake of the attainment and enjoyment of his son and wealth;
and with those [aids] by which [you protect] the sacrificers...

They overcome (*turvanti*). The suffix *iti* is an *auṇādika* (irregular) suffix. Regarding *dabhītim*: from the root *dambhu* in the sense of "to deceive," the suffix *kīti* is an *auṇādika* suffix. Regarding *dhvasantim*: from the root *dhvaṃsu* in the sense of "motion" and so forth, the suffix *jhi* is an *auṇādika* suffix; by the rule "of those [roots] ending in *an* or *it*," there is elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*), and "the *jhi* becomes *anta*. Regarding *puruṣantim*: one who bestows or gives much (*puru*) is *puruṣanti*. By the rule "the suffixes *ki*, *ka*, and *k* are used in technical names (*saṃjñā*)," the suffix is *kit*; by the rule "there is no [elision of the nasal] when *ki* follows, and there is lengthening," the elision of the nasal and the lengthening are prohibited.
O Aśvins, make our speech eloquent; O Dastras, O Bulls, fashion our inspired thought for us.
I invoke you both for protection against distress and for our prosperity; be present at the winning of the prize.

O Aśvins, bestow upon us speech that is not barren; O Dastras, O Bulls, grant us inspired thought. I invoke you both for the sake of non-deprivation and for protection; be present for our increase in the winning of booty. 24.
O Aśvins, make our speech full of wealth—*ama* being a name for ritual action; that is, make it endowed with the prescribed rites. Make it effective.
Likewise, O Ashvins—O you who shower down desires (*vavṛṣaṇā*), O destroyers of enemies (*vadatras*)—bestow upon us a mind capable of understanding the meaning of the Vedas.
Moreover, since you two are distinguished by such qualities, I invoke you both most intensely for protection (*vavāṃ... vaavase*) and for the sake of attaining what is desired (*vani vavaye*).
When? [Now.]
At night—devoid of the play of light, devoid of illumination—in the final watch;

for at that time this hymn is recited during the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*) and the *āśvina* litany (*śastra*). O you two, come when summoned to the winning of the prize, to the acquisition of food (*vāja*).
Or rather, this is a name for battle:
"In battle, you two have grown; you became [a source] of growth for us."
*Amasvatīm*:
[The suffix] *asun* is applied with the augment *nuṭ* and the root *gam*, according to the rule "In the sense of an action, the suffix *asun* is optionally applied with *nuṭ* and the short vowel.
Then, the possessive suffix *matup* is added according to the rule "That which belongs to this."
The substitution of *v* for *matup* occurs by the rule *mādupadhāyāḥ*.
Because of the rule *tasau matvarthe*, there is no status as a *pada* (word-final) due to the presence of *aśvena*; consequently, there is no shortening of the vowel and so forth.
[The form is] *asme*.
By the rule "supāṃ suluk...", the sixth case ending is replaced by the substitute "śe".
[The form] "kṛtam" is derived from the root *kṛ* in the imperative mood (*loṭ*), with the elision of the suffixal augment (*vikaraṇa*) according to the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi".
For the sake of non-shining; from the root *dyut* in the sense of "shining," the suffix *ṇyat* is applied in the sense of an abstract action (bhāva) according to the rule *ṛhaloṇyat*.
The vowel *u* results from a transposition of phonemes (*varṇavyatyaya*).
In this case, because there is no manifestation (*prakāśana*) of the meaning within it, the term is a *bahuvrīhi* compound; by way of transposition, the final syllable is circumflex (*svarita*).
[Thus] "I invoke" (*ni hvaye*).
The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied by the rule "nisamupavibhyaḥ hraḥ.
[The word] *vṛdhe* [is derived from] the root *vṛdh*,
meaning "to grow" or "to increase."
The suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) after roots such as *sam-pad*;
the acute accent (*udātta*) on the case-ending is due to the rule "sāvekācaḥ."
O Aśvins, protect us with auspicious blessings that are free from harm, throughout the days and nights!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also the Sky grant us this.
By days and by nights, O Aśvins, protect us on every side with unharmed blessings. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also Heaven grant us this. ||25||
O Aśvins, with your days (*dyubhiḥ*) and nights (*vaktubhiḥ*), protect us, your worshippers, on every side; that is to say, protect us always.
Likewise, protect us with unharmed (*ariṣṭebhiḥ*) and auspicious (*saubhagebhiḥ*) riches that bring about good fortune.
Whatever we have prayed for from you—that wealth—may the five deities, beginning with Mitra, grant it to us.

*Pūjayamnu*: The word *uta* is used in the sense of conjunction (*samuccaye*). Regarding *śubhiḥ*: by the rule *diva ut*, the vowel *u* is substituted [for the final *i* of *div*]. By the rule *divo jhal* (Pāṇini 1.1.183), there is a prohibition of the acute accent on the case-ending (*vibhaktyudāttatva*) which would otherwise apply by the rule *sāvekācaḥ*. Regarding *ariṣṭebhiḥ*: the root *riṣ* means "to injure. The suffix *kta* is applied as a *niṣṭhā*. In this *nañ*-compound, the original accent of the first member, being an indeclinable, remains. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the substitution of *ais* for *bhis* does not take place. Regarding *aśvinā*: by the rule *supāṃ suluk*, the case-ending is replaced by *ā*. By the rule *āmantritasya ca*, the entire word becomes anudātta (unaccented). Regarding *saubhagebhiḥ*: one who possesses beautiful fortune (*bhaga*) or glory (*śrī*) is called *subhaga*. The state of being such is *saubhagam*. The suffix *am* is added because the word is listed among those beginning with *udātta* in the rule *subhagāmmanye*. The rule *hrasvasinvante pūrvapadasya ca*—which would have caused the vr̥ddhi of both members—does not apply here, because all rules are optional in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). As before, the substitution of *ais* for *bhis* occurs. By the rule *pinyādirnityam*, the first syllable is udātta. || 37 ||
By illuminating the meaning of the Vedas and dispelling the darkness of ignorance,
may the Great Lord of the Holy Tīrtha bestow the four aims of human life.

Thus ends the seventh chapter of the first book in the *Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa*, a commentary on the *Ṛgveda-saṃhitā*, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the bearer of the burden of the empire of the illustrious King Vīrabukka—the glorious Emperor, Supreme Lord, and promoter of the Vedic path.
1. The original accent of the final member of the compound [is retained] after *kṣa*. 2. *kṣa* = destroying. 3.
By the teacher Sāyaṇa.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
I bow to that Great Lord Vidyātīrtha, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire universe from the Vedas.
Having thus explained the seventh chapter, the eighth chapter is now begun to be explained.
In the first maṇḍala, seven hymns have passed in the sixteenth anuvāka.
"Idam" is the eighth hymn, consisting of twenty verses.
Regarding this, the *Anukramaṇī* states: "This [hymn] consists of twenty verses; the second half-verse belongs to Rātri.
By the governing rule (*paribhāṣā*) "The seer [is determined] from another source," and by its continued application, Kutsa Āṅgirasa is the seer.
By the rule concerning the lack of specific instruction, the metre is Triṣṭubh.
The deity is Uṣas;
for the second half-verse, Night (Rātri) is also the deity.
This hymn is recited in the Prātaranuvāka, in the Upastha ritual, in the Triṣṭubh metre.

And it is stated in the Sūtra: "This hymn, 'idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pṛthu rathaḥ,' [is used] in the Āśvina-śastra" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.14). Furthermore, this hymn is included in the Āśvina-śastra by extension from the Prātaranuvāka.
This most excellent light among lights has come; a wondrous sign has been born, spreading far and wide.
Just as [the dawn] was sent forth for the impelling of Savitṛ, even so has Night yielded her womb to the approaching Dawn.

This has come, the best light among lights; the brilliant sign has been born, spreading far and wide. Just as [the dawn] was sent forth for the impelling of Savitṛ, even so has Night yielded her womb to the Dawn.
Among the luminaries—the planets, constellations, and so forth—that shine, this light called Dawn (uṣas) is the most excellent, the most highly praised.
If one asks what its superiority consists of, it is said:
the light of the constellations and such illuminates only itself, not anything else.
Although the moon illuminates other things, its illumination is nonetheless not perfectly clear.
But this light of the Upaniṣads illuminates the entire world simultaneously and specifically by dispelling all other causes of ignorance;
therefore, it is most excellent—this is the meaning.
Such a light has come; it has arrived from the eastern direction.

And when it has arrived, its wonderful and praiseworthy radiance—the indicator of all objects enveloped in darkness—has been born, having become manifest as a pervasive and all-encompassing splendor. Furthermore, just as the night itself is brought forth and produced from Savitṛ, the Sun.
For as the sun sets, it generates the night;
when he has set, there is an absence of form (rūpa) during the night.

In this very same way, the night also, for the sake of the dawn—that is, for the production of the dawn—has prepared, that is to say, fashioned, a womb, meaning a place characterized by its own subsequent part, as an opening.
Or rather:

just as the Dawn (*uṣas*) was born from Night (*rātri*) for the impelling (*savāya*), that is, for the generation of Savitṛ, the Sun; even so did Night likewise prepare her womb—her own place characterized by the latter part—for the Dawn, for the sake of the Dawn’s birth. Regarding this, the *Nirukta* states: "This most excellent light among lights has arrived; it has become a wonderful sign, most clearly manifest, and most pervasive. Just as Night, having been impelled for the impelling of Savitṛ, entered the womb of this very Dawn—the place of non-destruction" (*Nirukta* 2.19).

*Śreṣṭha*. From the word *praśasta*, the suffix *iṣṭhan* is applied in the sense of superlative degree (*ātiśāyanika*). [This is according to] Pāṇini Sūtra 5.3.60: "For *praśasta*, [the substitute] *śraḥ*."
1. *Kṣa-ṭa-ṭha*: Thus the seventh chapter has been explained.
The eighth is now being explained; having thus explained the seventh chapter, the explanation of the eighth chapter begins.
2. *Kṣa-ṭa-ṭha*: Because of the extension [of the rule] by the principle of the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*).
3. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha* is praiseworthy (*praśasta*).
4. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha-na* is clear manifestation (*vispaṣṭaḥ prakāśaḥ*); [the absence of these] is indistinct manifestation (*asaṃspaṣṭaprakāśaḥ*).
5. *kṣa-ṭa-ṭha* means most praiseworthy (*praśastatama*).
6. *da*, *dha*, *la*—the illuminator.
7. *kṣa*, *ṭa*, *ṭha*—"san" does not exist.

Thus is the grammatical instruction (*śrādeśa*). Due to the *prakṛtibhāva* (non-application of suffixal changes) by the rule *prakṛtyaikāc* (Pāṇini 6.4.163), there is no elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant). *Agāt*: in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, the substitute *gā* is applied by the rule *iṇo gā luṅi*. By the rule *gātisthā*, there is the elision (*luk*) of the *sic* suffix. *Praketaḥ*: from the root *kita* in the sense of "knowing" (*jñāne*). With the causative sense (*antarbhāvita-ṇic*) implied, the suffix *ghañ* is added in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*). By the rule *thāthādinā*, the final syllable of the compound is accented. *Ajaniṣṭa*: from the root *janī* in the sense of "manifestation" (*prādurbhāve*). In the *luṅ* tense, the augment *iṭ* is added after *sic*. *Vivvā*: by the rule *viprasabhyo ḍupsaṃjñāyām*, the suffix *ḍup* is added to the root *bhū*. By the rule *supāṃ suluk0*, the substitution of *ā* for *s* occurs. Although the rule *o: supi* would normally require the *yaṇ* substitution [of *u* for *o*], the prohibition *na bhū sudhiyoḥ* applies; however, by the rule *chandasyubhayathā*, the *yaṇ* substitution does take place. The initial accentuation is by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). Alternatively, the suffix *ḍup* is added to *bhū* preceded by *vi* as an *auṇādika* formation. Because it is marked with *m* (*mittva*), it has the initial accent. *Prasūtā*: from the root *ṣūṅ* in the sense of "birth of living beings" (*prāṇiprasave*). The suffix *niṣṭhā* is used in the passive sense. By the rule *gatiranantaraḥ*, the preceding prefix (*gati*) retains its original accent (*prakṛtisvara*). *Savāya*: by the Vedic rule *chandasi javasavī vaktavyau*, the suffix *ac* is applied. Because it is marked with *c* (*cittva*), it has the final accent. By the rule *aṇo'pragṛhyasyānunāsikaḥ*, the vowel *a* becomes nasalized (*sānunāsika*) in *saṃhitā*. *Eva*: by the rule *nipātasya ca*, there is lengthening in *saṃhitā*. *Rātrī*: the suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *rātre śrājasau*. By the rule *yasyeti ca*, the *ikāra* is elided. *Arek*: from the root *ricir* in the sense of "separating" (*virecane*). In the *luṅ* tense, the *vikaraṇa* suffix is elided by the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*. After the *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel, the *ṭi* is elided by the rule *halḍyābhyaḥ*. Through the disappearance of the phoneme (*varṇavyāpatti*), the *ekāra* is replaced by *aikāra* by way of transposition (*vyatyaya*). 2.
The ruddy one has come with her ruddy calf; the white one has approached, while the black one follows closely behind her.
Of common kinship, immortal, following one another, they move across the sky, changing their colors.

The bright one with the bright calf has come, the white one; the black one has cleared her seats for her. Having a common kinship, immortal, following one another, the two move across the sky, changing their colors.
*Śvetyā* is a name for the dawn (*uṣas*). *Ruśatī* means shining or radiant; *śvetyā* means white-colored. *Ruśadvatsā* refers to her whose calf—the radiant sun—is shining.

Just as a calf moves about near its mother, so too, because the dawn (uṣas) always remains near the sun, she possesses the nature of a calf. Alternatively, just as a calf carries away the milk of its mother while drinking it, so the dawn is called a "calf" because she carries away the essence (rasa) while drinking it during her stay.
Being such, she has come; she has arrived.

Of this Night who has arrived—she who is dark, of black color—she has extended her own intoxicating places, characterized by the union of the two halves; she has stretched them out, she has spread them, that is to say, she has bestowed them.
The particle *u* is for the purpose of filling the meter.
